# Geopolitical Briefing: State of the World as of September 7, 2026

Compiled for evaluation of mid-2024 predictions. All information sourced from publicly available reporting through September 6, 2026. Last updated: September 6, 2026 (**Day 192**, incorporating the September 5 data cycle: the IRGC launches ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships — an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer — both of which evade, with no American personnel harmed; CENTCOM answers with a mix of Air Force and Navy fighters and drones against three Iranian crude oil carriers, permanently disabling the M/T Downy **off the coast of Kharg Island**, permanently disabling the M/T Stark 1 near Jask and completely destroying the unladen M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman after directing her crew to abandon ship; Adm. Brad Cooper publishes the exchange rate — *“if you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours”* — against what CENTCOM calls a “multibillion-dollar shadow network”; the Downy strike is the first American munition of the war to land in Kharg's waters and **the island, its jetties, tank farm, pumping stations and garrison are not struck, not approached and not landed on**; the IRGC Navy claims six vessels of its own and warns shipping against “unauthorized waterways,” and CENTCOM confirms none; Iran's foreign ministry calls the American strikes a war crime; no strike on Iranian territory and no Iranian launch at a Gulf host state is reported for a second consecutive night; the merchant blockade ledger holds at 87 redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded; Brent $96.28, up 0.53%, with the December 31 reopening probability holding at 27% and six transits against an 85/day baseline; Putin orders a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv as Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Moscow with what Trump calls “a plan to end the war,” Ukraine reciprocates on Moscow, and the reported front-wide Ukrainian hold-fire is denied by the Office of the President and confirmed by a southern brigade command simultaneously; the IDF strikes five locations in Lebanon after a Hezbollah drone attack on Commando Brigade troops, killing at least three and wounding 23 including six rescuers; and **the ground rung does not move for a 192nd day, on the day Iran fired ballistic missiles at an American aircraft carrier.**)

> **Daily update — September 6, 2026 (Day 192; September 5 data cycle).** **Iran fired ballistic missiles at an American aircraft carrier and missed, and the United States answered by destroying part of Iran's export fleet rather than by touching Iranian soil.** On **September 5** the **IRGC launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships** patrolling regional waters — a **US aircraft carrier** and a **guided-missile destroyer**. Per CENTCOM both **“successfully evaded multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks”**; **neither was hit and no American personnel were harmed.** CENTCOM did not name the ships; this briefing has carried **USS George Washington (CVN-73)** with **Carrier Air Wing 5** and **USS Shoup (DDG-86)** on station in the Arabian Sea for **Operation Epic Fury**, and identification with those hulls is **inferred from stationing, not confirmed**, and is logged as an inference. **The American answer was three commercial hulls.** CENTCOM struck **three Iranian crude oil carriers** with a **mix of Air Force and Navy aircraft, both fighters and drones**: the **M/T Downy permanently disabled off the coast of Kharg Island**; the **M/T Stark 1 permanently disabled near Jask**, roughly 700km away on the Gulf of Oman coast; and the **unladen M/T Kylo** (also known as the **“Noxen”**) **completely destroyed in the Gulf of Oman**, struck in multiple critical locations after **the crew was directed to abandon ship** — the same warn-evacuate-destroy sequence used on the two Iranian government tankers of September 1-2, and now the established pattern. **The theatre commander published the exchange rate.** **Adm. Brad Cooper**: *“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: **If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours**.”* He added that Iran **“has no means by which to defend”** its tanker fleet, and CENTCOM described the vessels as part of a **“multibillion-dollar shadow network”** funding the IRGC and its regional proxies. This is the **“tanker for tanker”** policy *Axios* reported on September 2 as **personally approved by the President**, now restated at a **three-for-two ratio** and **decoupled from its original trigger**: Iran attacked **warships**, and the United States answered against **commerce**. **The Kharg line moved by one word, and this briefing amends its own language precisely and no further.** For 191 days this record carried Kharg Island as **not struck, not landed on, not approached**. An American munition has now disabled a ship **in Kharg's anchorage** — the closest American ordnance has come to Iran's principal export terminal in this war, and it is recorded as a real change. It is also **not the tracked prediction**, which concerns **seizure of Kharg and strikes on its oil infrastructure**. The **island's loading jetties, tank farm, pumping stations and garrison were untouched**; **no surface formation approached**; **no American set foot on it**. The Downy was engaged by the same method, on the same day, as hulls near Jask and in the Gulf of Oman, and **Kharg is where roughly 94% of Iranian crude loads**, so any campaign against Iranian tankers will produce hits in its anchorage by arithmetic alone. Whether the position is a **probe** or a **coincidence of geography** cannot be settled from open sources and has been entered in the open-questions register rather than asserted here. Meanwhile the terminal continues to collapse without being touched: **Kpler puts Iranian loadings at 251,000 bpd in August against 1.98m bpd in February**, an **87% fall**, with operations at Kharg halted since **July 31**. **Iran claimed six ships and CENTCOM confirmed none.** The **IRGC Navy** stated it had targeted **three oil tankers** sailing through **“an unauthorized route”** in the Strait of Hormuz and **three vessels affiliated with the United States** elsewhere, warning mariners: *“Do not be deceived by the ‘terrorist’ US military and refrain from any suspicious movement aimed at passing through unauthorized waterways… **Otherwise, you will be targeted**.”* **Through the cutoff US Central Command had not confirmed any of the six**, and **no vessel names, positions, flags, operators or damage assessments were published by either side**. Logged as a **claim, not an event** — American silence is not disproof, and a belligerent's assertion is not evidence. **Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the American strikes as a war crime.** **The ground question received its sharpest test of the war and the answer did not change.** A ballistic-missile attack on a deployed American carrier is close to the maximum provocation available to Iran short of a hit, and is precisely the event against which any prepared ground option would be unsheathed. It produced **no reinforcement order, no alert change, no amphibious tasking, no deployment announcement, no strike on Iranian territory and no movement on the draft.** Force posture holds at **~50,000 personnel and 19 warships**, deployments extended **into 2027**, Army air-defence tours lengthened **from nine months to twelve**, **Adam Telle** still **acting** Secretary of the Army with **no Senate-confirmed chief of staff**. The **Boxer ARG** with the **11th MEU** — publicised by the Navy on **September 3** as carrying **over 2,600 sailors and Marines**, F-35Bs, Ospreys and LCACs and configured **“to support a Marine landing”** — remained on blockade patrol in the **Arabian Sea** and **was not employed**. The **Tripoli ARG** and **31st MEU** remain absent and unreplaced since July. **A theatre commander who answers a missile attack on his carrier by publishing an exchange rate denominated in tankers is describing attrition against revenue — the instrument a command uses instead of land forces, not as a prelude to them.** **Everything else in the theatre held.** No Iranian launch against **Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, the UAE or Erbil** for a second consecutive night; the merchant blockade ledger unchanged at **87 redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded**; the **Kuhestak** internal review, the **five dead** and the **Iranian Red Crescent's ICC letter** all still open; the **Secretary of Defense Orders Book off SIPRNet since September 2 and not restored**; **no USNI Fleet and Marine Tracker since August 31**, a sixth consecutive cycle. **The market's verdict on all of it was fifty-three basis points.** The **straits.live** board carried **Brent at $96.28** at **05 September 2026 2301Z**, **+0.53%**, roughly **34% above** the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline and **well below the ~$120.88 wartime peak**; **six transits** against an **85/day** baseline (**7% of normal**); Strait **closed to commercial shipping**; war-risk **40.0× pre-crisis** (~**$10.0m per VLCC passage**); **December 31 reopening probability held at 27%**; **AAA national average ~$4.14/gal**. **In Ukraine, both capitals stopped shooting at each other so that two American envoys could travel.** **Putin** ordered a **three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv** from **midnight Saturday, September 5**, as **Witkoff** and **Kushner** arrived in **Moscow**; **Peskov** said it is **“connected with the preparation for and conduct of the Americans' contacts in Kyiv”** and **covers the capital only, not the rest of the country**. **Ukraine agreed to refrain from strikes on Moscow** through Saturday, Sunday and Monday, and Washington had asked Kyiv to suspend **drone strikes on Moscow and on Russian energy facilities** for the duration. **Trump**: the envoys are **“bringing with them a plan to end the war.”** They are due in **Kyiv on September 6**; **no terms have been published**. The reported **front-wide Ukrainian hold-fire for September 5-8** is now **denied by a source in the Office of the President** and **confirmed by a servicemember in a southern brigade command** — **both on the record, and not compatible** — against *Ukrainska Pravda's* sourcing of **multiple brigades and a senior security official**. The front remains **largely deadlocked**. **The previous three-day arrangement in this war was violated.** **In Lebanon, the IDF struck five locations** in the southern **Tyre** and **Nabatieh** regions and the eastern **Beqaa Valley** after **Hezbollah** launched an explosive drone at **Commando Brigade** troops in the southern security zone; Lebanon reported **at least three killed and 23 wounded**, with the **Rmadiyeh** strike killing one and wounding **fifteen, including two children, three women and six rescuers**, and **two young men killed on the Ali al-Taher ridge** taken by the **36th Division** on September 4. **No Israeli casualties were reported.** **And the rest of the world produced no new development.** **Latin America:** Rodríguez interim presidency continuous, Maduro and Flores in US custody with no new proceedings, Cuba's blackouts into a sixth month on exhausted reserves, the **September 3-4 sanctions on five Cuban companies and a Castro grandson** standing as the most recent action. **US-China:** no bilateral development; a **summit is scheduled for September 24**; the **Apex Logistics** chip-smuggling investigation continues; **no Chinese action against Taiwan through 192 days of maximum American commitment elsewhere**. **North Korea:** no test, no launch, no incident; the operative Korean datum remains **Seoul's September 4 statement that no Hormuz deployment decision has been made**, with the options under review — **maritime patrol aircraft, logistics support vessel, mine detection and clearance unit** — containing **no ground element**. **Sources:** US Central Command statement and @CENTCOM post, September 5, 2026; > **Daily update — September 5, 2026 (Day 191; September 4 data cycle).** **The President declared possession of a country no American soldier has entered, and the theatre commander opened an investigation into his own command.** Asked about the war on **September 4**, **Trump** said it is **“small potatoes”** and **“not a big thing”** for the United States and that **“we took over Venezuela and we have essentially taken over Iran”**; pressed on the eighteen American service members killed he compared the conflict to **Vietnam** and **Afghanistan**, and asked about Vice President **Vance's** **“I wouldn't call it a war”** he said **“I would say it's a military conflict if you want... I don't think it matters what you call it.”** The claim has no stated referent and therefore no falsification condition, and **CENTCOM's own ledger — 87 vessels redirected, six transits a day against an 85/day baseline, a waterway prediction markets give a 2% chance of reopening this month — does not obviously support it.** Its direction on the tracked ground question is nonetheless unambiguous: **no ground campaign has ever been launched by an administration simultaneously arguing that its war is small and already substantially won.** Running the other way, **CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper ordered an internal review of the Kuhestak wedding strike.** *Reuters* put verified imagery to **four military weapons experts** — **Gareth Collett**, a retired British Army brigadier with a doctorate in explosives engineering (*“consistent with a direct hit, as opposed to secondary damage from a munition ricocheting off a separate target”*); **Trevor Ball**, a former US Army EOD technician (detonation *“on contact with the roof, or just above the roof,”* with remnants possibly from a **JSOW** glide bomb); **Sebastian Schutte** of the Peace Research Institute Oslo (the impact angle **rules out an air-defence missile**); and a fourth — all of whom concluded a **direct hit by a US munition**. **The New York Times**, the **BBC** and independent analysts separately identified a **US Precision Strike Missile**, an airburst weapon dispersing thousands of tungsten pellets. The toll **rose to five** when a 22-year-old woman died in hospital, with **nearly seventy wounded**, most of them women and children per the **Hormozgan Red Crescent**; the **Iranian Red Crescent** wrote to the **International Criminal Court** seeking *“an independent, impartial, thorough, and effective investigation.”* **Vance** moved in one day from *“I'm extremely skeptical of this”* to *“We're investigating it because obviously we care. We want to know.”* **Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick apologised** for having claimed that no Americans died in the Iran war, saying he had meant the **Venezuela** operation; the Pentagon's **wounded figure rose to 767** from 758 on August 28. **There was no third night of Iranian launches and no new American strike wave**; the blockade ledger held at **87 redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded**. **Rubio** restated the price as nuclear and **“primarily economic”** while asserting Iran has **lost control of the waterway**; **Vance's** condition remains maritime. **Brent $95.83, up 0.16%** (Trading Economics: $95.23, −0.31%), **six transits** against an **85/day** baseline, **December 31 reopening 28% → 27%**, and **Mitsui O.S.K. Lines**, the world's largest tanker operator, withdrew its resumption timeline entirely — *“it's difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year.”* **The only ground taken in this war this cycle was taken by the IDF's 36th Division on the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon**, above and below ground, clearing the two-decade Iranian-planned and Iranian-funded headquarters of **Hezbollah's Badr Unit** — and **the Iranian red line that seizure was said to cross produced no attack on Israel**. **Two corrections run against this briefing's own record and both are recorded:** **(1)** the September 4 downgrade of **Dan Driscoll's** departure to *contested* is **withdrawn** — his last day was Wednesday and **Adam Telle**, the Army's civil-works assistant secretary, was named **acting Army Secretary** on Thursday; **(2)** the September 4 finding that **South Korea's Hormuz deployment** was the first new allied military contribution of the war is **withdrawn to untested** — Seoul said publicly that **no decision has been made**, and the options under review are a **maritime patrol aircraft**, a **logistics support vessel** and a **mine detection and clearance unit**. **Kuwait** invoked **Article 51** and **UNSCR 2817** by name, asserting its right to **“take all necessary measures,”** and fired nothing. **Kpler** puts Chinese imports of Iranian crude at **~534,000 bpd in August** against **~823,000 bpd in July**; **Bangladesh's LNG imports fell ~83% in a month**; and **De Nederlandsche Bank moved 86 tonnes of gold out of New York and Ottawa to London**, citing **“increasing geopolitical unrest.”** In Ukraine, **Witkoff and Kushner** go to **Moscow on September 5** and **Kyiv on September 6** with what Trump calls **“a proposal to end the war”**; **Zelensky** pledged **no Ukrainian airstrikes** for the duration and *Ukrainska Pravda* reports an **unannounced order for Ukrainian units to hold fire along the front from September 5 to 8**, while a **Russian drone struck the SBU headquarters in central Kyiv in daylight**, wounding twelve. **The ground rung did not move for a 191st day.**

> **Daily update — September 4, 2026 (Day 190; September 3 data cycle).** **Both governments prosecuting this war named the fall of the Iranian state as the objective on the same day, and neither moved a soldier toward it.** At a Rosh Hashanah toast with the **IDF General Staff Forum** in Tel Aviv, Prime Minister **Benjamin Netanyahu** said toppling the Iranian regime is Israel's **“central mission”** and that the goal is **“within reach”** — *“The regime is now faltering. It is weaker than ever. It is fighting for its survival”*; *“I am confident in our ability to remove this threat once and for all – in other words, to topple this regime.”* President **Trump**, who said in **June** that he **“never cared about regime change”** and was negotiating with **“very rational people,”** posted **“When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?”** and **“I'm not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table. I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing,”** and, asked whether the CIA is supporting Iranian dissidents, answered: *“I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say.”* **US intelligence assessments reported this cycle continue to judge a mass uprising unlikely** despite inflation at **87.9%**, a rial near **2.02 million to the dollar**, and exports and imports down **25-35%** on President Pezeshkian's own account. **The Pentagon answered the ground question in writing, and the answer is duration rather than depth.** The *Wall Street Journal* reports that Secretary of Defense **Pete Hegseth** is extending troop-deployment timelines across the Middle East **into 2027** and has decided the US military will maintain a **“presence of 50,000 troops in the region in part to give the president flexibility on next steps.”** Roughly **50,000 troops and 19 warships, including two aircraft carriers**, are assigned to missions from missile defence to blockade enforcement and shipping escort; elements of the **82nd Airborne Division** may be held **“well into 2027”** per a letter military leaders sent to families; and **standard Army air-defence tours have grown from nine months to twelve**. **A force being prepared for a ground campaign is enlarged and refreshed. This one is capped and stretched — the same units, longer tours, no new brigades, no new amphibious lift, no mobilisation — and no objective on Iranian soil is named anywhere in the reporting.** **The written military objection to going further was removed from the network rather than answered.** *The Washington Post* reported on **September 2** that the Pentagon removed decades of documents associated with the **Secretary of Defense Orders Book** from **SIPRNet** — the record of **“the location and availability of U.S. warships, military units, weapons systems, and other resources”** and the vehicle for the **non-concur** process by which flag officers formally register disagreement with orders from the President and the Secretary. The removal followed the Post's reporting that military leaders warned Hegseth in the **August 14 edition** that **“a prolonged, large-scale conflict against Iran is unsustainable”** and that such operations risked readiness against other threats. Spokesman **Sean Parnell**: *“The Department of War does not publicly discuss internal operational deliberative processes.”* He did not deny that it happened. **This briefing has cited the SDOB and its four recorded four-star non-concurs in every cycle since August 14 as its best open-source evidence that the force is being held rather than raised, and records that its own evidentiary base for the ground negative has narrowed. The judgement stands unreversed; the record of it is no longer visible from outside the building.** **Escalation is not abandoned but dated.** *Reuters* reported that senior aides have pushed to prevent the war from escalating ahead of the **November 3 midterms** to curb Republican losses; that the administration has meanwhile focused on tightening economic pressure to extract concessions **“months of military action have failed to secure”**; that White House officials **will consider ramping up military action after the vote**, though a return to full-scale conflict **“remains far from certain”**; and that a tactical pause would **“give the US military some breathing room to replenish its depleted ammunition stockpiles.”** *Reuters/Ipsos*, late August: **31% support**, roughly **63% oppose**, with voters unhappy about fuel prices. **Trita Parsi** (Quincy Institute): the strategy is *“maintaining a low-level conflict until the midterms.”* **The only rung that actually climbed was maritime boarding.** CENTCOM's ledger moved to **87 vessels redirected** (from 83), **3 disabled** and — new — **2 boarded** to ensure **“total compliance”** with the blockade. **Armed American personnel on a merchant deck against the master's will, twice in 190 days, in international water: that is the ceiling of American physical intrusion in this war, against zero landings, zero raids and zero seizures of territory.** **The Institute for the Study of War published the first independent assessment of what the strikes achieved**, judging Iran's ability to **surveil the Strait** and to **lay mines** likely **significantly degraded** — evidenced by the IRGC's fallback to **shore-based rocket launchers** to deploy mines and **fast-attack craft to physically identify vessels**, because Iran has **only a few functioning radars** covering the southern route. ISW counted approximately **40 vessels** transiting on September 1. **The Iranian toll became official and the geography reached Kermanshah.** Iran's **Health Minister** put the September 1-2 wave at **18 killed and 108 wounded**; *Reuters* reported **13 Iranian military personnel** killed that week. **Kuhestak** settles at **4 dead — two women and two children — and more than 60 wounded** per the **Iranian Red Crescent**; **Qeshm Island** at least **3 Basij**; **Khuzestan 7**; and **Kermanshah Province 4 military personnel**, in **western Iran on the Iraqi border, roughly 1,200 km from the Strait — the furthest inland fatality logged in this phase**. Foreign Ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baqaei** alleged a **war crime**; CENTCOM's **Capt. Tim Hawkins** said the reports were being **“looked into.”** **Iran struck four countries for a second consecutive night and hit nothing:** drones at **Kuwait** and **Bahrain**, missiles and drones at **Jordan**, and IRGC-claimed drones and missiles against US bases at **Erbil**, all intercepted; one drone burned a **residential complex** with **no casualties**. Kuwait's Ministry of Defence called it **“blatant Iranian aggression”** and its army said it repelled **“heinous”** attacks. **Vice President Vance set the only price for talks and it is maritime:** Washington resumes negotiations when Iran stops **“shooting at commercial shipping”** — *“My advice to the Iranians is stop acting like crazy people.”* No channel is open; envoy **Steve Witkoff** met UAE National Security Adviser **Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed** on **Sardinia**, unannounced. **Oman quietly refused Iran's joint Hormuz transit-fee scheme outright**, including the voluntary version, removing the only littoral cover for a toll regime; **Iran blacklisted 11 more hulls, 56 in all**. **And the cost of the war was priced per barrel for the first time.** **David Osler** of *Lloyd's List*: **“around $2 billion in war risk claims… with over 70 claims to date,”** against **more than 72 attacks on ships since March** — the **second-largest marine underwriting loss in over a decade** — and **“roughly $7 or $8 on the price of a barrel of crude is now down to war-risk insurance alone.”** Against a **~$24 premium** over the pre-crisis baseline, **about a third of the war premium in the oil price is an insurance artefact rather than a physical shortage**. **Brent $95.87, up 0.60%. The ground rung did not move for a 190th day.**

> **Daily update — September 3, 2026 (Day 189; September 2 data cycle).** **The wave was roughly twenty times larger than first reported, and it carried a named new doctrine.** *Axios* reports that Tuesday's strikes hit **approximately 100 targets** and included **two Iranian government tankers** struck under a **“tanker for tanker” policy approved by President Trump**: **US drones launched missiles into the tankers' engine rooms** while they lay **at anchor north of the US naval blockade line**. It is the **first time the US military has struck Iranian tankers in retaliation for Iranian attacks on shipping** rather than to enforce the blockade, and it was chosen **with a Marine expeditionary unit within reach**. Two categories were added to CENTCOM's published set — **anti-ship cruise missile launchers** and **attack drone launchers** — and both are launchers. **The geography widened inland for the first time since the August 1 cancellation of the energy campaign:** impacts are placed at **Konarak, Bandar Abbas, Jask, Qeshm, Sirik, Chabahar**, **Asaluyeh** — the **South Pars gas complex** — and near **Ahvaz and Aghajari in Khuzestan**. **A US official stated the objective in units of time:** the strikes *“bought at least a month”* of lowered threat levels for commercial ships. **The Iranian death toll rose from two to at least eighteen** and four of the dead acquired names and ages — **Amir Ali Karimi, 4; Mohammad Malahi, 16; Kolsoum Malahi, 43; Zarkhatoun Taheri, 43** — killed at the **Kuhestak** wedding with **more than sixty wounded** (Iranian Red Crescent: 4 dead, 67 injured), alongside **seven killed and eight injured in Khuzestan**; CENTCOM's **Capt. Tim Hawkins** said the reports *“originated from Iranian state media,”* were under review, and that *“the U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.”* **Saudi Arabia broke six months of silence to name Iran**, condemning *“Iran's targeting of the Saudi tanker (Sidr)”* and disclosing that **two Filipino seafarers were killed** — superseding the September 1 record of *“all crew safe”* — with **Qatar, Kuwait and Jordan** condemning alongside it and Riyadh separately condemning the **Iranian attacks on Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait**. **Tehran answered not with a denial but with a different cause:** the IRGC says both tankers **struck sea mines** on an *“illegal route,”* that the crews were evacuated with US assistance, and that shipping companies using unapproved routes face *“double punishments”* — which **CENTCOM called *“FALSE,”*** stating *“no ships have hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz.”* **Secretary of State Marco Rubio foreclosed the June memorandum** — *“that ship, in many ways, has sailed”* — while **Trump** said the campaign would not last *“too much longer,”* threatened that Iran would be *“totally wiped out”* if it retaliated again, and floated renaming the waterway the **“Trump Strait.”** **Brent moved six basis points to $95.32.** **Russia ran a seventh consecutive day on Kyiv** — 13 injured on September 2 after 12 killed on September 1 — while **Putin ruled out negotiating with Ukrainian “terrorists” but said he is comfortable dealing with Trump's envoys**, and **Germany blamed Russia for a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle and announced it will close Moscow's consulate**. **And this briefing corrects its own record on the ground question:** the **Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group and the 31st MEU left the theatre in July 2026 and were never replaced** — *USNI News*, July 22, and the USNI Fleet and Marine Tracker for August 31, which places **USS Tripoli in port at Sasebo, Japan** — so the United States has **one amphibious ready group in CENTCOM, not two**: the **Boxer ARG** with the **11th MEU** and **BLT 3/5**. **The ground rung is unchanged at zero for a 189th consecutive day**, and the Army side degraded again: **Hegseth blocked six to seven more two-star selectees**, a *New York Times* analysis puts his total at **more than 80 generals and admirals fired or blocked — about 10% of the flag corps** — and **Army Secretary Driscoll's resignation takes effect today**.

> **Daily update — September 2, 2026 (Day 188; September 1 data cycle).** **The enforcement exchange became a campaign wave, and the United States struck five coastal locations inside Iran without seizing any of them.** At **12:00 ET on Tuesday September 1**, US Central Command *“began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran,”* stating that the strikes followed *“recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region.”* **The published target categories are the cycle's central fact:** *“air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites,”* with **six to eight distinct explosions** reported at **Bandar Abbas**, **Qeshm Island**, **Sirik**, **Konarak** and **Chabahar**. It is the largest wave since **August 1** and CENTCOM subsequently announced it *“successfully completed.”* **The stated trigger was two supertankers and nobody has claimed them.** Late on **August 31**, within minutes of each other, the **Sidr** — a Saudi-flagged VLCC operated by **Bahri** — was struck by unknown projectiles at ~**1952 UTC**, **16.6 nautical miles north-east of Khasab**, Oman; and the **Senegal Prosperity** — a Liberian-flagged VLCC operated by South Korea's **Sinokor** — was struck by **three** unknown projectiles **17 nautical miles east of Khasab**. Each had loaded **2 million barrels of Saudi crude** at the **Juaymah** terminal the previous week; both had been **sailing dark**; **all crew were reported safe**. **Marisks** and **Kpler** recorded the incidents and **UKMTO** reported two separate attacks that night. **Every source of record describes the projectiles as “unknown” and no party has claimed responsibility** — and the United States nonetheless made the attacks the stated predicate for striking five locations inside a sovereign state. That gap is **logged as an open question**, not assumed away in either direction. **The President's language escalated three times in one day.** On Truth Social: *“the United States is, as we speak, striking Iranian Targets near the Strait of Hormuz … The strikes are large and powerful, and in retaliation for the Iranians' failed attempt at adding sea mines.”* Then: *“If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level — but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings,”* adding that *“there will be very little left”* of the country. To Fox News he described the targeting himself: *“They tried to rebuild their radar because they can't see anything. We waited until it was almost built and then we hit it,”* and *“If they retaliate, they'll be hit much harder. And if they do it again, they'll be no longer.”* He separately **renewed the threat to Kharg Island** and again raised the prospect of the United States **taking control** of Iranian energy infrastructure. **The first documented civilian deaths of this phase are Iranian, and the source is an Iranian official on the record.** A US strike hit a **house hosting a wedding ceremony** at **Kuhestak**, in **Sirik district, Hormozgan province**. **Ahmad Nafisi**, deputy governor of Hormozgan, said **two people were killed and at least twenty wounded**; Iranian accounts include a child among the dead. **There is no US comment and no CENTCOM acknowledgement of civilian casualties.** This briefing has repeatedly logged Iranian casualty claims that could not be checked; this one carries a named provincial official, a named village and a specific count. **Iran answered within hours, across four countries.** The **IRGC Aerospace Force** said it *“launched a heavy ballistic missile attack on the American Marines' barracks in Jordan,”* naming **Camp Titin** — a **US Marine base on the Gulf of Aqaba coast** — and **Prince Hassan Air Base**, which hosts RQ-4 and MQ-9 drones, and claimed **a large number of US personnel killed** with facilities and **attack helicopters destroyed**. **Jordan's military** said it detected **13 ballistic missiles**, **intercepted 10**, and that **three fell in remote areas** with **no casualties**; explosions were observed over **Aqaba**. **US officials reported no American casualties.** **Kuwait's** air defences engaged hostile drones — the Kuwaiti army posted that *“the sounds of explosions, if heard, are the result of air defense systems intercepting the hostile attacks”* — with no injuries or damage. The **Bahrain Defence Force** said it **intercepted and destroyed several aerial attacks**; the IRGC's separate claim of **kamikaze drones against Sheikh Isa Air Base** was confirmed by **neither Manama nor Washington**. Multiple explosions were reported near the **US consulate in Erbil**. **And Tehran named its next two targets.** Iranian military spokesman **Ebrahim Zolfaghari** said Iran *“will no longer exercise restraint regarding Bahrain and Kuwait”* — *“Gifts are on the way.”* That is **seventy-two hours** after the Supreme Leader's written message asked Gulf rulers to *“identify your real enemy”* and build mutual defence with Iran. Iran's **Armed Forces General Staff** and **Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters** promised *“crushing and devastating blows to the vile and hostile American enemy,”* adding that *“the more the US military persists in its aggression in the region, the greater and heavier the losses it will have to endure.”* **The market moved more in one session than in the preceding two combined.** The **straits.live** board carried **Brent at $95.29** at its **01 September 2026 2301Z** timestamp, **+4.99%** over 24 hours and **+32.3%** above the ~**$72** pre-crisis baseline, with **WTI at $90.68**; **TradingEconomics** carried **$95.27, +4.60%**. The **AAA national average** reached **$4.0954/gal** against under **$3.00** before the war. **The shape of the move matters more than its size:** near-dated reopening probabilities barely changed (September 15 **1%**, September 30 **3%**, December 31 **28%**) while the **long-dated probability fell from 62% to 53% by July 1, 2027**. The market did not price a short crisis intensifying; it priced a long one extending. **The ground rung did not move for a 188th day, and the published target set is why.** Every category CENTCOM named — air defence, radar, maritime assets, mine-laying, communications — is a sensor, an emitter, a launcher or a node. **Not one is terrain that must be occupied to be denied.** This is a **suppression** target set, not a **shaping** target set: shaping fires for a landing concentrate on one objective, persist, and are followed by movement. These dispersed across five locations in a single wave, across the exact littoral an amphibious operation would use, with the **31st MEU** and the **Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group** and the **11th MEU** within a day's steaming — and **nothing moved**. **The cycle's second hard ground datum is bureaucratic and cuts the same way.** On **August 31**, **Army Secretary Dan Driscoll** submitted his resignation to the White House, **effective September 3**, after months of friction with Secretary **Pete Hegseth** — reportedly over Army transformation and readiness, Hegseth's firing of the generals responsible for it, and Hegseth's removal of **four officers** from a promotion list after Driscoll refused to do so. Hegseth had **already asked the Army chief of staff to step down**. Per the *Wall Street Journal*, **the United States Army now has neither a Senate-confirmed civilian secretary nor a Senate-confirmed military chief** — a service whose deployed brigade combat team is on a **twelve-month tour** for want of replacements and whose allocation is **capped at 50,000** by the August 14 Orders Book over **four formal four-star non-concurs**. **The counter-case is logged and is not trivial:** the President renewed the Kharg threat, again spoke of **taking control** of Iranian energy infrastructure — which air power cannot deliver, since a destroyed terminal is not a captured one — and expressly reserved *“the biggest attack of them all.”* **Russia-Ukraine.** Russia bombarded **Kyiv for more than twelve hours** overnight into Tuesday, killing **at least 12** and wounding more than a dozen **including three children**, in the **sixth consecutive day** of heavy strikes on the capital — reported as unprecedented in more than four and a half years of full-scale war. **Cruise and ballistic missiles, jet-powered drones, glide bombs and artillery** struck Kyiv and **eight other regions**, hitting residential areas, railway and port infrastructure and a **Romanian border crossing**. Ukraine answered on the energy axis and reached the Baltic: a drone barrage set fire to **Ust-Luga**, Russia's largest Baltic terminal (~**700,000 bpd** crude; **32.9m tonnes** of oil products exported in 2025), with Leningrad Governor **Alexander Drozdenko** claiming **52 drones** downed over four hours and the fire out by ~**09:30** Moscow time; Ukraine's **GUR** confirmed the strike. It is the **second strike on Ust-Luga since August 14**. **The war touched NATO airspace again and NATO again did not escalate:** a drone crossed **Latvian** airspace into **Estonia**, which scrambled **Turkish F-16s** under NATO's **Baltic Air Policing Mission**; Estonian Air Force Commander **Riivo Valge** said around a dozen drones moved near the border, one briefly entering south-eastern Estonia and another approaching **Narva** before retreating; **the fighters did not engage, warnings ended by 05:30, and no Article 4 consultation was requested** — the fourth such incident this summer to end that way. Reuters reports the fields were **previously operated by Chinese and Russian firms**. **Cuba:** the state utility **UNE** forecast a peak-hour shortfall of up to **2,310 MW** for September 1 after a day whose peak reached **2,323 MW**, as the 2026-2027 school year opened. **US-China.** Two senior administration officials told Reuters that state-owned **COSCO** uses **concealed equipment** aboard its commercial fleet to collect **military communications** near the coastlines of target nations **including the United States**, in a **decades-long partnership** with Beijing spanning Europe, North America and Asia and aimed at *“military communications technologies and encryption developments.”* China's embassy called it *“totally baseless.”* **No sanction, no designation, no port restriction and no tariff followed, and the Trump-Xi Washington summit remains on for later this month** — a fifth consecutive cycle of maximal accusation and minimal action. **DPRK.** A **thirteenth consecutive day** without a launch. The concession ledger is unchanged and unreciprocated, and the cycle's Korean datum is American: the service that mans the ~**28,500**-strong contingent in Korea now has no Senate-confirmed leadership at either apex. **Hormuz-dependent economies.** Both stricken supertankers carried **Saudi** crude and one was operated by **South Korea's Sinokor** — neither state a belligerent. **South Korea** draws ~**70%** of its crude and **18%** of its LNG through the Strait; **Japan** takes **over 90%** of its crude from the Middle East with ~**75%** transiting Hormuz; **India** ~**40%** of oil and ~**30%** of LNG. **LNG carrier rates ~$300,000/day (+~650%)**; Cape of Good Hope rerouting adds **50-80%** to freight; **Lotte Chemical**, **LG Chem** and **Hanwha Solutions** are on force-majeure notice and **Yeochun NCC** has declared supply disruption. Against all of it, **Bessent** told the **G20 in Asheville** that the Strait will be a *“worthless piece of water”* within **two years** — a claim the same reporting notes requires pipelines that take **multiple years** to build.

> **Daily update — September 1, 2026 (Day 187; August 31 data cycle).** **Iran answered Larak by name and by operation, and the United States answered the answer with a threat rather than a strike.** Overnight into **Monday August 31** the **IRGC Aerospace Force** conducted a combined drone-and-missile operation it named **"Punishment of the Aggressor"** against **King Hussein Air Base** and **Al Azraq Air Base** in **Jordan**; Iran's Foreign Ministry said the bases *"had been used to launch and support attacks on Iran."* Iran's **army** separately said **dozens of drones** were launched at US forces and helicopters at **Al Minhad Air Base** in the **United Arab Emirates**. The **UAE Ministry of Defence** called reports that missiles struck Al Menhad **"false,"** urged reliance on official sources rather than rumours, and confirmed only that its air force **intercepted one drone** over territorial waters approaching from Iran. **No casualties were reported by any party**, and the **United States — the only actor that knows what happened to its own aircraft — said nothing about any of the three bases.** Logged as `punishment-of-the-aggressor-damage-claims-august-2026`. **The American answer was verbal and maximal.** President **Trump** told Fox News the United States would **"hit them hard"** and **"hit them very hard"** — while in the same remarks describing the Strait as being in **"extremely good shape,"** Iran's economy, military and leadership as **"largely deteriorated,"** and adding the conditional **"it doesn't mean we won't smack them to see what happens."** **No second confirmed US strike inside Iran was reported in the following twenty-four hours.** **CENTCOM put the enforcement frame on the record in its own name for the first time**, rejecting the IRGC's *"act of aggression"* characterisation as **"absolutely false"** and stating that *"U.S. forces took **limited, precise action** against IRGC **minelaying forces** posing an **imminent threat** in the Strait of Hormuz,"* aimed at protecting civilian mariners, commercial shipping and the movement of global trade. **The cycle's hardest data are two documents, and one of them corrects this briefing.** *First:* on **August 30-31** the Army extended the Middle East deployment of the **82nd Airborne Division** to a **full twelve months**, carrying soldiers into **2027**. The published unit list is the material fact — **Division Headquarters, 1st Brigade Combat Team, Combat Aviation Brigade, DIVARTY, ADSB (sustainment), 3rd Battalion 4th Air Defense Artillery, 307th Division Engineer Battalion**, approximately **2,000 soldiers** deployed from Fort Bragg in **March 2026**. Division commander **Maj. Gen. Brandon R. Tegtmeier** to families: *"We do not share that lightly, and we understand that a longer tour weighs heavily on every household, including our own."* **This briefing has carried "approximately 1,000 paratroopers" and the standing statement that no brigade combat team, division headquarters or corps-level enabler set had been identified in theatre at any point in the war. Both were wrong and are corrected here.** The units arrived in March; the extension letter is what made their composition public. What the extension is **not**, on the published evidence, is a build: it **adds no soldiers, moves nobody forward and assigns no mission** — it holds a force in place because there is nothing to relieve it with. *Second:* **The Washington Post published contents of the August 14 edition of the Secretary of Defense Orders Book**, the classified twice-monthly document allocating warships, aircraft, personnel and weapons worldwide. **Four formal non-concurs** were filed against continued allocation to the Iran theatre — **Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle**, **INDOPACOM's Adm. Samuel Paparo**, **EUCOM's Gen. Alexus Grynkewich** and **SOUTHCOM** — with the **Army and Air Force chiefs concurring** while recording increased risk. **Caudle:** the Navy **"cannot sustain its current level of support"** because there is no end date, with **barely a quarter of the destroyer fleet ready to deploy**. **More than half** the cruise-missile and advanced air-defence-missile inventories expended; **~25% of the Reaper drone fleet** lost; **THAAD redeployed from South Korea** to the Middle East; the **USS George Washington** moved from **Japan** to the Persian Gulf, **leaving the Pacific without carrier coverage**; a Pacific carrier redirected to relieve one deployed **more than 300 days**; billions in base damage. Gil Cisneros** on Hegseth: *"He either does not comprehend the consequences of his decisions, or he just doesn't give a damn."* **Read together: the United States is extending tours because it cannot rotate, and four four-star commanders are formally on record that the current commitment already exceeds what the force can sustain.** **The Larak toll resolved to three IRGC personnel killed and two injured**, two named as **Hamid Avazzadeh** and **Ali Fayazi**. **Kpler put Kharg loadings at 135,000 bpd in August against 1.98m bpd in February** — a **93% collapse achieved by blockade with nobody on the island**, against a facility handling ~90% of Iranian crude exports. **UKMTO published the first full transit count in weeks — 101 outbound and 103 inbound in the seven days to August 28**, traffic *"significantly reduced"* and **~90% below** pre-conflict levels, with **16 of 18 projectile-strike incidents since July 6 on the southern Omani route**. **Brent closed above $90 for the first time since the pause began**, at **$90.78**, **+26.1%** on the pre-crisis baseline; **515 hulls** are holding position away from berth, up from 396. > **Daily update — August 31, 2026 (Day 186; August 30 data cycle).** **The twenty-nine-night strike pause broke, and it broke at Larak Island — the piece of ground through which Iran administers the traffic it claimed the day before to be permitting.** On **Sunday August 30** US forces struck **two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island**; a US official said the IRGC *"was preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the strait when US forces struck,"* and *Axios* reported the rockets were armed with sea mines. The two readings are observationally identical on August 30; logged as `larak-strike-enforcement-or-campaign-resumption-august-2026`. **Tehran promised retribution and delivered missiles.** The IRGC reported *"the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots"* with no toll and vowed *"we will take retribution"*; spokesman **Sardar Mohebi** called the strike *"a strategic and fatal mistake"* with consequences *"in both the economic and military arenas"*; parliament's **Ebrahim Azizi**: *"Retaliation is coming."* **Iranian missiles were fired at US forces in Jordan** and a US source said *"nearly all incoming missiles have been intercepted"* with *"no significant impacts so far"* — **no US casualties**. **Both commands now claim permissioning authority over the same water.** Cooper, August 28: *"No ships have entered or left an Iranian port without our permission, and we have only allowed ships to pass through on humanitarian grounds."* Gharibabadi, August 29: *"Any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran."* Adjacent but distinguishable water, **not strictly incompatible**, and **neither verifiable from open sources**. **And both governments now claim Iranian oil exports are zero while the only disinterested measurement disagrees with both:** CENTCOM and Iran's **central bank governor** both say zero; **Kpler** records approximately **260,000 barrels a day loaded** at Iranian ports in August, down **more than 80%** on August 2025 and **~70%** on July. Adversarial convergence normally corroborates; here both parties benefit from the same figure. Logged as `iran-oil-exports-zero-or-loading-august-2026`. **The Supreme Leader wrote to the Gulf and Reuters explained his absence.** **Mojtaba Khamenei**'s Islamic Unity Week message told *"the rulers of Islamic countries, especially the countries of West Asia and the Gulf"* to *"identify your real enemy, understand his plan and confront it"* and called for **mutual defence** — his **second written statement in two days** — and Reuters reported that he has not appeared publicly **because he was injured in the February 28 strikes** that killed his father. **No Gulf government answered**, in a region that has absorbed attacks on ~**80 energy facilities** at an estimated **$58 billion**. **The financial track peaked in rhetoric and landed on an Egyptian bank's Emirati branches.** **Bessent**: *"This is going to be financial violence if we have to"*; another bank *"this week"*; *"all options are on the table"* on China ahead of the **G20 in Asheville, North Carolina**; reports of his reluctance *"a completely false narrative that the media picked up on."* *Fortune*: the world **"mostly shrugged off"** the threat — **no Chinese institution designated for a third consecutive package**, branches open in **Dubai**, flights running to **Turkey**, **Pakistan** *"not obliged"* to comply, and **Alex Zerden** saying the actions *"do not match the hype."* **Russia announced its own escalation in advance:** its Defence Ministry said the armed forces *"have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure"* in retaliation for Ukraine's refinery campaign — logged as a **stated intention, not an executed act** (`russia-announced-energy-campaign-order-or-signal-august-2026`). > **Daily update — August 30, 2026 (Day 185; August 29 data cycle).** **The day after the President said no American troops had deployed into Iran, Iran's deputy foreign minister said the Strait is still closed — and that every ship crossing it does so "in coordination with Iran."** On **August 29** Deputy Foreign Minister **Kazem Gharibabadi** said: *"The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran."* This is a **new class of claim**. For six months the public dispute has been binary — Washington says open, Tehran says closed — and this briefing has logged both counts side by side. Tehran now advances a third position that is consistent with **both** governments' published numbers: that the traffic the United States cites as proof of openness is traffic Iran is **permitting**. No permissioning, clearance or de-confliction record exists in the open source base on either side, and none of the named operators has stated whether Iranian clearance was sought. The claim is logged as contested and unresolved, and the briefing records that six months of framing the question as **open versus closed** may have been the wrong question. **The Iran-Oman understanding is confirmed as reached and simultaneously suspended,** its implementation conditioned on the United States honouring the **Islamabad memorandum** — and on Gharibabadi's own description it would **close both** the temporary **northern route near Larak Island** and the **UN-authorised southern route** hugging Oman's coast, replacing them with a **single corridor seven miles wide** whose entry and part of whose exit lie in **Iranian territorial waters**. The southern route is the channel announced under the June MOU, which Iran said violated that agreement and against whose users it attacked shipping. That is a change in the legal character of transit through Hormuz, not a restoration of the pre-war regime. The **IRGC Navy** called American statements that the Strait is open *"an obvious lie"* and its own control *"completely decisive."* **The transit data ran against the rhetoric.** *USNI News*, citing **Lloyd's List Intelligence**, recorded **114 transits between August 17 and August 27** — up **more than 30%** on the week, led by tankers and gas carriers — with **at least 42 westbound** against **29** the week prior, among them crude tankers from **Sinokor** and **ADNOC** and Saudi- and Kuwaiti-owned hulls, against a pre-war baseline near **138 vessels a day**. **Goldman Sachs** puts Persian Gulf exports at **15-16 million bpd** against a pre-conflict **22-24 million** and a **March low near 5-6 million**. Recovery without normalisation. **The six-month economic admission came from the top of the Iranian state and it came in writing.** Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** — who *Al Jazeera* recorded has **not appeared publicly since his father's death on February 28** — issued a **Government Week** message calling for serious attention to *"inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services,"* saying *"the main key to resolving all these issues lies in relying increasingly on domestic production,"* and setting out a roadmap to **gradually phase the US dollar out** of the economy with **"resistance economy"** policies at the centre of the government's agenda. **Pezeshkian** put numbers to it: exports and imports **down nearly 35%**, roughly **90 million barrels** of oil sold during the June MOU window, against **66% annual inflation** — while saying Iran will *"stand strong against any aggressor."* Tehran formalised its posture as **"diplomacy and defence,"** *"complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings."* **Araghchi**: *"Pressure doesn't work."* Acting Defence Minister Brig. Gen. **Majid Ebn al-Reza**: adversaries *"will become aware of Iran's surprises in due time."* **The American offensive's geography was named and Beijing is not on it.** *Iran International*'s analysis of the Banque Misr action found the campaign aimed at **Dubai, Istanbul and Baghdad** as Iran's financial channels rather than at Beijing — the second consecutive package to spare China's major banks, now with an articulated geography rather than merely an absence. **Banque Misr UAE** said it treats the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking *"with the utmost seriousness and attention."* **The domestic constraint acquired a date, for the first time in the record.** Reuters and Bloomberg reported the President will meet **at least ten fuel makers and distributors** — **Valero**, **Marathon Petroleum** and **PBF Energy** expected — on **Tuesday September 1**, over gasoline **above $4 a gallon** and diesel **near $6**, the highest seasonal level ever recorded and roughly **a dollar above the February 28 level**, ahead of November's midterms. **On the ground rung the load-bearing movement was a dispersal.** CENTCOM published its first imagery of Marine ground personnel in this theatre in some weeks — and it shows **Marines refuelling an MV-22 Osprey**, published rather than concealed, the inverse of pre-assault operational security. Meanwhile the **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group split**: **USS Boxer** remains in the **Arabian Sea** while **USS Comstock** — the dock landing ship that puts vehicles and heavy equipment ashore — moved into the **Indian Ocean**. **USS Tripoli** is in homeport at **Sasebo**. CENTCOM strength remains **~50,000**, reaffirmed August 28, none inside Iran. **Kharg Island was not seized, not targeted and not mentioned.** **In Ukraine, the deadliest single attack of the year and a causal dispute both sides' accounts make unresolvable.** At about **20:10 local on August 28** a Russian drone struck an enterprise in **Myla**, five kilometres west of Kyiv, touching off sustained **ammunition detonations** that killed **at least 37**, among them the mayor of Dmytrivka, damaging a **care home** and forcing **380+** evacuations. Ukrainian prosecutors described *"explosive objects"* and **Zelensky** pointed to ammunition; **Russia's Defence Ministry** said it struck a warehouse holding **components and launch boosters for long-range drones**. Both agree munitions were present and drove the toll. Ukraine downed or suppressed **233 drones** overnight as national alerts ran into a **third consecutive day**. **A twenty-ninth consecutive night passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran.** The war remains **air, naval, financial and judicial** — **no landing, no Kharg seizure, no draft order**.

> **Daily update — August 29, 2026 (Day 184).** **Six months, and the President described his own war as one "in which no American troops have deployed into Iran."** The war launched on **February 28, 2026** reached its **six-month mark on August 28**, against a presidential forecast of **four to five weeks** made the day after it began; reporting across outlets found **none of the six objectives** stated at the launch fully achieved. Defending the campaign, Trump characterised it as one **"in which no American troops have deployed into Iran"** — the **first affirmative statement by the commander-in-chief** of the precise negative this briefing has tracked for 184 days by inference. It is a claim about the past six months, not a commitment about the next six. **The American instrument of the cycle was financial and it cut a bank out of the dollar for the first time.** Treasury, through **FinCEN**, proposed severing the **six UAE branches of Egypt's Banque Misr** from US correspondent banking over approximately **$1.8 billion** processed for roughly **103 companies** in Iran's shadow banking network between **January 2024 and June 2026** — the first branch-level correspondent action under **Operation Economic Outcast**. It is a **proposed rule with a 30-day comment period**, not a designation; **Cairo, Paris, Frankfurt, Riyadh, Beirut and Djibouti** are unaffected; **China's major banks were spared for a second consecutive package**. **Tehran moved toward paper rather than water:** **Mohsen Rezaei** said Iran is drawing up a **list of conditions** to reopen the Strait at the mediators' request — *"The US must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran's conditions"* — with **Iran-Oman corridor coordinates agreed** and a **central channel** available on compliance; the price is unchanged. > **Daily update — August 27, 2026 (Day 182).** **A double cycle — the August 26 update was not run, so this consolidates August 25-27 — and its organising fact is that the United States spent it making the Strait navigable rather than taking it.** **The non-kinetic posture acquired a reported duration for the first time in 182 days.** On **August 25** *Axios*, citing US officials, reported that Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** has told several allied foreign ministers that **"for the time being"** the United States is **not expected to launch new strikes** against Iran and will instead focus on other means of pressure, without ruling out strikes if Iran attacks first — and that **a second official said the posture is expected to remain in place until after the midterm elections**, when another military campaign could again be considered. The named priorities were **sanctions, the naval blockade, and "moving ever-increasing amounts of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz."** Three instruments, none of them a ground force. Logged as reporting from two unnamed officials about an unannounced future decision, not as an order. **The capability actually applied to the chokepoint was an unmanned vehicle and a commercial contractor.** On **August 25** President Trump announced that the US Navy has disposed of **all mines** in the Strait's international waters and declared **"Zero Tolerance"** — *"Any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed"* — with the **Space Force** *"watching every square inch."* US officials confirmed the method: over recent months Navy **underwater drones** scanned the Traffic Separation Scheme and located **more than 100 objects suspected to be mines**, and the military **contracted with private companies** to remove or detonate them; the CENTCOM operation began in **April**. Trump also said all **28 Iranian mine-laying boats** had been destroyed. **Gharibabadi** answered that *"no one except Iran knows the location"* and that the claim was *"only aimed at calming markets"*; **Mark Hilborne** (King's College London) gave the CENTCOM-sourced claim *"strong confidence"* for the main lanes while warning *"there may be risks beyond the lanes"*; **Alex Almeida** (Ambrey) said mines *"have never been the primary threat,"* with drones and anti-ship cruise and ballistic missiles the greater danger. **Neither traffic nor insurance moved:** three transits on **August 23**, two on **August 24** — the fewest since early May — and war-risk premiums held at **7.5-10% of hull value** against 1-3% pre-war. **The Strait's future governance went into a document signed by Tehran and Muscat.** Oman's Foreign Minister **Badr Albusaidi** met **Abbas Araghchi** in Tehran on **August 25** and the two ministries announced a **"phased framework"** comprising a **joint temporary navigational corridor** and **"an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines,"** with technical talks to continue toward a **permanent corridor**, **"the future administration of the Strait,"** and mechanisms for information exchange, traffic management and maritime and security services, under **Article 5 of the Islamabad Memorandum**. On **August 26** Deputy Foreign Minister **Kazem Gharibabadi** gave the terms on state television: **seven miles (11.3 km) wide**; **entry beginning in Iranian territorial waters** with part of the exit also through them; **Iranian permission and surveillance** required; **military vessels barred**; a **permanent arrangement in 30-60 days**. *"The agreed-upon transit route with Oman is a temporary route."* Full reopening is conditioned on US compliance with the **June 17 MoU**, **sanctions relief**, **release of frozen assets**, **an end to the war** and **war-damage compensation**. IRGC spokesman **Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi** said the two had agreed **"each country's share of the strait's waters and Iran and Oman's share of its revenues"** and that *"the Strait of Hormuz belongs to Iran and the Sultanate of Oman."* **What is unpublished matters as much as what was announced:** coordinates, start date, revenue mechanics, eligible flags and any mine-clearing timeline. **The enforcement record contradicted the diplomacy within a day.** Iran's shipping monitoring agency, via **Mehr**, said the Indian tanker **HAANA** planned to transit the southern **Oman Corridor** *"but received a warning that it had to stop"* and turned back, and that **"no vessel traffic has been observed on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours"** — against the CNN Business/**Kpler** finding of **more than 80% of liquids transits** on that route. **The market fell three sessions running:** Brent about **$89** on August 25, a one-week low, with WTI near **$82**; Brent about **$86** and WTI about **$80** on August 26. **BBH**: *"more of a warning shot than a decisive blow."* **Ole Hansen** (Saxo Bank): the shift from military confrontation to economic sanctions *"had helped calm nerves across energy markets."* **Trump removed the clock.** To Al Jazeera's **Tanya Noury** on **August 26**: *"I have no time schedule, none. I'm not in a hurry. I have no time schedule at all,"* adding *"We are winning very big"* and that economic and military measures *"are both effective."* To **Glenn Beck** the same day: the waterway is *"a very functioning strait,"* and of Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei**, absent about six months, *"I don't think he's dead. He was very seriously wounded."* **Inside Iran the petrol ran out:** station closures and queues across Tehran under a **20-litre limit**, a state body warning of a **"critical"** shortfall, quotas to be cut and non-subsidised prices raised, Executive Vice-President **Ghaempanah** — *"with the US naval blockade, we cannot import gasoline"* — **Pezeshkian** — *"the worst conditions of an economic war"* — and the rial at a record **2,060,000** to the dollar on August 25. **The ledger moved to 776 — 18 killed and 758 wounded** — with more than 90% of the newest additions Army, against a service split of **580+ Army, 86 Navy, 64 Air Force and 19 Marines** (~2.5% across 182 days); *The Intercept* restated the undercount dispute, including **200+ USS Gerald R. Ford** fire casualties excluded and an **April 21** WIA count that fell by 15 unexplained, with an official calling it an *"accounting trick."* **Elsewhere:** **CIA Director John Ratcliffe** made an **unannounced visit to Moscow on August 25** — the first by a US spy chief since **William Burns** met Putin in **November 2021** — meeting Russian intelligence counterparts, with **Peskov** saying Putin did not plan to meet him and that there were **no plans for talks with Witkoff or Kushner**; Washington had asked Kyiv to pause strikes on Moscow **Monday through Wednesday**. > **Daily update — August 25, 2026 (Day 180).** **The financial offensive arrived and it has a name.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** held his 2 p.m. ET news conference on **August 24** and unveiled **"Operation Economic Outcast"**: **five sectoral determinations** against **digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping**; **nearly 60** Iran-linked people, entities and vessels designated across the **UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland**; a **defined wind-down timeline** for every country; **most secondary sanctions deferred behind a "cure period"**; and a **major financial institution** signalled for designation by the end of the week. **The objective was stated without euphemism** — *"It is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime"* — and the White House positioned the operation as the **"endgame" phase** succeeding Operation Epic Fury. **Regime collapse is now a declared American war aim and the declared instrument is the banking system.** **The counter-indicator is logged in full:** Secretary of War **Pete Hegseth** said the same day that military force is **not ruled out** in the Strait of Hormuz **"or anywhere else."** **Brent fell** on announcement day after a week of >5% gains — Reuters -1.4% to ~$93, CNBC -2.5% to $92.06, straits.live $92.10 at -1.67%. **The rial hit a record 2.02 million to the dollar**, with rice up ~60% and beef up >150% since February. **Two tankers were hit in twenty-four hours:** the Saudi VLCC **Amzan** (Bahri) by Houthi ballistic missiles and drones **~63nm west of Yanbu** — *"siege for siege,"* per Yahya Saree — and an unnamed tanker **disabled in its engine room ~9nm northeast of Ash Shishah, Oman at 0131 UTC on August 25**, unclaimed. **CENTCOM reached 71 redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded** and disclosed for the first time that **more than 40 humanitarian aid vessels** have been permitted through. **CNN Business, citing Kpler, reports more than 80% of liquids transits took the Omani route or were dark transits that likely did — "Iran has lost significant control of the Strait of Hormuz"** — while straits.live still carries **one transit against a 73-a-day baseline** and **370 hulls off berth**. **Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir returned to Tehran** as the **June 17 Islamabad Memorandum's 60-day window lapsed without extension**; **Oman's FM Sayyid Badr Albusaidi arrives in Tehran today**. **A twenty-fourth consecutive night** passed with no confirmed strike inside Iran. **Pentagon casualties hold at 775**, and the service split is new and pointed: **580+ Army, 86 Navy, 64 Air Force, 19 Marines**. **USNI confirms USS Abraham Lincoln has left CENTCOM for 7th Fleet**, completing the relief that leaves **carrier presence at two**. **Ground rung: every execution indicator at zero for a 180th day.**

Hours earlier, **Iran's parliamentary National Security and Foreign Policy Commission approved Article 3** of its **"Strategic Action to Ensure the Security and Progress of the Strait of Hormuz"** plan — **service fees on "authorised" transiting ships**, payable **"in Rials or any other currency desired by the Islamic Republic of Iran,"** with a floor vote and Guardian Council review still to come. **SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei escalated from selectivity to totality and named the bypass routes as targets**, warning via IRNA that Tehran **"will not allow a single drop of oil to leave the Persian Gulf"** if pressure escalates and that Iran would **"retaliate in a seismic manner."** **President Pezeshkian broke publicly with the Supreme Leader's reported position**, saying Iran **"cannot continue with war forever"** and defending the June memorandum **despite the purported misgivings of Mojtaba Khamenei** — the first on-record elite split of the war on the Iranian side. **A twenty-third consecutive night passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iran.** **CENTCOM's blockade tally reached 70 vessels redirected, three disabled and two boarded as of August 23.** **The traffic estimates are now openly irreconcilable** — 20% of pre-war average (CNN), one transit against a 73-a-day baseline (straits.live), and 15-20 escorted transits a night carrying about ten million barrels a day (an unnamed US official) — and a new open question has been opened for it. **In Paris, Macron and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman meet on August 24 with Hormuz alternatives as the headline file**, alongside a France-Saudi ministerial task force on Middle East-Europe energy and logistics. **Brent $94.39; pump $4.0986; diesel $5.6074 at a record August level; US casualties hold at 775.** **The ground file carries one correction and one backfill against this project's own record:** net carrier presence in CENTCOM is **TWO, not one** — USS George H.W. Bush since April 23 and USS George Washington since August 19, a rotation matching CENTCOM's own July figure — and **CNN reported on June 12 that Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Gen. Dan Caine flew from Brussels to CENTCOM headquarters on May 19 to be briefed on sending US ground troops into Iran to seize its enriched uranium, and that Trump declined the operation after warnings of a large number of US casualties**, after which Iran sealed the cache with collapsed tunnels and mined entrances. **One amphibious ready group is deployed worldwide against combatant-commander requests for "well north of three" pairings.** **Every execution indicator stood at zero for a 179th consecutive day, and the predicted US ground seizure remains DISCONFIRMED.**

> **Daily update — August 23, 2026 (Day 178).** **Two sovereignty claims were made over the same water on the same day, and neither of them moved a soldier.** On **August 22** President Trump told supporters in South Carolina: **"We don't even know if we won, because I view the Strait of Hormuz as an American territory right now,"** and re-posted on Truth Social the image labelling the waterway **"NEW U.S. TERRITORY"** he first published on August 18. Hours apart, **IRNA announced that Tehran had granted a number of Iraqi oil tankers permission to transit the Strait** after repeated requests from Baghdad through several channels, including during parliament speaker **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf's** visit to Iraq — **the first named state-level transit exemption of the war**. Iraq produced roughly four million barrels a day before the conflict, has no national tanker fleet, and is building alternatives through **Ceyhan, Baniyas and Aqaba**; Iraqi President **Nizar Amidi** said Iraqi territory **"will not be used to launch attacks against any other country."** **The strike pause held for a twenty-second night.** No US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory has been confirmed since the **August 1** cancellation. **Tehran aimed its counter-threat at third parties rather than at Washington.** FM spokesman **Esmaeil Baghaei** called the sanctions package due Monday a **"declaration of war"** on all countries and an attempt **"to exert extraterritorial sovereignty over all independent UN member states,"** warning that pairing sanctions with a naval blockade would produce **"the complete erosion of sovereignty as the foundational basis of the UN-based inter-State system, and a recipe for an abysmal return to full-scale classic colonialism."** **Mohsen Rezaei**, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said on state television that **"any country participating in the imposition of economic restrictions against us is considered an enemy,"** that states refusing to **"distance themselves"** from Washington would have their interests **"harmed"** — naming **Gulf and Hormuz oil shipments** as the instrument — that **"the Strait of Hormuz is closed and will not reopen"** absent a change in US behaviour, and that **"if Trump wants to take action, we will retaliate in an earthquake-like manner"**; he added that Iran had **"not yet attacked any American economic interests."** **The first route-share dataset of the war cuts against the American claim of control.** Al Jazeera's **August 20** analysis of **August 1-19** counted **236 vessels** of all cargo types crossing: **83 openly using Iran's prescribed northern route, three openly using the US-backed Omani route**, two on the pre-war central route and **148 (62%) dark**; of **112 oil and gas vessels**, 21 Iranian route, two Omani route, **89 (over 80%) dark** — its conclusion, **"the fear of offending Tehran appears to outweigh Trump's threats."** **CENTCOM's blockade tally reached 68 vessels redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded** as of August 21, with **more than 20 warships** enforcing and **USS Ross (DDG-71)** cited. **The month's merchant casualties inside the chokepoint enter this record for the first time:** the ***Minoan Pioneer*** struck in her engine room northeast of Khasab on **August 3**, third engineer missing; an **ADNOC tanker** hit by missile on **August 8**, which Abu Dhabi called piracy by the IRGC; the ADNOC vessels ***Navig8 Messi*** and ***Tarif*** hit by drones on **August 13**; and the ***Minoan Dignity***, whose chief engineer was killed on **August 17-18**. **ADNOC counts 16 vessels attacked since February 28, one crew member killed and 20 injured.** **Kharg was restarted, not taken:** an NITC VLCC loaded about two million barrels at the **Azarpad jetty on August 14**, the first loading since late July, after a roughly 25-day halt and with no US move against the island. **And the largest structural fact of the month had not been recorded in this briefing at all:** on **August 7** Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan signed the **Mecca Joint Defence Agreement**, declaring an armed attack on one an attack on all, with Turkish FM **Hakan Fidan** describing a NATO-like structure of a ministers' committee, political and military committees and a permanent secretariat; **Trump welcomed it** as a **"big, bold, and important first step."** **Diplomacy moved to Paris:** **Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman** travelled to France for an **August 24 Franco-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council** with **Macron** devoted to **Hormuz alternatives** — maritime diversification, pipelines and regional rail. **Markets:** Brent **$93.93** at the August 22 close on a $92.76-$94.82 range, a second consecutive weekly gain of roughly 6%; **AAA national average $4.1024**; **Pentagon casualties 774-775** (18 killed, 756-757 wounded). **Elsewhere:** ISW records Ukraine **engineering around American resupply**, developing domestic means to target Russian ballistic launchers and jet-powered drones expressly to avoid dependence on foreign materiel amid global interceptor shortages, and **North Korean drone operators deployed to Kursk Oblast**; Pyongyang answered the **August 18 announcement of scaled-back US-South Korea drills** with about **ten short-range ballistic missiles on August 20** after **Kim Yo Jong** dismissed the gesture; Beijing restated that it **does not recognise** the coming sanctions, with **Lin Jian** saying **"sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue."** **Ground-invasion rung unchanged for a 178th day:** every execution indicator at zero, the **Boxer ARG** still the sole ARG in CENTCOM while the Navy's other deployed ARG (**Iwo Jima / 22nd MEU**) is committed to the **Caribbean under SOUTHCOM** and the **24th MEU is deployed without an ARG at all** as *Littoral Combat Force 24*; the only ground-planning indicator in the record remains the **single-sourced, unconfirmed July 26 New York Post report** of a uranium-seizure operation requiring **"thousands of ground troops."**
