> **Daily update — August 22, 2026 (Day 177).** **The war changed category rather than intensity, and the President put the reason on the record.** Late on **August 1** Trump announced he was **cancelling the planned multi-day attack** on Iran's energy and civil infrastructure, saying Iran and **"other Middle Eastern countries"** had asked him to hold off and conditioning the cancellation on **"being able to rapidly make a DEAL"** covering the **"Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat."** **Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman** had pressed him that Saturday, with Qatar, the UAE, Turkey and Pakistan also urging de-escalation. Tehran denied requesting anything — **"nothing but a new lie"** — and Trump then called Iranian leadership **"unbelievably duplicitous."** This resolves the previous cycle's open question about why the reported campaign never began. **The pause then held for twenty nights:** no US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory was confirmed by CENTCOM through the 0500 ET cutoff on **August 19**, with **no new Iranian civilian casualties from strikes** across the span. **The negotiating window closed with nothing signed.** **August 17** marked the expiry of the 60-day period agreed in June. Trump demanded Iran **"put up the white flag of surrender,"** said **"I have no time schedule"** and was not **"in a hurry,"** threatened to **"bomb the s\*\*\* out of"** **Oman** — the war's principal mediator — if it **"gets in the way,"** and said he liked **"the idea of declaring [the Strait] a territory,"** asserting **"we have total control over the strait"** and calling the blockade a **"wall of steel."** FM **Araghchi** said Tehran **"had not yet made a decision to restart negotiations"**; MFA spokesman **Baghaei** said the US had violated the MOU weeks after signing. On **August 18** Trump said no talks were under way or scheduled and the IRGC dismissed his backchannel claim as **"fantasies."** **On August 20 the administration named its successor phase, and it is financial.** Vice President **JD Vance** said the war had entered a **"new phase"** of economic pressure and that this is **"the best way to ultimately accomplish the final objective here"**; Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** promised **"the toughest sanctions in history"** and **"the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world,"** with a news conference set for **Monday August 24** — and, in the same interview, **said the US likely would not restart large-scale combat operations.** Treasury separately re-designated **Hezbollah** for acting on behalf of the IRGC Quds Force. **Iran contested the Strait by announcement rather than by battle:** its **August 6-7 Oman-brokered arrangement** bars **American and Israeli vessels outright**, fines violators **up to 20% of cargo value**, denies passage to states deemed to have damaged Iran until compensated, and assigns Iran navigation guidance, traffic monitoring, maritime security and environmental protection. **Washington rejected it.** **Force was used at sea:** two **Hellfire missiles into the engine room of the container ship *Vela Nova*** on **August 11**; CENTCOM's blockade tally at **67 vessels redirected, 3 disabled, 2 boarded** by August 20; **six killed aboard the *Tihamah*** in the Bab al-Mandeb on August 11-12, the first Houthi-attributed shipping deaths of the war; Brad Cooper** told the White House the strikes had **"significantly degraded"** Iran's ability to target commercial vessels and that designated targets were **"mostly exhausted"**; **Gen. Dan Caine** warned that **"a dwindling supply of air defence intercept"** could expose US personnel and allies; **VP JD Vance** cautioned against escalating at the July 24 White House meeting. **Washington paired that with non-foreclosure:** Amb. **Mike Waltz** said the pause was **"giving diplomacy some space"** and that Oman is **"engaging in a helpful way,"** but also **"Not only do we have what we need in theater, there's more moving into theater"** and **"I'm not going to take that option off the table for the president"**; Trump denied any munitions shortage and posted AI-generated images depicting attacks on Iranian facilities. **The Iran-Oman channel firmed:** deputy foreign ministers met in Tehran July 24-25 on **"shared principles and operational mechanisms for managing the safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while respecting the sovereign rights of the two coastal states"**; 35% approve of Trump's handling. **Netanyahu meets Trump July 28.** **GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED — AND THE AMPHIBIOUS RUNG FELL FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE WAR:** the **Tripoli ARG offloaded ~2,500 Marines of the 31st MEU at Okinawa on July 22** after four months under CENTCOM, with **no relief ARG announced**, removing the very MEU the Pentagon's reported raid-and-seizure options had named. > **Daily update — June 14, 2026 (Day 108).** The war reached its **scheduled signing day with the agreement still unratified by Tehran.** On **Saturday June 13** President Trump posted on Truth Social that the deal was **"scheduled to get signed tomorrow [Sunday June 14], and immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL,"** framing it as a guarantee of **"long-term peace in the region"** and as the inverse of the 2015 JCPOA — **"A WALL TO NO NUCLEAR WEAPON,"** with Iran that **"no longer want[s] a Nuclear Weapon, nor will they have one."** He introduced two new wrinkles: that **"no money will exchange hands"** (cutting against the reported **$24 billion** frozen-assets release Iran had made a precondition) and that the United States **"will go in and get the Nuclear Dust, buried deep under the powerful sunken granite mountains"** at an undetermined later time **"when all is calm,"** to be down-blended and destroyed. The signing was set for **Europe — reported as Geneva —** with Vice President **JD Vance** plus negotiators **Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner** attending and Trump himself not attending; **four US Air Force C-17 transport planes** had departed to Europe to move equipment for Vance's possible travel to the ceremony. **BUT IT REMAINED UNSIGNED AND UNRATIFIED BY TEHRAN:** a senior administration official said Friday the US was **not "100%"** confident the agreement would be signed; > **Daily update — June 9, 2026 (Day 103).** The cycle's most serious escalation **climaxed in the first direct, two-sided Israel-Iran territorial exchange since the April ceasefire — and then de-escalated within roughly 24 hours.** Following Iran's June 7 barrage, **Israel struck Iranian territory for the first time since the April 8 ceasefire,** hitting **Tehran, Isfahan, Karaj and Tabriz** early June 8 with **air-launched ballistic missiles;** Israeli strikes also hit a **petrochemical plant in Mahshahr (Khuzestan province)** — confirmed by the IDF — and **truck-based surface-to-air missile launchers.** Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Israel had used air-launched ballistic missiles (NPR/Times of Israel, "Daily Briefing June 8"; Al Jazeera, "Iran and Israel bomb each other: Is the ceasefire over?"; ABC News, June 8, 2026). **Iran fired approximately 30 ballistic missiles in total since Sunday night,** launching a second wave after the Israeli strikes; the IRGC branded the campaign **"Operation Nasr" ("Victory")** and said it had targeted **two Israeli military bases.** Israel said it downed the missiles; most were intercepted, with **debris reaching Jordan and the West Bank,** and **no casualties were confirmed from the exchange itself** (the only deaths in the cycle remain the June 7 Beirut strike: 2 killed, ~20 wounded). **President Trump intervened directly to block a larger Israeli strike** that had been prepared for late June 8 afternoon — saying he **"made Netanyahu stop,"** that **"I call the shots,"** telling the Financial Times that Netanyahu **"won't have any choice"** on a US-Iran agreement, and (per a US official) telling Netanyahu by phone to refrain because **"we are close to doing something good in terms of a deal";** he separately said he had warned Netanyahu that Israel could be **"left alone"** if it escalated. By **June 8-9 both sides halted:** Iran's military command announced **"the cessation of armed forces operations is hereby announced"** after a **"painful response,"** and the Iranian Foreign Ministry confirmed Iran had ceased its strikes but **warned hostilities would resume if the IDF continues military operations in Lebanon;** Israel halted its attacks, with Netanyahu confirming the halt while **stopping short of acknowledging a ceasefire;** and Trump posted on Truth Social that **"Both sides, Israel and Iran, are looking to do an immediate CEASEFIRE!"** (Arab News; MS NOW liveblog; CNN/CBS live updates, June 8-9, 2026). **Oil** spiked then faded: **Brent crossed ~$98/bbl intraday June 8** before easing back to **~$94** once Iran announced it had ended operations (WTI jumped more than 4% above $94); prices faded on ceasefire optimism, and **OPEC+ approved a July production-quota increase of 188,000 bpd.** **Hormuz** traffic stayed near-zero (~36/week); nuclear talks stayed **deadlocked over Iran's $24B frozen-assets demand,** with reporting that Washington was weighing redirecting some frozen assets to Gulf states for reconstruction rather than front-loading relief to Tehran. **DPRK:** **Xi Jinping visited Pyongyang June 8-9** (his second visit in seven years) as **Kim Jong Un ordered a 10,000-tonne destroyer** and "secret underwater weapons" and reiterated "exponential" nuclear expansion (new bomb-fuel plant unveiled June 3). **Russia-Ukraine:** front static, next Istanbul round June 20-30. **Venezuela:** Maduro + Flores face a June 30 NYC court date. **Ground-invasion rung UNCHANGED:** the war's most extreme escalation to date stayed entirely in the **missile/air register** and **resolved toward de-escalation** — **no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order and no draft** — and, decisively, **the US was not the kinetic actor; On **Sunday June 7** Israeli warplanes **struck Beirut's southern suburbs (Dahieh, a Hezbollah stronghold) without warning** — despite a US request days earlier that Israel stand down on Beirut — in what Netanyahu's office called retaliation for **Hezbollah firing at northern Israel** and a strike on Hezbollah **"command centers";** Lebanon's Health Ministry said the strike **killed two and wounded about 20, including four women and four children** (CSMonitor; The Washington Times; Al Jazeera, June 7, 2026). Iran's state broadcaster confirmed the launches; Israel's **Iron Dome and Arrow** systems were activated and intercepted missiles, but the IDF said **"the defense is not hermetic,"** with air-raid sirens across several areas of northern Israel and multiple explosions. **Casualty reporting diverged:** the IDF's initial statement said **no immediate casualties or damage,** while **NPR** reported an Iranian missile with a **cluster warhead** struck a building in **Ramat Gan, killing two residents in their 70s,** and that **debris fell on the Old City of Jerusalem,** damaging areas near the **Al-Aqsa Mosque/Temple Mount, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, and the Jewish Quarter** (NPR, "Israel says Iran launched a missile at it, in a first during fragile ceasefire," June 7, 2026; PBS NewsHour; Axios, June 7, 2026). Eyal Zamir** vowed to **"strike the enemy with determination as soon as the order is given."** The **IRGC** warned that any repeat would bring responses **"broader in scope"** encompassing **"all American and Zionist targets throughout the region,"** and **Iran's Foreign Ministry** called the **June 6 US strikes on radar sites at Goruk and Qeshm Island "a clear violation of the 8 April ceasefire and an act of military aggression"** — drawing the US, not only Israel, into the frame (CBS News live updates; PBS NewsHour; Al Jazeera, June 7-8, 2026). **President Trump pushed de-escalation:** he told Israel's **Kan** broadcaster he did not think Israel needed to respond further, said the Beirut strikes were **"not coordinated with the US and I'm not happy about it,"** told **Fox News** "What I would suggest to Iran: You've shot your missiles, that's enough… Get back to the table and make a deal," and told **Axios** he would call Netanyahu to urge him not to retaliate. > **Daily update — June 7, 2026 (Day 101).** The US-Iran exchange turned **kinetic a second time and widened to a second Gulf state.** On **June 6**, CENTCOM said US forces **shot down four Iranian one-way attack drones** launched toward the Strait of Hormuz — "an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic" — and **intercepted six of seven Iranian ballistic missiles fired at Kuwait AND Bahrain** (the seventh failed to reach its target). **Bahrain's Defense Ministry said it intercepted and destroyed three missiles and a number of drones** and that air-raid sirens sounded across the island, accusing Iran of "targeting civilians" — the **first time Bahrain was directly targeted** in the war (the June 3 barrage hit Kuwait only). In response, US forces **struck Iranian coastal surveillance radar sites in Goruk and on Qeshm Island** "to defend against further attacks," which CENTCOM said Iran uses to overlook the Hormuz maritime routes; CENTCOM said American forces "remain vigilant and postured to respond to unjustified Iranian aggression in self-defense." **Iran's Mehr news agency** characterized the drone launches as **"warning shots"** fired near the strait, most likely linked to movement of US ships (CENTCOM, "CENTCOM Forces Defeat Missiles, Drones Launched by Iran," June 6, 2026; Fox News live updates; RFE/RL; Middle East Monitor; ABC7; India TV News, June 6, 2026). **President Trump** said Iran's nuclear ambitions are **"finished,"** estimated Tehran now has only **"21-22%" of its pre-February missile arsenal,** and — via a White House official — said he **"isn't going to rush into a bad deal"** and would not allow Iran a nuclear weapon; the **US imposed fresh sanctions on Iranian LNG/LPG-smuggling networks** rather than front-load the $24B frozen-assets relief Iran demanded (Fox News; The Statesman, June 6, 2026). **Talks remained deadlocked** over the $24B demand, with **IAEA's Grossi** still seeing possible movement toward a preliminary framework. **Kuwait demanded two Iranian embassy staff leave** over the June 3 attack that killed one and wounded 63 at Kuwait International Airport (Gulf News). In **Lebanon, Israeli airstrikes killed nine June 6, including three Lebanese Army officers** — a sharp escalation of the fraying June 4 ceasefire framework, which envisions the LAF policing zones south of the Litani; the cumulative toll stands at ~3,500 since March 2 (Fox News; CNN; Al Jazeera). **Oil:** Brent **eased to ~$94.81/bbl** on June 6 (down from ~$95.25 June 5) despite the flare-up, with reduced Chinese crude imports a factor — risk/escalation pricing, not ground-commitment pricing. **Hormuz** traffic stayed near-zero (~36/week). In **Russia-Ukraine** the front stayed static (Russia unable to make operationally significant advances west of Pokrovsk since December 2025); next Istanbul round June 20-30. **North Korea** unveiled a new bomb-fuel plant (June 3) and vowed "exponential" nuclear expansion; **US-China** broadly unchanged; **Maduro + Flores** face a June 30 NYC court date. **Ground-invasion rung unchanged:** the flare-up was **horizontal escalation** (a second Gulf state) within the **air/naval + missile/drone register** — Iran fired drones and missiles, the US answered with intercepts and a proportional radar-site strike — with **no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order and no draft** (open-questions: june3-kuwait-kinetic-escalation-2026; iran-suspends-us-talks-lebanon-june-2026).

In an exclusive CNN interview in Tehran (June 5), **Mohsen Rezaei** — military adviser to Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** — said **"the negotiations are at a deadlock and Trump must break this deadlock,"** that **"the ball is in Trump's court,"** and that a potential interim deal now hinges on the US releasing **$24 billion in frozen Iranian assets** — **$12 billion upon signing and another $12 billion later** — which he cast as **"a test of trust that Iran wants to have with Trump … a test that America must pass and the path will be opened."** He warned Iran would **"drag the war"** beyond the Persian Gulf and **"give another dimension to the war by attacking these other American bases"** if fighting resumed, said **"our land power is many times greater than our missiles,"** proposed Iran and Oman jointly manage the Strait of Hormuz for **"maintenance fees"** rather than tolls, and characterized the conflict as Iran's **"first triumph"** in its 47-year history; US officials worry that unfreezing the funds now would surrender leverage and resemble handing over **"pallets of cash"** (CNN, "Exclusive: Iran supreme leader's adviser says talks deadlocked over $24 billion and warns of wider war," June 5, 2026; Newsmax; The Express Tribune; The Times of Israel, June 5, 2026). ## 0. MONTHLY VERIFICATION PASS — SEPTEMBER 1, 2026: THE GROUND NEGATIVE HOLDS AT 187 DAYS AND IS NOW CONFIRMED FROM INSIDE THE PENTAGON RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM OUTSIDE IT — AT THE COST OF A CORRECTION THIS BRIEFING OWES ON THE COMPOSITION OF THE FORCE ALREADY IN THEATRE

This section records the **September 1 monthly re-scoring pass**: what was re-checked against sources outside the daily cycle, what changed, what did not, and what this briefing got wrong. It supplements — it does not replace — the Day 187 daily update above. **Scope of the pass: 171 analysis files and 983 predictions re-reviewed; 134 predictions received a dated September block; two changed status.**

### The Two Status Changes

**(1) “The war has effectively lifted sanctions on Iran, allowing Iran to earn $14 billion from oil sales, exceeding its entire $10 billion annual military budget” — partially_confirmed → DISCONFIRMED.** Kpler data published **August 31** put loadings at **Kharg Island**, the terminal handling roughly **90% of Iran's crude exports**, at **135,000 barrels a day in August 2026** against **1.98 million bpd in February 2026** — a **93% collapse** — with satellite imagery showing all three berths empty for an extended period after operations halted on **July 31**. CENTCOM commander **Adm. Brad Cooper**, August 28: *“No ships have entered or left an Iranian port without our permission.”* Sanctions were **escalated, not lifted**: Treasury's **“Operation Economic Outcast,”** Secretary **Bessent's** *“this is going to be financial violence if we have to,”* three packages in August, and reported EU backing *“in the strongest terms.”* The one element of the original reasoning that survives is narrow and is retained: **no Chinese institution has been designated across three consecutive packages**, and the Associated Press reported this cycle that by sanctioning an Egyptian bank's Emirati branches rather than the bank itself the administration *“appeared to be signaling its reluctance to penalize major trading partners that do business with Iran, including China and India.”* **Selective enforcement against third parties is not sanctions relief for Iran.**

**(2) “China will invest in and modernize Venezuela's oil industry as part of a US-China grand bargain” — untested → DISCONFIRMED.** On **August 28, 2026** Venezuela granted a **100-year concession** over fields holding **65 billion barrels** — about **21% of the country's 303 billion** — to a joint venture in which the **United States government holds 55%**, secured *“at no cost to the American taxpayer.”* The counterparty is Washington, not Beijing; **no Chinese investment or modernisation agreement has been announced at any point in the war**; and the US-China grand bargain the prediction was conditioned on never materialised and is separately scored disconfirmed across the corpus.

### US-Iran — The Ground Question, Answered This Cycle From Inside the Building (through September 1, 2026)

**The negative holds for a 187th consecutive day, and for the first time it is documented rather than inferred.** *The Washington Post* published contents of the **August 14 edition of the Secretary of Defense Orders Book**, in which **four four-star commanders filed formal non-concurs** against continued allocation to the Iran theatre — Chief of Naval Operations **Adm. Daryl Caudle**, INDOPACOM's **Adm. Samuel Paparo**, EUCOM's **Gen. Alexus Grynkewich** and **SOUTHCOM** — while the Army and Air Force chiefs concurred but recorded increased risk. **Caudle told the Secretary of Defense the Navy “cannot sustain its current level of support”** absent an end date, with **barely a quarter of the destroyer fleet ready to deploy**. **More than half** the cruise-missile and advanced air-defence-missile inventories are expended; roughly **a quarter of the Reaper fleet** is lost; **THAAD** has been redeployed from **South Korea**; the **USS George Washington** moved from **Japan** to the Gulf, **leaving the Pacific without carrier coverage**; a Pacific carrier was redirected to relieve one deployed **more than 300 days**. The orders direct that **50,000 troops be HELD, not raised** — some units through September, others into **2027**. Collective formulation as reported: **“We will carry out the orders, but at a price.”** Pentagon spokesman **Sean Parnell** called publication *“a crime”* and *“a betrayal of the force”* while confirming its substance, adding that the Secretary sees non-concurs *“constantly. That's how you run a real military.”*

**Third-party confirmation, second consecutive month.** The **Council on Foreign Relations Global Conflict Tracker**, re-checked **September 1**, continues to record **no US ground force commitment** and operations that remain **primarily aerial and naval**, while classifying the conflict as **“worsening”** with **“critical”** impact on the United States.

**The cycle's own test, and it was the sharpest of the war.** On **August 30** the United States faced a discrete, located, time-sensitive military problem on **Iranian ground inside the Strait**: IRGC launchers on **Larak Island** preparing to fire rockets carrying **sea mines**. Five days earlier the President had declared the Strait's international waters cleared under a **“zero tolerance”** rule; two days earlier Adm. Cooper had called the shipping lanes free of mines a **“major milestone.”** **The answer was aircraft, not a landing party.** Iran retaliated on **August 31** with **“Punishment of the Aggressor”** against **King Hussein** and **Al Azraq** in **Jordan** and, on its army's account, **Al Minhad** in the **UAE** — **no casualties anywhere** — and the American answer to *that* was verbal: **“we're going to hit them hard,”** with **no second US strike inside Iran in the following twenty-four hours**.

### The Correction This Briefing Owes: The 82nd Airborne

**This briefing has been wrong on two points and corrects them here.** On **August 30-31** the Army extended the Middle East deployment of elements of the **82nd Airborne Division** to a **full twelve months**, carrying soldiers into **2027**, announced by letter from division commander **Maj. Gen. Brandon R. Tegtmeier**: *“We do not share that lightly, and we understand that a longer tour weighs heavily on every household, including our own.”* The published unit list is the material fact — **Division Headquarters, 1st Brigade Combat Team, Combat Aviation Brigade, DIVARTY, the 307th Division Engineer Battalion, 3rd Battalion 4th Air Defense Artillery** and a sustainment element, **approximately 2,000 soldiers**, deployed from Fort Bragg in **March 2026**.

This briefing carried **“approximately 1,000 paratroopers”** and the standing statement that **“no brigade combat team, division headquarters or corps-level enabler set has been identified in theatre at any point in the war.”** **Both are falsified by the published list.** The corrected record: **approximately 2,000 soldiers, comprising a division headquarters and a brigade combat team with organic artillery, engineer, air-defence, aviation and sustainment enablers, in CENTCOM since March 2026.** The correction is to the record and **not to the disposition** — no unit moved in this cycle; the extension letter is simply what made the composition public.

**What the extension is not.** It **adds no soldiers, moves nobody forward, changes no mission and names no objective.** Extending tours to twelve months is what a volunteer force does when it has **no replacements available**, and the August 14 Orders Book says why: the Navy cannot sustain the current commitment and three geographic combatant commands say their own obligations are already degraded. **A tour extension is the inverse of the concentration signature this briefing watches for.** The counter-case is logged and is not trivial: a force that cannot sustain an open-ended blockade has a rational incentive to seek a decision, and the ground capability documented in theatre is larger than this briefing had recorded. **Capability is not intent, and an extension order is not a warning order.**

### The Kharg Option After Six Months: Achieved by Blockade, Claimed by Video, Never Taken

**The objective has been met without the operation.** Kpler's **August 31** figures put Kharg loadings at **135,000 bpd against 1.98m bpd in February — a 93% collapse produced by naval blockade with no American on the island.** The seizure requirement is unchanged at **~1,200+ troops** against anti-personnel and anti-armour mines emplaced on the landing shoreline itself plus added MANPADS, with specialists identifying **holding** the island as the harder problem.

**And this cycle the strike was claimed rather than conducted.** Late on **August 31** the President posted to **Truth Social** an **AI-generated video** of oil infrastructure erupting in flames, captioned **“Kharg Island being blown to smithereens!!! President DJT.”** **A US official said no such attack had taken place** and that Kharg was **not among the locations targeted overnight**; **CENTCOM's own statement named only Larak.** National Iranian Oil Company chief executive **Hamid Bovard** called the post **“laughable”** and said conditions on the island were **“calm and appropriate.”** Crude rose about **2%** on the Monday. Because this administration treats Truth Social posts as official presidential statements, the gap is itself the datum: **the first claimed destruction of Kharg in this war is a fabrication contradicted within hours by the President's own government.** Analysts scoring “the US will destroy Kharg” predictions must not score this.

### Iran — Two Unreliable Narrators, and What Sits Between Them

On **August 31** the President also declared that **“Iran is officially a Failed Nation”** and **“It is dead!”**, adding: *“They have no Navy, they have no Air Force, they have no currency, they are not paying their soldiers or police, **Inflation is at 300%**, and their leadership is in total disarray.”* He claimed **more than 100,000** anti-regime protesters killed and demanded the regime be **tried for war crimes**. **The protester figure exceeds every documented count:** **~7,002** verified by **HRANA**, **3,117** conceded by the Iranian government, **“at least 5,000”** assessed by the **UN Special Rapporteur** (who noted medical sources suggesting a possibly far higher figure; Iran International's outlier estimate is ~36,500).

On the other side, **Reuters reported on August 30** that Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** *“has not been seen in public since being **injured** in U.S.-Israeli airstrikes six months ago”* — the first published explanation for an absence logged here since February 28 — and at the **SCO summit in Bishkek on August 31** President **Pezeshkian** told Modi, with Xi and Putin present, that *“continuing the war is neither in our interest, nor in the interest of the region.”* **Both belligerents' characterisations of Iranian resilience are now unreliable in opposite directions.** The measurable indicators sit between them: **command and control survived a six-month decapitation campaign well enough to run a named two-country retaliation**, and **Kharg is loading at 7% of its February rate**.

### The Six-Month Ledger (published August 28, 2026)

At least **7,900 killed** across all parties — **Lebanon 4,350**, **Iran 3,527**, **Gulf states 28**, **Israelis 60**, **US service members 18** — with **757 US wounded**, **12,510 injured in Lebanon**, **70 ship incidents** in the Strait and **19 seafarer deaths**. **3,580** US/Israeli attacks against **2,053** Iranian, **5,500+** total. Hormuz: **pre-war 100 transits a day**, a six-month average of **7**, a low of **5** and a post-agreement peak of **20** — a series that does not reconcile with UKMTO's **204 full transits in the seven days to August 28** and is retained alongside it as a logged dispute rather than resolved. Brent **$72.48 → $88.58 (+22%)** after a **$120.88** closing-basis peak (against the **$144.42** dated-spot print of April 7). **US SPR at 290 million barrels — 41% of capacity, the lowest since 1982.** Official war cost **$37.5 billion** against **$80-100 billion** reported internally. Presidential approval **33%**; **80%** of Americans expect an extended conflict.

### Russia-Ukraine — An Energy Campaign Announced in Advance and Endorsed by the Kremlin (August 30-31, 2026)

Russia's **Ministry of Defence** said the armed forces *“have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure”*; **Dmitry Peskov** then endorsed it as an appropriate response to Kyiv's *“path of escalation,”* moving a ministry communiqué to a political commitment **eight weeks before the heating season**. Moscow, treating talks as deadlocked, is reported to be weighing conventional ballistic strikes on **Kyiv including the city centre**. The **Myla** toll from the August 28 munitions-warehouse strike reached **38 killed, 20 injured and 4 missing** — the deadliest attack in Ukraine this year. The line holds: **225 combat engagements on August 31** with 36 in the Pokrovsk direction, after 250 clashes on August 28; **net 2026 Russian gains remain 81.1 km²**. On **NATO**, the escalation-management reading of July 30 is unchanged — Poland absorbed a Russian **Kh-101** roughly 100km inside its territory and **declined to invoke Article 4**, a deliberate step down from September 2025.

### Latin America, East Asia, Israel-Lebanon, and the Draft Rung — Re-Verified, No Change of State

- **Venezuela / Cuba / Colombia.** Fifth consecutive cycle without a new event beyond the **August 28** concession (100-year grant, 65 billion barrels, **US government holding 55%** of the joint venture). Maduro's trial date remains **June 1, 2027**. Cuba's figure of record remains **six** nationwide grid collapses in 2026 against Cuban outlets' seven. Colombia's **Abelardo de la Espriella** was inaugurated **August 7**. The cycle's new datum came from the leaked Orders Book: **SOUTHCOM filed a formal non-concur**, stating that diversion to the Iran theatre has degraded its ability to meet homeland-defence obligations — the command that removed Maduro in January is on record saying it cannot cover its own region.
- **DPRK / Korean Peninsula.** North Korea fired **more than ten short-range ballistic missiles** on **August 20**, the day after shrugging off the US drawdown, then went twelve consecutive days without a launch. **No nuclear test and no ICBM launch.** The concessions ran the other way: **Ulchi Freedom Shield cut from eleven days to five** on presidential order with its counteroffensive phase never conducted, a further exercise cancelled, and — per the Orders Book — **THAAD physically removed from South Korea**. **Pyongyang has reciprocated with nothing.**
- **China-Taiwan.** No blockade, no quarantine, no invasion, no cross-strait kinetic action. **The month in which the American Pacific posture was documented at its thinnest of the war — INDOPACOM's formal non-concur, the George Washington out of Japan, THAAD off the peninsula — produced no Chinese move.** Xi spent August 31 at Bishkek. Beijing's internal news of the cycle was an expanded purge of senior generals.
- **Israel-Lebanon.** The **Rome** round opened **August 4**. Israel's defence minister on **August 13** tied withdrawal from southern Lebanon explicitly to **Hezbollah's disarmament**, walking back remarks that had suggested indefinite occupation and drawn US criticism. Lebanon and Israel have agreed a **shortlist of countries** that could send troops to verify disarmament, with the United States to choose from it. Hezbollah's secretary general called on Beirut to halt the talks. Military and strategic assessments expect **no significant Israeli withdrawal** while disarmament is unresolved.
- **The draft rung — still zero, and the one moving part is still moving backwards.** There is **no active US draft**; conscription requires authorisation from **both Congress and the President** during a declared national emergency, and no draft legislation is moving. The statutory mandate is unchanged: automatic Selective Service registration of men aged **18-26** must begin **December 19, 2026** under the December 2025 NDAA. But the implementing rulemaking **withdrawn by the Selective Service System on July 23, 2026** — after the White House held it nearly four months — **has still not been re-proposed**, and no explanation has been given. **Manpower pressure this cycle produced a twelve-month tour extension, not a draft call.**
- **Force posture.** US theatre strength remains **~50,000**, roughly 10,000 above the standing presence, which Adm. Cooper on August 28 described as *“executing a blockade on Iran”* with **more than 20 warships** and **hundreds of aircraft** — **~1,500 vessels escorted** carrying roughly **750 million barrels**, **75 vessels turned around**, **3 disabled**. **None of it is inside Iran.**

## 0-PRIOR. MONTHLY VERIFICATION PASS — AUGUST 1, 2026: INDEPENDENT SOURCING CONVERGES WITH THE DAILY RECORD, AND ON THE GROUND QUESTION IT CONVERGES HARD

This section records the August 1 monthly re-scoring pass: what was checked against sources outside the daily cycle, what changed, and what did not. It supplements — it does not replace — the Day 156 daily update above.

### US-Iran — Third-Party Confirmation That the War Has No Ground Component (through July 29, 2026)

The **Council on Foreign Relations Global Conflict Tracker**, an assessment produced independently of this project's daily cycle, records that **"no significant US ground force commitment is documented"** and that operations have **"remained primarily aerial and naval, with US military focus on air strikes and enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports."** It also logs the July 27 halt after thirteen consecutive nights of bombing, Iran's reciprocal suspension, and Saudi Arabia's July 28 participation in strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq that killed at least 26 fighters and advisers.

**Independent human and fiscal ledger:** approximately **1,701 documented civilian deaths in Iran**; up to **3.2 million Iranians displaced**; a US strike on an Iranian school that killed at least **175**; war cost put by the Defense Secretary at roughly **$37.5 billion** as of late July. CFR's US military death count (13+, at least 3 in July) runs below the running ABC News tally of **18 KIA** carried in the daily record — a difference in counting basis and confirmation lag, not a correction to either figure. **US wounded stand at 685.**

### The Kharg Option After Four Months: Available, Staffed, Repeatedly Reported, Never Taken

The open-source force requirement has not moved since March: **at least ~1,200 troops**, most plausibly a **Marine battalion landing team**, a **reinforced Army airborne battalion**, or a combination of the two. What has moved is the cost of trying. Iran has emplaced **anti-personnel and anti-armour mines around the island — including on the shoreline where an amphibious landing would come ashore** — and moved additional **MANPADS** onto it, on top of layered air defences and reinforced personnel. US officials and outside experts warn of significant US casualties, and specialists identify **holding** the island afterward as the harder problem than taking it.

Set that against the July 31 reporting: the coercive package now under consideration or ordered — accounts differ — aims at **Iranian capitulation through cumulative destruction from the air**, targeting **power plants, refineries, Tehran's electricity grid and dual-use bridges**. That is the same objective the Kharg seizure was designed to deliver, reassigned to a different instrument. **No ground element appears in any of the four independent accounts of the package. Kharg is not named in any of them.**

### Russia-NATO — Poland Declines to Invoke Article 4 (July 30-31, 2026)

A Russian cruise missile crossed roughly **100 km into Polish territory** and detonated in a field in **Lublin province**, leaving a crater about **10 metres wide and 5 metres deep**. PM **Donald Tusk** said fragment analysis indicated a **Kh-101**. Warsaw convened an emergency coordination group and consulted European leaders, **but did not invoke Article 4 while the investigation continued** — a deliberate step *down* from **September 2025**, when roughly 19 Russian drones crossed into Polish airspace and Poland *did* invoke it. Two NATO fighters, a NATO tanker, a Polish AEW aircraft and a Polish helicopter responded; NATO forces were reportedly **seconds from shooting the missile down** before assessing it would crash on its own. **Nobody was hurt.** The escalation-management reading matters more than the incident: a NATO member absorbed a live Russian munition on its soil and chose the lower rung.

### Russia-Ukraine — The Line Holds (July 2026)

The roughly 1,000-km front continued to hold, with divergent territorial assessments for late June into early July: **~31 square miles** of net Russian gains per DeepState, **~6 square miles** per ISW. Russian assault pressure stayed concentrated around **Kostiantynivka** and north and west of **Pokrovsk**, with no confirmed gains despite Moscow's claim to have taken Kostiantynivka outright; Russia has not advanced significantly west of Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad since December 2025. Ukraine's long-range strike campaign against Russian oil and energy infrastructure continued. Zelensky authorised two new commands within the armed forces on **July 10**. **The war remains a grinding attritional conflict; Ukraine has not lost.**

### Venezuela — Transition Talks Open on Schedule (August 1, 2026)

The **State Department** backed a joint agenda beginning **August 1** aimed at stability, democracy and national recovery, with the interim government's endorsement. **Jorge Rodríguez**, National Assembly President, leads the government delegation; **Dinorah Figuera**, former head of the 2015 legislature, is on the opposition side. **María Corina Machado** confirmed she will not participate in the design, development or operation of the talks, will not obstruct "real progress," and will judge the outcome on restored democratic institutions, freed political prisoners and a scheduled election. Analysts note that sidelining the two principal opposition figures fuels doubt about the process.

### Israel-Lebanon — Rome, August 4-6 (2026)

Trilateral **Israel-Lebanon-US** talks are set for **Rome, August 4-6**, to expand the pilot zones for Israeli withdrawal, resolve outstanding border issues and work toward a comprehensive peace and security agreement. The **late-June US-brokered framework** provides for an end to the war in Lebanon, **disarmament of Hezbollah**, deployment of Lebanese troops in the south, and gradual Israeli withdrawal through two pilot zones. **Hezbollah is not a party to the talks.**

### China-Taiwan — Exercises, Not Escalation (July 2026)

The PLA completed a **two-day live-fire drill inside PRC territorial waters in the Taiwan Strait, July 23-24**, assessed as intimidation signalling toward Taipei. **Joint Sea-2026** with Russia ran off **Qingdao, July 6-13**; a joint PRC-Russian aerial patrol encroached into **South Korea's ADIZ**; PLA personnel trained at a Russian military complex on unmanned-systems warfare in a drone-saturated environment. Analysts note the interoperability gains may contribute to amphibious-invasion capability and to diluting Japanese involvement in a Taiwan contingency. **No blockade, no quarantine, no invasion, no cross-strait kinetic action.**

### DPRK — The Naval Track (July 3-5, 2026)

**Kim Jong Un** observed a **strategic cruise-missile launch** and evaluations of **anti-ship, anti-submarine and air-defence systems** aboard the newly built 5,000-tonne destroyer ***Kang Kon*** — target detection, information processing, integrated firepower, naval guns, automatic cannon and electronic-warfare equipment — a first assessment of the vessel's major weapons systems ahead of induction into the navy **within two months**. **No nuclear test and no ICBM launch this cycle.**

### The Draft Rung — Still Zero, and the One Change Is Administrative

**There is no active US draft.** Reinstating conscription requires authorisation from **both Congress and the President** during a national emergency. Two facts sit together here. The **statutory mandate is unchanged**: automatic registration of men aged **18-26** must begin **December 19, 2026** under the December 2025 NDAA, and the switch would remove the opportunity to object or demonstrate non-qualification at the point of registration. But the **implementing rulemaking was withdrawn on July 23, 2026**, when the Selective Service System pulled the proposed rules it had submitted to the White House on March 30 — held there nearly four months without action, withdrawn without explanation, and not re-proposed. That is the draft indicator's **first backward movement of the war**. **A registration mechanism is not a mobilisation.** A coalition of organisations is publicly campaigning to halt draft preparations — evidence that the question is live in public debate, not that conscription is imminent.

### Force Posture — Above 50,000, None of It Inside Iran

US troop levels in the Middle East remain **above 50,000**, roughly **10,000 above the standing presence**, following the deployment of **2,500 Marines and 2,500 sailors**. **Kuwait** hosts about **13,500** — the largest single-country deployment in the region; **Al Udeid** in Qatar, with capacity for 10,000 personnel, is the largest US installation and CENTCOM's forward headquarters. This is theatre reinforcement. **No US ground troops are inside Iran.**

## 1. US-Iran Military Actions — SEPTEMBER 6-7 (DAY 193): IRAN ANSWERED THE DESTRUCTION OF THREE OF ITS TANKERS WITH A MAP, A ZONE AND A SANCTIONS LIST — MOHSEN REZAEI ANNOUNCED A “RESTRICTED ZONE” OUTSIDE THE STRAIT BEGINNING FROM THE LINE OF THE US NAVY'S BLOCKADE, AND CLAIMED PASSAGE MAPS AGREED WITH OMAN FOR A CORRIDOR “UNDER IRAN'S MANAGEMENT.” OMAN SAID NOTHING. TEHRAN CLAIMED A STRIKE ON AN UNMANNED US VESSEL AND THE US MILITARY CALLED IT A “TOTAL LIE.” GHALIBAF DECLARED THE ERA OF PROPORTIONATE RESPONSES OVER AND NO LAUNCH FOLLOWED. THE AMERICAN ANSWER WAS A BLOCKADE LEDGER AND A TREASURY BARREL COUNT. THE GROUND RUNG DID NOT MOVE FOR A 193rd DAY.

**Iran replied to a kinetic defeat with a jurisdictional instrument.** **Mohsen Rezaei**, Secretary of Iran's **Supreme National Security Council**, said on **September 6** that Tehran will declare a **“restricted zone”** — rendered elsewhere as an **“exclusion zone”** — **outside** the Strait of Hormuz **within days**. Its stated geometry is unusual enough to record precisely: the zone **begins from the line of the US Navy's blockade** and **extends into parts of the Gulf**. Its stated enforcement mechanism is not a weapon but a list: *“Any ship that enters this area with the intention of passing through the Strait of Hormuz and is identified will be placed on our sanctions list.”* An Iranian sanctions list has no practical purchase on a Greek-owned, Liberian-flagged, London-insured VLCC. The instrument is **declaratory**, and this briefing records the announcement rather than an effect.

**The Oman corridor moved, in Tehran's telling, from proposal to pending signature.** Rezaei stated that **maps detailing the passage of ships in the Strait of Hormuz have been agreed with Oman and will be signed in coming days**, and that a **new international corridor** designated by Iran and Oman would be announced — emphasising that the corridor would be **“under Iran's management.”** He added that Iran is **“now pursuing diplomacy with guarantees.”** **Muscat published no text, no map, no signature and no confirmation.** Every description of the arrangement originates with Tehran, and Oman's role in this war has been mediation rather than alignment. The entry stands in the open-questions register as `iran-oman-hormuz-corridor-concession-or-consolidation-august-2026`, strengthened as to Iranian **intent** and unmoved as to **effect**.

**For the first time, both belligerents described the same traffic volume.** Rezaei called the Strait **“completely closed,”** with only **seven to eight ships** passing. The **straits.live** board carried **six transits** against an **85/day pre-crisis baseline** — 7% of normal — at its **06 September 2026 2257Z** timestamp. For 193 days the two governments have disputed **whose** closure this is; this is the first cycle in which they have not disputed **how large** it is.

**A third figure does not reconcile, and the reason is a category difference rather than a contradiction.** US Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** put flows through the Strait at approximately **9 million barrels per day**, roughly **two-thirds of pre-conflict levels**, a figure that **counts pipeline substitution** — volumes routed through the Saudi **East-West pipeline** and the UAE's **Fujairah** terminal that **never enter the Strait**. Wright also said the American military's role was **“strangling their economy.”** This briefing carries the **transit count** as its metric of record and logs the throughput figure separately; the dispute is registered as `hormuz-transit-volume-dispute-august-2026`.

**A claim, and a categorical denial — which is a change of form from the previous cycle.** Iran said it had **struck an unmanned US vessel** attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz. The **US military dismissed the claim as a “total lie.”** **Neither side published a vessel name, hull type, position, imagery or damage assessment.** On **September 5** CENTCOM met the IRGC's six-vessel claim with **silence**; on **September 6** the American denial was **explicit and categorical**. Experts quoted by the Associated Press noted that a strike on a **US government-operated hull**, if real, would mark an escalation beyond Iran's previous pattern of attacking **commercial** shipping. The claim is logged as `unmanned-vessel-strike-claim-september-2026` — an unmanned vessel has no crew to interview, no flag state to file a claim and no insurer to record a loss, and is therefore among the hardest categories of maritime assertion to adjudicate from open sources.

**Tehran's declaratory ladder went up and its kinetic ladder stayed still.** **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf** — speaker of parliament and Iran's chief negotiator — said in a speech posted to **Telegram** that the United States has realised **“the era of ‘proportionate responses’ is over,”** described recent strikes on *“the aggressors' bases”* as **“just the beginning,”** and warned that any further aggression against Iran will draw a **“faster, stronger and more painful”** response. **No Iranian launch against a US base, a Gulf host state or Israel was reported in the cycle that followed** — a third consecutive night without one.

**The American escalation was accountancy.** US Central Command published an updated blockade ledger on **September 6**: **92 commercial vessels redirected, three disabled, two boarded**, with **20+ warships** enforcing. The redirection figure had stood at **87 since September 3**; **five more merchant hulls were turned in three days**, while the **disabled** and **boarded** counts — the blockade's two escalatory rungs — did not move. Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** said Iran has approximately **30 million barrels** of crude remaining that **China has not purchased**, and that sanctions and the blockade **“will soon prevent Tehran from supplying more.”** Foreign ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baghaei** accused the United States of causing the disruption and then blaming Tehran for its consequences.

**The nuclear file moved to Vienna.** The **United States** and the **E3** — Britain, France and Germany — drafted a resolution for the **IAEA Board of Governors**, meeting **September 7-11 in Vienna**, seeking to **refer Iran to the UN Security Council** for failure to comply with its nonproliferation obligations. The dispute centres on approximately **440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%** that inspectors cannot verify. The resolution would follow the **June 10, 2026** text, carried **21 in favour, 3 against (Russia, China, Niger) and 10 abstentions**. **Punitive Security Council measures remain unlikely on the arithmetic: Russia and China hold vetoes.**

**Market and cost.** Brent **$96.28** at the straits.live board's **06 September 2026 2257Z** timestamp, **unchanged at +0.00%** over 24 hours on a **closed weekend session** — a non-price, not a judgement — roughly **34%** above the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline and well below the ~$120.88 wartime peak, with WTI in an unchanged **$88.10-$97.36** band. **Six transits** against an 85/day baseline; the Strait recorded as **closed to commercial shipping**; war-risk insurance at **40.0× pre-crisis**, about **$10.0 million per VLCC passage** (**+3,900%** versus peacetime). **The tradeable information is in the probability structure, and it softened at both ends:** **December 31** reopening slipped **27% → 26%**; **January 1 2027** slipped **22% → 20%**; **September 30** held at **2%**; **September 15** at **1%**. An announced Iranian exclusion zone made the market marginally **less** confident the Strait reopens this year. **US gasoline: AAA national average ~$4.14/gal, unchanged.**

**Kharg, unchanged and untouched.** No US munition landed on or near **Kharg Island** this cycle and no surface formation approached it. The **September 5** disabling of the **M/T Downy** in the water off the island remains the closest American ordnance has come to Iran's principal export terminal in this war, and it remains a strike on a **hull** rather than on the **island**, its **jetties**, its **tank farm**, its **pumping stations** or its **garrison**. *Kpler* carry-forward: **Iranian loadings 251,000 bpd in August 2026** against **1.98m bpd in February**; **stocks at Kharg 19.45 million barrels** against roughly **30 million barrels** of capacity; **Kharg's share of Iranian crude exports 94%**; **operations halted July 31**. **Chinese imports of Iranian crude ~534,000 bpd in August**, from **~823,000 bpd in July** against a **1.4m bpd** average last year. **The blockade is achieving by interdiction what the tracked prediction expected from seizure.**

**What did not happen on Day 193:** no American ground operation inside Iran; no landing; no raid; no seizure of Iranian territory; no special-operations action reported anywhere in Iran; no US strike on Iranian territory; no third night of Iranian launches at a Gulf host state; **no reinforcement order, no alert change, no announced deployment and no amphibious tasking — 48 hours after an IRGC ballistic-missile attack on a US aircraft carrier**; no change to the **50,000** ceiling, to force composition or to tour lengths; no approach to Kharg; and no movement on the draft. **US casualties of record hold at 18 killed and 767 wounded.** **Kuhestak** holds at **five dead and nearly seventy wounded**, under **Adm. Brad Cooper's** internal review, with the **Iranian Red Crescent's ICC letter** outstanding. **The Secretary of Defense Orders Book has been off SIPRNet since September 2 and has not been restored.**

**Sources:** Associated Press, “Iran claims strike on US ship in Strait of Hormuz as fighting escalates,” September 6, 2026 (carried by ABC News, NBC News, PBS NewsHour, The Washington Times and WTOC); PBS NewsHour, “Iran says it plans to announce a new ‘exclusion zone’ near the Strait of Hormuz,” September 6, 2026; Al Jazeera live blog, “Iran war live: Tehran to announce restricted zone outside Strait of Hormuz,” September 6, 2026; The Jerusalem Post, “Iran ready to announce restricted zone in Strait of Hormuz, security council secretary claims,” September 6, 2026; Xinhua, “Iran to announce ‘restricted zone’ outside Hormuz Strait: top security official,” September 7, 2026; SBS News, September 6, 2026; Investing Live, “Iran to declare Hormuz restricted zone, warns of ‘more painful’ attack response,” September 6, 2026; ABC News live blog entry timestamped September 6, 2026 6:48 AM EDT (Ghalibaf); Sunday Guardian Live and Voice of Emirates, “US CENTCOM says 92 commercial vessels redirected, three disabled, two boarded during Iran naval blockade,” September 6, 2026; Iran International live blog, September 5-6, 2026 (Bessent, Wright, Rezaei, Baghaei); The Washington Post, “UN nuclear agency members draft resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council,” September 4, 2026; Security Council Report, “Iran, September 2026 Monthly Forecast”; straits.live board, 06 September 2026 2257Z; AAA national average, September 6, 2026.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — SEPTEMBER 5-6 (DAY 192): IRAN SHOT BALLISTIC MISSILES AT AN AMERICAN AIRCRAFT CARRIER AND A GUIDED-MISSILE DESTROYER AND MISSED BOTH, AND THE UNITED STATES ANSWERED BY DESTROYING OR PERMANENTLY DISABLING THREE IRANIAN CRUDE CARRIERS — INCLUDING, FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE WAR, A VESSEL LYING OFF KHARG ISLAND. THE CENTCOM COMMANDER PUBLISHED THE EXCHANGE RATE IN PUBLIC. THE IRGC CLAIMED SIX VESSELS AND CENTCOM CONFIRMED NONE. NO STRIKE ON IRANIAN TERRITORY AND NO MOVEMENT ON THE GROUND RUNG.

**Iran shot at a carrier.** On **September 5** the **Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps** launched **ballistic missiles** toward **two US Navy warships** patrolling regional waters — a **US aircraft carrier** and a **guided-missile destroyer**. CENTCOM's account is that both ships **“successfully evaded multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks”** and that **no American personnel were harmed**. No US vessel was struck. This briefing records the attempt rather than the outcome: a ballistic-missile salvo aimed at a deployed American carrier is among the **highest-consequence actions Iran has taken in this war**, and it failed.

**The United States answered in hulls, not in territory.** CENTCOM struck **three Iranian crude oil carriers** with a mix of **Air Force and Navy aircraft**, both fighters and drones. The **M/T Downy** was **permanently disabled off the coast of Kharg Island**. The **M/T Stark 1** was **permanently disabled near Jask**. The unladen **M/T Kylo**, also known as the **“Noxen,”** was **completely destroyed in the Gulf of Oman**, struck in multiple critical locations **after her crew was directed to abandon ship** — the same warning-evacuation-destruction sequence CENTCOM used on the two government tankers of September 1-2.

**The commander published the exchange rate.** **Adm. Brad Cooper:** *“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: if you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours.”* He added that Iran **“has no means by which to defend”** its tanker fleet and would not hesitate to see that fleet destroyed, and CENTCOM characterised the vessels as part of a **“multibillion-dollar shadow network”** funding the IRGC and regional proxies. This is the **“tanker for tanker”** policy *Axios* reported on September 2 as personally approved by the President — **restated at a three-for-two ratio** and applied not to a shipping attack but to an attack on **warships**. The retaliatory currency has been **decoupled from its trigger**: Iran shot at combatants, and the United States answered against commerce.

**The first American munition of the war landed off Kharg Island — and the amendment this briefing makes is narrow.** For 191 days this record carried Kharg as **not struck, not landed on, not approached**. A US munition struck **a ship in the water off Kharg Island**. It did **not** strike **the island**, its **loading jetties**, its **tank farm**, its **pumping stations** or its **garrison**. No American set foot on it. The distinction is the whole substance of the tracked prediction, which concerns **seizure** and **strikes on the terminal**, not the water around it. The Downy was engaged **by the same method, on the same day, as hulls 700km away**.

**Iran claimed six ships and CENTCOM confirmed none.** The **IRGC Navy** stated that it had targeted **three oil tankers** sailing through **“an unauthorized route”** in the Strait of Hormuz and **three vessels affiliated with the United States** elsewhere, and warned mariners: *“Do not be deceived by the ‘terrorist’ US military and refrain from any suspicious movement aimed at passing through unauthorized waterways… otherwise, you will be targeted.”* Through the cutoff, **US Central Command had not confirmed any of the six**, no vessel names were published, and no damage was independently verified. The claim is logged as a claim, in the register as `irgc-six-vessel-claim-september-2026`.

**Legal and political residue.** Iran's **foreign ministry** condemned the American tanker strikes as a **war crime**. The **Kuhestak** wedding strike of September 1 remained under an **internal review** ordered by Adm. Cooper, its toll at **five dead** and nearly **seventy wounded**, with the **Iranian Red Crescent's** letter to the **International Criminal Court** outstanding.

**Market and cost.** Brent **$96.28** at the straits.live board's **05 September 2026 2301Z** timestamp, **up 0.53%** over 24 hours and roughly **34%** above the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline. **Six transits** against an 85/day baseline; war-risk **40.0×** pre-crisis (~**$10.0m per VLCC passage**); the **December 31 reopening probability held at 27%**. **A ballistic-missile attack on an American aircraft carrier and the destruction of three Iranian tankers moved crude fifty-three basis points.**

**What did not happen on Day 192:** no strike on Iranian territory; no Iranian launch against Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, the UAE or Erbil for a second consecutive night; no new blockade boarding, disabling or redirection; **no change in troop posture, no amphibious order, no approach to Kharg by any surface formation, and no movement on the draft.**

**Sources:** U.S. Central Command statement and @CENTCOM post, “CENTCOM Destroys 3 IRGC Oil Tankers After Iran Targets 2 U.S. Navy Warships,” September 5, 2026; Stars and Stripes, September 5, 2026; CNBC, September 5, 2026; NPR, “U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers after Navy ships targeted,” September 5, 2026; Air & Space Forces Magazine, September 5, 2026; ABC News live blog, September 5, 2026; The Jerusalem Post, September 5-6, 2026; Press TV, September 5, 2026; Middle East Eye live blog, September 5, 2026; straits.live board, 05 September 2026 2301Z.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — SEPTEMBER 4-5 (DAY 191): THE PRESIDENT DECLARED THE WAR “SMALL POTATOES” AND SAID THE UNITED STATES HAS “ESSENTIALLY TAKEN OVER IRAN” — A CLAIM OF POSSESSION ADVANCED WITH NO AMERICAN SOLDIER ON IRANIAN SOIL. THE CENTCOM COMMANDER ORDERED AN INTERNAL REVIEW OF THE KUHESTAK WEDDING STRIKE AFTER FOUR INDEPENDENT WEAPONS EXPERTS AND TWO MAJOR NEWS ORGANISATIONS ATTRIBUTED IT TO AN AMERICAN MUNITION, THE TOLL ROSE TO FIVE AND THE IRANIAN RED CRESCENT FILED WITH THE ICC. THERE WAS NO THIRD NIGHT OF IRANIAN LAUNCHES AND NO NEW AMERICAN WAVE. THE ONLY GROUND SEIZED WAS SEIZED BY AN ISRAELI DIVISION IN LEBANON.

**The commander-in-chief described a war he has not won as one he has already won, and called it small.** Asked about the campaign on **September 4**, President **Trump** said it is **“small potatoes”** and **“not a big thing”** for the United States, and that **“we took over Venezuela and we have essentially taken over Iran.”** Pressed on the **eighteen** American service members killed, he compared the conflict to the years-long wars in **Vietnam** and **Afghanistan**. Asked about Vice President **Vance's** statement that *“I wouldn't call it a war,”* he said: *“I would say it's a military conflict if you want... I don't think it matters what you call it.”* **This briefing records the sentence about Iran precisely because of what it does not contain.** Whatever *“essentially taken over”* is meant to denote — the blockade, the collapse of the rial, the destruction of Iranian coastal radar — **it does not denote territory**, and no element of the American instrument changed on the day it was said. The claim has **no stated referent and therefore no falsification condition**; CENTCOM's own published ledger of **87 vessels redirected**, **six transits a day against an 85/day baseline** and a waterway prediction markets price at a **2% chance of reopening this month** does not obviously support it. Its significance for the tracked ground prediction is **directional rather than factual**: a president arguing in public that his war is small and already substantially won, two months before a midterm his war polls at **31% support and roughly 63% opposition**, is not building the domestic case for the most expensive escalation available.

**The wedding strike became an investigation, an attribution and an ICC filing in a single cycle.** CENTCOM commander **Adm. Brad Cooper** ordered an **internal review** of the civilian-casualty incident at **Kuhestak**, in **Sirik district, Hormozgan**, struck at about **21:30 local on September 1** during the war's largest strike wave. *Reuters* put verified photographs and video to **four military weapons experts**. **Gareth Collett**, a retired British Army brigadier with a doctorate in explosives engineering: the damage **“is consistent with a direct hit, as opposed to secondary damage from a munition ricocheting off a separate target.”** **Trevor Ball**, a former US Army explosive ordnance disposal technician: the damage **“appears to be from a munition which detonated on contact with the roof, or just above the roof,”** with remnants potentially from a **JSOW** glide bomb. **Sebastian Schutte** of the **Peace Research Institute Oslo**: the impact angle **rules out an air-defence missile** — which excludes the errant-Iranian-interceptor explanation. Separately, investigations by **The New York Times**, the **BBC** and independent analysts concluded the weapon was a **US Precision Strike Missile (PrSM)**, designed to detonate in the air and scatter thousands of **tungsten pellets** over a wide area. **The two munition identifications are not the same weapon, and this briefing carries both, unreconciled.** The nearest military-adjacent object was a **telecommunications tower roughly 135 metres away**, which was also struck; communications sites were a published category in CENTCOM's own target set for the wave.

**The toll rose and the case moved to an international court.** Iranian state television reported on **September 3** that a **22-year-old woman** had died in hospital, taking the incident's toll to **five**, with **68 to nearly 70 wounded** — most of them women and children per the **Hormozgan Red Crescent**. The named dead include **Amir Ali (Amir Mohammad) Karimi, aged 4**, **Mohammad Mallahi, aged 16**, a motorcyclist near the tower, **Kolsoum Mollahi, 43**, and **Zarkhatoun Taheri**. The **Iranian Red Crescent** wrote to the **International Criminal Court** on **September 2** calling for *“an independent, impartial, thorough, and effective investigation,”* citing the **civilian character** of the site. **Vice President Vance** moved in a single day from *“I'm extremely skeptical of this”* on Wednesday to *“We're investigating it because obviously we care. We want to know”* on Thursday. CENTCOM's **Capt. Tim Hawkins** had earlier said the reports *“originated from Iranian state media”* and that *“the U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.”* **What the open-source evidence can establish — that an American munition struck the building directly — is close to settled. What it cannot establish is intent: a direct hit is equally consistent with a targeting error, a mis-registered aimpoint, an intelligence failure about who was inside, a fuzing or ballistic failure on a strike aimed at the tower, and a deliberate strike. Every document that would adjudicate between those is classified.**

**The American casualty record moved, and an official who had misstated it apologised.** The Pentagon's wounded figure rose to **767**, from **758** on August 28 — **nine added with no single incident publicly attached and no CENTCOM casualty release**, which is most consistent with delayed database entry rather than a new engagement, and this briefing says so rather than inferring an event. Independent tallies continue to put the true wounded figure **above 900** against the official **757-767** range. **Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick apologised** for having stated that no Americans died in the Iran war, saying he had meant the **Venezuela** operation; the President had already corrected the record at **18 killed**. Standing caveats hold: the Pentagon **reclassified four deaths and 207 wounded** out of the official Iran-war totals in July, and the **Secretary of Defense Orders Book came off SIPRNet on September 2** — both the numerator and the reporting channel have been altered during the war they measure.

**Iran did not fire a third night.** After two consecutive nights of missiles and drones against **Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, the UAE and Erbil**, no Iranian launches were reported through the cutoff. A **US official** said the **September 3** strikes *“didn't impact any military facilities in the Middle East where U.S. forces are based, including in Kuwait.”* **ISW** records that operation as conducted by the **Iranian Artesh** — the conventional military rather than the IRGC — claiming hits on **satellite communications systems, equipment warehouses and fighter aircraft hangars** at **Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base** and **troop positions and radar installations** at **Al Minhad**. No host government reported casualties or damage. **ISW-CTP separately assessed that the roughly 50% failure rate of Iranian ballistic missiles fired at Jordan in recent days may reflect degraded longer-range missile capabilities.** The blockade ledger was unchanged at **87 vessels redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded** for *“total compliance.”*

**The diplomatic price was restated and it is still maritime and nuclear, not territorial.** Secretary **Rubio** told Fox News that *“at the core issue here is that they're never going to have a nuclear weapon. As long as they continue to endeavor, or claim to want one, they're going to pay a price for it,”* describing the price as **“primarily economic”** while reserving military force, and said Iranian forces have **lost control** of the strategic waterway. **Vance's** condition is unchanged: *“We're not talking to them... unless they stop shooting at commercial shipping,”* adding that *“the United States is the only country with the capability to ensure that those oil and gas ships get to market.”*

**The ground that changed hands this cycle changed hands in Lebanon.** Defence Minister **Israel Katz** announced on Friday that the IDF's **36th Division** had taken **“operational control”** of the **Ali al-Taher ridge** — a roughly **600-metre** feature north of the **Litani** commanding south-eastern Lebanon — **above and below ground**, after clearing a subterranean complex the IDF says was built over about **two decades with Iranian planning and funding** and served as the headquarters of **Hezbollah's Badr Unit**, its main formation in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah operatives were killed or fled; the group did not immediately comment. **Iran had reportedly warned Washington that the loss of this position would trigger a large-scale attack on Israel. Through the cutoff there was no such attack, and Israel was not among Iran's named targets for a fourth consecutive cycle.** Israel released **five Lebanese detainees** with no militant links through the Red Cross; **35 Lebanese remain in Israeli custody, including 20 civilians.** **This briefing logs the seizure for contrast rather than as a US ground indicator: the coalition prosecuting this war demonstrated on September 4 that it retains both the capability and the will to take and hold terrain from an Iranian-built position — roughly 900 kilometres from Iran, with no American formation involved.**

**Market and cost.** Brent **$95.83** at the straits.live board's **04 September 2026 2301Z** timestamp, **up 0.16%** over 24 hours and roughly **33%** above the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline, with WTI in an unchanged **$88.10-$97.36** band; *Trading Economics* recorded a **$95.23** close, **down 0.31%** — the two series bracketing a flat session. **Six transits** against an **85/day** pre-crisis baseline (**7% of normal**); the Strait recorded as **closed to commercial shipping**; **war-risk insurance at 40.0× pre-crisis**. Reopening probabilities: **September 15 <1%; September 30 2%; December 31 27%, down from 28%; January 1, 2027 22%.** Crisis Pressure Index **91/100** (Extreme, unchanged); Escalation Forecast **52/100** (Elevated, −1). US retail gasoline **$4.14/gal**, nearly a dollar above a year earlier. **The cycle's most consequential price-relevant statement was not a trade but a commercial judgement: Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, the world's largest tanker operator, withdrew its resumption timeline entirely — CEO Jotaro Tamura, *“Given the current situation, it's difficult to see operations resuming in any form by the end of the year”* — having previously assumed phased resumption from October and normal operations from January, and it will not return without guarantees and evidence of sustainably safe passage. The party bearing the hull risk is now more pessimistic than the prediction markets.**

**Kharg, unchanged, and now corroborated from the demand side.** *Kpler* puts **Iranian loadings at 251,000 bpd in August 2026** against **1.98m bpd in February**, with **stocks at Kharg down 550,000 barrels to 19.45 million** against roughly **30 million barrels** of capacity; **Kharg handles about 94% of Iranian crude exports** and loading operations halted **July 31**. New this cycle from the buyer's books: preliminary *Kpler* figures put **Chinese imports of Iranian crude at ~534,000 bpd in August**, down from **~823,000 bpd in July** against a **1.4m bpd** average last year, with **September and October offers collapsed** and **Shandong teapots** substituting **Russian Urals and fuel oil** because **ESPO sold out weeks ago**. **The loading terminal and the principal buyer now tell the same story, and the entire collapse has been achieved with no American on the island and no strike on its oil infrastructure at any point in the war.** Kharg was neither struck nor approached this cycle.

**Inside Iran.** Central bank governor **Abdol-Nasser Hemmati** said on **September 1** that Iran has accumulated **$18 billion** and is injecting **$2 billion** to stabilise the currency. **Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei** has warned President **Pezeshkian** against eroding **“public solidarity”** after Pezeshkian said on **August 28** that negotiation is the best way out of the economic crisis. Iran's Foreign Ministry continues to allege that American strikes have hit **“schools, hospitals, residential neighbourhoods.”**

**What did not happen on Day 191:** no American ground operation inside Iran; no landing; no raid; no seizure of Iranian territory; no special-operations action reported anywhere in Iran; no new US strike wave; no third night of Iranian launches; no change to the blockade ledger; no approach to Kharg; no amphibious sailing order; no draft, call-up, Presidential Reserve Call-up or IRR activation; and no Iranian large-scale attack on Israel following the Ali al-Taher seizure.
