## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — SEPTEMBER 3-4 (DAY 190): BOTH GOVERNMENTS PROSECUTING THIS WAR NAMED THE FALL OF THE IRANIAN STATE AS THE OBJECTIVE ON THE SAME DAY, AND THE PENTAGON ANSWERED THE GROUND QUESTION IN WRITING WITH A LONGER OCCUPATION OF THE SAME POSITIONS. NETANYAHU CALLED TOPPLING THE REGIME ISRAEL'S “CENTRAL MISSION” AND “WITHIN REACH”; TRUMP REVERSED HIS JUNE DISAVOWAL TO ASK WHEN IRANIANS WOULD “RISE UP AND FIGHT” AND DECLINED TO SAY WHETHER THE CIA IS ARMING THEM. HEGSETH EXTENDED DEPLOYMENTS INTO 2027 WHILE HOLDING THE FORCE AT 50,000 “TO GIVE THE PRESIDENT FLEXIBILITY.” THE ORDERS BOOK CAME OFF SIPRNET. THE ONLY RUNG THAT CLIMBED WAS MARITIME BOARDING.

**The declared objective rose on both sides of the alliance, in public, on the same day.** At a Rosh Hashanah toast with the **IDF General Staff Forum** in Tel Aviv, Prime Minister **Benjamin Netanyahu** said that toppling the Iranian government is Israel's **“central mission”** and that the goal is **“within reach.”** His words: *“The regime is now faltering. It is weaker than ever. It is fighting for its survival”*; *“I am confident in our ability to remove this threat once and for all – in other words, to topple this regime.”* Israeli outlets reported it as the formalisation of a war aim previously left implicit — *“Netanyahu makes it official: Toppling Iran's regime is now a war aim.”*

**Washington returned to the same theme after disowning it three months ago.** President **Trump** posted: **“When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?”** and, separately, **“I'm not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table. I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing.”** Asked whether the CIA is supporting Iranian dissidents, he said: *“I'd love to tell you that, but it wouldn't be appropriate to say.”* He launched the war in **late February** telling Iranians *“this will be probably your only chance for generations,”* then said in **June** that he **“never cared about regime change,”** that he was negotiating with **“very rational people,”** and that American attempts to oust foreign governments **“never work.”** He also said of the September 1-2 wave: **“It was a very heavy attack last night and we're prepared to do another one any time we want.”**

**The intelligence community's own assessment runs against the method.** US assessments reported this cycle continue to judge **regime protests unlikely** despite conditions described as dire — inflation at **87.9%** in July, a rial near **2.02 million to the dollar**, food prices rising weekly, and President **Pezeshkian** acknowledging a **“full-scale economic, military, and security war”** with exports and imports down **25-35%** — citing the severity of the crackdown earlier in 2026, described as one of the worst in the Islamic Republic's history.

**The price of talks was set, and it is neither nuclear nor territorial.** Vice President **JD Vance** said Washington will resume negotiations with Tehran only when it stops **“shooting at commercial shipping”** in the Strait of Hormuz, adding: *“My advice to the Iranians is stop acting like crazy people.”* He tied the war's duration to Iranian compliance with freedom of navigation and claimed **15 million barrels** left the Strait overnight. There are no talks; Secretary **Rubio** foreclosed the June memorandum the day before — *“that ship, in many ways, has sailed”* — and Special Envoy **Steve Witkoff** met UAE National Security Adviser **Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed al Nahyan** on **Sardinia**, unannounced, to discuss next steps. **Rubio** separately downplayed reports of Russian assistance to Iran, saying **“nothing”** has impeded US objectives.

**And the Pentagon put its intention on paper: duration, not depth.** The *Wall Street Journal* reports that Secretary of Defense **Pete Hegseth** is extending troop-deployment timelines across the Middle East **into 2027**, and has decided the US military will maintain a **“presence of 50,000 troops in the region in part to give the president flexibility on next steps.”** Roughly **50,000 troops and 19 warships, including two aircraft carriers**, are assigned to missions ranging from shooting down Iranian missiles to enforcing the blockade and guarding commercial shipping. The Pentagon **“could also keep elements of the Army's 82nd Airborne Division in the Middle East well into 2027,”** per a letter military leaders sent to families, and **standard Army air-defence tours have grown from nine months to twelve**. Hegseth is reported to back **“periodic”** bombing campaigns to keep the shipping lanes open. **Read against the tracked prediction this is the strongest documentary evidence yet recorded for the ground negative: a force being readied for a ground campaign is enlarged and refreshed; this one is capped and stretched, with no new brigades, no new amphibious lift, no mobilisation and no objective on Iranian soil named anywhere in the reporting.**

**The written military objection to going further was removed from the network rather than answered.** *The Washington Post* reported on **September 2** that the Pentagon removed **decades of classified documents associated with the Secretary of Defense Orders Book** from **SIPRNet**, the secret network used by defence officials and deployed troops. The SDOB details **“the location and availability of U.S. warships, military units, weapons systems, and other resources,”** and it carries the **“non-concurring”** process through which top generals and admirals formally register disagreement with orders from the President and the Secretary while complying with them. The removal followed the Post's reporting that military leaders had warned Hegseth in the **August 14 edition** that **“a prolonged, large-scale conflict against Iran is unsustainable”** and that such operations risked readiness against other threats. Pentagon spokesman **Sean Parnell** declined to discuss it — *“The Department of War does not publicly discuss internal operational deliberative processes”* — and did not deny that it happened; it is unclear whether the material was moved to a more restricted system. **This briefing declares its own interest: the SDOB and its four recorded four-star non-concurs — CNO Adm. Daryl Caudle, INDOPACOM's Adm. Samuel Paparo, EUCOM's Gen. Alexus Grynkewich and SOUTHCOM — have been cited in every cycle since August 14 as the best open-source evidence that the 50,000-troop level is being held rather than raised. That window is now shut. The professional military's judgement stands unreversed, but it stands concealed, and the confidence behind future ground-rung findings is discounted accordingly.**

**Escalation is not abandoned but dated, and one stated reason is inventory.** *Reuters* reported that senior aides to the President have pushed to prevent the war from escalating ahead of **November's midterms** to curb Republican losses; that the administration has focused meanwhile on tightening economic pressure to extract the concessions **“months of military action have failed to secure”**; that White House officials **will consider ramping up military action after the November 3 vote**, speaking on condition of anonymity, though a return to full-scale conflict **“remains far from certain”**; and that a tactical pause would also **“give the US military some breathing room to replenish its depleted ammunition stockpiles.”** A *Reuters/Ipsos* poll from late August found **31% of Americans support the war** while roughly **63% oppose it**, with voters notably unhappy about high gas prices. **Trita Parsi** of the Quincy Institute characterised the approach as **“maintaining a low-level conflict until the midterms.”**

**The only rung that actually climbed was maritime boarding.** US Central Command reported on **September 3** that it has **redirected 87 vessels** in the Strait of Hormuz — up from **83** — **disabled three ships** and **boarded another two** to ensure **“total compliance”** with the blockade. **Boarding is the closest thing to a ground action the United States has taken in this war: armed American personnel physically on a deck, against the will of the master. It has happened twice in 190 days, on merchant hulls, in international water. That is the ceiling of American physical intrusion to date.**

**The first independent assessment of what the strikes achieved was published, and it credits air and sea power alone.** The **Institute for the Study of War** judged that Iran's ability to **surveil the Strait of Hormuz** and to **lay mines** in it has likely been **significantly degraded** by US attacks. Its evidence is the IRGC's own workarounds: Iran has attempted to use **shore-based rocket launchers** instead of fast-attack craft to deploy mines, and has used **fast-attack craft to physically identify vessels** because it has **only a few functioning radars** capable of covering the southern route. ISW counted approximately **40 vessels** carrying millions of barrels transiting on **September 1**, reading the rise as evidence that Iran is having difficulty preventing commercial use of the southern route. **Every capability being degraded is being degraded without occupying ground.**

**The Iranian casualty figure for the September 1-2 wave became official, and the geography reached Kermanshah.** Iran's **Health Minister** put the toll at **18 killed and 108 wounded**. *Reuters* reported that the count of **Iranian military personnel** killed by US strikes that week rose to **13**. The documented breakdown: at **Kuhestak** in **Sirik district, Hormozgan** — the wedding — **4 dead, two women and two children**, and **more than 60 wounded**, per the **Iranian Red Crescent Society**, the toll settling back to four after Tuesday's deputy-governor figure of five including a child and 68 wounded; on **Qeshm Island**, at least **3 members of the Basij**; in **Khuzestan Province**, **7 killed**; and in **Kermanshah Province**, **4 Iranian military personnel**. **Kermanshah is in western Iran on the Iraqi border, roughly 1,200 km from the Strait of Hormuz and further from the waterway than any target logged in this phase.** Foreign Ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baqaei** accused the United States of a **war crime**; CENTCOM's **Capt. Tim Hawkins** said the military was **“looking into reports about the strike.”** No battle damage assessment and no American acknowledgement of civilian deaths has been published.

**A target-count discrepancy is logged and not resolved.** *Axios* put the September 1-2 wave at **approximately 100 targets**. *CNN*, citing two US officials, put it at **nearly 60 military targets** struck around the Strait, alongside **40 commercial vessels escorted and 18 million barrels protected**, with most escorted ships running with **transponders off**. CENTCOM has published categories but no count. Both figures are carried.

**Iran answered for a second consecutive night, across four countries, and hit nothing.** Drones at **Kuwait** and **Bahrain**; missiles and drones at **Jordan**; and, claimed by the IRGC on Wednesday morning, drones and missiles against US bases at **Erbil** in Iraq's Kurdistan region. Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain all reported interceptions. One Iranian drone struck a **residential complex**, sparking a fire and causing damage with **no casualties**. Kuwait's Ministry of Defence characterised the attack as **“blatant Iranian aggression”**; its army said it had repelled **“heinous”** missile and drone attacks. **No American casualties anywhere, and no Gulf state fired into Iran.**

**Tehran's own instrument is now administrative.** Iran's **Persian Gulf Strait Authority** blacklisted **11 more vessels** for **“non-compliance”** with its Hormuz transit protocols, bringing the list to **56** — a week after it listed **45**. Blacklisted ships face **restricted future passage, fines, detention or confiscation**, and any vessel **cooperating with a listed ship** may itself be added. At least **three Indian refiners and one global energy major** plan to stop using listed vessels. **Iran is regulating a waterway it can no longer patrol.**

**And Oman refused the one structure Iran has been trying to build.** A senior regional official told the *New York Post* that Muscat has quietly rejected Iran's proposal for **jointly charged Hormuz transit fees** — refusing even the voluntary version framed as security and environmental services — to avoid a quarrel with President Trump, who threatened on **August 17** to *“bomb the hell out of”* the sultanate if it obstructed a resolution. Foreign Minister **Sayyid Badr** has called transit fees **“internationally prohibited,”** while leaving open discussion of voluntary maritime services with companies; Oman told the United Nations in **July** that it opposes transit fees. **The IRGC had claimed a deal was reached. There is no deal.**

**Market and cost.** Brent **$95.87** at the straits.live board's **03 September 2026 2257Z** timestamp, **up 0.60%** over 24 hours and **33.2%** above the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline, with WTI in an **$88.10-$97.36** band; AAA gasoline **$4.17/gal** against a projected **$4.80** on a full closure. Reopening probabilities: **September 15 1%**, **September 30 2%** (from 3%), **December 31 28%** (from 26%), **July 1 2027 57%** (from 55%). Crisis Pressure Index **91/100** (Extreme, −1); Escalation Forecast **53/100** (Elevated, +1). **David Osler**, law and marine insurance editor at *Lloyd's List*, published the cycle's most transferable figure: **“There have been around $2 billion in war risk claims since the outbreak of the fighting in the Middle East, with over 70 claims to date,”** against **more than 72 attacks on ships since March** — the **second-largest marine underwriting loss in over a decade**, behind only the 2024 Baltimore bridge collapse — with hull war-risk rates as high as **10% of a ship's value** per transit, and **“roughly $7 or $8 on the price of a barrel of crude is now down to war-risk insurance alone.”** **Against a ~$24 premium over the pre-crisis baseline, about a third of the war premium in the oil price is an insurance artefact rather than a physical shortage — the clearest mechanical explanation yet published for why a seven-month blockade of a chokepoint carrying a fifth of the world's oil has not produced $150 crude.**

**Kharg, unchanged and still draining.** *Kpler* puts **Iranian loadings at 251,000 bpd in August 2026** with **oil stocks held at Kharg falling 550,000 barrels to 19.45 million**; **Kharg handles 94% of Iran's crude exports**. Operations there halted on **July 31**. **The island has never been landed on, and its oil infrastructure has never been struck.**

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — SEPTEMBER 2-3 (DAY 189): THE WAVE WAS ~100 TARGETS, NOT FIVE LOCATIONS, AND IT CARRIED A NAMED NEW DOCTRINE. UNDER A “TANKER FOR TANKER” POLICY APPROVED BY THE PRESIDENT, US DRONES PUT MISSILES INTO THE ENGINE ROOMS OF TWO IRANIAN GOVERNMENT TANKERS AT ANCHOR NORTH OF THE BLOCKADE LINE — THE FIRST AMERICAN STRIKE ON IRANIAN TANKERS FRAMED AS RETALIATION RATHER THAN ENFORCEMENT, CHOSEN WITH A MARINE EXPEDITIONARY UNIT IN RANGE. THE GEOGRAPHY WIDENED INLAND TO ASALUYEH AND KHUZESTAN. THE IRANIAN DEATH TOLL ROSE FROM TWO TO AT LEAST EIGHTEEN AND FOUR OF THE KUHESTAK DEAD WERE NAMED WITH AGES. SAUDI ARABIA BROKE SIX MONTHS OF SILENCE TO CONDEMN “IRAN'S TARGETING OF THE SAUDI TANKER (SIDR)” AND DISCLOSED TWO DEAD FILIPINO SEAFARERS. RUBIO FORECLOSED THE JUNE MEMORANDUM. AND THIS BRIEFING OWES A CORRECTION ON THE AMPHIBIOUS ORDER OF BATTLE.

**The scale was an order of magnitude larger than first reported.** *Axios* reports that **around 100 targets** were attacked in Tuesday's strikes. The categories US Central Command published — *“air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites”* — are supplemented in the same reporting by **anti-ship cruise missile launchers** and **attack drone launchers**. CENTCOM subsequently issued a release titled *“CENTCOM Completes Strikes on IRGC Targets in Iran.”* **The count changes the magnitude of the wave and not the character of the target set: every category remains a sensor, an emitter, a launcher or a node, and not one is terrain that must be occupied to be denied.**

**The doctrine has a name, an author and an instrument.** The United States struck **two Iranian government tankers** under what *Axios* reports is a new **“tanker for tanker” policy approved by President Trump**, designed to deter Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait. **US drones launched missiles into the tankers' engine rooms.** The vessels were **at anchor off Iran's coast, north of the US naval blockade line**. This is the **first time the US military has struck Iranian tankers in retaliation for Iranian attacks on ships**, as distinct from striking or interdicting them to prevent a blockade violation. **The mechanism is a mobility kill delivered from the air, and it is symmetrical by design: a hull for a hull.**

**The stated objective is a duration, not a place.** A US official told *Axios* that the strikes degraded Iran's attack capabilities in the Strait and **“bought at least a month”** of lowered threat levels for commercial ships. **That is the plainest articulation of American war aims in this phase yet placed on the record, and nothing in it is territorial.** A campaign that measures its output in weeks of deferred threat is a campaign that expects the threat to regenerate and expects to strike it again.

**The geography widened, and it widened inland.** Iranian media and *Al Jazeera*'s reconstruction place impacts at **Konarak**, **Bandar Abbas**, **Jask**, **Qeshm Island**, **Sirik**, **Chabahar**, **Asaluyeh** — the **South Pars gas complex** on the northern Gulf coast, roughly **500km north-west of the Strait** — and in **Khuzestan province** near **Ahvaz** and **Aghajari**, Iran's principal onshore oil-producing region, where **7 were killed and 8 injured**. **Asaluyeh and Khuzestan are not Strait littoral.** They are Iran's gas and oil heartland, and they were struck **five weeks after the President cancelled the multi-day energy-infrastructure campaign by name on August 1**. **CENTCOM has named only military target categories and no installation at either location; Iran has published no production or export loss.** This briefing logs the geography as documented and the reading as contested, and does not upgrade the corpus's Iran energy-strike predictions on a target-city list alone.

**The civilian toll rose by an order of magnitude and acquired names.** *Al Jazeera*'s explainer puts **at least 18 killed in Iran** across the wave. At **Kuhestak** in Sirik district, Hormozgan, where a house hosting a wedding was hit, the **Hormozgan governor's office** identified four of the dead: **Amir Ali Karimi**, aged **4**; **Mohammad Malahi**, aged **16**; **Kolsoum Malahi**, aged **43**; and **Zarkhatoun Taheri**, aged **43**. **More than 60 were wounded**, some seriously; the **Iranian Red Crescent** reported **4 dead and 67 injured**; other Iranian accounts give **5 dead including a child and 63 wounded**. In **Khuzestan**, near **Ahvaz and Aghajari**, **7 were killed and 8 injured**. **This briefing carried two dead and at least twenty wounded on the deputy governor's account yesterday; the figure of record moves to at least 18 killed.**

**CENTCOM answered without conceding.** Spokesman **Capt. Tim Hawkins** said the command was aware of reports of civilian casualties that *“originated from Iranian state media,”* that the reports were being reviewed, and that **“The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.”** Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baqaei** called Kuhestak part of a *“catalogue of atrocities.”* **No CENTCOM battle damage assessment and no acknowledgement of civilian deaths has been published.**

**Saudi Arabia broke six months of silence, and it broke it to name Iran.** The **Saudi Foreign Ministry** condemned **“Iran's targeting of the Saudi tanker (Sidr) while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz”** and disclosed that **two Filipino seafarers were killed** aboard the Bahri-operated VLCC. **Bahri** extended *“its deepest condolences and sincere sympathies to the families, relatives, and colleagues.”* Riyadh **also condemned the Iranian attacks on Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait** and stressed the need to halt escalation and protect international navigation. **For six months this briefing has recorded Saudi silence as a structural fact — no statement on American strikes, none on Iranian ones, none on the blockade. That silence is now broken, and it was broken against Tehran.** **Every account published on September 1 — Marisks, Kpler, UKMTO, Bloomberg, the *Korea Herald* and this briefing — reported all crew safe. That record is superseded.**

**Three more states condemned, and one of them was the state Iran had just struck.** **Qatar**: *“freedom of navigation through the vital waterway is an established principle that cannot be compromised,”* explicitly **rejecting use of the Strait as a bargaining chip** — a direct repudiation of the IRGC's permissioning-and-tolls regime. **Kuwait**: *“an immediate halt to all escalatory actions and compliance with international law.”* **Jordan**: *“a blatant violation of international law and a threat to the security and safety of maritime navigation.”* **Three days after the Supreme Leader asked Gulf rulers to “identify your real enemy” and build mutual defence with Iran, four Arab states condemned Iran and none condemned the American strikes.**

**Tehran answered — and its answer is not a denial.** The IRGC's account is that **two oil tankers struck sea mines** and were disabled while transiting what Iran calls an **“unauthorised”** or **“illegal route”**; that the **crews were evacuated with the assistance of US personnel**; that Iran had warned about the mined passage; and that shipping companies using unapproved routes face **“double punishments.”** Iran has **not responded directly to the Saudi allegation**. **This is an assertion of Iranian causation — Iranian mines, laid and announced by Iran — coupled with a denial of Iranian targeting.**

**And the United States contradicted Iran on the mechanism, in categorical terms.** US Central Command called the IRGC mine claim *“yet another IRGC attempt to intimidate regional commercial shipping through disinformation”* and stated: **“This is FALSE. No ships have hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz.”** The **UK Maritime Trade Operations** centre did not corroborate the Iranian claim. **Two of these three statements cannot both be true, and the decisive evidence — a hull survey distinguishing an above-waterline projectile strike from a below-waterline mine strike — is held by the operators and their war-risk underwriters in an active claims process.** This briefing notes that the mine account, if true, would falsify a **second** American declaration that the lanes were clear, which gives Washington a motive of its own for the categorical denial. Logged as an open question, updated rather than retired.

**The diplomatic track was closed from Washington.** Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** ruled out reviving the June memorandum of understanding: **“that ship, in many ways, has sailed.”** He said the object now is to prevent an Iranian nuclear weapon through economic pressure while reserving the right to military action. **This is the first explicit American foreclosure of the June deal, and it lands twenty-four hours after President Pezeshkian offered immediate reciprocity for an American return to it.**

**The President spoke in three registers.** On duration: the campaign would not last *“too much longer”* — *“As soon as it's over, which I don't think will be very much longer”* — with no timeline offered, and he said electoral considerations were not influencing his Iran decisions. On threat: Iran would be *“totally wiped out”* if it retaliated further, and the United States stands ready to strike *“at any time.”* On the waterway: he floated renaming the **Strait of Hormuz** the **“Trump Strait,”** claiming American control of it and joking it would be hotter than ever.

**Iran said the operation continues.** Khatam al-Anbiya spokesman **Ebrahim Zolfaghari** said the military operation against the United States will continue *“as a lesson to the Americans until they regret their crime,”* and warned that **any country in the region that cooperates with Washington would face the consequences**. The IRGC framed the strikes on **Camp Titin** and **Sheikh Isa** as retaliation for **Kuhestak** and as an exercise of the *“inherent right of legitimate self-defense.”* Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** said Iran's armed forces have *“unforgettable lessons”* prepared for Washington. The full Iranian retaliatory target set as documented this cycle: **Camp Titin** and **Prince Hassan Air Base** in Jordan (the latter against hangars housing **RQ-4** and **MQ-9** airframes); **Sheikh Isa Air Base** in Bahrain; **Ali Al Salem Air Base** in Kuwait — **newly named**; and US facilities in **Erbil** province, Iraq. **Jordan intercepted 10 of 13 ballistic missiles with three falling in remote areas and no casualties; Kuwait reported interceptions with no casualties; no confirmed American casualties anywhere.**

**The market did not move.** The **straits.live** board carried **Brent at $95.32** at its **02 September 2026 2305Z** timestamp, **+0.06%** over twenty-four hours and **+32.4%** above the ~**$72** pre-crisis baseline, after a **4.99%** session the day before. The **AAA national average** was **$4.1203/gal**. **A ~100-target strike wave, an inland widening, a new maritime doctrine, the first Saudi attribution of the war and the closure of the diplomatic track produced six basis points of crude repricing.** The probability structure split: the **December 31** reopening probability **fell from 28% to 26%** while the **July 1, 2027** probability **rose from 53% to 55%** — the near term worse, the far term marginally better, which is a market pricing a long war with a negotiated end rather than a short war with a military one.

**The shipping picture, and a throughput dispute that is unusually resolvable.** Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** told CNBC that **more than 17 million barrels** of oil transited Hormuz on **Monday August 31** — a war-high — and that with the Saudi and Emirati bypass pipelines included, regional exports **exceeded pre-war levels**. **TankerTrackers.com** co-founder **Samir Madani** called this **“mathemagics,”** saying it aggregated **multi-day ship-to-ship transfers into a single day's count**, and put the August 31 figure at **~9.14 million barrels** out of the Arabian Sea including the bypass, against a **7-day average of 8.27m**, a **28-day average of 6.85m**, and a **pre-war baseline of ~15 million barrels through Hormuz alone** (~20m with products). **Volumes then fell to an estimated 6.81 million on September 1 and 4.63 million on September 2** as hostilities resumed. **Kpler** assesses Middle East exports at approximately **65-70% of pre-war** by late August. The board's own figures: **6 transits** on the most recent completed day against a typical **85 per day** — **7% of the pre-crisis baseline**; **111** vessels actively transiting; **469 hulls** holding position away from berth; **74 tankers went AIS-dark in twenty-four hours**; **2,399** vessels flagged high-risk; **war-risk insurance at 40.0× pre-crisis rates**, roughly **$10 million per VLCC transit**; **Crisis Pressure Index 92/100 (Extreme)**.

**The financial campaign widened.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent**, at the **G20 finance ministers' meetings**: **“We are going to economically asphyxiate this regime,”** with **weekly new secondary sanctions** beginning with **Iranian banks** and extending to **airline leasing companies** and anyone doing business with the **IRGC** — *“we know where in the British Virgin Islands your accounts are at these trust companies, we know the $100 million houses you have around the world, and we are going to freeze those.”* The campaign is named **“Operation Economic Outcast.”** **Several G20 members raised concerns about market disruption.**

**The ground rung did not move for a 189th day — and this briefing owes a correction on the force that would have to move it.** For months this briefing has recorded the **31st Marine Expeditionary Unit** and the **Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group** as present in the theatre and within a day's steaming of the Strait, and has used their repeated non-employment as evidence. **That has not been true since July.** *USNI News* reported on **July 22, 2026** that **USS Tripoli (LHA-7) wrapped a six-month Indo-Pacific and Middle East patrol**, and the **USNI Fleet and Marine Tracker for August 31, 2026** places her **in port at Sasebo, Japan**. The 31st MEU is the forward-deployed Okinawa unit and returned with her. **The amphibious force actually in the Arabian Sea is the Boxer Amphibious Ready Group** — **USS Boxer (LHD-4)**, **USS Comstock (LSD-45)** and **USS Portland (LPD-27)** — with the **11th Marine Expeditionary Unit** and its ground combat element **Battalion Landing Team 3/5**, which sailed from San Diego on **March 20, 2026** about three weeks early and arrived in CENTCOM on **June 30, 2026**; approximately **2,200-2,500 Marines**, ~4,000 Marines and sailors ARG-wide. **One ready group, not two. One MEU, not two.**

**The correction makes the finding stronger, and this briefing states that against its own prior argument.** A force preparing an amphibious operation does not send half its amphibious lift back to home port in the sixth month of the campaign and decline to replace it. **The United States reduced its amphibious presence in this theatre in July and has not restored it.** On the day it ran a hundred-target wave across four provinces, the single MEU in range was not employed; and presented with Iranian attacks on shipping, it chose **a missile in an engine room over a boarding party**.

**The Army side degraded again, and it is now the strongest sustained capacity signal in this record.** Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth** removed **six** — seven on some accounts — further Army officers from the list for promotion to **two-star general**, reported by *The Hill* and *NBC News*; **two of those named are Black and two are women**. This follows **four one-star blocks in August** and **four in March**. A ***New York Times*** analysis finds he has now **fired or blocked the promotions of more than 80 generals and admirals — a purge of around 10% of the military's top officers**. **Army Secretary Dan Driscoll's resignation takes effect today, September 3**, leaving the Army with **neither a Senate-confirmed civilian secretary nor a Senate-confirmed chief of staff**. Separately the President nominated **acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao** for permanent confirmation. **An army cannot generate a multi-division ground campaign while a tenth of its flag corps is being removed and both of its apexes are vacant.**

**The naval rotation is relief, not reinforcement.** **USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71)** is preparing to relieve **USS George Washington (CVN-73)** in the Arabian Sea; George Washington had itself relieved **USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72)**, which **docked in Thailand this cycle after 286 days at sea**. One carrier out, one in, one recovering from the longest deployment of its class in years — and the Pacific's dedicated carrier coverage is now absent **indefinitely rather than temporarily**, since George Washington's relief is going to the Gulf too.

**The draft rung moved in the opposite direction.** Automatic Selective Service registration for men aged 18-26 still carries a statutory **December 18, 2026** effective date under the FY2026 NDAA; the implementing rulemaking, submitted **March 30, 2026** and **withdrawn on July 23, 2026**, **has still not been re-proposed**. Newly logged this cycle: Senators **Ron Wyden**, **Rand Paul** and **Cynthia Lummis** have introduced the **Military Selective Service Repeal Act**, which would **abolish registration altogether**. **On the 189th day of this war, the only draft-adjacent bill before Congress runs against conscription, and it is bipartisan.**

**Kharg.** Not struck, not landed on, **not among the approximately 100 targets**. **Kpler** puts Iranian loadings at **251,000 bpd in August 2026** with **oil stocks held at Kharg falling 550,000 barrels to 19.45 million barrels** against roughly **30 million barrels** of storage capacity — a collapse against **1.98m bpd in February** produced **entirely by blockade, with no American on the island** and no strike on its oil infrastructure at any point in the war. On September 1 the President renewed the Kharg threat and again raised **taking control** of Iranian energy infrastructure, which air power cannot deliver, and reserved *“the biggest attack of them all.”* **That is the live counter-case and it is not dismissed.**

**A Russian technical channel into this war was documented.** A ***Financial Times*** investigation, published this cycle on leaked Russian communications, travel records and defence-patent analysis, describes a multi-year covert programme codenamed **C430L** to help Iran develop **ramjet-propelled supersonic cruise missiles**. The contract was signed with **Iran's Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics in November 2023**, arranged by state arms exporter **Rosoboronexport** in coordination with **NPO Mashinostroyenia** (US-sanctioned since 2014); Russian specialists helped Iranian engineers debug and improve an already-tested propulsion system; the programme **continued into 2026**. **There is no evidence any such missile has entered operational service.** The Kremlin, Rosoboronexport, NPO Mashinostroyenia and the Iranian government did not respond to the *FT*.

**And one domestic Iranian item.** A car struck a **pro-government gathering in Mashhad**, killing **four** people. No claim and no attribution has been published.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — SEPTEMBER 1-2 (DAY 188): THE ENFORCEMENT EXCHANGE BECAME A CAMPAIGN WAVE AND THE PUBLISHED TARGET SET CONTAINED NO TERRAIN. AT 12:00 ET ON TUESDAY SEPTEMBER 1 CENTCOM BEGAN STRIKING IRGC TARGETS AT FIVE COASTAL LOCATIONS — BANDAR ABBAS, QESHM ISLAND, SIRIK, KONARAK AND CHABAHAR — HITTING "AIR DEFENSE SITES, RADAR SYSTEMS, MARITIME ASSETS AND FACILITIES, MINE LAYING CAPABILITIES, AND COMMUNICATIONS SITES," AND SEIZING NONE OF THEM. THE STATED PREDICATE WAS TWO LADEN SUPERTANKERS STRUCK OFF KHASAB BY PROJECTILES EVERY SOURCE OF RECORD CALLS "UNKNOWN," WITH NO CLAIM OF RESPONSIBILITY. IRAN ANSWERED WITHIN HOURS ACROSS FOUR COUNTRIES, NAMED A US MARINE BASE IN JORDAN AS ITS TARGET, AND THEN NAMED BAHRAIN AND KUWAIT AS NEXT — "GIFTS ARE ON THE WAY." BRENT ROSE 4.99% IN A SESSION TO $95.29. THE FIRST DOCUMENTED CIVILIAN DEATHS OF THIS PHASE ARE IRANIAN, AT A WEDDING IN KUHESTAK, REPORTED BY THE DEPUTY GOVERNOR OF HORMOZGAN. AND THE UNITED STATES ARMY LOST ITS CIVILIAN SECRETARY TWENTY-FOUR HOURS BEFORE ALL OF IT.

**The strike has a time, a target set and a stated cause.** **US Central Command:** *"Today at 12 p.m. ET, U.S. forces began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran."* The command said the strikes followed *"recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region,"* and named the categories hit: **air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites**. Iranian state-affiliated media and local reporting placed impacts at **Bandar Abbas**, **Qeshm Island**, **Sirik**, **Konarak** and **Chabahar**, with **six to eight distinct explosions** across southern Iran. CENTCOM subsequently announced the wave *"successfully completed."* It is the largest American strike wave since **August 1** and the second inside Iran since the twenty-nine-night pause broke at Larak on **August 30**. Iranian authorities released no damage assessment in the immediate aftermath.

**The trigger was two supertankers, and nobody has claimed them.** Late on **Monday August 31**, within minutes of each other, two very large crude carriers outbound through the Strait were struck by projectiles. The **Sidr**, a Saudi-flagged VLCC operated by Saudi Arabia's **Bahri**, was hit at approximately **1952 UTC**, **16.6 nautical miles north-east of Khasab**, Oman. The **Senegal Prosperity**, a Liberian-flagged VLCC operated by South Korea's **Sinokor Group**, was hit by **three** projectiles about **17 nautical miles east of Khasab**. Each had loaded **2 million barrels of Saudi crude** at the **Juaymah** terminal the previous week; both had been **sailing dark**; **all crew were reported safe**. Shipping intelligence firms **Marisks** and **Kpler** recorded the incidents; **UKMTO** reported two separate attacks on shipping that night, one a tanker struck by three projectiles in transit and one an incident involving a tanker and military forces off Oman's coast. **No party has claimed responsibility and every account — Marisks, Kpler, UKMTO, Bloomberg, the Korea Herald — describes the projectiles as "unknown."** The United States has nonetheless made those attacks the stated predicate for a five-location strike wave inside a sovereign state. **This briefing records the attacks as documented and the attribution as asserted-but-unclaimed, and logs it as an open question** (`khasab-tanker-attacks-attribution-september-2026`). It does not treat the American assertion as established, and it does not treat the absence of published evidence as disproof.

**The President's language escalated three times in a single day.** On Truth Social: *"the United States is, as we speak, striking Iranian Targets near the Strait of Hormuz … The strikes are large and powerful, and in retaliation for the Iranians' failed attempt at adding sea mines."* Then the threat: *"If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level — but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings,"* adding that *"there will be very little left"* of the country. To Fox News he described his own targeting logic: *"They tried to rebuild their radar because they can't see anything. We waited until it was almost built and then we hit it."* And: *"If they retaliate, they'll be hit much harder. And if they do it again, they'll be no longer."* He separately **renewed the threat to Kharg Island** and again raised the prospect of the United States **taking control** of Kharg and other Iranian energy infrastructure — the live counter-indicator on the ground question, since a destroyed terminal is not a captured one.

**The first documented civilian deaths of this phase are Iranian, and the source is an Iranian official speaking on the record.** A US strike hit a **house hosting a wedding ceremony** at **Kuhestak**, in **Sirik district, Hormozgan province**. **Ahmad Nafisi**, deputy governor of Hormozgan, said **two people were killed and at least twenty wounded**; Iranian accounts include a child among the dead. There is **no US comment** on the strike and **no CENTCOM acknowledgement of civilian casualties**. Across 188 days this briefing has repeatedly recorded Iranian casualty claims that could not be checked; this one carries a named provincial official, a named village and a specific count, and is recorded on that basis.

**Iran answered within hours and it answered across four countries.** The **IRGC Aerospace Force** said it *"launched a heavy ballistic missile attack on the American Marines' barracks in Jordan,"* naming **Camp Titin** — a **US Marine base on the Gulf of Aqaba coast** in southern Jordan — and **Prince Hassan Air Base**, which hosts **RQ-4** and **MQ-9** drones. The IRGC claimed **a large number of US personnel killed** and several facilities and **attack helicopters destroyed**. **Jordan's military** said it detected **13 ballistic missiles** originating from Iran, **intercepted 10**, and that **three fell in remote areas** away from populated centres with **no casualties**; explosions were observed over **Aqaba**. **US officials reported no American casualties.** **Kuwait's** air defences engaged hostile drones, with the Kuwaiti army posting on X that *"the sounds of explosions, if heard, are the result of air defense systems intercepting the hostile attacks"* — no injuries, no damage. The **Bahrain Defence Force** said it **intercepted and destroyed several aerial attacks** from Iran; the IRGC separately claimed **kamikaze drones** against **Sheikh Isa Air Base**, which **neither Manama nor Washington confirmed**. Multiple explosions were reported near the **US consulate in Erbil**.

**And Tehran named its next two targets, three days after courting them.** Iranian military spokesman **Ebrahim Zolfaghari** said Iran *"will no longer exercise restraint regarding Bahrain and Kuwait,"* adding: *"Gifts are on the way."* That is **seventy-two hours** after the Supreme Leader's written message asked Gulf rulers to *"identify your real enemy"* and build a mutual-defence architecture with Iran against the United States. Iran's **Armed Forces General Staff** and **Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters** promised that the *"Armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran will deliver crushing and devastating blows to the vile and hostile American enemy,"* and that *"the more the US military persists in its aggression in the region, the greater and heavier the losses it will have to endure."* **This briefing has spent months tracking two Iranian tracks toward the Gulf — courtship and coercion — and asking which would dominate. The question is answered for now, and the Gulf answer was to shoot the drones down and say nothing:** no Gulf state condemned the American strikes, none announced any change to basing, and Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Oman issued no statement on the exchange at all.

**For the second time in three days the attacker's damage claims and the host states' accounts are irreconcilable, and the party with the answer is silent.** The IRGC claims US deaths and destroyed helicopters at Camp Titin; Jordan reports a near-clean intercept with no casualties; the United States — the only party that knows what happened to its own Marines, aircraft and facilities — **has published no battle damage assessment for either the August 31 or the September 1-2 Iranian operations**. Note the recurring partial concession: **Jordan's own count concedes that three of thirteen missiles reached the ground**, the second time in three days that an intercepting state has walked back a clean-intercept narrative in part. Logged as an open question (`punishment-of-the-aggressor-damage-claims-august-2026`, updated).

**The market moved more in one session than in the preceding two combined, and the shape of the move is the finding.** The **straits.live** board carried **Brent at $95.29** at its **01 September 2026 2301Z** timestamp, **+4.99%** over twenty-four hours and **+32.3%** above the ~**$72** pre-crisis baseline, with **WTI at $90.68**; **TradingEconomics** carried **$95.27, +4.60%**. The **AAA national average** reached **$4.0954 per gallon** against under **$3.00** before the war — a **~37% increase carried by American consumers in six months** — and the President met **at least ten refining and distribution executives** on September 1 after accusing refiners of gouging. **Near-dated reopening probabilities barely changed** — September 15 **1%**, September 30 **3%**, December 31 **28%** — while the **long-dated probability fell sharply, from 62% to 53% by July 1, 2027**. Markets did not price a short crisis getting worse; they priced a long crisis getting longer. **Still below the ~$120.88 wartime peak, and still far below what a sustained US ground commitment would imply.**

**The shipping picture, and a caution about one number that improved.** **472 vessels** were holding position away from berth, **down 43** from 515 in a single cycle and back inside the seven-day range of 249-997. That decline runs against the escalation and is best read as reshuffling rather than release: **114 of 325 screened tankers went AIS-dark in twenty-four hours**, and vessels that stop broadcasting stop being counted as holding — **which is precisely the behaviour both stricken supertankers exhibited before they were hit**. **151 vessels** were actively transiting (26 tankers, 49 cargo, 75 other, 1 military); **338** were flagged high-risk and **221** moderate-risk; the **war-risk premium** stands at **40.0x pre-crisis**, roughly **$10.0 million** to insure a VLCC transit. UKMTO's most recent full transit count of record remains **101 outbound and 103 inbound** in the seven days to **August 28** — roughly **29 a day** against a **130-138** baseline, about **90% below** pre-conflict.

**The diplomatic track ran in the opposite direction on the same day.** President **Pezeshkian**: *"Iran will immediately reciprocate if the United States returns to its commitments,"* and Tehran urged a return to the June memorandum. Iran's central bank governor reported sufficient foreign reserves despite sanctions. At the **SCO summit in Bishkek**, the **declaration** signed by **Xi Jinping**, **Vladimir Putin**, **Narendra Modi** and **Shehbaz Sharif** condemned *"military strikes on the territory of the Islamic Republic of Iran, which have resulted in numerous civilian casualties and significant damage to the country's economy,"* stated that such actions *"violate the principles and norms of international law and the UN Charter,"* opposed *"unilateral coercive measures"* contrary to UN and WTO rules, and upheld Iran's NPT entitlement to peaceful nuclear energy *"without discrimination."* Pezeshkian proposed an SCO development bank, an export and investment insurance union and an energy consortium. **It is a paper alignment with no material action attached.** At the **G20 in Asheville**, Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** told a fireside chat with Larry Kudlow that the Strait of Hormuz will be a *"worthless piece of water"* within **two years** as overland pipelines bypass it, and that new sanctions on **Iranian banks** could be announced *"this week and next"*, alongside preparations to sanction **global airline leasing companies**. The same reporting notes that the Saudi, Emirati, Iraqi and Turkish pipeline agreements would take **multiple years** to build. The **State Department** issued a **region-wide Middle East travel alert**.

**Vice President Vance addressed the previous cycle's fabricated Kharg video.** He said Trump was *"sending a message"* to Iran with the AI-generated post, that Trump would not *"make announcements about military actions on social media,"* and that he likes to *"switch it up on social media."* The underlying record is unchanged: a US official said no such attack took place, CENTCOM's own statement named only Larak, and NIOC chief executive **Hamid Bovard** called the post *"laughable."* **No Kharg prediction may be scored on it.**

**The ground rung did not move for a 188th day, and the published target set is the reason.** Every category CENTCOM named — air defence, radar, maritime assets, mine-laying, communications — is **a sensor, an emitter, a launcher or a node**. **Not one is a piece of ground that must be occupied to be denied.** This is a **suppression** target set, not a **shaping** target set: shaping fires for a landing concentrate on a single objective, persist over it, and are followed by movement. These dispersed across five locations in one wave, across the **exact littoral** an amphibious operation would use — Qeshm is an island inside the Strait, Bandar Abbas is the naval headquarters at its mouth, Sirik and Konarak sit on the Makran coast — with the **31st Marine Expeditionary Unit** and the **Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group** and the **11th MEU** within a day's steaming. **Nothing moved.** For 188 days this disconfirmation has been argued from absence; since August 30 it has been argued from conduct under pressure; this cycle argues it from **the striking command's own published target list**.

**The cycle's second hard ground datum is bureaucratic and cuts the same way.** On **August 31**, **Army Secretary Dan Driscoll** submitted his resignation to the White House, **effective September 3**, after months of friction with Defense Secretary **Pete Hegseth**. Driscoll — the youngest Army secretary in US history, civilian head of the service since February 2025, and a participant in the Russia-Ukraine talks — had raised concerns about Army transformation and readiness and about Hegseth firing the generals responsible for it; the immediate flashpoint reported was Hegseth removing **four officers** from a promotion list after Driscoll refused to do so. Hegseth had **already asked the Army chief of staff to step down**. Per the *Wall Street Journal*, **the United States Army now has neither a Senate-confirmed civilian secretary nor a Senate-confirmed military chief.** Ground campaigns are generated by the Army and the Marine Corps; the Army is the service that would have to source, equip, sustain and rotate a force for a country of ninety million; **its deployed brigade combat team is on a twelve-month tour because there are no replacements, its allocation is capped at 50,000 by the August 14 Orders Book over four formal four-star non-concurs, and from September 3 it has no confirmed leadership at either apex.** None of those constraints was imposed by an adversary.

**Marines are in this war, and the cycle showed where they are.** The IRGC's retaliation named **Camp Titin**, a **US Marine base on Jordan's Gulf of Aqaba coast**, as a ballistic-missile target. That is the documented disposition of American Marines in this theatre: **garrisoned ashore in a friendly Arab state and under Iranian fire — not embarked and inbound.** It is a useful corrective to any reading in which "Marines in theatre" implies an impending landing.

**The counter-case is logged plainly and is not dismissed.** Trump renewed the Kharg threat and again raised **taking control** of Iranian energy infrastructure, an outcome air power cannot deliver. He expressly reserved *"the biggest attack of them all."* Hegseth's standing position is unchanged: *"We're not gonna foreclose any option … to include boots on the ground."* A president who wants the **asset** rather than its destruction has a structural reason to reach for Marines eventually. Capability is present, intent is expressly reserved, and this briefing does not read 188 days of restraint as proof of permanent abstention. **The draft rung remains at zero:** automatic Selective Service registration carries a statutory **December 18, 2026** effective date under the pre-war NDAA, the implementing rulemaking was **withdrawn on July 23, 2026** and has not been re-proposed, automatic registration is not a draft, a draft would require an act of Congress, and no such legislation has been introduced.

**Russia-Ukraine.** Russia bombarded **Kyiv for more than twelve hours** overnight into Tuesday **September 1**, killing **at least 12** and wounding more than a dozen **including three children** — the **sixth consecutive day** of heavy strikes on the capital, reported as unprecedented in more than four and a half years of full-scale war. **Cruise and ballistic missiles, jet-powered drones, glide bombs and artillery salvos** struck Kyiv and **eight other regions**, hitting residential areas, **railway and port infrastructure** and a **Romanian border crossing**; Ukrainian officials characterise the consecutive assaults as designed to grind down civilians by disrupting daily life. **This is the campaign that was announced in advance** — the Defence Ministry's August 30 statement that forces *"have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure,"* endorsed by **Peskov** on August 31 as an appropriate response to Kyiv's *"path of escalation."* Ukraine answered on the oil axis and reached the Baltic: a drone barrage set fire to **Ust-Luga**, Russia's largest Baltic shipping terminal and second-largest nationwide, handling ~**700,000 bpd** of crude and exporting **32.9 million tonnes** of oil products in 2025; Leningrad Governor **Alexander Drozdenko** said air defences downed **52 drones** in a four-hour assault, with damage and fire in the port area, **no casualties**, and the fire out by ~**09:30** Moscow time; Ukraine's **GUR** confirmed the strike. **Second Ust-Luga strike since August 14.** **NATO spillover without NATO escalation:** a drone crossed **Latvian** airspace and continued into **Estonia**, which scrambled **Turkish F-16s** serving in NATO's **Baltic Air Policing Mission**; **Riivo Valge** said around a dozen drones moved near the border, one briefly entering south-eastern Estonia and another approaching **Narva** before retreating into Russia; Latvia issued two overnight warnings; **the fighters did not engage, warnings ended by 05:30, and no Article 4 consultation was requested** — the fourth such incident this summer to end that way. At Bishkek, **Modi** told **Putin** to end the war *"for the sake of humanity."* **Ratcliffe's** proposed **Trump-Putin-Zelensky trilateral** was accepted by Kyiv and **rejected by Moscow**; **Budanov** says US-mediated talks could resume in September; Bloomberg reports Kyiv hunting for **Patriot** interceptors. Line static at ~**81.1 km²** net 2026 Russian gains.

**Latin America, and a correction this briefing owes.** The White House named the Venezuela counterparty: **North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP)**, owned by Venezuelan businessman **Alejandro Betancourt** and already **the country's second-largest operator behind Chevron**. Acting President **Delcy Rodríguez** is granting NABEP **100-year rights over 17 oil fields** holding **65 billion barrels** of proven reserves. **The US Defense Department takes a 35% equity stake** in a joint-venture company; the **State Department takes the right to buy 20% of NABEP's output at the cost of production**, plus a **right of first refusal** on everything else. **This briefing has carried "a joint venture in which the United States government holds 55%" since August 28, and that conflated two categorically different instruments — equity is ownership, an offtake right at cost is a purchase option. The corrected record is 35% DoD equity plus a 20% State offtake right.** Reuters reports the fields were **previously operated by Chinese and Russian firms**, which makes the transaction a **displacement of Beijing and Moscow** as well as a commercial arrangement; Rodríguez says sovereignty remains secure; analysts expect legal challenges; **Chevron is separately expanding** in Venezuela. **Cuba:** state utility **UNE** forecast a peak-hour shortfall of up to **2,310 MW** for September 1, after a day whose peak reached **2,323 MW**, as the 2026-2027 school year opened; six nationwide grid collapses in 2026 stand, the most recent **August 2-3**. **Maduro's** trial before Judge **Hellerstein** remains set for **June 1, 2027**. No Colombian development.

**US-China.** Two senior Trump administration officials told Reuters that state-owned **COSCO** uses **concealed equipment** aboard its commercial vessels to collect **military communications** near the coastlines of target nations **including the United States**, describing a **decades-long collection partnership** with Beijing spanning **Europe, North America and Asia**, *"sophisticated signals intelligence collection"* platforms aimed at *"military communications technologies and encryption developments,"* and product used for **territorial-dispute leverage, maritime reconnaissance and early-warning indications of foreign military targets**. China's embassy in Washington said Beijing *"would never ask any company to collect intelligence abroad against local laws"* and called the allegations *"totally baseless."* **No sanction, no vessel designation, no port-entry restriction, no tariff and no export control followed — and Trump and Xi are still due to meet in Washington later this month.** That is the **fifth consecutive cycle of maximal American accusation and minimal American action**, matching the two Iran sanctions packages that spared China's major banks and the *"financial violence"* threat that landed on an Egyptian bank's Emirati branches. Chinese state media separately reported **solar overtaking coal** as the country's top installed power source in July.

**DPRK.** A **thirteenth consecutive day without a launch** — none since the ~**ten KN-25 short-range ballistic missiles** of **August 20**, which remain **unpublicised in North Korean domestic media**. The concession ledger is unchanged and entirely one-sided: **THAAD** off the peninsula, the **USS George Washington** moved from Japan to the Gulf leaving the Pacific without carrier coverage, **Paparo's** formal non-concur, **Ulchi Freedom Shield** cut from eleven days to five with its counteroffensive phase never conducted, and a further exercise cancelled — with **nothing returned**. The cycle's Korean datum is American: the service that mans the ~**28,500**-strong US contingent in Korea now has **no Senate-confirmed leadership at either apex**. What Pyongyang is doing instead is selling: **North Korean ballistic missiles** continue to appear in Ukraine's accounting of Russian expenditure.

**Hormuz-dependent economies.** **Both stricken supertankers carried Saudi crude and one was operated by South Korea's Sinokor — neither state a belligerent.** That is the structural fact of this campaign: the states absorbing its costs are overwhelmingly not the states fighting it. **South Korea** draws ~**70%** of its crude and **18%** of its LNG through the Strait; **Japan** takes **over 90%** of its crude from the Middle East with ~**75%** transiting Hormuz; **India** takes ~**40%** of its oil through the Strait and ~**30%** of its LNG from Qatar and the UAE; comparative supply-disruption risk scores put **Japan at 6.4**, **South Korea 5.3**, **India 4.9**. **LNG carrier rates ~$300,000/day, up ~650%**; crude tanker rates at historic highs; **Cape of Good Hope** rerouting adds **50-80%** to freight; war-risk premia at **3-10% of hull value** against **0.25%** pre-war. **Korean petrochemicals are the first heavy-industrial casualty:** **Lotte Chemical**, **LG Chem** and **Hanwha Solutions** on force-majeure notice, and **Yeochun NCC**, Korea's largest ethylene producer, declaring supply disruption. India is absorbing inflationary pressure on food and essentials through logistics costs. And the oil-exporting belligerent is **rationing fuel**: petrol queues in Tehran form from midnight, officials have signalled **quota cuts** and higher prices above allotment while denying a shortage, and **Pezeshkian** has asked the public and the government's own vehicle fleet to exercise restraint.
