## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 31-SEPTEMBER 1 (DAY 187): IRAN ANSWERED LARAK WITH A NAMED TWO-COUNTRY OPERATION AND THE UNITED STATES ANSWERED WITH A THREAT AND NO SORTIE. THE IRGC'S "PUNISHMENT OF THE AGGRESSOR" STRUCK KING HUSSEIN AND AL AZRAQ IN JORDAN AND, ON TEHRAN'S ACCOUNT, AL MINHAD IN THE UAE; ALL THREE HOSTS AND THE ATTACKER PUBLISHED IRRECONCILABLE DAMAGE ACCOUNTS AND NOBODY WAS KILLED. THE CYCLE'S HARDEST EVIDENCE IS DOCUMENTARY: THE 82nd AIRBORNE'S DEPLOYMENT EXTENDED TO A FULL YEAR — DISCLOSING A DIVISION HEADQUARTERS AND A BRIGADE COMBAT TEAM IN THEATRE SINCE MARCH, WHICH CORRECTS THIS BRIEFING — AND THE LEAKED AUGUST 14 SECRETARY OF DEFENSE ORDERS BOOK, IN WHICH FOUR FOUR-STAR COMMANDERS FORMALLY NON-CONCUR AND THE CHIEF OF NAVAL OPERATIONS TELLS THE SECRETARY OF DEFENSE THE NAVY "CANNOT SUSTAIN ITS CURRENT LEVEL OF SUPPORT."

**Iran retaliated, named the operation, and reached two countries.** Overnight into **Monday August 31** the **IRGC Aerospace Force** conducted what it described as a joint drone-and-missile operation named **"Punishment of the Aggressor"** against **King Hussein Air Base** and **Al Azraq (Azraq) Air Base** in **Jordan**, in response to the **August 30** US strike on **Larak Island**. Iran's **Ministry of Foreign Affairs** said the bases targeted *"had been used to launch and support attacks on Iran."* Separately, Iran's **army** said **dozens of drones** were launched at US military assets at **Al Minhad (Al Menhad) Air Base** in the **United Arab Emirates**, targeting sites where **US forces and helicopters** were stationed. It is the first Iranian retaliation of this phase to reach two countries and the first **named** Iranian operation since the twenty-nine-night pause.

**Three accounts of the same night, and they do not meet.** The **IRGC** claims **"heavy damage"** to *"technical infrastructure, maintenance and fighter jet site"* at both Jordanian bases and says it *"destroyed the technical and repair infrastructure."* **Jordan's military** says it **intercepted eight ballistic missiles** that entered Jordanian airspace early on August 31, before they threatened infrastructure or troops, with **no injuries** at either base; Jordanian state media had reported eight intercepted on the evening of August 30. **Two Jordanian security sources** then said on **August 31** that **some missiles were not successfully intercepted**, while maintaining that there were no casualties — a partial concession inconsistent with a clean-intercept narrative, and unattributed and unquantified. The **UAE Ministry of Defence** called reports that missiles struck **Al Menhad** **"false,"** urged reliance on **official sources** rather than rumours, and confirmed only that its air force *"intercepted a drone over the country's territorial waters, approaching from Iran."* **No party — Iran, Jordan, the UAE or the United States — reported a single casualty.** The **United States**, which owns the aircraft, helicopters and facilities at all three bases and is the only actor with a complete picture of damage to them, **issued no statement about any of the three**. The structure of the dispute is that every party to it is also the sole custodian of the evidence that would settle it, and the incentives run in opposite directions. Logged as `punishment-of-the-aggressor-damage-claims-august-2026`.

**The American answer was a threat, and the threat was not followed by a sortie.** President **Trump** told Fox News on Monday that the United States would **"hit them hard"** and **"hit them very hard."** In the same remarks he said the **Strait of Hormuz** is in **"extremely good shape,"** described Iran's economy, military and leadership as **"largely deteriorated,"** and added the conditional that is the cycle's most precise statement of American intent: **"it doesn't mean we won't smack them to see what happens."** **No confirmed US strike inside Iran was reported on August 31.** A single quiet night discriminates weakly between restraint and preparation — it is consistent with a red line enforced and re-sheathed, and consistent with targeting, deconfliction or deliberate timing inside a renewed campaign — but it is the first night after, and it went the enforcement way while the rhetoric went the other. Logged against `larak-strike-enforcement-or-campaign-resumption-august-2026`.

**CENTCOM put the enforcement frame on the record in its own name.** The command rejected the IRGC's characterisation of the Larak strike as an *"act of aggression"* as **"absolutely false,"** and stated that *"U.S. forces took **limited, precise action** against IRGC **minelaying forces** posing an **imminent threat** in the Strait of Hormuz,"* aimed at protecting civilian mariners, commercial shipping and the movement of global trade; the command noted it had completed clearing sea mines from the strait's international shipping routes the previous week. This is the first formal command-level articulation of the narrow-enforcement reading — a party's own framing, not an adjudication of it.

**The Larak toll acquired a number and two names.** Iranian state media identified casualties over August 30-31 and the toll rose from two to **three IRGC personnel killed** with **two injured**, two of the dead named as **Hamid Avazzadeh** and **Ali Fayazi**. This partly resolves the IRGC's original formulation of *"the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots"* — fighters and civilians both — without a precise toll. No independent count has been published and no Iranian government figure has been issued. **No US casualties were reported at any point in the exchange.**

**The 82nd Airborne's deployment was extended to a full year — and the unit list corrects this briefing.** On **August 30-31** the Army extended the Middle East deployment of elements of the **82nd Airborne Division** to a **full twelve months**, carrying soldiers into **2027**, announced by letter from division commander **Maj. Gen. Brandon R. Tegtmeier**: *"We do not share that lightly, and we understand that a longer tour weighs heavily on every household, including our own."* **Units named: Division Headquarters, 1st Brigade Combat Team, Combat Aviation Brigade, DIVARTY, ADSB (sustainment), 3rd Battalion 4th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 307th Division Engineer Battalion.** **Approximately 2,000 soldiers**, deployed from **Fort Bragg** in **March 2026** as part of the surge after the war began. **This briefing has carried "approximately 1,000 paratroopers" and the standing statement that "no brigade combat team, division headquarters or corps-level enabler set has been identified in theatre at any point in the war." Both statements are falsified by the published list and are corrected here.** The corrected record: approximately 2,000 soldiers, comprising a division headquarters and a brigade combat team with organic artillery, engineer, air-defence, aviation and sustainment enablers, in CENTCOM since **March 2026**. The correction is to this briefing's record and **not to the disposition** — no unit moved in this cycle. **What the extension is not:** it adds no soldiers, moves nobody forward, changes no mission and names no objective. It holds an existing force in place, and the reason is in the second document. Reporting on the extension notes that the military *"refused to rule out ground operations against Iran, although that has yet to happen,"* and restates **18 US service members killed and more than 750 wounded** since February 28.

**The Secretary of Defense Orders Book leaked, and it is the most substantial documentary evidence in the war about American capacity to escalate.** *The Washington Post* published contents of the **August 14 edition of the Secretary of Defense Orders Book (SDOB)**, the classified document produced approximately twice monthly setting out worldwide availability of US warships, aircraft, personnel and weapons systems and reflecting presidential priorities. **Four formal non-concurs** were filed against continued allocation to the Iran theatre: **Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle**; **INDO-PACIFIC COMMAND's Adm. Samuel Paparo**; **EUROPEAN COMMAND's Gen. Alexus Grynkewich**; and **SOUTHERN COMMAND**. The **Army and Air Force chiefs concurred** on resources while recording increased operational risk; Chairman **Gen. Dan Caine** is named in the document chain. **Caudle:** the Navy **"cannot sustain its current level of support"** because there is no end date to the conflict, with **barely a quarter of the destroyer fleet ready to deploy**. **Paparo** objected to the continued demand for an aircraft carrier strike group and destroyers. **EUCOM and SOUTHCOM** said the continued diversion of ships, surveillance aircraft and other assets to CENTCOM has degraded their ability to fulfil **homeland-defence** obligations. **Materiel as reported:** more than **half** of cruise missiles and advanced air-defence missiles depleted; approximately **25% of the Reaper drone fleet** lost; **THAAD redeployed from South Korea** to the Middle East; the **USS George Washington** repositioned from **Japan** to the Persian Gulf, **leaving the Pacific without carrier coverage**; a Pacific-dedicated carrier redirected to relieve a carrier deployed **more than 300 days**; Patriot and THAAD interceptor stocks under pressure; Tomahawk supplies strained; **billions of dollars in base damage** sustained. **Orders:** **50,000 US troops** and hardware to remain in the Middle East **through September** and, for some units, **into 2027**; CENTCOM to keep 50,000 **on alert** for months; Patriot units extended; multiple Air Force units into 2027. **The collective formulation as reported: "We will carry out the orders, but at a price."** Headline characterisation across outlets: the campaign has been **"too much for too long."**

**The reaction confirmed the document in the act of condemning its disclosure.** Chief Pentagon spokesman **Sean Parnell**: *"Publishing highly classified assessments from the Secretary's orders book is a crime. It's a betrayal of the force."* On the substance he did not deny it: the Secretary sees non-concurs *"constantly. That's how you run a real military."* **Rep. Gil Cisneros** on Hegseth: *"He either does not comprehend the consequences of his decisions, or he just doesn't give a damn."*

**The export ledger got a terminal-level figure and the seizure rationale weakened.** Kpler data published on **August 31** puts loadings at **Kharg Island** — the complex handling approximately **90% of Iran's crude exports** — at **135,000 barrels a day in August 2026** against **1.98 million bpd in February 2026**, a **93% collapse**. Kharg has a loading capacity of **7 million bpd**, storage of **30 million barrels**, sits roughly **30km** off the Iranian coast, and connects by pipeline to the Ahvaz, Gachsaran and Agha Jari fields with deepwater berths for VLCCs; before the conflict about **80% of its shipments went to China**. **Larak**, struck on August 30, is described as a key IRGC naval and logistics base and secondary oil storage and transfer hub, hosting fast boats, missile systems and sea-mine infrastructure, whose primary value is *"military-geographic as it overlooks the Strait of Hormuz"* — and it sits roughly **660km east of Kharg**. The Kharg figure is compatible with the ~260,000 bpd all-Iranian-ports figure and **both contradict the zero-export claim asserted by CENTCOM and, separately, by Iran's own central bank governor**. Logged against `iran-oil-exports-zero-or-loading-august-2026`.

**Shipping: the first authoritative full transit count in weeks.** **UKMTO** recorded **101 outbound and 103 inbound full transits** in the **seven days to August 28**, described vessel traffic as **"significantly reduced"** and about **90% below pre-conflict levels** despite a brief recovery in late June, and noted operators increasingly favouring a **northern route**; **tankers are 45%** of all movements. Roughly **204 transits in seven days is about 29 a day** against a pre-war baseline near **130-138** — an order of magnitude above the **PortWatch** count of **3 vessels** on August 23 that the straits.live board still carries, and far below any claim of normalisation. The two series are not reconciled by any party and this briefing logs both. **Risk is geographically concentrated:** the **southern Omani route** accounts for **16 of 18 projectile-strike incidents** reported by UKMTO since **July 6**, against **23 incidents** in total, causing bridge, engine-room and structural damage — the operational reason operators are moving north, and the northern route runs through the water Iran claims to administer.

**Price and the board.** The straits.live board carried **Brent at $90.78** at its **31 August 2026 2301Z** timestamp, **up 1.19%** over 24 hours and **26.1% above** the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline; **TradingEconomics** carried **$90.69, +2.93%** on the day, and intraday reporting recorded crude up **more than 3%**. **First close above $90 since the pause began**, and a second consecutive session of geopolitical repricing. Also on the board: **Day 184** since closure declared; war-risk insurance **40.0x** pre-crisis (~**$10.0M per VLCC**); **515 hulls** holding position away from berth, **up from 396**; **Crisis Pressure 91** (extreme); **Escalation Forecast 49** (elevated); reopening **1%** by September 1, **3%** by September 30, **28%** by December 31, **62%** by July 1, 2027; US pump price **$4.12** with **$4.72** projected if fully closed; **4 of 9** major container lines with suspended or limited Hormuz service, **41+ vessels** and **204,000+ TEU** stranded, reroute surcharges **$600-$1,200/TEU** via the Cape.

**Diplomacy moved, and not toward Washington.** At the **SCO summit in Bishkek**, with **Xi Jinping**, **Vladimir Putin** and **Narendra Modi** present, Iranian President **Masoud Pezeshkian** said: *"We continue to strive for a path of agreement and understanding, and we believe that **continuing the war is neither in our interest, nor in the interest of the region**."* It is the most explicit statement of Iranian war-weariness in this record, delivered to Delhi, Beijing and Moscow rather than to the United States, on the same day as the IRGC's retaliation. **No US-Iran negotiating round was held or scheduled**; Araghchi's standing position is that the Islamabad MOU was *"an end to the war,"* not a ceasefire, and *"cannot be extended."*

**The financial track: louder allies, unchanged targets, and a softened war aim.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** opened the **G20 finance ministers' and central bank governors' meetings in Asheville, North Carolina** on **August 31**. He said the **European Union** had backed the sanctions effort with **"fulsome support"** and **"in the strongest terms."** On effect: *"I think it could be **within weeks or months** — and **the economy doesn't have to collapse**."* That clause is a retreat from his own earlier statement that the campaign would *"collapse this regime,"* and is logged against `us-war-aim-regime-collapse-or-leverage-august-2026`. Also: *"We want the rest of the world to come along with our growth agenda"*; *"The world has this mountain of debt, and we do have to grow our way out of it"*; and readiness to exact *"financial violence if we have to."* France's **Roland Lescure** described the global economy as *"a bit like the weather in Asheville — it's unpredictable, it's foggy."* **No Chinese financial institution was designated for a third consecutive package**, and the **Associated Press** stated the mechanism explicitly: in stopping short of sanctioning the Egyptian bank itself and designating only its Emirati branches, the administration *"appeared to be signaling its **reluctance to penalize major trading partners** that do business with Iran, **including China and India**."*

**Ground rung — the extension is not a build, and the Orders Book says why.** *No landing, no lodgement, no seizure of Iranian territory or offshore infrastructure, no Kharg action, no reinforcement order, no change in the 50,000 figure, no mobilisation, no draft order — a **186th consecutive day** with every execution indicator at zero.* The two documents of this cycle are the strongest evidence yet on the question and they point the same way. The Army extended tours to twelve months because it has no replacements; four four-star commanders formally recorded that the **current** commitment already exceeds what the force can sustain; the Chief of Naval Operations — whose service would lift, escort and cover any amphibious operation — told the Secretary of Defense the Navy **cannot sustain its current level of support** with **barely a quarter of the destroyer fleet deployable**. The **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group** remains dispersed with **USS Boxer** in the **Arabian Sea**, **USS Comstock** in the **Indian Ocean** and the **11th MEU's 2,200-2,500 Marines** embarked and untasked; **USNI News** published no Fleet and Marine Tracker for August 31. **The correction cuts the other way and is recorded as such:** the ground capability in theatre is larger than this briefing had stated — a division headquarters and a brigade combat team with enablers, in place since March — and it has never been moved, reinforced or tasked. **The counter-case is held open:** the strike pause is broken, Iran has struck American basing in two countries, the President has promised to hit Iran hard, and a force told in writing that it cannot sustain an open-ended blockade has a rational incentive to force a decision before the instruments are gone. Capability is not intent, and an extension order is not a warning order.

### Russia-Ukraine — The Kremlin Endorses the Announced Campaign Against Ukraine's Power System, and the Diplomacy Happens in Bishkek (August 31, 2026)

**A ministry communique became a political commitment.** On **August 31** Kremlin spokesman **Dmitry Peskov** described the Defence Ministry's declared preparations for **massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure** as an **appropriate response** to what he termed Kyiv's **"path of escalation."** The August 30 announcement — *"have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure"* — is now endorsed at the highest level, which strengthens the warning-order reading of `russia-announced-energy-campaign-order-or-signal-august-2026` without settling it: an announcement that forfeits surprise, repeated and elevated rather than executed, is also what a deterrent signal looks like. Reporting adds a separate and more specific option: Moscow, viewing peace negotiations as **effectively deadlocked**, is **weighing stepped-up strikes with conventional ballistic missiles on Kyiv, including on the centre of the capital**. **No massive strike on the Ukrainian power system had been executed as of the close of the cycle**, and **Ukraine did not modify its behaviour** — it struck the **Kirishi refinery** in Russia's **Leningrad region**, the country's second-largest at roughly 20 million tonnes a year.

**The timing is the threat.** The announcement lands roughly **eight weeks** before the heating season, against Ukrainian air-defence stocks that are short and an interceptor supply chain competing with the Iran theatre. **Zelensky:** *"this year, winter is an obvious priority for everyone."*

**The Myla toll and the line.** The death toll from the **August 28** strike on the warehouse west of Kyiv stands at **38 killed with 4 missing**, ~50 buildings damaged and 380+ residents evacuated; the attribution dispute over what the site held is unresolved and the site is destroyed. The **Ukrainian General Staff** logged **225 combat engagements on August 31**, of which **36 in the Pokrovsk direction**; on **August 28** it logged **250 clashes** with **40** Russian attacks repelled on the **Pokrovsk** front and **35** on the **Kostiantynivka** front. **Net 2026 Russian territorial gains remain 81.1 km²** — a fifth year of war producing an area smaller than a mid-sized city.

**The diplomacy was in Bishkek and Ukraine came up "in passing."** At the **SCO summit** marking the organisation's 25th anniversary, **Putin** met **Xi Jinping**. Xi: he was *"happy"* to meet again; ties have grown **"more solid"** with **"even brighter"** prospects; *"uncertainty and unpredictability in the international order has obviously increased."* Putin: *"cooperation is successfully developing on all fronts."* To **Modi**, Putin said he was **"following the path"** toward a Ukraine resolution, without elaboration. **Peskov said the leaders "largely discussed economic relations" and addressed Ukraine only "in passing."** Also present: **Erdogan**, **Modi**, **Shehbaz Sharif**, **Pezeshkian**. **CIA Director John Ratcliffe** is reported to have visited Moscow for discussions. **No negotiating round was held or scheduled.**

**The Iran war's cost to this theatre is now documented.** The leaked **August 14 Secretary of Defense Orders Book** records **EUROPEAN COMMAND** filing a **formal non-concur** on the grounds that diversion of ships and surveillance aircraft to CENTCOM has degraded its ability to fulfil its obligations. The competition for interceptors between Kyiv's winter and the Strait of Hormuz is no longer an inference; it is recorded inside the Pentagon's own allocation process.

### Gulf States — The War Reaches Emirati Soil Again and Abu Dhabi's First Act Is to Deny It (August 31, 2026)

**The claim and the denial.** Iran's **army** said dozens of drones were launched at US military assets at **Al Minhad (Al Menhad) Air Base** early on Monday, targeting sites where **US forces and helicopters** were stationed, in retaliation for the Larak casualties. The **UAE Ministry of Defence** responded within hours: reports that missiles struck Al Menhad are **"false"**; the public should rely on **official sources** rather than rumours; the UAE air force *"intercepted a drone over the country's territorial waters, approaching from Iran."* No damage, no casualties.

**The rest of the Gulf said nothing at all.** Neither **Saudi Arabia**, **Kuwait**, **Bahrain**, **Qatar** nor **Oman** issued a statement on the August 30-31 exchange, including on a claimed Iranian attack on a fellow GCC member's territory. That silence matches the posture map the **Congressional Research Service** now publishes: the **UAE**, having faced **the most attacks of any GCC state**, has adopted a **defiant and forceful** posture toward Iran; **Saudi Arabia** calls for **de-escalation** and promotes the **Pakistan-based peace talks** while asserting its **right to self-defence**; and the remaining members say as little as possible. The CRS also records that Iranian strikes have targeted US embassies and military installations in the **UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq, Oman and Jordan**, and that the de facto closure of the Strait presents fundamental risks to the security and economic vitality of all six GCC states.

**The ledger they are being asked to overlook is unchanged and severe.** Roughly **80 Gulf energy facilities** hit by Iranian missiles and drones at an estimated **$58 billion** in damage; **World Bank** 2026 regional growth cut from **4.4% to 1.3%**; **Oxford Economics** expects some GCC economies to enter recession in the second half; **Kuwait** and **Qatar** both forecast to contract, Qatar holding the world's **third-largest proven gas deposits** and deprived of most of its LNG export route; **Saudi Arabia** and the **UAE** partly insulated by large non-oil sectors and by the **two pipelines** that bypass the waterway. **Dubai** remains the first-named target geography of the American financial campaign, with Iranian bank branches still open there.

### Other Theatres — SOUTHCOM Says It Cannot Cover Its Own Region, THAAD Leaves Korea, and China Still Does Not Take the Opening (August 31, 2026)

**US-China.** The **Associated Press** named the mechanism this briefing has logged for three packages as a gap: by designating only the **Emirati branches** of an Egyptian bank rather than the bank itself, the administration *"appeared to be signaling its **reluctance to penalize major trading partners** that do business with Iran, **including China and India**."* **Bessent** at the **G20 in Asheville** said the EU backed the campaign *"in the strongest terms"* and predicted effects *"within weeks or months — and the economy doesn't have to collapse."* **No Chinese financial institution was designated for a third consecutive package**; China buys around **90%** of Iran's oil. Beijing's standing public position is unchanged: military means, sanctions and pressure tactics *"are not the solution"* and *"will only lead to escalation that serves no one's interests."*

**Taiwan and the Pacific.** The opportunism prediction fails again, and this cycle removes the last excuse for it. The opening is now documented **from the American side**: the **August 14 Orders Book** records **INDOPACOM's Adm. Samuel Paparo** filing a formal non-concur against the continued demand for an aircraft carrier strike group and destroyers; the **USS George Washington** was repositioned from **Japan** to the Persian Gulf, **leaving the Pacific without carrier coverage**; and **THAAD** was redeployed from **South Korea**. US reconnaissance sorties in the South China Sea remain **down roughly 30%** since the war began, and Beijing has not moved. The **US-Taiwan** agreement holds at a **15%** headline tariff (~**12.3%** average with carve-outs) against approximately **$85bn** of Taiwanese purchases of US energy, aircraft and equipment; electronics, semiconductors and Section 232 goods excepted.

**DPRK.** A **twelfth consecutive day without a launch**, and the cycle's Korean datum is that **THAAD has left the peninsula**. The concessions logged since August have been verbal or exercise-related — **Ulchi Freedom Shield** cut from **eleven days to five** on presidential order hours before it began, its **counteroffensive phase never conducted**, a further exercise cancelled, and the President linking his displeasure to **Seoul's refusal to join US action against Iran**. This one is an interceptor system **physically leaving the country it was deployed to defend**, recorded in the Pentagon's own allocation document rather than announced as policy. **Pyongyang has returned nothing**: no launch since the roughly **ten KN-25** short-range ballistic missiles of **August 20**, still not publicised domestically, and no response on talks. President **Lee Jae-myung** says South Korea must brace for a **"worst-case scenario."** What Pyongyang is doing instead is **selling**: Zelensky's weekly accounting of Russian expenditure — nearly **2,000 strike drones**, more than **1,600 aerial bombs** and **31 missiles** — **included North Korean ballistic missiles**.

**Latin America.** A **fifth consecutive quiet cycle**, and the only new datum came from Washington. The **August 14 Orders Book** records **US SOUTHERN COMMAND** among the four formal non-concurs, stating that continued diversion of ships and surveillance aircraft to CENTCOM has **degraded its ability to fulfil homeland-defence obligations** — the command that conducted the **January 3** operation capturing **Nicolás Maduro** and **Cilia Flores** is now formally on record that it cannot cover its own area of responsibility. **No seventh Cuban grid collapse** has been reported; this briefing carries **six nationwide collapses** in 2026 against Cuban outlets' seven (a counting rule), with rolling blackouts of **18 or more hours a day** and plants unable to meet **half** of national demand. The **Venezuelan concession** of August 28 stands unamended: a **100-year** grant over fields holding **65 billion barrels**, with the **US government holding 55%** of the joint venture — about **21%** of Venezuela's **303 billion barrels** — secured *"at no cost to the American taxpayer."* **Maduro's trial date remains June 1, 2027.**

**Hormuz-dependent economies.** **UKMTO's 204 full transits in the week to August 28** — roughly **29 a day** against a **130-138** baseline, about **90% below** pre-conflict — is the most authoritative traffic figure since the dispute began and it excludes both extremes previously asserted. The Asian ledger is itemised: **Japan** draws about **87%** of its energy from imported fossil fuels with about **93%** of its crude imports transiting the Strait in peacetime; **South Korea** about **81%** and **70.7%**; both hold large reserves (~**254 days** Japan, ~**208 days** South Korea) and **neither has faced physical shortage** — both have taken the price instead, with the **Kospi down 12%** and the **Nikkei 225 down 8.6%** and Asian energy prices since March running roughly **50-100% above** February 2026. More than **80%** of the affected cargo was bound for **China, India, Japan and South Korea**; **India** sits in the acute-risk tier and **South Asia** faces a crisis of both supply and storage. **The shock reached the American domestic calendar:** President Trump meets executives of **at least ten** fuel producers and distributors on **September 1** — **Marathon Petroleum, Delek US Holdings, Chevron, PBF Energy** and **Valero Energy** among them — after publicly **accusing refiners of gouging** consumers, with **gasoline above $4/gal** and **diesel approaching $6**. The administration's chosen instrument for the pump price is pressure on domestic refiners rather than a reserve release or a change of course in the Gulf.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 30-31 (DAY 186): THE TWENTY-NINE-NIGHT STRIKE PAUSE BROKE, AND IT BROKE AT LARAK ISLAND — THE PIECE OF GROUND THROUGH WHICH IRAN ADMINISTERS THE TRAFFIC IT CLAIMED THE DAY BEFORE TO BE PERMITTING. US FORCES DESTROYED TWO IRGC ROCKET LAUNCHERS SAID TO BE PREPARING TO FIRE ROCKETS CARRYING SEA MINES INTO THE STRAIT, FIVE DAYS AFTER THE PRESIDENT DECLARED THE WATERWAY DE-MINED UNDER A "ZERO TOLERANCE" RULE AND TWO DAYS AFTER THE CENTCOM COMMANDER DECLARED THE LANES CLEAR. THE IRGC VOWED RETRIBUTION AND IRAN FIRED MISSILES AT US FORCES IN JORDAN. BOTH COMMANDS NOW CLAIM PERMISSIONING AUTHORITY OVER THE SAME WATER, AND BOTH GOVERNMENTS NOW CLAIM IRANIAN OIL EXPORTS ARE ZERO WHILE TANKER TRACKING RECORDS 260,000 BARRELS A DAY LOADED. GROUND RUNG: THE UNITED STATES ANSWERED AN ISLAND WITH AIRCRAFT, WITH 2,200-2,500 MARINES EMBARKED A DAY'S STEAMING AWAY.

**The pause ended, and where it ended matters more than that it ended.** On **Sunday August 30** US forces struck **two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island**. A US official said the IRGC *"was preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the strait when US forces struck"*; *Axios* reported the rockets were armed with sea mines; Iranian media reported explosions on the island. It is the **first confirmed US strike inside Iran since August 1** — a **twenty-nine-night pause**, the longest of the war and the interval this briefing has logged nightly since the President cancelled the planned energy campaign. **Larak is not an arbitrary target.** It hosts the **North Larak anchorage**, through which Iran has rerouted export flow under blockade conditions and where maritime intelligence recorded **35 tanker and cargo hulls** on **August 12** with roughly **74% dark** and **10 sanctioned vessels** identified; the **temporary northern transit route** named in the Iran-Oman understanding runs near it; and Gulf Business has described the island as Iran's **"toll gate"** on the waterway. The strike hit the **launchers** and did not touch the anchorage, the moorings or the route.

**The target set is the finding, not the fact of the strike.** Five days earlier, on **August 25**, President Trump declared that the Navy had disposed of **all mines** in the Strait's international waters and announced **"Zero Tolerance"** — *"Any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed"* — with the **Space Force** *"watching every square inch,"* and said all **28 Iranian mine-laying boats** had been destroyed. Two days earlier, on **August 28**, CENTCOM commander **Admiral Brad Cooper** declared the internationally recognised shipping lanes **free of Iranian sea mines**, cleared by **Navy divers, Navy SEALs and air power from the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps**, and called it a **"major milestone."** A resumption of mining from Larak would have falsified both claims inside a week. On its own published terms the strike is therefore the **enforcement of a declared rule against a specific act**, not the opening of a campaign — and it is also exactly what the opening night of a renewed campaign would look like, since a defensive predicate is available for any first strike. **The two readings are observationally identical on August 30 and diverge only on what follows.** This briefing logs the strike, logs both predicates, and treats the campaign's successor state as undetermined; see the open question `larak-strike-enforcement-or-campaign-resumption-august-2026`.

**Tehran promised retribution and delivered missiles.** The IRGC confirmed the strike and said it caused *"the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots"* — fighters and civilians both — **without providing a toll**. Its spokesman told state broadcaster **IRIB**: *"We will take retribution"*; the IRGC *"will punish those responsible."* Spokesman **Sardar Mohebi** called the strike *"a strategic and fatal mistake"* for which the United States would face consequences *"in both the economic and military arenas."* Parliament official **Ebrahim Azizi**: *"Retaliation is coming."* No time or place was specified. In the same cycle **Iranian missiles were fired at US forces stationed in Jordan**; a US source told Fox News that *"nearly all incoming missiles have been intercepted at this point"* with *"no significant impacts so far."* **No US casualties were reported.** The retaliation ran through missiles and interceptors, not through any ground contact, and the interceptor expenditure has not been published against a standing ledger of roughly **half the Patriot inventory** and **two-thirds of the THAAD stockpile** already spent.

**Both commands now claim permissioning authority over the same water, and this is new in kind.** CENTCOM commander **Admiral Brad Cooper**, **August 28**: *"No ships have entered or left an Iranian port without our permission, and we have only allowed ships to pass through on humanitarian grounds."* Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister **Kazem Gharibabadi**, **August 29**: *"Any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran."* The two statements address **adjacent but distinguishable water** — access to Iranian ports versus transit of the Strait itself — and are therefore **not strictly incompatible**: the United States could control who reaches Iranian terminals while Iran de-conflicts who crosses the waterway, with the same hulls subject to both regimes. **Neither claim is verifiable from open sources.** No permissioning, clearance or de-confliction record exists on either side, and none of the operators named by Lloyd's List has stated whose clearance it sought. This briefing records the **symmetry** rather than adjudicating it, and updates the standing open question `hormuz-control-attribution-august-2026` accordingly.

**A third claim is contradicted by the only disinterested measurement in the set, and the shape of the dispute is unusual.** **CENTCOM** says Iran has exported **zero barrels** since the blockade was reimposed on **July 14**. Iran's own **central bank governor** said on **August 20** that the country's oil exports had **fallen to zero**. **Kpler**'s tanker tracking, reported by *CNBC* on **August 28**, records approximately **260,000 barrels a day loaded for export at Iranian ports** in August — down **more than 80%** from **1.7 million bpd** in August 2025 and about **70%** from **893,000 bpd** in July, but **not zero**. Washington and Tehran are on the same side of this dispute and each has an independent reason to prefer the zero figure: Washington to validate the economic instrument it chose over a ground campaign, Tehran to justify emergency measures and to price its conditions for reopening the Strait. **Adversarial convergence normally functions as corroboration; here it does not**, because the convergence is on a number both parties benefit from. The likeliest reconciliation is definitional — loadings are not departures and departures are not deliveries — but no party has stated the definition, which is itself the finding. Logged as `iran-oil-exports-zero-or-loading-august-2026`.

**The Supreme Leader wrote to the Gulf, and Reuters supplied the reason for his absence.** In an **Islamic Unity Week** message published on his Telegram account marking the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad, **Mojtaba Khamenei** urged Muslim countries to unite: *"My emphatic and repeated recommendation to the rulers of Islamic countries, especially the countries of West Asia and the Gulf, is to identify your real enemy, understand his plan and confront it."* He called for cooperation across fields and **mutual defence**, and said anyone who creates divisions among Muslims *"knowingly or unknowingly"* helps Islam's enemies. It is his **second written statement in two days**, following the Government Week economic directive of August 29. **Reuters reported that he has not been seen in public since being *injured* in the US-Israeli airstrikes six months ago that killed his father** — the first published explanation in this record for an absence logged since **February 28**. It converts a six-month anomaly into a physical fact, and it does not establish incapacity: the state is executing against both directives. It is also a **coalition-splitting appeal** addressed to governments that have absorbed Iranian attacks on roughly **80 of their own energy facilities** at an estimated **$58 billion** in damage. No Gulf government answered.

**The financial track reached its loudest register and landed softest.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** told the Associated Press that the administration would sanction another bank **within the week**: *"This is going to be financial violence if we have to. We are showing people that we know who you are, you know who you are, and this has got to stop."* On China he said he would speak to his counterparts at the **G20 finance ministers' and central bank governors' meeting in Asheville, North Carolina** and that *"all options are on the table"* in terms of sanctioning Beijing for its continued purchases, rejecting the account of his reluctance as *"a completely false narrative that the media picked up on."* The same day *Fortune* reported that the world had **"mostly shrugged off"** the *"D-Day"* threat. **China**, which buys around **90% of Iran's oil**, *"issued a defiant warning to Washington rather than back down"*; **no Chinese financial institution was designated**, a **third consecutive package** sparing them. The **UAE** said it would cut ties with Iran while **Iranian bank branches remained open in Dubai** and commercial flights continued, a stance Abu Dhabi called a *"sovereign decision reflecting its strategic assessment."* **Turkish** officials had received no formal US guidance and flights continued. **Pakistan**'s foreign ministry spokesman **Tahir Andrabi** said the country *"is not obliged"* to respond to unilateral sanctions, with overland trade in rice and mangoes persisting. Former Treasury official **Alex Zerden** said the actions *"do not match the hype."* Against a promised *"major announcement of a financial institution,"* the action taken was against the **UAE branches of Egypt's Banque Misr**.

**The blockade's own numbers were published by its commander.** Cooper's **August 28** operational update: **around 50,000 US troops** *"executing a blockade on Iran, preventing the country from shipping oil since mid-July"*; **more than 20 warships** and **hundreds of aircraft**; **nearly 1,500 vessels** carrying roughly **750 million barrels** of crude transited the Strait under US protection; **75 vessels turned around** attempting to breach the blockade and **3 disabled**; *"Bottom line, today, international shipping lanes are open and momentum is building."* CENTCOM's published tally moved to **83 commercial vessels redirected and 3 disabled** by **August 30**. Gulf crude crossing the blockade averaged **6.7 million barrels per day** over the past week.

**Shipping was attacked again and the transit series did not move.** **UKMTO** issued an advisory on **August 30** for an incident at **2035 UTC on August 29**: a tanker transiting inbound into the Arabian Gulf was struck by an **unknown projectile** approximately **12 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman** — no casualties, no environmental impact, investigation under way, vessels advised to transit with caution. It follows **Warning 121-26** of August 27. No new transit count was published; the figures of record are unchanged — **114 transits August 17-27** (Lloyd's List Intelligence via *USNI News*) against a pre-war baseline near **138 vessels a day**, and **236 ships August 1-19** (Kpler via *Al Jazeera*) against roughly **130 a day** pre-war, with **89 vessels — more than 80% of oil and gas traffic in the period — moving dark or on unclassified routes**.

**Price.** The straits.live board carried **Brent at $89.75** at its **30 August 2026 2301Z** timestamp, **up 1.87% / +$1.65** over 24 hours and **24.7% above** the ~**$72** pre-crisis baseline; TradingEconomics still showed the stale Friday print of **$89.786**, its commentary unrevised for the strike and still attributing the level to an economic and sanctions contest rather than an imminent threat to physical supply. **A 1.87% move on the resumption of strikes — with the pause broken and IRGC retaliation promised — prices a narrow enforcement action rather than a renewed campaign.** **Goldman Sachs** is unchanged at **15-16 million bpd** of Persian Gulf exports against a pre-conflict **22-24 million** and a March low near **5-6 million**. Board detail: **Day 183** since closure declared; PortWatch transit count **3 vessels** (August 23 data, stale) against an **85/day** pre-crisis average = **4% of normal**; war-risk insurance **40.0× pre-crisis** (~**$10.0M per VLCC**, **+3900%** versus peacetime); **396 hulls** holding position away from berth, **down 29** on the week against a 7-day range of **253-469**; **dark-tanker count 87 of 260** screened in 24 hours; **Crisis Pressure 90/100** (extreme); **Escalation Forecast 49/100** (elevated); reopening by **August 31 <1%**, by **December 31 28%** (down from 31%); US pump price **$4.12/gal** with **$4.71** projected if fully closed; **4 of 9** major container lines have stopped Hormuz service and **8 of 9** are rerouting via the Cape, with **41+ vessels** stranded including **204,000+ TEU** from three carriers. The **Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell below 300 million barrels** (standing figure of record **290m**, **41% of capacity**, **lowest since 1982**), with the **September 1 refiners meeting** — Valero, Marathon Petroleum and PBF Energy expected — now two days out.

**Ground rung — the cycle that tested the tracked negative, and the answer was aircraft.** *This is the most informative cycle of the war on this question and it deserves stating plainly.* The standing objection to a disconfirmation built on 185 days of nothing happening was that nothing had been **required** to happen: the United States had faced no situation inside Iran demanding a physical presence, so its failure to land proved only that the occasion had not arisen. **On August 30 the occasion arose.** IRGC launchers on a small island inside the Strait were preparing to re-mine the waterway the United States has spent six months and roughly 50,000 personnel keeping open, five days after the President staked his credibility on an anti-mining rule and two days after his theatre commander declared the lanes clear. Destroying launchers and denying a small island is the **textbook employment of a Marine Expeditionary Unit**, and the **11th MEU's approximately 2,200-2,500 Marines** have been embarked in the **Arabian Sea** — within a day's steaming — for two months with **no publicly reported tasking**. **The United States destroyed two launchers from the air and put nobody ashore.** No landing, raid or occupation was reported by any party, **including Tehran**, which has every incentive to announce one. *The commander's own description of his force says the same thing:* "**around 50,000 US troops are executing a blockade**," more than 20 warships and hundreds of aircraft, **the only ground personnel named being Navy divers and SEALs doing underwater ordnance work and the only Marine Corps contribution named being air power**. *The counter-indicators are real and are not discounted:* the pause is broken; Iran fired missiles at US forces in Jordan; the IRGC promised consequences *"in both the economic and military arenas"*; Secretary **Hegseth** said the United States remains *"prepared to use military force if needed"*; the declared objective remains the collapse of the Iranian government; a third carrier strike group is being generated inside seven months; and the blockade's efficacy is now in question with **~260,000 bpd** of tracked loadings against a claim of zero, which strengthens the case for escalation if the economic instrument is failing. **Iranian escalation is the historical mechanism by which shelved American ground options are re-examined, and that machinery restarted in this cycle.** *What did not move:* no landing, no lodgement, no seizure of Iranian territory or offshore infrastructure, **no Kharg action — Kharg was not seized, not targeted and not mentioned on the day the United States struck a different Iranian island** — no reinforcement order, no change in the troop figure, no reserve mobilisation, no forward accumulation of ground-force fuel, ammunition or medical capacity, **no draft order**. The **Boxer ARG remains dispersed**, with **USS Comstock** — the dock landing ship that puts vehicles and heavy equipment ashore — in the **Indian Ocean** while **USS Boxer** stays in the Arabian Sea; one carrier in theatre, its relief the **USS Theodore Roosevelt** not expected in the Arabian Sea until the **second half of September**; **USS Tripoli** in homeport at **Sasebo, Japan**, outside CENTCOM entirely. **Every execution indicator at zero for a 185th consecutive day.**

### Russia-Ukraine — Moscow Announces Its Own Escalation in Advance, and the Myla Toll Reaches 38 (August 29-30, 2026)

**Russia published an intention to attack Ukraine's power system.** Russia's **Ministry of Defence** said the Russian Armed Forces *"have begun preparations for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure"* in response to what Moscow describes as ongoing attacks by the Kyiv regime on Russia's civilian infrastructure and fuel and energy facilities. **Announcing a strike campaign in advance forfeits surprise against a defended target set**, which is the fact that makes the statement ambiguous: it reads as a **warning order** describing a decision already taken, and equally as a **conditional deterrent signal** aimed at stopping Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries, whose value depends on being heard rather than executed. This briefing logs it as a **stated intention, not an executed act**, so that a campaign that follows is scored as an escalation when it occurs and a campaign that never comes is not quietly dropped. See `russia-announced-energy-campaign-order-or-signal-august-2026`.

**The predicate is documented.** Ukrainian drones struck the **Kirishi oil refinery** in Russia's **Leningrad region** — the country's **second-largest**, processing approximately **20 million tonnes** of crude annually — igniting a fire. Across **August 26-28** Ukraine's **Unmanned Systems Forces** struck **21 energy facilities** in occupied **Donetsk**, **Luhansk** and **Zaporizhzhia** and in **Crimea**, plus the **Luhansk Thermal Power Plant**.

**The Myla toll rose to 38 and the causal dispute is unchanged.** President **Zelensky** said the death toll from the **August 28** drone strike on the munitions warehouse at **Myla**, Bucha district, had reached **38 killed, 20 injured and 4 missing**, with approximately **50 buildings** damaged and more than **380 residents** evacuated; the mayor of nearby **Dmytrivka**, **Taras Didych**, was among the dead. Zelensky: *"the extent of contamination in the area is significant."* It is the **deadliest single attack in Ukraine this year**. Both belligerents agree munitions were stored at the site and that **secondary detonation drove the toll**; Ukrainian prosecutors described *"explosive objects"* and Russia described **components and launch boosters for long-range drones**; the site has been destroyed and the dispute cannot be resolved from open sources. See `myla-depot-storage-attribution-august-2026`.

**The bombardment ran into a third consecutive night.** Between late Saturday and early Sunday Russia launched **2 Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 130 drones** of various types, per the Ukrainian air force, and struck a **cement and asbestos plant** and a **drone and munitions manufacturing site** in Kyiv. Near-continuous drone attacks on the capital ran for a **third consecutive night** on August 29-30, **killing a two-year-old girl and injuring 12**. **Zelensky put the week's Russian expenditure at nearly 2,000 strike drones, more than 1,600 aerial bombs and 31 missiles — *including North Korean ballistic missiles*.** That last item is a DPRK datum as much as a Ukrainian one and is recorded in both theatres: Pyongyang's munitions are being consumed in Europe while Pyongyang itself has launched nothing since August 20.

**The line and the diplomacy.** Net 2026 Russian territorial gains hold at **81.1 km²**; the line is static and the war is being fought through the air. Ukraine's Presidential Office puts the Russian mobilisation plan at **600,000 across 2026-2027** — 300,000 this year, 300,000 next. **No negotiating round was held or scheduled**, and no NATO troop commitment was reported; reporting characterised four years of fighting as showing no sign of nearing a diplomatic end. The standing US intelligence assessment that **Russia reads the Iran war as American weakness** is unchanged — and it now sits alongside a US defence official's **August 27** statement that European interceptor shortages caused by the Iran war are **"beyond critical,"** with NATO confirming low Patriot inventories. **The interceptors that would answer a Russian campaign against the Ukrainian grid are the ones being expended over the Gulf.**

### Gulf States — Tehran Asks the Gulf to Change Sides, and the Damage It Is Asking Them to Overlook Is Priced at $58 Billion (August 2026)

**The appeal.** Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei**'s **Islamic Unity Week** message told *"the rulers of Islamic countries, especially the countries of West Asia and the Gulf"* to *"identify your real enemy, understand his plan and confront it,"* and called for cooperation and **mutual defence**. **No Gulf government answered.** The standing regional security instrument of the period — the **August 7 Mecca Joint Defence Agreement** — binds **Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan** to one another, not to Iran, and remains untested.

**The bill it asks them to overlook.** Around **80 energy facilities** — production plants, refineries and pipelines — have been targeted by Iranian missile and drone attacks, at an estimated **$58 billion** in damage. Since the war began in February the **World Bank** has cut its **2026 regional GDP growth forecast from 4.4% to 1.3%**, and **Oxford Economics** expects some GCC economies to enter **recession** in the second half of the year.

**The distribution still tracks the pipelines.** **Kuwait** and **Qatar** are forecast to take the deepest hit and **both economies are expected to contract**; Qatar, holder of the world's **third-largest proven gas deposits**, has been deprived of most of its LNG export route by the closure and by Iranian strikes on its energy facilities. The **Arab Monetary Fund** expects **Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Oman** to keep growing more slowly, with Riyadh and Abu Dhabi partly insulated by large non-oil sectors and by the **two pipelines that bypass the waterway**. The natural experiment stands: **the two Gulf states with bypass pipelines are the two forecast to keep growing; the two without are the two forecast to contract.** Saudi port calls remain the least affected in the region, down **15%** against **86%** for Kuwait.

**The UAE's double position is the cycle's sharpest Gulf datum.** Abu Dhabi says it is cutting ties with Iran while **Iranian bank branches remain open in Dubai** and commercial flights continue, a balance it describes as a *"sovereign decision reflecting its strategic assessment."* **Dubai is the first-named node of the American financial campaign**, and the FinCEN action against the **six UAE branches of Egypt's Banque Misr** — over approximately **$1.8 billion** processed for roughly **103 companies** between January 2024 and June 2026 — was taken on Emirati soil. That is compliance as declaration and continuity as practice, in the one jurisdiction where the campaign has chosen to act.

### Other Theatres — China's Banks Spared a Third Time While the Rhetoric Peaks, an Eleventh Quiet Day on the Peninsula, and Venezuela's Reserves Change Hands (August 30, 2026)

**US-China.** The rhetorical position reached its maximum and the target set did not move. **Bessent** promised *"financial violence,"* said *"all options are on the table"* on China ahead of the **G20 in Asheville, North Carolina**, and called reports of his reluctance *"a completely false narrative that the media picked up on"* — in the same interview in which the action described was against **an Egyptian bank's Emirati branches**. **No Chinese financial institution has been designated in three consecutive packages.** *Fortune* reported the world **"mostly shrugged off"** the threat and quoted former Treasury official **Alex Zerden** that the actions *"do not match the hype."* **The structural trap is now stated plainly in the reporting: an effective campaign requires sanctioning China, sanctioning China risks a global economic shock, and not sanctioning China leaves insufficient pressure on Iran.** The material position is unchanged — Chinese imports of Iranian crude **down 48%** since the war began from a base of roughly **90%** of Iran's sanctioned exports; Beijing paying without being designated; **Lin Jian**'s line unmoved; no Chinese countermeasure following any package.

**Taiwan.** The opportunism prediction continues to fail, and the opening is now measurable rather than merely asserted. **US reconnaissance sorties in the South China Sea have fallen roughly 30% since the war began**, and the redeployment of the **USS Abraham Lincoln** left only **one other forward-deployed US carrier in the Asia-Pacific**. Beijing has not converted the gap: **PLA fighter sorties near Taiwan fell to a three-year low in the first half of 2026**, below the pre-Lai baseline, with late-August tracking recording **7 PLAN ships and 7 official ships** around the island. PLA incursions into Taiwan's ADIZ have climbed every year since 2022; 2026's first half broke the trend during the deepest US commitment to the Middle East in a generation.

**DPRK.** An **eleventh consecutive day without a launch**, and the cycle's only North Korean datum came from Kyiv: Zelensky said the past week's Russian strikes on Ukraine included **North Korean ballistic missiles**. Pyongyang's munitions are being expended in Europe while Pyongyang has fired nothing since roughly **ten KN-25 short-range ballistic missiles** on **August 20**, and has **still not publicised that barrage domestically**. The American concession remains measurable and unreciprocated: **Ulchi Freedom Shield** was ordered *"substantially reduced"* hours before it began on **August 17**, the eleven-day two-phase exercise ran **five days** and ended **August 21** with its **counteroffensive phase never conducted**, and a further exercise has since been cancelled. **Kim Yo Jong** says her brother retains *"good memories and feelings"* about Trump and that the leaders' relationship remains *"excellent"* — a line delivered shortly before the August 20 launches — while the Foreign Ministry says US-Japan-South Korea cooperation is *"turning into a nuclear alliance"* to be met with *"a new level of deterrent."* **No talks announced, offered or scheduled.**

**Latin America.** A **fourth consecutive quiet cycle**, and the standing item is a transfer of oil rights rather than a crisis. **No seventh Cuban grid collapse** has been reported; this briefing carries **six nationwide collapses** in 2026 — twice in March, three times inside ten days in July, and once on **August 2-3** when thunderstorms broke the restoration attempt — against Cuban outlets that count the failed reconnection separately and report **seven**; the divergence is a **counting rule** and six is retained. Standing conditions hold: scheduled blackouts exceeding **twenty hours a day**, parts of Havana dark more than twenty-four and some rural communities more than seventy, and **exactly one oil tanker — Russian — permitted to dock since January**. The material development is the **Venezuelan oil concession** announced **August 28**: interim President **Delcy Rodríguez** granted a private joint venture a **100-year concession** over fields holding **65 billion barrels** of proven reserves, with the **US government controlling 55%** of the venture — approximately **21% of Venezuela's 303 billion barrels** — described by the President as creating the world's **second-largest corporate owner of proven reserves after Saudi Aramco**, secured *"at no cost to the American taxpayer."* **The concession text, its private counterparties, its ratification route under Venezuelan law and its treatment of pre-existing claims against PDVSA assets have not been published.** Read against Hormuz it is the **hemispheric half of an energy position whose other half is a blockade**, and it sits alongside the same administration's seizure of Venezuelan cargoes bound for Cuba. **Maduro** and **Cilia Flores** remain scheduled for trial in New York on **June 1, 2027**. Nothing new was reported in Colombia.

**Hormuz-dependent economies.** The closure's share of world energy trade was quantified and it is larger than the figure this briefing has carried: **34% of global crude oil trade flow** and **19% of global LNG trade flow** disrupted, described in the analytical literature as the **largest disruption of energy flow in modern history**. (This is distinct from, and larger than, the standing pre-war figure that the Strait handled roughly **20% of globally traded oil and gas**; the two measure different things — share of traded flow disrupted versus share of global trade transiting — and both are retained.) **East Asia absorbs 80-84%** of the direct impact and more than **80%** of the affected cargo was bound for **China, India, Japan and South Korea**. **Japan**'s exposure is now itemised: **87% of total energy use** from imported fossil fuels, **95% of crude imports** from the Middle East and **1.6 million barrels a day** through the Strait, against approximately **254 days** of reserve cover; **South Korea** holds approximately **208 days**. Neither faced physical scarcity and both took the price: the **Kospi is down 12%** and the **Nikkei 225 down 8.6%**. **Reserves insulate against volume risk and not against price risk** — the cleanest finding in the theatre. The macro bill now has named institutions: the **IMF** cut its 2026 global growth forecast by **0.22 points** and the **OECD** expects growth to slow from **3.4% in 2025 to 2.8% in 2026**, with **South Korea, India and Thailand** among the most exposed. **India** is classified an **acute-risk** economy; **Pakistan**'s power prices rose **4.25%** in April and Islamabad says it *"is not obliged"* to observe unilateral US sanctions on Iran. **The states bearing the cost of the closure and the states declining to enforce the sanctions regime are substantially the same states.**
