## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 29-30 (DAY 185): TEHRAN STOPPED ARGUING THAT THE STRAIT IS CLOSED AND STARTED CLAIMING IT IS ADMINISTERED — "ANY VESSEL PASSING THROUGH THE STRAIT DOES SO IN COORDINATION WITH IRAN." THE IRAN-OMAN CORRIDOR IS REACHED AND SUSPENDED, AND ITS PUBLISHED DESIGN WOULD CLOSE THE UN-AUTHORISED SOUTHERN CHANNEL AND ROUTE ALL TRAFFIC THROUGH IRANIAN TERRITORIAL WATERS. THE SUPREME LEADER CONCEDED THE ECONOMIC DAMAGE IN WRITING AND SET A DE-DOLLARISATION ROADMAP, STILL WITHOUT A PUBLIC APPEARANCE IN SIX MONTHS. THE AMERICAN CAMPAIGN'S GEOGRAPHY WAS NAMED — DUBAI, ISTANBUL, BAGHDAD, NOT BEIJING. GROUND RUNG: THE AMPHIBIOUS READY GROUP DISPERSED, AND EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR REMAINS AT ZERO FOR A 185TH DAY.

**The dispute over the Strait changed shape, and the change is the most analytically significant development of the cycle.** On **August 29** Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister **Kazem Gharibabadi** said: *"The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and any vessel passing through the strait does so in coordination with Iran."* For six months this briefing has logged a binary dispute — Washington asserting the Strait is open, Tehran asserting it is closed — and has published both governments' transit counts side by side without selecting between them. Gharibabadi's formulation is a third position, and it has the property that makes a claim genuinely unresolvable rather than merely unverified: **it is consistent with every number both governments have published.** If the residual traffic moves by Iranian permission, then Washington's count of vessels and Tehran's declaration of closure can both be accurate. The briefing records that **no permissioning, clearance or de-confliction record exists in the open source base on either side**, that none of the named commercial operators has stated whether Iranian clearance was sought, and that all three parties who could resolve the question have reasons not to: operators transiting a war zone will not confirm dealings with a sanctioned belligerent, Washington cannot concede that traffic moves by Iranian consent, and Tehran gains more from the ambiguity than from proof. The claim is logged as contested and unresolved and is carried in the open-questions register under `hormuz-control-attribution-august-2026`.

**The IRGC restated the maximal version of the same claim.** The **IRGC Navy** said on **August 29**: *"The statements by U.S. officials regarding the Strait of Hormuz being open are an obvious lie,"* and *"The control of the warriors of Islam over this strategic waterway is completely decisive."* **US Central Command** maintains the opposite — that the Strait is open and that Iran does not control it — and reports **82 ships redirected** under its port blockade. The briefing notes what Tehran did **not** say in a cycle in which it claimed decisive control of the waterway: it made no allegation of American forces ashore, which is the claim a government asserting control would make first if it had one.

**The Iran-Oman understanding is confirmed as reached and simultaneously suspended, and its published design is consolidating rather than restorative.** Gharibabadi confirmed an understanding with Muscat and conditioned its implementation on the United States honouring the **Islamabad memorandum**. On his own description, once implemented the **temporary northern route near Larak Island** and the **UN-authorised southern route** following Oman's coast would **both be closed** and replaced by a **single new corridor, seven miles wide**, whose **entry** and part of whose **exit** lie in **Iranian territorial waters**. The southern route is the channel announced in June under the Islamabad MOU; Iran said the route violated that agreement, attacked ships using it, and the interim deal collapsed. The briefing records the analytical consequence plainly: the dispute is no longer whether the corridor is a concession or a consolidation in the abstract, but whether **extinguishing a UN-authorised transit channel and substituting an Iranian-entered corridor** constitutes a reopening or an annexation of a transit right. That is a legal question the published summaries cannot settle, in an arrangement that remains suspended behind an American precondition Washington has not met — so no conduct exists to interpret. Carried under `iran-oman-hormuz-corridor-concession-or-consolidation-august-2026`.

**The commercial transit data was published independently and it shows recovery without normalisation.** *USNI News*, citing **Lloyd's List Intelligence**, recorded **114 transits between August 17 and August 27** — up **more than 30%** on the week, with the increase led by **tankers and gas carriers** — and **at least 42 westbound transits** into the Strait against **29** the week prior. Crude tankers tracked included vessels from **Sinokor** and **ADNOC** alongside **Saudi- and Kuwait-owned** ships. The pre-war baseline cited is **about 138 vessels daily**. **Goldman Sachs** estimates Persian Gulf oil exports have climbed to around **15-16 million barrels per day**, still well below the pre-conflict **22-24 million** but far above the **March low of about 5-6 million**. The briefing carries **four unreconciled transit series** and selects between none of them, because they use different vessel-class definitions, baselines and lags: Lloyd's List at 114 transits over eleven days; *Al Jazeera*'s six-month series at a **~100/day pre-war baseline**, a **current average of seven a day**, a **post-closure low of five** and a **post-June peak of twenty**; the President's figure of **24 a day** against roughly **130** pre-war; and the straits.live PortWatch feed carrying **three vessels on August 23** against an **85/day** pre-crisis average — **4% of normal** — on data six days stale.

**Maritime risk did not ease with the transit count.** The **United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations** centre assessed **"SEVERE risk for the Strait of Hormuz and SUBSTANTIAL across the Gulf of Oman, Gulf of Aden, and Bab el Mandeb,"** with vessel traffic **"significantly reduced"** and operators favouring **northern routes** following projectile attacks and heightened enforcement activity. No new UKMTO attack warning was issued on August 29; the last remains **Warning 121-26** of August 27. The **International Maritime Organization**'s figures were restated and not revised: **more than 6,000 seafarers stranded** aboard hundreds of Persian Gulf ships, **19 seafarers killed**, and **at least 70 attacks** on international shipping since February 28. The straits.live board carried **461 hulls holding position away from berth** at its **29 August 2305Z** timestamp against a seven-day range of **253-465** — a range spanning nearly a factor of two, which the briefing reads as convoy batching rather than monotonic accumulation — with **war-risk insurance at 40 times pre-crisis rates**, roughly **$10 million per VLCC**.

**The economic admission came from the top of the Iranian state, and it came in writing.** Marking **Government Week**, Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** issued a message calling on the government to give *"serious attention"* to *"inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services,"* stating that *"the main key to resolving all these issues lies in relying increasingly on domestic production,"* urging authorities to promote growth, increase investment and direct funds toward productive and essential sectors, and setting out a roadmap to **gradually reduce the US dollar's role** in the economy with **"resistance economy"** policies at the centre of the government's agenda. *Al Jazeera* recorded explicitly that Khamenei **has not appeared publicly since his father's death on February 28, 2026** and that the statement was written. The briefing records both halves of what this means for the succession question: the directive is **substantive and programmatic**, and the government executed against it within a day — **President Pezeshkian** announced the same day that the government would focus on *"curbing inflation, creating jobs and gradually reducing dependence on the dollar,"* tracking the message point for point — which is authority being exercised. Equally, **six consecutive months of exclusively written communication** from an office constituted substantially through public appearance, by a man reported wounded in the strike that killed his predecessor, is an anomaly no published account explains. Carried under `iran-succession-mojtaba-khamenei-2026`.

**Pezeshkian put numbers to the damage and paired them with defiance.** Exports and imports have **slumped nearly 35 percent** because of US sanctions and the port blockade; Iran sold approximately **90 million barrels** of oil during the **June memorandum** window when sales were briefly permitted; **annual inflation reached 66 percent** last month. He also said: *"We will stand strong against any aggressor, and no power can force a nation that stands with all its might and will to surrender,"* and that Iran will *"not bow to any threat."* Iranian officials framed **"diplomacy and defence"** as *"complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings"* for protecting national interests. Iran's Ambassador to Germany **Majid Nili** told IRNA: *"Despite the existing political atmosphere and pressures, the path of dialogue and engagement based on mutual respect is still being pursued."* **Araghchi** posted on X: *"Pressure doesn't work."* Acting Defence Minister Brig. Gen. **Majid Ebn al-Reza** told Tasnim that adversaries *"should know that they will become aware of Iran's surprises in due time,"* and that Iranian youth and defence industries *"will bring good surprises."* Army Commander **Amir Hatami** said the drone and missile stockpile had been fired *"with the utmost intensity until the last moment."* **Arvand Petrochemical** in Mahshahr has been suspended since **August 22** on instruction from the state-owned National Petrochemical Company, citing electricity shortages; **Ghadir Petrochemical**, which it supplies, shut with it.

**The American financial campaign's geography was named, and Beijing is not on it.** *Iran International*'s analysis of the **Banque Misr** action concluded that the offensive is aimed at **Dubai, Istanbul and Baghdad** as Iran's financial channels rather than at **Beijing**. This is the second consecutive package to spare China's major banks, and the restraint now has a stated geography rather than merely an unexplained omission. The structural point is recorded plainly: the instrument used — a **FinCEN proposed rule** severing six UAE branches of an Egyptian bank from US correspondent banking over roughly **$1.8 billion** moved for about **103** Iran-linked companies between **January 2024 and June 2026** — is exactly the instrument that would be used against a Chinese institution. **It was demonstrated on a target with no capacity to retaliate.** **Banque Misr UAE** responded that it affirms *"full respect for the relevant regulatory and legal frameworks"* and treats the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking *"with the utmost seriousness and attention"* while preparing responses within the specified periods.

**The domestic constraint on the blockade acquired a date, which it has never had before.** Reuters and Bloomberg reported that President Trump will meet **at least ten fuel makers and distributors** on the afternoon of **Tuesday, September 1** — **Valero Energy**, **Marathon Petroleum** and **PBF Energy** expected alongside major retailers — to hear directly on market dynamics, what can be done to lower gasoline prices, and how to bolster domestic refining capacity. A White House official declined to confirm, saying only that *"The Trump Administration will make a decision that is best for consumers, farmers, and energy supply chains."* The levels the meeting concerns: US fuel prices are at the **highest seasonal level ever recorded**, with gasoline **above $4 a gallon** and diesel **almost $6 a gallon** nationwide — down from this year's **May peak above $4.50** but roughly **a dollar higher than at the February 28 start of the war**. The **AAA national average** printed at **$4.090** for regular on August 28; straits.live carries the current pump price at **$4.12** and projects **$4.70** if the Strait fully closes. Read alongside the **Strategic Petroleum Reserve at 290 million barrels — 41% of capacity and the lowest since 1982** — presidential approval at **33%** against 65% disapproval, and **midterm elections in November**, this is the clearest measurable domestic constraint in the record on how long the blockade can be sustained, and the first time the administration has scheduled an action directed at it.

**Price.** Brent settled the week near **$88-$89** after a weekly loss exceeding **5%**. TradingEconomics carried Brent at **$88.29** on **August 28**, down **0.26%** on the day, with intraday prints to **$89.20-$89.30**; the straits.live board carried **$88.10** at its **29 August 2305Z** timestamp with markets closed, down **0.40%** over 24 hours and **22.4%** above the ~**$72** pre-crisis baseline. The range of record for the August 28 close is therefore **$88.10-$89.30** and the divergence is logged rather than resolved. Every print agrees on the attributed cause and every attribution is de-escalatory: traders are pricing the confrontation as an **economic and sanctions contest rather than an imminent threat to physical supply**, with improving Hormuz flows and the proposed Iran-Oman corridor further reducing perceived supply risk. There has been no strike inside Iran since August 1 — a **twenty-ninth consecutive night** — so the price continues to track sanctions and diplomacy rather than supply events.

**Adjacent and regional.** The **State Department** said *"Hizballah must disarm"* and that the group *"is simply taking orders from Iran,"* calling Lebanon the *"sole legitimate interlocutor"* for discussions about the country's future. Former US Ambassador to the EU **Gordon Sondland** said Europeans *"have been doing contortions in trying to appease us and continue to do business with Iran. It's really despicable,"* framing the choice as *"Are you part of the coalition or are you not?"* Israel's **Shin Bet** confirmed the urgent extraction of **Yair Netanyahu** from Miami over a *"significant threat"*; **Netanyahu** told Channel 14 that *"Iran targeted one of my sons"* and *"tried to kill, to murder"* him. Four British nationals — **Hamza Iqbal** (20), **Rehan Khan** (19), **Judex Atshatski** (18) and **Saif Ali** (18) — pleaded guilty to destroying **four Hatzola ambulances** in Golders Green, London, on **March 23**, causing about **£1 million** ($1.4m) of damage in an attack claimed by the Iran-linked group **HAYI**; sentencing is scheduled for spring 2027. The **IDF** said it struck a Hamas commander sheltering within the compound of **Shuhada Al-Aqsa Hospital** in Gaza.

**Ground rung — one published Marine datapoint that is sustainment, one amphibious dispersal that is the cycle's load-bearing finding, and three counter-indicators.** *The Marine datapoint is real and it is routine.* On **August 29** **US Central Command released images of US Marines refuelling an MV-22 Osprey** during a stop in the Middle East, described as supporting **Operation Epic Fury**. This is the first CENTCOM-published imagery of Marine ground personnel in this theatre in some weeks, and the tracker logs it on principle. It also records what it is not: aviation refuelling is the most routine task an expeditionary unit performs, it was **publicised rather than concealed**, and the operational-security posture preceding an amphibious assault runs in precisely the opposite direction — units going ashore go quiet. The tell for a landing has never been the presence of Marines in CENTCOM, who have been there since March; it is their **concentration**, their **silence**, and the accumulation of fuel, ammunition and medical capacity close to an objective. *The dispersal is the finding.* Per the most recent **USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker**, the **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group is no longer operating as a single formation**: **USS Boxer (LHD-4)** remains in the **Arabian Sea** on its 61st day in theatre with no publicly reported tasking, while **USS Comstock (LSD-45)** — the **dock landing ship**, the element that puts vehicles and heavy equipment ashore — has moved into the **Indian Ocean**. An amphibious ready group split across two oceans cannot execute a landing without a reconstitution visible days in advance, and this is the **second consecutive cycle** in which the amphibious picture moved **away** from a massing signature. *The standing negatives all returned negative.* **Kharg Island** was not seized, not targeted and not mentioned by any party — approximately **152 days** since the reported March discussion of a ground operation against it. **USS Tripoli (LHA-7)** is in homeport at **Sasebo, Japan**, having offloaded the **31st MEU** at White Beach, Okinawa on **July 22** after a six-month 5th and 7th Fleet deployment — outside CENTCOM entirely. **No draft order exists**; the only Selective Service change of record remains the **administrative automatic-registration rule due December 18, 2026**, which automates registration and does not activate conscription, and the briefing adds the structural point that the binding constraint in this war is **munitions, not manpower** — troop strength has been flat at **~50,000 since July**, reaffirmed by the Pentagon on **August 28**, while roughly half the Patriot inventory has been expended. **Conscription does not manufacture interceptors.** *The counter-indicators are logged without discount:* the **Boxer ARG and the 11th MEU's ~2,200-2,500 Marines** remain in theatre untasked on a 61st day, a **third carrier strike group** is being generated for this theatre inside seven months with **USS Theodore Roosevelt** sailing within weeks to relieve **USS George Washington** and expected in the Arabian Sea in the second half of September, and **Iran's acting defence minister is promising unspecified "surprises."** *The cycle's most revealing American action was domestic:* a **September 1 pricing meeting with oil refiners**, which is the behaviour of a government managing the domestic cost of a blockade it intends to sustain rather than one preparing a public for casualties. **Every execution indicator remains at zero for a 185th consecutive day.**

### Russia-Ukraine — The Deadliest Attack of the Year, and a Causal Dispute Both Sides' Own Accounts Make Unresolvable (August 28-29, 2026)

**The strike.** At about **20:10 local (17:10 GMT) on August 28** an unmanned aerial vehicle struck or fell on the grounds of an enterprise in the town of **Myla**, roughly **five kilometres west of Kyiv** along the **Kyiv-Chop highway**. The impact started a large fire followed by **sustained ammunition detonations**. **At least 37 people were killed** — the deadliest single attack in Ukraine in 2026 — among them the **mayor of the nearby town of Dmytrivka**, per Kyiv region governor **Tymur Tkachenko**. The blast damaged surrounding residential areas and a **care home for elderly and disabled people**; **more than 380 residents** were evacuated.

**The causal dispute is on the record from both sides and is logged without adjudication.** **Ukrainian prosecutors** said the depot appeared to have been storing *"explosive objects"*; **President Zelensky** suggested ammunition was responsible for the scale of the casualties; Ukrainian officials described the warehouse as holding **shells, mines and other ammunition**. **Russia's Ministry of Defence** said it had hit a warehouse in Myla storing **components and launch boosters for long-range drones**, and separately claimed attacks the same night on the ports of **Mykolaiv** and **Izmail** and on a logistics centre and warehouse facilities storing parts for Ukraine's **Flamingo cruise missiles** in the Kyiv region. **The two accounts converge on the decisive physical fact** — munitions were present and secondary detonation drove the death toll — **and diverge on everything that determines responsibility**: what the site was, whether it was a licit military object, whether Russia held targeting intelligence identifying it as such, and why it sat beside a care home. The site has been destroyed, wartime munitions-storage locations are classified by the state that owns them, and targeting intelligence is not published by the state that acts on it. The briefing records **37 dead at Myla**, records that both governments agree munitions were stored there, records that they describe the site differently, and **declines to assign the event to either the deliberate-targeting ledger or the co-location ledger**. Carried under `myla-depot-storage-attribution-august-2026`. This entry exists to prevent the absence of documentation from being read as proof of either account.

**The bombardment ran into a third consecutive day.** Ukraine's military said air defences **shot down or suppressed 233 Russian drones** overnight into **August 29** across northern, southern, eastern and central Ukraine, with drones targeting Kyiv and its surroundings into the morning; explosions were heard in Kyiv around **9 a.m.** and the alert remained active at **10:30 a.m.** Near-continuous air raid alerts across large parts of the country stretched into a **third consecutive day**, a rare duration. The previous cycle's figure was **164 Shahed-type drones** overnight into August 28, half of them jet-powered, of which **137** were intercepted.

**Ukraine's counter-campaign stayed on energy and logistics.** The **Unmanned Systems Forces** struck **21 energy facilities** in occupied **Donetsk**, **Luhansk** and **Zaporizhzhia** and in **Crimea**, plus the **Luhansk Thermal Power Plant**, across **August 26-28**. Ukrainian forces also struck an **Ozon warehouse** and sites across **Rostov Oblast** in a mass attack on southern Russia; the **Novoshakhtinsky refinery** in Rostov was damaged and suspended processing around August 25.

**Mobilisation and diplomacy.** Ukraine's Presidential Office put the Russian General Staff's plan at **600,000 recruits across 2026-2027** — **300,000** to be called up this year and **300,000** next — refining the figure Ukrainian intelligence reported on August 27. On the diplomatic track nothing moved: Deputy Foreign Minister **Sergey Ryabkov** says Moscow is ready to hear new ideas provided they align with Putin's position and *"realities on the ground"*; **Zelensky** has handed the United States new proposals; **no formal round is scheduled**, and the Kremlin said in July there was no immediate prospect of resuming formal negotiations. **Net Russian territorial gains for 2026 remain 81.1 square kilometres** and the line is effectively static. The linkage to the Iran theatre established in the previous cycle is unchanged and still material: fresh US intelligence that **Russia views America as weakened by the Iran war**, corroborated by a US defence official describing European interceptor shortages caused by that war as **"beyond critical."**

### Gulf States — The Bill Disaggregated by Country, and the Bypass Pipelines Decide Who Pays (August 2026)

**The regional aggregate and its distribution.** Since the war began in February the **World Bank** has cut its **2026 GDP growth forecast for the region from 4.4% to 1.3%**, and **Oxford Economics** expects some GCC economies to enter **recession** in the second half of the year. The distribution is sharply uneven and it tracks exposure to the waterway. **Kuwait** and **Qatar** are expected to suffer the deepest fallout, with **both economies forecast to contract** this year as Hormuz disruption hits energy exports; Qatar, which holds the world's **third-largest proven gas deposits**, has been deprived of most of its LNG export route by the closure and by Iranian missile and drone attacks on its energy facilities. The **Arab Monetary Fund** expects **Saudi Arabia**, the **UAE**, **Bahrain** and **Oman** to continue growing at a slower pace, with Riyadh and Abu Dhabi partially insulated by relatively large **non-oil sectors** and by **two pipelines** that allow crude to bypass the Strait.

**The natural experiment is worth stating explicitly.** The two Gulf states with bypass pipelines are the two forecast to keep growing; the two without are the two forecast to contract. This briefing records it as the cleanest evidence in the corpus on the value of chokepoint redundancy. The physical ledger behind the macro number: around **80 energy facilities** — production plants, refineries and pipelines — have been targeted by Iranian missile and drone attacks since February 28.

**The diplomatic track ran through Doha and it is substantive.** Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister **Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani** visited Tehran on **August 27** — the first high-level Qatari visit since the war began — and met Foreign Minister **Araghchi**, President **Pezeshkian**, Parliament Speaker **Ghalibaf** and Supreme National Security Council Secretary **Mohsen Rezaei**. The talks covered the phased framework for a temporary joint Iranian-Omani shipping corridor and a joint mine-clearing project; Al Thani emphasised respect for the sovereignty of neighbouring states and freedom of navigation; Araghchi called the talks **"creative."** Qatar hosts **Al Udeid Air Base**, shares the world's largest gas field with Iran, and brokered the June ceasefire. The briefing records the significance: a state hosting the principal American air base in the region, taking Iranian strikes on its energy infrastructure and facing a contracting economy responded by sending its Prime Minister to Tehran to **mediate**. Costly alignment is not defection. No new Iranian strike on a Gulf state was reported this cycle; the Gulf casualty figure of record remains **28 killed**.

### Other Theatres — China's Banks Spared With a Named Geography, a Peninsula Ten Days Quiet, and a Third Silent Cycle in Latin America (August 29, 2026)

**US-China.** The financial campaign's target map was drawn and Beijing is not on it: *Iran International*'s analysis of the Banque Misr action found the offensive aimed at **Dubai, Istanbul and Baghdad** rather than at Beijing — the second consecutive package to spare China's major banks, now with an articulated geography. The material position is unchanged and is that **Beijing is already paying without being designated**: Chinese imports of Iranian crude are **down 48%** since the war began, from a base in which China took roughly **90%** of Iran's sanctioned exports. **Lin Jian**'s position is unchanged — cooperation with Iran *"has always been conducted within the framework of international law"*; China *"firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions"* and will *"take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests"*; *"sanctions and pressure will not resolve disputes"* — and **no Chinese countermeasure has followed either package**. On tariffs the August actions were **sectoral and multilateral rather than China-specific**: a **15% tariff plus minimum import prices on polysilicon** and certain derivatives, and **forced-labour duties of 10% to 12.5%** across about **60 economies** representing roughly **99.4% of US trade** (10% for jurisdictions with forced-labour statutes, 12.5% for those without). **Taiwan's rate was lowered from 20% to 15%** under commitments in the **January 15, 2026 AIT-TECRO memorandum**. China's Ministry of Commerce has issued retaliatory measures over the US ban on imports of **advanced robots and power inverters** and the addition of **43 Chinese companies** to the **UFLPA Entity List**. US-PRC talks have run since 2025 without a deal; the fall 2025 pause on some tariff and export-control actions holds, and the May 2026 trade and investment boards continue.

**Taiwan.** The military picture is **below baseline, not above it**. **PLA fighter sorties near Taiwan fell to a three-year low in the first half of 2026**, having reverted to the pre-Lai baseline after peaking above 300 incursions a month following the May 2024 inauguration; late-August tracking recorded **7 PLAN ships and 7 official ships** operating around the island, with ROC forces responding using CAP aircraft, navy ships and coastal missile systems. **No Chinese military response to the American sanctions campaign was reported.** This briefing records the asymmetry: US intelligence assesses that **Russia** reads the Iran war as American weakness, and **no equivalent published assessment of Chinese opportunism exists**. The previous cycle's legislative development stands — on **August 27** Taiwan's opposition-controlled parliament rejected a **$6.6 billion drone procurement budget** and approved a **$7.6 billion alternative**: total spending up, asymmetric capability down.

**DPRK.** A **tenth consecutive day without a launch**, and still nothing from Pyongyang about Washington. No DPRK missile activity has been reported since roughly **ten KN-25 short-range ballistic missiles** were fired on **August 20** during the truncated Ulchi Freedom Shield, and North Korea has still not publicised that barrage domestically. The American concession remains real, measurable and unreciprocated: Trump ordered the Pentagon to **"substantially reduce"** the exercise hours before it began on **August 17**; the **eleven-day two-phase** exercise ran **five days** and ended **August 21**, its **counteroffensive phase never conducted**; the drills involved **18,000 South Korean troops** alongside elements of the **28,500-strong** US contingent and focused on counter-drone, GPS-disruption and cyber scenarios drawn from North Korea's Russia-war experience; a further exercise has since been cancelled. Pyongyang's published position has not softened — the Foreign Ministry says US-Japan-South Korea cooperation is **"turning into a nuclear alliance"** and that the North will meet *"a new level of threat"* with *"a new level of deterrent"* — while **Kim Yo Jong** calls the Trump-Kim relationship **"excellent"**, says the exercise reduction changed nothing about American hostile policy, and denies recent contact. Trump said on **August 19** he plans to meet Kim this year; **no summit announcement, no date, no new provocation and no resumption of the cancelled exercises** has been reported. The previous cycle's analytical consensus — that Kim is in a far stronger position than in 2019 and needs neither sanctions relief nor a summit — is unchallenged by anything in this cycle.

**Latin America.** A **third consecutive quiet cycle**, and the one new item is a **counting dispute rather than an event**. No new Cuban nationwide grid collapse and no new Venezuelan measure was reported. This briefing carries **six nationwide collapses** of the Cuban electricity system in 2026 — twice in March, three times inside ten days in July, and once on **August 2-3** when thunderstorms broke the restoration attempt and produced two nationwide outages within hours. Cuban outlets that count the August 2 collapse and the failed reconnection as **separate events** give a 2026 total of **seven**. No distinct seventh blackout has been reported; the divergence is entirely a counting rule applied to the same August 2-3 sequence, and the briefing retains **six** as its figure of record while logging the alternative count with its basis. The standing figures hold: scheduled blackouts exceeding **twenty hours a day**, parts of Havana dark for more than twenty-four hours and some rural communities for more than seventy; protests in **Marianao, La Lisa, El Cerro, San José de las Lajas and Santiago de Cuba**; and since January the United States has permitted **exactly one oil tanker — Russian — to dock in Cuba**. In **Venezuela** the pot-banging protests, road blockades and burning tyres continue over daily outages reported at **five to ten hours**, with **Turmero** in **Aragua** the focal point and acting president **Delcy Rodríguez's** National Electricity and Water Savings Plan openly rejected. The transition remains **normalisation without transition**: Rodríguez has held the acting presidency since **January 5**, **131 political prisoners** were released on **August 15** under talks opened August 6, and **no electoral calendar, new electoral authority or constitutional timetable** has been announced. **Maduro** and **Cilia Flores** remain in US custody with trial set for **June 1, 2027**. No new Colombian development was reported.

**Hormuz-dependent economies.** The burden was quantified by region and **East Asia absorbs 80-84% of the direct impact**. **Japan** holds roughly **254 days** and **South Korea** roughly **208 days** of strategic petroleum reserve cover, which has insulated both from physical shortage but not from price: the **Kospi is down 12%** and the **Nikkei 225 down 8.6%**. The distinction is one the briefing records explicitly because it is frequently elided — **reserves insulate against volume risk and not against price risk**. **India** is classified an **acute-risk** economy facing immediate industrial disruption and inflationary pressure on food and essential goods as energy-related logistics costs rise. **Pakistan** has joined **more than thirty-two nations** calling for immediate resolution of the blockade, and an unprecedented coalition of **more than thirty states** — including **South Korea, Japan, China and India** — has formed around soaring energy costs and supply shortages, a grouping that spans the US-China divide. On the American side of the same ledger: gasoline **above $4 a gallon** and diesel **near $6**, the highest seasonal level on record and roughly **$1 above the February 28 level**, with the President meeting **at least ten refiners and fuel retailers on September 1**.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 28-29 (DAY 184): SIX MONTHS, AND THE PRESIDENT DESCRIBED HIS OWN WAR AS ONE "IN WHICH NO AMERICAN TROOPS HAVE DEPLOYED INTO IRAN" — THE FIRST AFFIRMATIVE STATEMENT OF THIS BRIEFING'S TRACKED NEGATIVE BY THE COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF. TREASURY AND FinCEN MOVED TO SEVER AN EGYPTIAN BANK'S UAE BRANCHES FROM THE DOLLAR, THE FIRST BRANCH-LEVEL CORRESPONDENT ACTION OF OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST, AND AGAIN SPARED CHINA'S BANKS. TEHRAN AGREED AT THE MEDIATORS' REQUEST TO WRITE ITS HORMUZ CONDITIONS DOWN, AND THE PRICE DID NOT MOVE. THE SIX-MONTH LEDGER WAS PUBLISHED AND THE PENTAGON'S HALF OF IT IS A DEPLETION LEDGER: HALF THE PATRIOT INVENTORY, TWO-THIRDS OF THE THAAD STOCKPILE, A THIRD OF THE TOMAHAWKS. GROUND RUNG: EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR AT ZERO FOR A 184TH DAY.

**The anniversary arrived and the forecast that opened the war is now measurable against it.** The US-Israeli war on Iran, launched on **February 28, 2026**, reached its **six-month mark on August 28**. The day after he announced it, **Trump said the fight could last four to five weeks**. It has now run six times that. Reporting across outlets on the anniversary converged on a single finding: **none of the six objectives** the President outlined when he announced the war has been fully achieved. Iran's nuclear programme retains its enriched-uranium stockpile and the knowledge to rebuild, though it has been set back. Senator **Jack Reed** called the campaign a **"policy failure of historic consequence,"** noting zero achieved objectives after six months. The President spent **August 28** in **Houston**, honouring the **Artemis II** NASA crew for their ten-day mission around the moon, and made no set-piece anniversary statement.

**The most consequential sentence of the cycle for this briefing was spoken by the President in his own defence.** Pressed on the war's duration and cost, Trump characterised it as a campaign **"in which no American troops have deployed into Iran."** This briefing has established that fact for 184 consecutive days by inference — from USNI fleet trackers, from force-disposition reporting, from CENTCOM's own descriptions of the campaign, and from the silence of an Iranian government that would announce an American landing within hours of one occurring. It has never before been able to record the negative as an **affirmative description of the war offered by the commander-in-chief**, and offered not as a denial extracted under questioning but as a defence of how the campaign has been designed. The limit is stated plainly: this is a claim about the past six months, not a commitment about the next six, and a president who says no troops have deployed retains every authority to deploy them. What it does is close the gap between this briefing's inference and the government's own account of itself. In the same exchange Trump said Iran is **"in deep trouble,"** has **"very little capacity,"** and that **"they're not paying their troops"**; that **"we don't want to speak to them. We're not looking to meet or anything"**; and, asked why he has not sanctioned Chinese banks, **"Who said I'm not? You don't know if I'm doing it. I don't have to announce everything, do I?"**

**The American instrument of the cycle was financial, and for the first time it cut a bank out of the dollar.** On **August 28** the Treasury Department, acting through **FinCEN**, proposed a rule that would sever the **six United Arab Emirates branches of Egypt's Banque Misr** from correspondent banking relationships with US financial institutions, cutting off their access to dollar transfers. Treasury's finding is that the branches processed approximately **$1.8 billion** for roughly **103 companies** potentially forming part of Iran's shadow banking network between **January 2024 and June 2026**. Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent**: *"Banque Misr UAE decided to find out the hard way, and today, we are taking the first step in holding it accountable for its continued, egregious support of the Iranian regime,"* adding that Washington had *"also warned that Iran's enablers cannot continue to enjoy access to the U.S. dollar and the global financial system."* **The limits belong in the record with the action.** It is a **proposed rule** subject to a **30-day public comment period**; it is **not** a full designation of the bank; and it leaves Banque Misr's **Cairo** headquarters and its **Paris, Frankfurt, Riyadh, Beirut and Djibouti** branches able to transact in dollars. Egypt's central bank confirmed the measure *"is limited to the bank's branches in the UAE and only to its dollar transfers,"* affecting no other Egyptian bank and no domestic operation. Treasury simultaneously targeted the **UAE branch manager of Bank Melli** and a **Hong Kong entity** alleged to have laundered funds for sanctioned Iranian exchange operations. Bessent is due to meet **G-20 finance ministers** next week to press for wider participation in Iran's economic isolation. This is the **first branch-level correspondent-banking action under Operation Economic Outcast**, announced four days earlier — and reporting attributed the decision to stop short of full sanctions to reluctance to penalise **major trading partners including China and India**, with Bessent's stated position being that countries should have the opportunity to shift away from Iran before facing consequences.

**Tehran moved toward paper rather than water.** **Mohsen Rezaei**, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said on **August 28** that Iran is drawing up a **list of conditions** for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, at the request of mediators who had asked Tehran to set its demands out explicitly. Rezaei: *"The US must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran's conditions, and then Iran will proceed to open the Strait of Hormuz."* He confirmed that Iran and **Oman** have agreed the **coordinates** of the corridor, with **parts of the route in Omani waters and parts in Iranian waters**, and said ships would use a designated **central channel** if Washington met the conditions. The conditions as stated by the IRGC and the Foreign Ministry are unchanged across four mediators in five days: **end the blockade of Iranian ports, pay compensation for war damage, remove sanctions, end the war**. The agreement to enumerate them is procedural movement toward a negotiable text; the price itself has not moved. Rezaei separately denied reports of an Iranian plot against the President's son **Barron Trump**, calling the claim *"a lie"* in an interview with Al Manar TV.

**Both governments asserted control of the same water on the same day.** The **IRGC** claimed **"decisive control"** over the Strait of Hormuz and said US officials continue to **"lie"** about the waterway's status. Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** said the US-Israeli war had **"failed."** Iran's Foreign Ministry called the new sanctions a **"crime against humanity"** endangering civilians' health and livelihoods. Against this, the **White House** told *Al Jazeera* that the Strait is **de-mined and safe for transit** and reiterated that no talks with Iran are occurring or scheduled.

**The transit counts published on August 28 are irreconcilable and both are logged.** Trump said the **"Strait of Hormuz is open"** and put transits at **24 vessels a day** against roughly **130** before the war. The same day, *Al Jazeera* counted **seven commodity ships** transiting on Thursday, **down from 17** the previous day, against a pre-war baseline of about **100 a day**; its six-month series gives a **current average of seven a day**, a **post-closure low of five**, and a **post-June-agreement peak of twenty**. This briefing selects between neither figure. The administration has published **no counting rule, vessel-class definition or measurement window** for its number, and its pre-war denominator of ~130 a day is roughly **30% above** the ~100 a day used by every published tracker — a separate and unexplained divergence. One genuine reconciling mechanism is documented: *Al Jazeera*'s own reporting notes that residual traffic consists mostly of tankers **under naval escort or with tracking systems switched off**, a category a public AIS-based count cannot fully observe, so a government count with access to escort manifests would legitimately exceed a tracker count. That reconciliation is plausible and undocumented.

**The six-month ledger is the fullest this briefing has carried.** Compilation of official figures as of **August 28**: **Lebanon 4,350 killed and 12,510 injured**; **Iran 3,527 killed**; **Gulf states 28 killed**; **Israel 60 killed**; **United States 18 service members killed and 757 wounded**. US and Israeli attacks on Iran since February 28: **more than 3,580**. Iranian attacks across the Gulf and wider Middle East: **more than 2,053**. Ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz: **70 confirmed incidents** with **19 seafarer fatalities**. Official US war costs: **$37.5 billion**, with internal estimates reported at **$80-100 billion**. Brent crude: from **$72.48** to **$88.58**, a **22%** rise, having peaked at **$120.88** — 67% above pre-war. The **US Strategic Petroleum Reserve** stands at **290 million barrels — 41% of capacity and the lowest level since 1982**. Trump's approval rating is **33%** against **65%** disapproval, and **80%** of Americans expect the conflict to continue. Two divergences are noted rather than resolved: the wounded figure of **757** sits one below the Pentagon total of record of **758** (776 including the dead), and the Iranian death toll of **3,527** sits one below the Iranian government's **3,528**.

**The Pentagon's half of the ledger is a depletion ledger, and it is the most structurally significant material of the cycle.** Six months of war has expended **more than 1,000 Patriot interceptors** — roughly **half** the US inventory; **more than 200 THAAD interceptors** — approximately **two-thirds** of the stockpile; and **at least 1,000 Tomahawk missiles** — an estimated **one-third** of the inventory. Individual replacement missiles require approximately **two years** to build and field, so the depletion cannot be reversed inside this conflict on any plausible timeline. The shortfall has propagated outside the theatre: a US defence official told the *Associated Press* on **August 27** that shortages of advanced missile interceptors in **Europe** caused by the Iran war are **"beyond critical,"** and **NATO** confirmed low Patriot inventories. Iranian attacks damaged US military infrastructure in **Bahrain** — a major naval supply hub and the headquarters of the Fifth Fleet — forcing reliance on alternative locations including **Diego Garcia**, extending logistics operations and degrading conditions for deployed troops through delayed mail and poorer food. **Six troops died in a single drone strike** on a command centre in **Kuwait**. Retired General **Joseph Votel**, a former CENTCOM commander, gave the summary judgement: *"Iran's strategy is to extend the war in both time and geography, and frankly, they've succeeded."*

**Iran's home front deteriorated further on fuel, currency and prices.** Daily gasoline consumption of about **135 million litres** against refinery production of about **121 million litres** leaves a **daily deficit of 15 million litres**; queues stretched through parts of **Tehran** and other cities and some stations suspended operations. The government is weighing three rationing options: capping availability at domestic production, cutting subsidised quotas and selling the balance at market prices, or transferring quotas from vehicles to individuals. A pilot price rise in **Kerman Province** was **halted within hours**, with the **2019** protests the explicit reference. The rial remains above **2 million** to the dollar. President **Masoud Pezeshkian** said foreign trade has **"shrunk by nearly 35%"** under the sanctions and naval blockade; annual inflation was reported at **66%** last month; and **90 million barrels** were sold under the June arrangement before it lapsed.

**The succession question moved slightly.** Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** was reported making substantive public remarks on the economy — *"There is the need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment"* — and urging officials against *"committing anything that harms social cohesion."* This is logged against Trump's **August 26** statement that Mojtaba Khamenei is not dead but **"very seriously wounded"** after roughly six months out of public view. Attributed remarks are not a public appearance and do not resolve the question: a statement issued in the Supreme Leader's name is compatible with incapacity, and Iran has every incentive to project continuity. What changed is that the reporting record now carries substantive economic guidance attributed to him rather than only ceremonial references.

**The seafarers were counted for the first time.** The **International Maritime Organization** confirmed **19 seafarers killed** in attacks on shipping in the Persian Gulf, **more than 6,000 seafarers stranded**, and **more than 70 verified attacks** on international shipping. It is the first published count of the human cost borne by merchant crews, a population that appears in no belligerent's casualty figures.

**Oil prints for August 28 diverged and are logged rather than resolved.** TradingEconomics carried **Brent at $88.22**, down **0.34%** on the day, up **0.15%** over the month and up **30.73%** year on year. *Al Jazeera*'s six-month compilation carried **$88.58**. *Fortune* recorded **$90.55** at **6:30 a.m. Eastern Time**, up **$0.87 or 0.97%** on the day and up **32.75%** year on year. The **range of record for August 28 is $88.22-$90.55**. The attributed causes are diplomatic rather than supply-driven: signs of diplomatic progress and improving supply prospects through the Strait following the Iran-Oman revenue-sharing report. There has been **no strike inside Iran since August 1**, a **twenty-eighth consecutive night**, so the price continues to track sanctions and diplomacy rather than supply events.

**Ground rung — one datapoint that is new in kind, one structural constraint that is the strongest material evidence yet logged, and three counter-indicators.** *The new-in-kind datapoint is the presidential statement above.* *The structural constraint is the depletion ledger:* an amphibious lodgement or the seizure of a defended offshore terminal is the **most air- and missile-defence-intensive** option on the escalation ladder, requiring layered coverage of the objective, the sea base and the sustainment chain simultaneously and for as long as the position is held — and the covering force has been drawn down by half. *The logistics picture moved backwards:* sustainment has been pushed roughly **2,500 nautical miles** away from the objective by enemy action, the inverse of the accumulation that precedes a landing. *The carrier picture is unchanged and the new detail sharpens it:* the **USS Theodore Roosevelt** (CVN-71), with roughly **5,000 crew**, sails from **San Diego within weeks** on a deployment of **more than seven months** with crews told to expect about **eight**, makes a **September port call in Thailand**, and is **not expected in the Arabian Sea until the second half of September** — to **relieve** the **USS George Washington**, not to join it. No additional American combat power arrives in theatre for roughly three weeks, and when it does it replaces rather than adds; the Navy is meanwhile exploring **additional port calls in Africa, India and Singapore** to sustain crew morale on lengthening deployments. *The counter-indicators are logged without discount:* **(1)** a **third** carrier strike group is being generated for this theatre inside seven months; **(2)** the **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group** — USS Boxer (LHD-4), USS Portland (LPD-27), USS Comstock (LSD-45) — with approximately **2,200-2,500 Marines** of the **11th MEU** remains in the **Arabian Sea** on its **60th day** with no publicly reported tasking, a preserved and not foreclosed amphibious option and the single formation whose movement would change the tracker's status fastest; **(3)** the declared American objective remains the **collapse of the Iranian government**, and the President described Iran on August 28 as having **"very little capacity"** — the class of assessment that has historically preceded a decisive move. *Two standing indicators returned negative:* **Kharg Island** was **not seized, not targeted and not mentioned** — its western terminal resumed loading on **August 12** after a 25-day shutdown and operates under blockade conditions rather than American control, roughly **150 days** after the reported March discussion of putting ground forces on it — and the **USS Tripoli** (LHA-7) remains last logged **in port at Sasebo, Japan**, outside CENTCOM entirely. *The draft rung is unchanged:* automatic **Selective Service** registration for men aged 18-26 takes effect on **December 18, 2026** under an NDAA requirement passed before the war, automating registration only; a draft requires a further **act of Congress** that no one has requested; polling records **77%** of Americans opposed to conscription or unsure against **23%** in support. **Every execution indicator remains at zero for a 184th consecutive day.** Total US force presence in the CENTCOM region remains approximately **50,000** service members, **none of them inside Iran**.

### Russia-Ukraine — Moscow Strikes Kyiv for a Second Straight Day While American Intelligence Concludes Russia Reads the Iran War as Weakness (August 27-28, 2026)

**The strike war ran a second consecutive day against the capital region.** Overnight into **August 28** Russia launched **164 Shahed-type drones** against Ukraine, **half of them jet-powered**, of which Ukrainian air defences intercepted **137**. The attacks hit **more than a dozen** apartment buildings and storage depots across the **Kyiv region**, damaging **14 warehouses, 16 private houses, three apartment buildings and 16 vehicles**, **killing one person** and **wounding two**. On **August 27** prolonged air-raid alerts had effectively **locked the capital down for fifteen hours**, choking economic activity and disrupting civilian life. Ukrainian officials characterise the renewed targeting of the power grid as the annual campaign to **"weaponize winter."** Ukraine's **Ministry of Economy** is revising its **2026 GDP growth forecast down from about 1.3% to 0.8%** on the impact of the strike campaign.

**The intelligence channel was disclosed in full, and its limits with it.** CIA Director **John Ratcliffe's** unannounced Moscow visit — reported on **August 25** and confirmed by the Kremlin on **August 26** — involved talks with FSB Director **Alexander Bortnikov** in which Ratcliffe delivered a **pessimistic American assessment** of the war's course for Russia and urged the Kremlin to begin genuine negotiations **before** its military and economic position deteriorates further. *The New York Times* reported on **August 28** that Ratcliffe made **no threat of consequences** should Putin choose to continue the war. Before meeting Bortnikov, Ratcliffe spoke with his **Ukrainian** counterparts, assuring them he would be exploring Russian positions rather than making concessions on Ukraine's behalf. President **Trump** told *Axios* that **Putin will not attack NATO** territories, downplaying the visit's significance.

**The two wars were linked explicitly by American intelligence for the first time in the open record.** *The Washington Post* reported on **August 27** that fresh US intelligence indicates **Russia views America as weakened by the Iran war** and sees an opportunity to escalate. This briefing has tracked the interceptor-depletion and force-allocation consequences of the Iran campaign as a matter of American capability; this is the first reported assessment that an adversary is reading the same facts as an invitation. It is corroborated materially by the **"beyond critical"** European interceptor shortages attributed to the Iran war in the same week. It is logged with its qualification: an intelligence assessment of another government's perception, reported by a newspaper, is not an observed Russian action.

**The mobilisation rung moved in Moscow while it stayed static in Washington.** On **August 27** Ukraine's **Defence Intelligence** and **Foreign Intelligence Service** reported that the **Russian General Staff** has prepared a plan for the **additional mobilisation of 600,000 people across 2026-2027**. The claim is Ukrainian intelligence describing Russian planning and is logged as such rather than as a confirmed Russian decision. The contrast with the American record is the relevant one for this briefing: on the same day a 600,000-person Russian mobilisation plan was reported, the United States had no draft order, no call-up legislation and no request for either. **Net Russian territorial gains for 2026 remain 81.1 square kilometres** and the line is effectively static; the war is being prosecuted through the air and against infrastructure rather than through manoeuvre.

### Gulf States — The Six-Month Bill Comes Due and It Is Denominated in GDP (August 2026)

**The economic reckoning sorts the region by geography rather than by alignment.** **Qatar** and **Kuwait** are forecast to suffer the deepest fallout of any Gulf states, with both economies expected to **contract** across 2026 — **Qatar by 8.6%** — because both depend most heavily on energy exports that must pass through Hormuz and neither has an alternative coastline. **Oman**, whose waters carry the residual traffic and whose ports absorb diverted cargo, is the region's **fastest-growing** economy at **3.5%** despite a slight downgrade. **Saudi Arabia** and the **UAE** have partly escaped, the first through pipeline capacity and a Red Sea coast, the second through re-export infrastructure, both through large non-oil sectors. This is the same asymmetry the **August 27** port-call data showed — **Kuwait -86%**, **UAE -69%**, **Qatar, Iraq and Bahrain -66 to -68%**, **Saudi Arabia -15%** — restated as national income.

**The infrastructure bill is long-dated and the service economy took the visible damage.** Repairing the **Ras Laffan** complex, which produces roughly **5% of the world's natural gas and 20% of its LNG** and was struck in March, is estimated to take **up to five years**; total Middle East infrastructure repair costs are put at approximately **$58 billion**. The **World Travel and Tourism Council** expects the Gulf to shed about **137,000 tourism jobs** this year, **46,000** of them in the UAE alone, against an estimated **$600 million a day** in lost regional visitor spending. Airline capacity fell more than a **third** in April and has recovered to roughly **5% below normal** by August. Dubai property launches fell nearly **90%** between the first and second quarters; the emirate recorded **86,000 residential sales** between January and June, **down almost 13%** year on year. Most Gulf equity indexes proved resilient, with Dubai and Qatar the exceptions at double-digit declines and the Saudi index outperforming. **War-risk insurance has risen sharply** and cargo continues to shift toward **Omani and UAE ports**, with energy companies investing in pipelines and other chokepoint-bypass infrastructure.

**The American financial campaign reached a Gulf financial centre for the first time.** The **Banque Misr** action is treated in full above; its significance for the Gulf is jurisdictional rather than institutional. The target is an Egyptian bank, but the conduct and the branches are **in the UAE**, and the action establishes that Operation Economic Outcast will reach into Emirati financial infrastructure. Treasury simultaneously targeted the **UAE branch manager of Bank Melli**. **Qatar's mediation**, following Prime Minister **Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani's** **August 27** Tehran visit pressing for freedom of navigation and a return to pre-war status, produced the cycle's one piece of diplomatic movement: Tehran's agreement to write its conditions down. **The Gulf's six-month share of the human cost is 28 killed.**

### Other Theatres — Chinese Banks Spared Again, a Taiwanese Drone Budget Voted Down, a Quiet Peninsula, and a Second Silent Cycle in Latin America (August 27-28, 2026)

**US-China.** The escalation the previous cycle flagged as pending was executed against a different target. The **August 28** FinCEN action severed the **UAE branches of an Egyptian bank** from US correspondent banking — demonstrating that the instrument exists, functions, and can be applied to a foreign bank's overseas branches without designating the institution itself — while **China's major banks were spared for the second consecutive package**, with reporting attributing the restraint to reluctance to penalise **major trading partners including China and India**. Asked directly why he had not sanctioned Chinese banks, Trump replied: **"Who said I'm not? You don't know if I'm doing it. I don't have to announce everything, do I?"** — a non-answer that neither confirms a covert measure nor rules one out, and no such designation has appeared in Treasury material. **The material position is that Beijing is already paying without being designated:** Chinese imports of Iranian crude have fallen **48%** since the war began, from a base in which China accounted for roughly **90%** of Iran's sanctioned oil exports. Foreign Ministry spokesman **Lin Jian**'s position is unchanged — **"sanctions and pressure tactics are not the solution"**; China will **"take all necessary measures to safeguard its own interests firmly"** — and where the United States has designated independent Chinese refineries, Beijing has **ordered its companies to ignore** the restrictions. Retaliation has been promised in general terms and not specified.

**Taiwan.** On **August 27** Taiwan's **opposition-controlled parliament rejected a $6.6 billion drone procurement budget** and **approved a $7.6 billion alternative spending plan** in its place. The shape of this is worth stating precisely: **total defence spending rose** while the specific **asymmetric-defence capability** US planning has emphasised for Taiwan was **voted down**. No Chinese military action followed and no change in cross-Strait military posture was reported.

**DPRK.** A **ninth consecutive day without a launch**. No North Korean missile activity has been reported since roughly **ten KN-25 short-range ballistic missiles** were fired on **August 20** — a barrage launched after Pyongyang dismissed an American overture — and North Korea has still not publicised those launches domestically. The analytical consensus hardened this cycle and is unusually uniform: *Foreign Policy* published on **August 27** under a title that states the conclusion, **"Why North Korea's Kim Jong Un Won't Meet With Trump,"** arguing that Kim is in a **far stronger negotiating position than in 2019** and sees little need for US sanctions relief or a summit; the **Korea Economic Institute of America** and *Asia Times* reached the same conclusion independently. **The American concessions are real and unreciprocated:** Trump ordered the Pentagon in mid-August to **scale back joint exercises with South Korea**, calling the drills **"hostile"** toward Pyongyang and citing his **"very good relationship"** with Kim, and has since **cancelled another** joint exercise. **Kim Yo Jong** described the personal relationship as **"excellent"** while stating that scaling back **Ulchi Freedom Shield** had **not changed** what she views as the United States' hostile policy, and **denied** that Trump and Kim have been in recent contact. Seoul's reported anxiety is that it is being **sidelined** in decisions about its own defence.

**Latin America.** A second consecutive quiet cycle; the record is carried forward rather than inflated. **Cuba**: **six nationwide collapses** of the national electricity system in 2026 — twice in March, three times within ten days in July, and once on **August 2-3**, when thunderstorms disrupted the restoration attempt and produced two nationwide outages within hours — with scheduled blackouts **exceeding twenty hours a day**, parts of **Havana** dark for more than **twenty-four** consecutive hours and some rural communities for more than **seventy**. Since **January** the United States has permitted exactly **one oil tanker — Russian — to dock** in Cuba. **Venezuela**: **Delcy Rodríguez** has held the acting presidency since **January 5**; **131 political prisoners** were released on **August 15** under talks led by **Dinorah Figuera** and National Assembly President **Jorge Rodríguez**; and **no electoral calendar, new electoral authority or constitutional timetable** has been announced — the basis of the **"normalization without transition"** critique. **Nicolás Maduro** and **Cilia Flores** remain in US custody with trial set for **June 1, 2027**, both having pleaded not guilty and both disputing the court's legitimacy. No new Colombian development was reported.

**Hormuz-dependent economies and the American price level.** At six months the blockade has sorted the importing world by **days of storage** and **fiscal capacity to subsidise**. **Bangladesh** is the worst-placed: negligible reserves, **university closures**, fuel rationing, appeals for international assistance, and **four of its five state-run fertiliser factories halted** so their gas can keep power plants running — a government choosing electricity now over the next agricultural season's inputs, and the clearest indicator that costs have moved from prices into **physical allocation**. **Pakistan** has passed the shock through with an **Rs 55-per-litre** increase on petrol and diesel. **India** is absorbing it as **food and essentials inflation** rather than rationing. **Japan** and **South Korea** carry critical **LNG deficits** from Qatari and Emirati supply, and of the two only **South Korea** has answered with concrete renewable-expansion plans. In the **United States**, the AAA national average stands at **$4.090** a gallon with **August 2026 on course to be the highest August on record** — the month-to-date average of **$4.06** surpassing 2022's **$3.97** — and the **Strategic Petroleum Reserve** at **290 million barrels, 41% of capacity, the lowest since 1982**. With a presidential approval rating of **33%** and midterms in November, that is the clearest measurable domestic constraint on the blockade's duration in the record.
