## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 27-28 (DAY 183): THE STRAIT THAT WAS DECLARED CLEARED WAS ATTACKED AGAIN, AND THE UNITED STATES ANSWERED BY BUILDING A COURT. UKMTO WARNING 121-26 RECORDED A TANKER STRUCK BY AN UNKNOWN PROJECTILE THIRTY-SIX HOURS AFTER THE 'ZERO TOLERANCE' DEMINING DECLARATION — A PROJECTILE, NOT A MINE. THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT IS REVIVING CIVIL WAR-ERA MARITIME PRIZE COURTS TO CONDEMN SEIZED IRANIAN TANKERS AS US PROPERTY, WITH PROCEEDS TO THE TREASURY. QATAR'S PRIME MINISTER BECAME THE THIRD MEDIATOR IN FOUR DAYS AND THE IRANIAN PRICE DID NOT MOVE, WHILE A SENIOR IRANIAN SOURCE SAID THE OMAN AGREEMENT 'HAS NOT BEEN FINALIZED.' THE WHITE HOUSE SAID THERE ARE NO TALKS SCHEDULED. AL JAZEERA MEASURED TRANSITS AT FIVE A DAY AGAINST A HUNDRED-A-DAY BASELINE. GROUND RUNG: THE CARRIER FORCE IS BEING ROTATED, NOT MASSED, AND EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR IS AT ZERO FOR A 183RD DAY.

**The attack came thirty-six hours after the declaration, and the weapon matters.** At **06:35 GMT on August 27** the **United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations** centre issued **Warning 121-26**: a tanker transiting the **Strait of Hormuz** was **hit by an unknown projectile**, causing a fire that has since been extinguished, with **no casualties**, **no environmental damage** and the crew reported safe; vessels were advised to transit with caution. It was the **second vessel struck in the waterway this week**. The attack landed thirty-six hours after President Trump declared every mine cleared from the Strait's international waters and announced a **"Zero Tolerance"** rule under which *"any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed."* **The distinction this briefing records is that the weapon was a projectile, not a mine.** The demining claim is therefore not falsified by the attack. What the attack falsifies is the inference from it — and it confirms, within forty-eight hours, the assessment of Ambrey's **Alex Almeida** that mines *"have never been the primary threat,"* the greater danger being drones and anti-ship cruise and ballistic missiles. **No US strike, boarding operation or force movement was announced in response within the cycle.**

**The American instrument of the cycle was a court.** *Bloomberg* reported on **August 26** that the **Justice Department** is preparing to activate **maritime prize courts** — dormant since the **Second World War** and of negligible use since the **Spanish-American War of 1898** — to give federal prosecutors a faster route to condemn **oil and other cargo taken from enemy or neutral vessels** as **United States property**, to be **sold with proceeds transferred to the Treasury**. **Aaron Reitz**, the Houston-based US attorney whose office is partnering with department headquarters, confirmed that DOJ is **"now reviving"** what he described as an **"ancient body of maritime law."** The stated purposes are to **strengthen the blockade of Iran** and to **offset the cost of the conflict**. The reported trigger is procedural: in the ongoing case of a **seized Venezuelan supertanker** that supported Iran, DOJ filed a civil complaint seeking to liquidate ship and cargo, and multiple third parties — the shipping company and families of Iranian terrorism victims — have intervened and bogged the process down. The plans are described as **unfinalised**. **For an audit tracking a predicted ground seizure of the chokepoint, this is a class of evidence not previously available: institutional.** A state that expects to resolve a waterway by taking it does not spend the interval rebuilding nineteenth-century admiralty procedure. Prize courts are what a belligerent builds when it expects to be interdicting shipping for years and wants the proceeds.

**Diplomacy moved, and then one government contradicted itself.** Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister **Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani** spent **August 27** in Tehran, meeting Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi**, President **Masoud Pezeshkian**, Parliament Speaker **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf** and security chief **Mohsen Rezai**. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baghaei** said the talks covered the continuation of Qatar's mediation and wider regional developments. The published agenda was the proposed Hormuz framework — a **temporary shipping corridor** and a **joint mine-clearing operation** — together with *"efforts being made to reduce escalation"* and the creation of conditions for renewed US-Iran dialogue. Sheikh Mohammed said **"dialogue and diplomatic solutions remain the optimal path for addressing disputes,"** stressing respect for freedom of navigation in accordance with international law. **Rezai** gave the Iranian price without softening it: the United States **"must first take practical steps to fulfil Iran's conditions"** — lift the naval blockade, unfreeze assets, remove oil sanctions. **This is the third mediator through Tehran in four days**, after Pakistan's **Field Marshal Asim Munir** on **August 24** and Oman's **Badr Albusaidi** on **August 25**, and Qatar carries particular standing, having brokered the June arrangement that briefly halted hostilities. Three mediators, one unchanged price.

**And the corridor itself was put back in doubt from inside Iran.** A **senior Iranian source** told *Reuters* on **August 27** that the agreement with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz **"has not been finalized."** That came one day after IRGC spokesman Brigadier General **Hossein Mohebbi** said the two countries had agreed **"each country's share of the strait's waters and Iran and Oman's share of its revenues"** and that **"the Strait of Hormuz belongs to Iran and the Sultanate of Oman,"** and two days after the two foreign ministries announced a **"phased framework."** Oman has issued **no public confirmation or denial** of the revenue-sharing characterisation. **The contradiction is internal to the Iranian state and this briefing logs it rather than resolving it**: the IRGC and the diplomatic apparatus are describing the same instrument at different stages of completion, and no text has been published by either party.

**Washington closed the door it had left ajar.** The White House said on **August 27** that there are **"no talks or conversations"** going on or scheduled with Iran. President **Trump**: **"We don't want to speak to them. We're not looking to meet or anything."** Press Secretary **Karoline Leavitt** described the strategy: the administration is **"continuing to pull every economic lever,"** and **"the naval blockade continues to be in effect as well, which has proven hugely successful."** On negotiations: **"No negotiations are happening right now, and this will continue until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way."** On Iran's condition, in figures the Iranian government does not publish: **"Inflation is over 100%. They can't pay their police. They can't pay their military."** Reporting the same day indicated the administration is **no longer interested in reviving the June 17 memorandum of understanding**, having told mediating states it will not accept the previous terms after concluding the Iranians had *"burned"* it repeatedly.

**The traffic data landed against the President's own number, and the gap is now an order of magnitude.** *Al Jazeera* published a consolidated dataset on **August 27** measuring the closure's effect on global shipping. Transits ran at **about five vessels a day between July 15 and August 23** against a pre-war baseline of about **100 a day** — a fall of **nearly 95%**. **Gulf crude exports are down 47%**, from roughly **17 million barrels a day to about 9 million**; direct crude through the strait averages **2.2 million barrels a day**; analysts estimate **5-7 million barrels a day** of supply disrupted; and combined Gulf shipments fell from about **400 million barrels in February to about 200 million in July**. The strait carries **33% of global seaborne crude oil** and **29% of LPG flows**, and 80% of world trade by volume moves by sea. Port calls by country: **Kuwait -86%**; **UAE -69%**, from 78 daily calls to 24; **Qatar, Iraq and Bahrain -66 to -68%**; **Saudi Arabia only -15%**, because it alone has pipeline capacity and a Red Sea coast. **Richard Matthews**, director at Gibson Shipbrokers, stated the structural finding without hedge: **"There is no alternative maritime route. There are some pipelines, but there's no alternative."** **This sits directly against the President's own figure.** On **August 26**, on the Glenn Beck programme, Trump said **ten million barrels** passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday and that the waterway is *"functioning,"* qualified only by the observation that *"every once in a while there will be a drone or a rocket or something shot."* **Ten million barrels across about five hulls would require roughly two million barrels per vessel — some six times the capacity of a VLCC.** Either the presidential figure counts barrels leaving the Gulf by **all routes**, including pipeline bypass and US-escorted convoys, rather than hulls transiting the strait, or it is not a measurement; the administration has published no methodology. The same gap is visible one step back, in Energy Secretary **Chris Wright's** August 11 claim of about **15 million barrels a day** out of the Gulf with a seven-day Hormuz average near **9 million**, against an **IEA 2025 baseline of 19.87 million** and JMIC counts of **42 US-facilitated transits over August 9-10** versus roughly **138 a day** historically. This briefing carries both series and adjudicates neither.

**The market diverged within a single session and the divergence is logged rather than resolved.** TradingEconomics carried **Brent at $89.48 on August 27, up $1.86 or 2.12%**, which would break the three-session slide; the same service's own market commentary described Brent **"slipping toward $87 on Thursday, extending its decline to a fourth straight session"** on signs of diplomatic progress, and carried Brent just below **$89** on August 26 after two consecutive declines. *Fox News Digital* carried crude **"near $82 Thursday, maintaining losses for the third consecutive day,"** and a separate WTI blurb had crude falling toward **$81** on a fourth straight session. **The range of record for August 27 is therefore Brent $87-$89.48 and WTI $81-$82.** What every print agrees on is the attributed cause, and it is de-escalatory in every case: the Iran-Oman revenue-sharing report, Trump's ten-million-barrel claim, and a sanctions package that spared Iran's trading partners and was judged less aggressive than markets had feared. **The tanker attack priced into none of them.** Levels remain roughly 20% above the pre-crisis baseline near $72 and far below the ~$126-130 April wartime peak.

**Iran's home front was described by its own government as a red alert.** Executive Vice-President **Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah** said domestic gasoline production is insufficient to meet consumption and that the **American naval blockade prevents imports**; strategic fuel reserves are described internally as at **red alert**, with remaining stocks potentially exhausted **within weeks**. Car queues blocked streets in parts of **Tehran** and **Mashhad** on Tuesday and Wednesday. A **price increase and a rationing scheme** have been signalled within weeks, against an existing tier structure whose lowest band is **15,000 rials a litre** with further bands at **30,000** and **50,000**. The rial holds at its record of roughly **2.06 million to the dollar** on the open market against an official rate near **1.5 million**, with inflation at almost **90%** by the government's own **Statistical Center** — against the White House figure of *"over 100%."* *Iran International* reported **disagreement between President Pezeshkian and the Revolutionary Guard** over drawing down the fuel reserve. Pezeshkian addressed the **40th International Islamic Unity Conference** in Tehran on **August 27**.

**The war aim was stated in its maximal form by a third party, and questioned by a non-fringe analyst in the same cycle.** Former Mossad chief **Barnea** said on **August 27** that there is **"no choice"** but to keep striking Iran **"until the regime falls — and it will fall."** That stands alongside Treasury Secretary **Bessent's** August 24 statement that *"it is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime,"* and against Leavitt's framing three days later that pressure continues *"until the president feels that maybe they come to the table."* **Ali Vaez** of the International Crisis Group put the question directly, describing a possible **"financial apocalypse"** strategy and asking whether this is *"a zero-sum campaign aimed at collapsing the regime, or leverage towards an agreement."* **A regime that has collapsed cannot come to the table; a regime being brought to the table is not being collapsed.** The question is entered in the open-questions register as `us-war-aim-regime-collapse-or-leverage-august-2026` and is not resolved here.

**Lebanon.** On **August 27** the IDF launched a wave of strikes on Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon, shortly after confirming that the group had launched **two explosive drones** at Israeli soldiers operating inside the security zone in south-eastern Lebanon. The **Lebanese Health Ministry** reported **one woman killed and six wounded, including a child**. Cumulative Lebanese civilian deaths remain **4,346** with **12,301 wounded**; Israel continues to hold roughly **20% of Lebanese territory**.

**The ledger.** The Pentagon's published toll is **unchanged at 776 US casualties — 18 killed and 758 wounded** — with no new addition reported in this cycle. About **345 casualties** have occurred since **July 7**, approximately 44% of the war's total in under two months. The service split of record remains **more than 580 Army, 86 Navy, 64 Air Force and 19 Marines**. *The Intercept*'s undercount dispute stands unchanged: at least one officially recognised death is omitted from the Defense Casualty Analysis System, and a US government official described the Pentagon's revised counting method as *"designed to obscure the count."* CENTCOM published **no new blockade tally**; the figure of record remains **71 commercial vessels redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded** since the July 14 resumption, plus more than 40 humanitarian vessels permitted through.

**Ground rung — one force-generation datapoint that is the strongest structural evidence since April, one institutional datapoint that is new in kind, three counter-indicators, and no execution indicator.** *The force-generation datapoint is a rotation.* The **USS Abraham Lincoln** departed the CENTCOM area of responsibility on **August 22** after a deployment exceeding **200 days**. The **USS George Washington** entered the Fifth Fleet area in the week of **August 20**, having deployed from Japan to relieve it. And the **USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group** will deploy from **San Diego within weeks** to relieve the George Washington in turn, on a deployment expected to run **at least seven months** with crews told to plan for **eight**. The United States has maintained a **continuous carrier presence in the Arabian Sea since late February**. **The net effect is one carrier sustained on station** — against the **two** CENTCOM cited publicly in July and the **three-carrier posture** logged in April as a candidate invasion-staging signature. Amphibious and ground-assault operations are preceded by **concentration**; this is **relief-in-place**, and the eight-month planning horizon carries the posture into 2027, consistent with the previous cycle's *Axios* report that the non-kinetic posture is expected to hold until after the midterm elections. *The institutional datapoint* is the prize-court revival treated in full above. *The White House named its own instruments and a landing force was not among them*: **"continuing to pull every economic lever"** and **"the naval blockade... proven hugely successful."** *The counter-indicators, logged without discount:* **(1)** a **third** carrier strike group is being generated for one theatre inside seven months, and the capability being sustained is a strike capability that a decision could redirect; **(2)** the **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group** — USS **Boxer** (LHD-4), USS **Portland** (LPD-27) and USS **Comstock** (LSD-45) with approximately **2,200 Camp Pendleton Marines** of the **11th Marine Expeditionary Unit** — remains in the **Arabian Sea** on its **59th day** in theatre with **no publicly reported tasking**, which preserves rather than forecloses an amphibious option; **(3)** a former Mossad chief has publicly demanded strikes **"until the regime falls,"** alongside a Treasury Secretary who has already declared regime collapse the objective, and a declared collapse aim is the class of war aim that historically produces ground commitment when economic instruments fail. *Two standing indicators returned negative and are recorded explicitly:* **Kharg Island** was **not seized, not targeted and not mentioned** — its western terminal was reactivated on **August 12** after a 25-day shutdown, with a VLCC berthed for the first time since **July 18**, and no sustained export recovery has been confirmed; and the **USS Tripoli (LHA-7)** is **in port at Sasebo, Japan**, outside CENTCOM entirely. *The draft rung is unchanged with one point of new precision*: automatic Selective Service registration of males aged 18-26 is now dated to **December 18, 2026**, which builds the registration **pool** and confers **no induction authority** — no lottery, no call-up, no congressional induction measure, and no administration official has raised conscription in connection with Iran at any point in the war. **A twenty-seventh consecutive night passed with no confirmed US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory. Every execution indicator remains at zero on a 183rd day: no mobilisation order, no reserve call-up, no hospital-ship movement, no casualty-reception surge, no reported forward fuel or ammunition prepositioning, no ROE change enabling ground action, no congressional authorisation sought, and no ground-operation statement from the Pentagon.**

### Russia-Ukraine — The Moscow Agenda Is Disclosed and It Links the Two Wars, While Ukraine Takes Russia's Fourth-Largest Refinery Offline (August 26-27, 2026)

**The agenda of the unannounced visit was disclosed.** CIA Director **John Ratcliffe's** **August 25** trip to Moscow — the first publicly known visit to the Russian capital by a sitting US intelligence chief since **William Burns** met Putin in **November 2021** — was reported on **August 27** to have carried two messages. **First**, a warning to Russian officials not to take actions that could escalate tensions with US allies in NATO, naming **Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania**. **Second**, a request that Russia **reduce its military and economic support for Iran**. The underlying assessment reported alongside it is that Russia may attempt to **test NATO's readiness to respond to limited aggression** in the coming years — through a limited military operation or a hybrid attack against a member state — with the **Baltic states among the most likely targets**. Kremlin spokesman **Dmitry Peskov** confirmed that Ratcliffe met representatives of Russian intelligence agencies **but not Putin**, who was briefed on the results of the talks. President **Trump** called the trip **"semi-routine"** and said it might be linked to efforts to end the war in Ukraine; Ratcliffe visited the White House on his return to brief him. **This is the clearest public evidence to date that Washington is running the Iran and Ukraine files through a single channel** — one meeting, one intelligence chief, a NATO deterrence message and an Iran decoupling request. It also fixes a boundary: the message was *don't attack NATO*, not a settlement proposal, and the Ukraine channel itself remains shut, with Peskov having said on **August 25** that there were **no plans** for talks with Witkoff or Kushner.

**The strike war ran through the visit.** Overnight into **August 27** Russia attacked **Kyiv** and other Ukrainian cities with **ballistic missiles and drones**. Several consecutive explosions were heard in Kyiv around **3 a.m.** local time, with at least six inside about a minute, injuring **at least seven people**. Foreign Minister **Andrii Sybiha** said the strikes targeted **warehouses, ports, and energy and industrial facilities**. Ukrainian air defences downed **seven ballistic missiles, one anti-ship cruise missile and nearly 90% of the drones** — an interception performance materially better than the ballistic-defence figures President Zelensky attributed to an interceptor deficit earlier in August.

**Ukraine's campaign reached the Russian refining base.** Ukrainian drones struck the **NORSI** refinery at **Kstovo** in **Nizhny Novgorod Oblast** overnight on **August 26**, sparking a large fire. NORSI is **Russia's fourth-largest refinery and second-largest gasoline producer**, and it **suspended crude oil processing** after the attack — the plant's **fifth drone-related shutdown in less than five months**. Separate reporting on **August 27** held that Ukrainian drones have now shut **all major Lukoil refineries** in Russia. This is the deep-strike campaign moving from disruption to cumulative capacity denial in Russian domestic fuel supply. **Ukraine incurred a civilian-harm entry of its own in the same window**: a Ukrainian strike hit a **bus in Russian-controlled Luhansk, killing nine people**. This briefing logs it in the same register as Russian strikes on civilians, without equivalence claims and without omission.

**Other movement.** EU member states are planning a renewed effort to leverage **frozen Russian sovereign assets** to fund Ukraine. President **Zelensky** awarded **Elon Musk** the **Order of Freedom** for Starlink's battlefield communications support. **Net Russian gains for 2026 remain 81.1 square kilometres** and the line is effectively static. **No NATO member has committed ground troops to Ukraine and none was requested in this cycle.**

### Gulf States — Doha Takes Its Turn in Tehran and a Greek Patriot Battery Defends Saudi Oil (August 27, 2026)

**Qatar's mediation is treated in full above.** The Gulf's kinetic event of the cycle was defensive and European-operated. On **August 27** an air-defence system operated by **Greek military personnel** in Saudi Arabia engaged a **swarm of drones** in the wider **Yanbu** region, which contains major oil-refining facilities. The Greek **Patriot** battery launched **three missiles** and intercepted **three Houthi unmanned aerial vehicles**, operating in **full coordination with the air-defence systems of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia**. It was the **third combat use** of the Greek-operated system since the Iran war began. **Two things follow.** First, **Yanbu is the Red Sea terminus of the East-West pipeline**, the principal Saudi route around Hormuz — so the bypass that has kept Saudi port calls down only **15%**, against **86%** for Kuwait and **69%** for the UAE, is itself now a target set. Second, the interceptor was European and the target was Houthi: air defence of Gulf energy infrastructure has become a **multinational undertaking without a multinational command**.

**The commercial workarounds remain the region's operating model.** ADNOC is running a shuttle service with **transponders off**; Saudi Arabia is running **ship-to-ship transfers with government-backed insurance**; and TankerTrackers has counted **more than fifteen ship-to-ship operations moving about 25 million barrels** in the Gulf of Oman, from *"every country in the region, minus Iran."* War-risk insurance holds at **7.5-10% of hull value** against 1-3% before the war. Qatar's production position is unchanged: the IMF April vintage projects **-14.7% for 2026**, with roughly **17% of LNG export capacity lost** and about **$20bn of annual revenue foregone** since the March Ras Laffan strike.

### Other Theatres — Chinese Banks, a Cyber Indictment, the Overstretch Thesis From Inside the Pentagon, and a Quiet Peninsula (August 27-28, 2026)

**US-China.** Reporting on **August 27** indicated the administration is considering **sanctions against Chinese banks** conducting business with Iran — the specific escalation that **Operation Economic Outcast** held back on August 24, when five sectoral determinations and nearly 60 designations were issued but **most secondary sanctions were deferred behind a "cure period"** and no partner country was named. Designating a Chinese financial institution would convert a deferred threat into an act, and it is the measure against which **Lin Jian's** pledge that *"China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests"* would actually be tested. On the same day the **Justice Department** announced that **Chinese hackers** carried out a string of intrusions targeting **federal agencies and hospitals** over the past year, mostly linked to the state-sponsored group **QTFY**. And **Pentagon officials** were reported concerned that a **prolonged Iran conflict could embolden China in the Indo-Pacific** — the overstretch thesis, attributed for the first time in this record to **serving officials in the department running the war** rather than to outside commentators. It is a concern, not a policy, and is logged at that weight. The underlying volumes continue to fall without any designation having bitten: **Kpler** puts Chinese imports of Iranian crude through Hormuz at about **530,000 barrels a day — 48% below pre-war and 72% below the October 2024 peak** of 1.9 million. The tariff track is unchanged: the **7.5% Section 301 overcapacity tariff** remains prepared ahead of the **September 24 Xi-Trump summit**; the November 2025 truce expires **November 10, 2026**; the USTR's **12.5% forced-labour tariff** on all Chinese goods has been in force since **July 24**; and the Commerce Department's BIS closed comments on **August 27** on expanding the Section 232 product list for steel, aluminium and copper. **Taiwan**: no escalation; the **15%** US tariff rate agreed in January stands and PLA sortie rates remain at the pre-Lai baseline.

**DPRK.** An **eighth consecutive day without a launch**. No North Korean missile activity has been reported since roughly **ten KN-25 short-range ballistic missiles** were fired on **August 20** during the closing phase of the US-South Korea exercise, and Pyongyang has still **not publicised that launch domestically**. The **August 25 enlarged Politburo meeting** of the Workers' Party Central Committee, reported on **August 26**, reviewed major economic sectors and 2026 policy goals, with **Kim Jong Un** calling for *"extraordinary responsibility and high prudence"* and citing *"a series of deviations"* caused by *"the immature operation and leadership of the economic guidance organs"* — and made **no reference to President Trump's renewed overture or to a possible summit**. **August 27** was the date on which **Ulchi Freedom Shield's counteroffensive phase** was originally scheduled to end; it never took place, the eleven-day two-phase exercise having been **cut to five days** as a goodwill gesture and ended on **August 21**. **That date has now passed without a DPRK acknowledgement, a launch, or a summit date.** A concession was made, a provocation was withheld, and nothing has been built on either.

**Latin America.** No new Cuban grid collapse and no new Venezuelan rationing measure was reported, so the figures of record stand. **Cuba**: **six nationwide collapses in 2026** — twice in March, three times within ten days in July, once on **August 2-3**, when thunderstorms disrupted the restoration attempt and produced two nationwide outages within hours — with blackouts **exceeding twenty hours a day** and some communities at up to **105 consecutive days** without steady power, and neighbourhood protests in Havana municipalities after outages beyond forty-eight hours. **Venezuela**: pot-banging protests continue over recurring blackouts and appliance damage from voltage fluctuation, with road blockades and burning tyres in **Turmero, Aragua**, against daily cuts of four to five hours; acting President **Delcy Rodríguez's** national electricity and water savings plan, blamed on **"Super Niño"** and an earthquake, remains openly rejected; the Caracas talks opened **August 6** under **Jorge Rodríguez** and **Dinorah Figuera** continue with **no published electoral timetable**. **Maduro** and **Cilia Flores** remain in US custody with trial set for **June 1, 2027** on four counts including narco-terrorism conspiracy. **Colombia**: the de la Espriella government's hardline programme and severance of ties with Cuba and Nicaragua continue.

**Hormuz-dependent economies and the American price level.** The six-month toll was put into numbers this cycle and the numbers are in the section above: **~5 transits a day against a ~100/day baseline**, **Gulf crude exports -47%**, and **5-7 million barrels a day** disrupted. Rationing is now the normal condition across South and Southeast Asia: **four-day working weeks, work-from-home mandates and school closures** in **Pakistan, Bangladesh, the Philippines, Vietnam and Sri Lanka**; **India** encouraging work from home and restricting foreign travel; **Bangladesh** promoting public transport; **Pakistan** restricting business hours; **Malaysia** encouraging limits on cooling temperatures; and hard purchase caps in **Indonesia (50 litres a day)** and **Sri Lanka (15 litres a day)**. The structural exposure behind those measures: **Bangladesh, India and Pakistan imported almost two-thirds of their total LNG via the Strait of Hormuz in 2025**, and natural gas accounted for **50%** of Bangladesh's and **25%** of Pakistan's electricity mix in 2024; Pakistan imports roughly **85%** of its supply by tanker and Bangladesh about **95%** of its petroleum needs; India, which takes **60%** of its LPG through the strait, is seeing black-marketing of domestic cylinders and restaurant closures. **North Asia is drawing down rather than rationing**: **Japan** takes more than 90% of its crude from the Middle East, about **75% via Hormuz**, holds about **146 days** of reserves and **has been drawing on strategic stocks**; **South Korea** draws about **70%** of its crude and **18%** of its LNG through the strait and holds about **206 days**, with **Lotte Chemical, LG Chem and Hanwha Solutions** having issued potential force majeure notices and **Yeochun NCC** declaring supply disruption. LNG carrier rates run around **$300,000 a day**, a **650% increase**. **The cleanest single measure of incidence published this cycle**: between **February and May 2026** European natural gas prices rose **44%** and Asian prices rose **66%**, while **US prices declined 6%**. In the United States the war is a price index rather than a shortage: the AAA national average for regular stands near **$4.0969**, with August 2026 on course to be the **highest August on record** at a **$4.06** month-to-date average against 2022's $3.97, diesel at successive records, and **July PCE inflation at 3.7%** year on year.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 25-27 (DAY 182): A DOUBLE CYCLE IN WHICH THE UNITED STATES SPENT ITS EFFORT MAKING THE STRAIT NAVIGABLE RATHER THAN TAKING IT. AXIOS REPORTED THAT RUBIO HAS TOLD ALLIED FOREIGN MINISTERS NO NEW STRIKES ARE EXPECTED 'FOR THE TIME BEING,' WITH A SECOND OFFICIAL PUTTING THE HORIZON PAST THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS — THE FIRST DURATION EVER ATTACHED TO THE PAUSE. TRUMP DECLARED THE STRAIT CLEARED OF MINES BY UNDERWATER DRONE AND PRIVATE CONTRACTOR UNDER A 'ZERO TOLERANCE' RULE. IRAN AND OMAN ANNOUNCED A PHASED FRAMEWORK FOR A JOINT TEMPORARY CORRIDOR AND JOINT MINE-CLEARING — THE FIRST DOCUMENT OF THE WAR TO ADDRESS THE STRAIT'S FUTURE ADMINISTRATION, AND WASHINGTON IS NOT A PARTY TO IT. BRENT FELL THREE SESSIONS RUNNING. GROUND RUNG: EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR AT ZERO FOR A 182ND DAY.

**The August 26 update was not run, so this cycle consolidates two days.** Nothing in the interval changed the tracked status; the volume of documented material did.

**The most consequential item of the week is a report, and it attaches a length to the pause.** On **August 25** *Axios*, citing US officials, reported that Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** has told several allied foreign ministers in recent days that **"for the time being"** the United States is **not expected to launch new strikes against Iran** and will instead focus on other means of pressure. Rubio did not rule out strikes if Iran attacks first. **A second official told *Axios* that the posture is expected to remain in place until after the midterm elections**, when another military campaign could again be considered. US officials described Washington's priorities as **sanctions**, **the naval blockade**, and **"moving ever-increasing amounts of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz."** Three instruments were named and none of them is a ground force. This briefing records the report with its full qualification — two unnamed officials describing an unannounced future decision, not an order — and notes that it is entirely compatible with a campaign resuming in November. What it is not compatible with is an imminent landing.

**The instrument the United States actually applied to the chokepoint was an unmanned underwater vehicle and a procurement contract.** On **August 25** President Trump announced on Truth Social that the US Navy has disposed of **all mines** present in the international waters of the Strait of Hormuz, and declared a **"Zero Tolerance"** policy: **"Any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed,"** with the **Space Force** **"watching every square inch"** of the waterway. US officials confirmed the substance: over the last several months US Navy **underwater drones** systematically scanned the **Traffic Separation Scheme** and located **more than 100 objects suspected to be mines**, and the US military **contracted with private companies** to remove or detonate them. **US Central Command began the major mine-clearing operation in April 2026.** Trump separately said the United States had destroyed **all 28 Iranian mine-laying boats**. For a briefing whose central tracked prediction is a US ground seizure of the Strait, the significance is the choice of tool: the physical obstacle at the chokepoint was removed by robots and contractors, and the future obstacle was addressed by a declaratory rule enforced from orbit.

**The clearance claim is disputed and the dispute is recorded rather than resolved.** Deputy Foreign Minister **Kazem Gharibabadi** said **"no one except Iran knows the location"** of the mines and that the announcement was **"only aimed at calming markets."** Independent specialists split the difference: **Mark Hilborne** of King's College London said **"the claim that the mines have been cleared came from CENTCOM initially, and in this we can have strong confidence"** for the main shipping lanes, while cautioning that **"there may be risks beyond the lanes"**; **Alex Almeida** of Ambrey said mines **"have never been the primary threat,"** with drones and anti-ship cruise and ballistic missiles the greater danger. Iran's sea-mine stockpile is estimated at **2,000-6,000**, comprising both moored contact and bottom-sensor types. **The observable consequences have not appeared:** IMF PortWatch recorded **three transits for August 23** and Reuters reported **only two vessels transited on Monday August 24**, the fewest since early May, and **war-risk insurance did not move** from **7.5-10% of hull value** against 1-3% before the war. Commercial workarounds continue — **ADNOC** is offering a shuttle service with **transponders switched off** and **Saudi Arabia** is running ship-to-ship transfers with **government-backed insurance**.

**The future governance of the Strait went into a document, and it was signed by Tehran and Muscat rather than by Washington.** Oman's Foreign Minister **Badr Albusaidi** arrived in Tehran on **August 25** and held consultations with **Abbas Araghchi**. A joint press statement from the two foreign ministries described a **"phased framework"** comprising a **joint temporary navigational corridor** through the Strait of Hormuz and **"an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines,"** with technical talks to continue **"with the aim of reaching agreement on a permanent shipping corridor and the future administration of the Strait,"** plus mechanisms for **information exchange, traffic management and the provision of maritime and security services**. ABC News records the framework as proceeding under **Article 5 of the Islamabad Memorandum**. Albusaidi posted that he was **"hopeful"** the two would **"soon announce a temporary corridor,"** adding that **"future management of the Strait and a permanent solution will follow in due course."** Araghchi posted that the proposal showed **"Iran's commitment to peace and stability is matched by steadfast diplomacy with our neighbours."** Muscat did this eight days after President Trump said on **August 17**: **"If Oman gets in the way, we'll bomb the s\*\*\* out of them."**

**The terms, as Tehran states them, place the waterway under Iranian jurisdiction at the point of entry.** On **August 26** Gharibabadi told state television that Iran and Oman have agreed a **temporary** maritime route: **seven miles (11.3 km) wide**; **entry beginning in Iranian territorial waters**, with part of the exit route also passing through them; vessels requiring **Iranian permission and surveillance** before entry; **military vessels not permitted**; and the arrangement holding while a **permanent** one is negotiated over **30 to 60 days**. **"The agreed-upon transit route with Oman is a temporary route."** He set out the conditions for full reopening: the United States must fulfil its **June 17 MoU** commitments, provide **sanctions relief**, **release frozen Iranian assets** and **end the war**, and Iran demands **war-damage compensation**; he added that **"Washington was mistaken about its ability to enforce sanctions."** IRGC spokesman **Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi** said on **August 26** that negotiations with Oman began about a month earlier and had produced agreement on **"each country's share of the strait's waters and Iran and Oman's share of its revenues,"** declaring that **"the Strait of Hormuz belongs to Iran and the Sultanate of Oman"** and that the United States is obstructing progress. **What remains unpublished is as important as what was announced:** precise route coordinates, a safe-passage start date, revenue-sharing mechanics, which vessels and flags qualify, and any mine-clearing timeline. The White House Deputy Press Secretary said on **August 26** that **no conversations are under way with Tehran**, and the United States has taken no public position on the corridor.

**The enforcement record cut against the diplomacy within a day.** Iran's shipping monitoring agency, via **Mehr**, said the Indian tanker **HAANA** planned to transit the **southern route** — the Oman Corridor — **"but received a warning that it had to stop,"** and turned back; the same agency said **"no vessel traffic has been observed on the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours."** **Fars** reported the IRGC continuing to warn ships by radio to use the Iranian-designated corridor instead. This sits directly against the CNN Business/**Kpler** dataset logged in the previous cycle putting **more than 80% of liquids transits** over two weeks on the Omani route. The likeliest reconciliation is that Kpler counts **completed** transits and the Iranian agency counts **permitted** ones; neither publishes a methodology, and this briefing records both without adjudicating.

**The market fell for three consecutive sessions, through the sanctions, the demining and the corridor.** On **August 25** Brent declined more than 3% to about **$89** a barrel, its lowest since **August 19**, with WTI near **$82**, the softest since **August 17**; one print carried Brent at **$89.44**, −2.67% over 24 hours. Traders judged the **August 24** sanctions less disruptive than a war because Treasury gave partners time to comply without naming target countries or an implementation timeline, and reporting that the State Department was **redeploying diplomats** to the Middle East was read as evidence against a full-scale resumption. **Ole Hansen** of Saxo Bank said the transition from military confrontation to economic sanctions **"had helped calm nerves across energy markets"**; **BBH** strategists called the announcement **"more of a warning shot than a decisive blow"**; **Tim Waterer** of KCM cautioned that **"prices had not fully deflated."** On **August 26** Brent fell about 3% again to roughly **$86** — Investing.com carried **$85.52** against a **$85.75** previous close on a $85.16-$86.10 range — with WTI off about 2.8% to about **$80**. The **straits.live** board diverged, carrying **$87.39** at its **26 August 2300Z** timestamp, +0.38% over 24 hours and about **21.4%** above the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline; the divergence is logged rather than resolved.

**The President removed the clock.** Asked by Al Jazeera's **Tanya Noury** on **August 26** how much time he was giving Iran to return to talks, Trump said: **"I have no time schedule, none. I'm not in a hurry. I have no time schedule at all."** He said **"We are winning very big. They've got massive inflation, their economy is falling apart, they're treating their people very badly, they are killing many, many protesters,"** and that economic and military measures **"are both effective."** Speaking to **Glenn Beck** the same day he called the waterway **"a very functioning strait"** — *"yes, every once in a while there will be a drone or a rocket or something shot"* — and said of Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei**, absent from public view for about six months, **"I don't think he's dead. He was very seriously wounded,"** describing wounds to *"the left side of his body, the arm, the leg, the whole thing"* and dismissing a contrary report in *The Atlantic*. Iran continues to recognise Mojtaba Khamenei officially as Supreme Leader.

**Diplomacy is now a queue of mediators, and the United States is in none of them.** Pakistan's **Field Marshal Asim Munir** and Interior Minister **Mohsin Naqvi** completed their day-long Tehran visit, meeting President **Pezeshkian**, **Araghchi**, Parliament Speaker **Ghalibaf** and Supreme National Security Council Secretary **Mohsen Rezaei**; on **August 25** Pakistani officials reported **"significant progress"** toward reviving the **Islamabad Memorandum**, with talks focused on preventing further military escalation, expediting the end of the war and reopening the Strait. Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister **Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani** arrives in Tehran on **Thursday August 27** for de-escalation talks centred on **freedom of navigation**, with Doha pressing to restore conditions to the **status quo that existed before February 28** — a broader objective than the Iranian-Omani corridor, and the two tracks have not been reconciled.

**The nuclear file hardened rhetorically on both sides.** Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** said **"Iran has a nuclear weapons program and our goal is to stop it,"** and that the United States could destroy Iranian nuclear facilities **"if necessary."** Atomic Energy Organisation head **Mohammad Eslami** said Iranian sites remain unsecured for inspection under wartime conditions and criticised the IAEA for failing to protest strikes on registered facilities: **"The facilities that have now been subjected to military strikes were all registered with the IAEA."** **Araghchi** petitioned UN Secretary-General **António Guterres** to **"condemn and reject"** US actions and sanctions, calling it a **"crucial moment"** for international law; Iran's UN ambassador **Gholamhossein Darzi** urged the Security Council to condemn unilateral coercive measures and characterised the naval blockade as a sovereignty violation.

**Iran's home front produced the sharpest deterioration of the cycle.** Long queues formed at petrol stations across Tehran and filling stations closed after running out; an Iranian state body warned the country faced a **"critical"** petrol shortfall; a **20-litre-per-car limit** forced motorists to keep returning. The government said **quotas would be reduced** and **non-subsidised fuel prices raised** while subsidised prices hold, describing the current pricing and quota mechanism as no longer sustainable. Executive Vice-President **Ghaempanah** said **"with the US naval blockade, we cannot import gasoline."** President **Pezeshkian** said Iran faces **"the worst conditions of an economic war."** The rial hit a record **2,060,000 to the dollar** on **August 25**, easing to about **2,005,000-2,007,000** on **August 26**, against an official Central Bank rate near **1.5 million**. Economy Minister **Ali Madanizadeh** said the government has a **"two-year plan"** to withstand sanctions. Separately, armed forces spokesman **Brig. Gen. Abolfazl Shekarchi** declared **BBC Persian, Iran International and Radio Farda** military targets — **"Hostile media outlets are soldiers of the Zionists and America"** — army spokesman **Mohammad Akraminia** claimed all damaged systems had been **"rebuilt"** with new equipment imported from unnamed suppliers, and military spokesman **Ebrahim Zolfaghari** said Iran will **"soon unveil the largest missile city on the planet."**

**The blockade published no new tally and became the stated centre of American strategy.** CENTCOM issued no update in this cycle; the figure of record remains **71 commercial vessels redirected, three disabled and two boarded** as of **August 24** since the **July 14** resumption, alongside **more than 40 humanitarian aid vessels** permitted through, with more than 20 warships supporting it. What changed is its billing: US officials told *Axios* that Washington will focus on **sanctions, the naval blockade and moving oil out of the Strait** in place of new strikes. **TankerTrackers** counted **more than fifteen ship-to-ship transfer operations** moving about **25 million barrels** in the Gulf of Oman, from **"every country in the region, minus Iran."** Iran's principal trade counterparties remain **China at $14.58bn**, **Iraq at $11.7bn**, the **UAE at $7.16bn** and **Türkiye at $6.1bn** — all now inside the cure period Treasury announced on **August 24**, and the **"major financial institution"** Bessent signalled for designation by the end of that week has not been named.

**The strike pause held for a twenty-fifth and twenty-sixth consecutive night.** No US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory has been confirmed since the President cancelled the planned multi-day energy campaign late on **August 1**.

**The ledger.** The Pentagon's published toll now stands at **776 US casualties — 18 killed and 758 wounded** — after **60 wounded** were added on **August 21**, taking the published wounded figure from **697 to 757**; other outlets carried 774 and 775 in the same window and the spread is noted. **More than 90% of the newest additions are Army soldiers**, consistent with the service split entered in the previous cycle: **more than 580 Army, 86 Navy, 64 Air Force and 19 Marines**. About **345 casualties** have occurred since **July 7**. *The Intercept*'s **August 25** accounting restates the undercount dispute: more than **200 sailors** treated for smoke inhalation and lacerations after the **USS Gerald R. Ford** fire of **March 12** are excluded; at least one officially recognised death is omitted; and on **April 21** the wounded-in-action figure **declined by 15** without explanation. A government official called the approach an **"accounting trick"** — *"They wanted the heat on them to slow down after the really devastating attacks"* — having previously described it as a **"casualty cover-up."** Independent tallies put the true wounded total above **900**. On the Iranian side, the **WHO** estimate carried in the same reporting is **37,181 casualties including 3,375 deaths**, against the Iranian government's own **3,528 killed and 27,170 injured**; the divergence is recorded, not adjudicated.

**Ground rung — one major negative datapoint, one structural datapoint about instrument choice, two counter-indicators, and no execution indicator.** *The negative datapoint:* the *Axios* report of **August 25** is the first item in 182 days to attach a duration to the non-kinetic posture, and the duration runs past the midterm elections. *The structural datapoint:* the capability applied to the chokepoint was **underwater drones and private contractors**, followed by a declaratory rule enforced by **Space Force** surveillance — coercive control by robot and by rule, not by lodgement. *The counter-indicators, logged without discount:* Secretary of War **Hegseth** continued to say strikes remain **"on the table,"** and Energy Secretary **Chris Wright** said the United States could destroy Iranian nuclear facilities **"if necessary"** — both air-and-missile formulations rather than ground ones, and neither forecloses anything. *No new naval data was published:* USNI News publishes its Fleet and Marine Tracker on **Mondays**, the edition of record remains **August 24** and the next is due **August 31**; it carries CENTCOM carrier presence at **two** after **USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72)** departed for **7th Fleet**, with **USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77)** in the northern Arabian Sea and **USS George Washington (CVN-73)** on station since August 19, and **USS Tripoli (LHA-7)** in port at **Sasebo, Japan**. The **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group** with the embarked **11th Marine Expeditionary Unit**, in theatre since **June 30**, remains the **only deployed ARG in the region** and has received **no tasking, no embarkation order and no rehearsal** in the **58 days** since arrival. **Kharg is unchanged** — terminals idle under blockade with a tanker backlog offshore, no US targeting, no naval repositioning and no statement in this cycle. **The draft rung is unchanged** — automatic Selective Service registration of men aged 18-26 remains scheduled for implementation **by December 2026**, a database change and not a call-up, with no draft order, no lottery and no induction authority. **Force level holds above 50,000** in the Middle East with approximately **2,000 soldiers of the 82nd Airborne Division** in contingency and base-defence roles and **none of it inside Iran**. **Still air, naval and financial only.**

### Russia-Ukraine — The CIA Director Flies to Moscow Unannounced While the Diplomatic Channel Stays Shut (August 25-26, 2026)

On **August 25** CIA Director **John Ratcliffe** travelled to Moscow. US officials did not announce the trip; publicly available **flight-tracking data** captured a US government transport aircraft moving from **Joint Base Andrews** to the Russian capital, with one account placing him aboard a US military **C-17**. It is the **first known visit to Moscow by a US intelligence chief since William Burns held talks with Vladimir Putin in November 2021**, Ratcliffe's first trip there since taking office, and the **highest-level visit by a Trump administration official to Russia since January**. The Kremlin subsequently said Ratcliffe met **Russian intelligence counterparts**; spokesman **Dmitry Peskov** initially neither confirmed nor denied the report and told Reuters that **Putin did not plan to meet him**. Nothing of the agenda has been disclosed by either government. Trump administration officials had asked Ukraine **several days earlier** to pause any strikes against **Moscow and other Russian cities from Monday through Wednesday**. On the same day, asked whether talks with US envoys were scheduled, Peskov said: **"No, there are no such plans."** Reporting since mid-August had suggested **Steve Witkoff** and **Jared Kushner** could travel to Moscow within a week to ten days to revive talks both belligerents describe as stalled; that visit has not happened. **The intelligence channel is open and the diplomatic channel is not.**

The war did not observe the requested pause. Russian attacks killed at least **four** and injured at least **95** across Ukraine over **August 25-26**. Overnight into **August 26** Russia launched **163 drones**, of which Ukrainian air defences **downed 132**, with strikes recorded at **18 locations** and debris at three; an earlier partial morning count carried **150 drones** plus one **Iskander-M** and one **Kh-31P**, with 124 downed by 9 a.m. and 17 locations struck. **By oblast:** **Donetsk** one killed and eight injured overall, with **Kramatorsk** carrying **26 injured**, **37 high-rise buildings**, three educational facilities and one infrastructure facility damaged; **Chernihiv** two killed — a **39-year-old woman and her four-year-old daughter**, by drone — and 14 injured across 28 attacks; **Kherson** one killed and 12 injured; **Kharkiv** 23 injured including two children; **Zaporizhzhia** nine injured across **935 attacks on 47 settlements**; **Dnipropetrovsk** six injured. On **August 25** in **Kramatorsk**, Russian forces struck a nine-storey residential block and then attacked the rescue workers clearing it: a Russian **first-person-view drone** hit an **armoured ambulance** belonging to the **State Emergency Service**, damaging the vehicle without injuring personnel. It was the **second attack on rescuers that week**, following the **Kryvyi Rih** shopping-centre double-tap of **August 21** that killed at least six. The service's statement: **"Despite the danger, emergency services continue to help people."**

Ukraine's deep-strike campaign resumed in the same window, hitting a **Wildberries logistics hub in Tambov Oblast** with what was described as a **"massive drone attack,"** causing a fire that spread across **more than 100,000 square metres**. ISW's **August 25** assessment finds Russia **escalating strikes against Ukrainian-Moldovan border infrastructure** in conjunction with its campaign against Ukrainian port and maritime infrastructure, judging the border strikes intended to achieve broader political effects; it also records the Kremlin managing concerns over **Putin's decree** setting conditions for the **nationalisation of critical infrastructure facilities**, and a further Russian military satellite launched on **August 24**, possibly part of the **Rassvet** programme, a Russian analogue to Starlink. The **August 24** assessment records a concerted Ukrainian **SEAD/DEAD campaign** against Russian air-defence assets in Russian border regions, and Ukrainian advances in the **Slovyansk** and **Hulyaipole** directions and in **western Zaporizhia Oblast**. The Ukrainian General Staff put cumulative Russian personnel losses at approximately **1,480,750** since **24 February 2022**, including about **1,450** over the preceding 24 hours. **No NATO troop commitment to Ukraine was announced.**

### Gulf States — Muscat Delivers an Instrument, Doha Follows, and the Civil Cost Appears in the Aviation Numbers (August 25-27, 2026)

Oman's corridor framework is treated in full above. Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister **Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani** arrives in Tehran on **Thursday August 27** for de-escalation talks focused on **freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz**, with Doha's stated objective the restoration of navigation to the **pre-February 28 status quo**. The UAE's **Anwar Gargash** said on **August 25** that the US-Iran conflict has moved **"to a new phase"** marked by **"escalating economic pressure"**; Abu Dhabi's **August 19** suspension of all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran stands, and UAE-domiciled entities were among the roughly 60 designated under Operation Economic Outcast on **August 24**. **ADNOC** is reported to be offering a shuttle service with **transponders switched off** — a state oil company operating its own dark fleet inside its own waters — while **Saudi Arabia** runs **ship-to-ship transfers with government-backed insurance** alongside the Franco-Saudi Hormuz bypass programme advanced in Paris on **August 24**. **TankerTrackers** counted **more than fifteen ship-to-ship transfer operations** involving about **25 million barrels** in the Gulf of Oman, from **"every country in the region, minus Iran."** **Dubai International Airport** reported **13 million passengers in the second quarter** against **31.5 million in the first**, a fall of **31.3%**; chief executive **Paul Griffiths** said: **"I'm very confident we'll be back to full operation in a very short space of time."**

### Other Theatres — China's Countermeasure Threat, Kim's Silence, Venezuela's Street, and the American Price Index (August 25-27, 2026)

**US-China.** Foreign Ministry spokesman **Lin Jian** said on **August 26** that **"China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights,"** restating that China's trade with Iran **"should not be disrupted"** and **"complies with international law,"** and condemning the American measures as **economic warfare** that *"will only further intensify tensions."* Iran's Parliament Speaker **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf** publicly **thanked China** for declining to comply. Beijing's countermeasures pre-date the designations: instructions to Chinese firms to disregard US restrictions on independent refiners importing Iranian crude, and invocation of the **2021 blocking statute**. Kpler data published on **August 26** puts Chinese imports of Iranian crude through the **Strait of Hormuz** at about **530,000 barrels a day — 48% below pre-war levels and 72% below the October 2024 peak of 1.9 million bpd** — with the **Red Sea route** at about **1.02 million bpd** in August against an **April peak of 2.62 million**. Shandong **teapot refiners** are substituting: one bought Brazil's **Lapa** crude this week and others are examining Iraq's **Basrah**. Freight via **Suez** now costs roughly **$10-11 a barrel** against about **$5 via Yanbu** before the Houthi campaign, and the **Cape of Good Hope** routing takes about **50 days** against 25-27. The separate tariff track is unchanged: a **7.5% Section 301 overcapacity tariff** is prepared ahead of the **September 24 Xi-Trump summit** in Washington, which would take second-term duties to roughly **20%** against a current replacement rate of **12.5%**, with the trade truce expiring **November 10**. **Taiwan** is quieter than the trade file: PLA sortie rates, which doubled to more than 300 a month after President Lai's May 2024 inauguration, have **reverted to the pre-Lai baseline** since the start of 2026.

**DPRK.** **Kim Jong Un** presided on **August 25** over an **enlarged meeting of the political bureau** of the Workers' Party Central Committee, reported by state media on **August 26**, reviewing progress in the country's **"major economic sectors"** and the implementation of 2026 policy goals. **The report carried no mention of President Trump's renewed diplomatic outreach or of a possible summit.** Kim called for **"extraordinary responsibility and high prudence"** in carrying out major state projects and cited **"a series of deviations"** attributed to **"the immature operation and leadership of the economic guidance organs failing to keep abreast of our greater ideals and progress."** **Today, August 27, is the date on which Ulchi Freedom Shield's counteroffensive phase was originally scheduled to end** — the exercise having been cut from eleven days to five as a goodwill gesture and terminated on **August 21**, so the half Pyongyang denounces as an invasion rehearsal never took place at all. No further DPRK launch has been reported since the roughly **ten KN-25 short-range ballistic missiles** fired on **August 20**, which Pyongyang has still not publicised. No date or venue for a Trump-Kim meeting has been announced.

**Latin America.** Pot-banging protests have **multiplied in recent days** across Venezuela in rejection of recurring blackouts and appliance damage from voltage fluctuations. In **Turmero, Aragua state** — about 80 kilometres southeast of Caracas — residents **blocked roads and set tyres alight** against daily cuts of **four to five hours** and government-imposed rationing. Acting President **Delcy Rodríguez** has called for **electricity and water rationing** and activated a national **Electricity and Water Savings Plan**, attributing the crisis to the **"Super Niño"** climate phenomenon and to a recent earthquake; the measures have been **openly rejected**. The Caracas government-opposition talks that opened on **August 6** under **Jorge Rodríguez** and **Dinorah Figuera** continue with no published electoral timetable; **Maduro** and **Cilia Flores** remain in US custody with trial set for **June 1, 2027**. In **Cuba** the cumulative figures are unchanged — **six nationwide grid collapses in 2026**, blackouts exceeding **twenty hours a day**, some communities at **up to 105 consecutive days** without steady power — and newly documented is the response: residents of several **Havana** municipalities staged **neighbourhood protests** after blackouts of **more than 48 hours**, banging pots and pans and burning rubbish. **Colombia's** President **Abelardo de la Espriella**, in office since **August 7**, continues the hardline security programme and the severance of ties with **Cuba and Nicaragua**.

**Hormuz-dependent economies and the American price level.** **Pakistan, Bangladesh, the Philippines, Vietnam and Sri Lanka** have imposed **four-day working weeks, work-from-home mandates or school closures** to conserve fuel; Pakistan imports roughly **85%** of its supply by tanker and Bangladesh about **95%** of its petroleum needs. **India**, which takes **60%** of its LPG through the Strait, is seeing **black-marketing of domestic cylinders** and restaurant closures. **South Korea** draws about **70%** of its crude and 18% of its LNG through Hormuz on about **206 days** of reserves; **Japan** takes more than **90%** of its crude from the Middle East, about 75% via Hormuz, on about **146 days**. Korean petrochemicals are already impaired — **Lotte Chemical, LG Chem** and **Hanwha Solutions** have issued potential **force majeure** notices and **Yeochun NCC** has declared supply disruption. **LNG carrier rates** are around **$300,000 a day**, a 650% increase, and crude tanker rates are at historic highs. In the **United States**, **July PCE inflation held at 3.7% year-on-year**, reported **August 26** and well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target; the **AAA national average** for regular stands at about **$4.10 a gallon**, roughly a dollar above a year ago, with **August 2026 on course to be the highest August on record** at a **$4.06** monthly average against **2022's $3.97**. Two-thirds of Democratic campaign advertisements mentioning gasoline prices cite the war as the cause — the domestic context in which the reported decision to hold off further strikes until after the elections has to be read.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 24-25 (DAY 180): THE FINANCIAL OFFENSIVE ARRIVED AND IT HAS A NAME. BESSENT UNVEILED 'OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST' — FIVE SECTORAL DETERMINATIONS, NEARLY 60 DESIGNATIONS ACROSS FIVE JURISDICTIONS, DEFINED WIND-DOWN TIMELINES AND A 'CURE PERIOD' — AND STATED THE OBJECTIVE WITHOUT EUPHEMISM: 'IT IS GOING TO WORK IN IRAN, AND WE ARE GOING TO COLLAPSE THIS REGIME.' THE WHITE HOUSE CALLS IT THE 'ENDGAME' PHASE. HEGSETH DECLINED TO FORECLOSE MILITARY FORCE IN THE STRAIT 'OR ANYWHERE ELSE.' BRENT FELL ON ANNOUNCEMENT DAY; THE RIAL HIT A RECORD 2.02 MILLION. TWO TANKERS WERE HIT. KPLER DATA SAYS IRAN HAS LOST SIGNIFICANT CONTROL OF THE WATERWAY. GROUND RUNG: EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR AT ZERO FOR A 180TH DAY.

**The pending event of the previous cycle happened, and it happened entirely on paper.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** held the announced **2 p.m. ET news conference on Monday August 24** and gave the successor phase of the war a name: **OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST**. The previous cycle closed recording the *announced shape* rather than the announced content; the content is now on the record. Treasury issued **sectoral determinations** against five parts of the Iranian economy — **digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping** — which is the legal architecture that makes whole industries sanctionable rather than named firms. Alongside it, **nearly 60 Iran-linked people, entities and vessels** were designated, located across the **United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland**. Bessent said every country would be given a **defined timeline** to wind down Iran-related business, that **most secondary sanctions would not be immediate**, and that a **"cure period"** would run before enforcement — *"We are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behavior,"* qualified by *"We do not have infinite patience here."* He indicated that the sanctioning of a **major financial institution** should be expected by the end of the week.

**The objective was stated without euphemism, and that is the cycle's most consequential sentence.** Bessent said of the campaign: **"It is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime."** He also said *"we are launching an economic onslaught against Iran's financial connections around the globe"*; *"our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone"*; *"No one is above the reach of US sanctions"*; and *"Let there be no ambiguity as to the position of the United States. An economic engagement of any kind with this murderous regime will expose those responsible to the full reach of American power."* The White House release positions the operation as the **endgame phase** succeeding Operation Epic Fury: *"Beginning today, the actions of Treasury and other agencies will tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue that funds the IRGC and the evil Iranian regime,"* with Iran's choice framed as **"complete global isolation and a subsistence economy"** or normalisation. **Regime collapse is now an openly declared American war aim, and the declared instrument for achieving it is the banking system.** For a briefing whose central tracked prediction is a US ground seizure, the significance is that the administration announced the **maximalist objective and the non-military means in the same room on the same afternoon**.

**The counter-indicator is real and is recorded without discount.** Secretary of War **Pete Hegseth** said the same day that military force is **not ruled out** in the Strait of Hormuz **"or anywhere else."** This is the same non-foreclosure formula tracked since April; it forecloses nothing, commits nothing, and is compatible with both a landing and no landing. It is logged because a record that captures only de-escalatory evidence is not a record.

**Not everyone accepted the billing.** Sanctions specialist **Brett Erickson** said of the package: **"This was not economic D-Day...It was something in the middle."** Iranian Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** dismissed it: *"They cannot think of any other solution in confronting the great Iranian people, so they repeatedly put forward the same old plans."*

**The market marked the offensive down.** Brent **fell** on the day of the announcement, after gaining more than 5% the previous week. Published figures diverge: Reuters carried Brent off **1.4% to about $93** and WTI off 1.6% to about **$85.70**; CNBC carried Brent off **2.5% to $92.06** and WTI off 2.5% to **$84.89**; the **straits.live** board carried **$92.10**, down **1.67%** over 24 hours and about **27.9% above the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline**. The explanation given across outlets is **profit-taking** after a two-week rally rather than a judgement on the sanctions. The direction is recorded plainly: the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary was announced, and the price of the commodity it targets went down.

**The rial went the other way.** Iran's currency hit a record low of **2.02 million to the dollar** on the open market as trading opened Monday, against an official Central Bank rate of about **1.5 million**. Reporting puts **rice up about 60%** and **beef up more than 150%** since the war began. This is where the campaign is already landing, and it was landing before the designations were issued.

**Tehran's answer was dismissal plus a targeting threat aimed at host states rather than at Washington.** Foreign Ministry spokesman **Esmail Baghaei** said *"Any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences"* and *"Our hands are not tied,"* and — the operative line — said Iran has the **right to target any location used to launch attacks against it**, warning countries against **providing territory or facilities** to the United States. Taken with SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei's August 23 warning that any state joining the sanctions is *"considered an enemy,"* the Iranian deterrent is now pointed at the American basing structure in Gulf states rather than at American forces at sea.

**Two tankers were hit in twenty-four hours, in two different seas.** Yemen's **Houthis** struck the Saudi VLCC **AMZAN**, operated by the national shipping company **Bahri**, about **63 nautical miles west of Yanbu** in the Red Sea with **ballistic missiles and drones** on **August 24**; a fire broke out on the main deck, nearby vessels fled the target area, all crew are safe and no environmental impact was reported. Houthi military spokesman **Yahya Saree** described the strike as part of a **"siege for siege"** operation targeting the Saudis. Then at **0131 UTC on August 25** — inside this cycle — **UKMTO** reported a tanker struck by an **unidentified projectile about nine nautical miles northeast of Ash Shishah, Oman**, with the **engine room damaged** and the **vessel disabled**; the crew were reported safe and no party has been identified as responsible.

**The blockade tightened by one hull and disclosed a number it had not published before.** CENTCOM said that as of **August 24** US forces had **redirected 71 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two** since the **July 14 resumption** — up from 70 on August 23, 68 on August 21, 67 on August 20, 64 on August 17, 44 on August 3 and 35 on August 2 — with more than **20 warships** supporting. And for the first time in this record, CENTCOM stated that **more than 40 humanitarian aid vessels have been permitted passage**. A blockade operating a declared humanitarian carve-out is a different instrument from one that does not.

**The traffic picture acquired its first dataset that points one way.** **CNN Business**, working from **Kpler** ship-tracking data, reported that **more than 80% of liquids transits over the preceding two weeks took the Omani route** — the UN-authorised channel Iran vehemently opposes — **or were dark transits that likely took it**, concluding that **Iran has lost significant control** of the waterway and that the US Navy is gaining ground. **Gulf News** separately reported **southern-corridor traffic up roughly 400% over two weeks to nearly 200 ships weekly**. Against that, the **straits.live** board still carries **one transit** on its latest daily datapoint against a **73-a-day baseline** (1% of typical volume), **370 hulls holding position away from berth**, **eight of nine major container carriers** routing via the **Cape of Good Hope**, and market odds of a **December 31 reopening at 34%** with **August 31 under 1%**. The estimates remain irreconcilable — a route-share statistic and an absolute-volume statistic are not in conflict as arithmetic but are in direct conflict as claims about **control** — and this briefing logs the spread while recording that the newest and best-sourced dataset has changed direction. The dispute is carried as an open question in its own right.

**Diplomacy ran through Islamabad and Muscat.** Pakistan's **Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir** travelled to Tehran on **August 24** with Interior Minister **Mohsin Naqvi** and met Iranian Interior Minister **Eskandar Momeni**, on a day-long visit aimed at a negotiated settlement. The **60-day window of the Islamabad Memorandum** — signed by **Pakistan, Iran and the United States on June 17** — **lapsed in mid-August without either side agreeing to extend it**, and Islamabad's position is that the framework remains available as a template. Separately, Oman's Foreign Minister **Sayyid Badr Albusaidi** arrives in Tehran on **August 25** to meet Araghchi on the Strait, bilateral relations, maritime safety and maritime governance, following their **August 21** telephone call and nearly three months of Iran-Oman negotiation over a safe shipping route with agreed coordinates.

**The strike pause held for a twenty-fourth consecutive night.** No US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory has been confirmed since the President cancelled the planned multi-day energy campaign late on **August 1**.

**The ledger.** The Pentagon's published toll held at **775 US casualties — 18 killed and 757 wounded** — with no addition since August 21. **The service breakdown is new to this briefing and is worth stating precisely: more than 580 of the wounded are Army soldiers, 86 are sailors, 64 are airmen and 19 are Marines.** Independent tallies counting casualties the Defense Casualty Analysis System omits put the true wounded total **above 900**. The **AAA national average** for regular gasoline was **$4.0991** on August 24, effectively flat on the day and **95 cents above a year earlier**; **diesel** reached **$5.6134**, a further record August level and **$1.93 above last year**. **War-risk cover** holds at about **$10.0m per VLCC passage, forty times pre-crisis**, with **six P&I clubs** withdrawn.

**Ground rung — one confirmation, one new structural datapoint, and no execution indicator.** *The confirmation:* USNI News's **August 24** fleet tracker records that **USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) has left the Middle East** after almost seven months and is now in **U.S. 7th Fleet**, completing the relief that leaves net carrier presence in CENTCOM at **two** — **USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77)** since April 23 and **USS George Washington (CVN-73)** since August 19 — which is the same number CENTCOM published in July, and therefore a **like-for-like rotation inside a static force level** rather than a build-up. *The new structural datapoint:* the casualty composition above. **After 180 days, 19 of 757 wounded are Marines — roughly 2.5% — which is the casualty signature of base defence and blockade enforcement, not of a force fighting for or preparing for a beach.** *And the standing picture is unchanged:* the **Boxer ARG** — USS Boxer (LHD-4), USS Comstock (LSD-45), USS Portland (LPD-27) — with the **11th MEU** remains the **sole deployed ARG in theatre**, in the Arabian Sea, with **no tasking, no embarkation, no landing rehearsal, no mine-countermeasures preparation and no repositioning toward Kharg** reported at any point in the war; **one ARG is deployed worldwide** against combatant-commander requests for **"well north of three"** pairings; the **Iwo Jima ARG / 22nd MEU** remains committed to SOUTHCOM counter-narcotics; **Kharg** saw no US activity and loading remains episodic after the mid-August restart; the **draft rung** is unchanged, with the reported **December 18, 2026** automatic-registration date under the FY2026 NDAA still separate from the **SSS rule withdrawn in July 2026 and not re-proposed**, and with no draft order, lottery, induction authority or IRR call-up at any point; and **force level holds above 50,000 with none of it inside Iran**. The standing June 12 backfill remains the war's strongest ground-planning evidence: CNN reported that **CJCS Gen. Dan Caine** flew from Brussels to CENTCOM headquarters on **May 19** to be briefed on sending **US ground troops into Iran to seize its highly enriched uranium**, and that **Trump declined the operation** on casualty grounds before Iran sealed the cache with collapsed tunnels and mined entrances. **The capability to plan such an operation exists and has been exercised; the decision to execute one has been made once, and it was negative.**
