## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 23-24 (DAY 179): BOTH BELLIGERENTS SPENT THE CYCLE DRAFTING DOCUMENTS RATHER THAN MOVING FORCES. BESSENT DECLARED 'AN ECONOMIC D-DAY — THE SINGLE GREATEST FINANCIAL OFFENSIVE EVER MARSHALLED AGAINST AN ADVERSARY' IN THE FINANCIAL TIMES, WITH HIS DETAILING NEWS CONFERENCE SET FOR 2 P.M. ET ON MONDAY. HOURS EARLIER IRAN'S PARLIAMENTARY COMMISSION APPROVED A HORMUZ SERVICE-FEE ARTICLE PAYABLE 'IN RIALS OR ANY OTHER CURRENCY DESIRED BY THE ISLAMIC REPUBLIC.' REZAEI ESCALATED TO 'NOT A SINGLE DROP OF OIL' AND NAMED THE BYPASS ROUTES AS TARGETS. PEZESHKIAN SAID IRAN 'CANNOT CONTINUE WITH WAR FOREVER' AND DEFENDED THE JUNE MOU AGAINST THE SUPREME LEADER'S PURPORTED MISGIVINGS — THE FIRST ON-RECORD IRANIAN ELITE SPLIT OF THE WAR. A TWENTY-THIRD CONSECUTIVE NIGHT PASSED WITHOUT A CONFIRMED STRIKE INSIDE IRAN. GROUND RUNG: ONE CORRECTION (CARRIER PRESENCE IS TWO, NOT ONE) AND ONE BACKFILL (THE MAY 19 CJCS BRIEFING ON A GROUND MISSION, DECLINED BY THE PRESIDENT) — EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR AT ZERO FOR A 179TH DAY.

**The American instrument went into print before it went into effect.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** published an opinion piece in the *Financial Times* on **Sunday August 23** opening: **"At dawn begins an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary."** His news conference detailing the package was set for **2 p.m. ET on Monday August 24** and had not been held when this cycle closed; what follows is therefore the **announced shape** rather than the announced content. The declared targets, from the President's **August 20** Truth Social post, are **"oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies — It all needs to stop NOW,"** and the declared mechanism is **secondary sanctions** against **"ANY country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran,"** which will **"itself face TREMENDOUS economic consequences."** Bessent has separately promised **"the toughest sanctions in history,"** **"the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world,"** and — the line that matters most to the ground question this briefing tracks — told CNBC on **August 20** that **"if we are doing the maximum economic pressure, then that means that likely there will not be a large-scale kinetic restart."** The administration's declared theory of victory now runs through correspondent banking rather than through a beachhead.

**Tehran's answer was also a document, and it is the most concrete step Iran has taken toward monetising the chokepoint.** On **August 23** the Iranian parliament's **National Security and Foreign Policy Commission approved Article 3** of its plan titled **"Strategic Action to Ensure the Security and Progress of the Strait of Hormuz."** Ships of countries **permitted** to transit will pay for services **"including maritime, environmental, fueling under special conditions, insurance, safety, and other services provided in the Strait of Hormuz,"** and **"these fees will be charged in Rials or any other currency desired by the Islamic Republic of Iran."** The straits.live status board adds that violating vessels would face **fines, detention or confiscation**. The commission spokesman is named as **Hassan Qashqavi** by Middle East Eye and Al Jazeera and as **Ebrahim Rezaei** by Reuters and the Tribune; both attributions are recorded here rather than adjudicated. **The measure is not law:** it requires a full parliamentary vote on its provisions and on overall passage, and then **Guardian Council** review for constitutional and Islamic compliance. Passage through the Strait was **free before the war**. This is the toll regime Washington rejected in July, and which Iranian sources said the June MOU did not bar, now advancing through Iran's own legislature rather than through an Omani negotiation.

**The security chief escalated from selectivity to totality, and for the first time named the workarounds.** **Mohsen Rezaei**, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, warned through **IRNA** that Tehran **"will not allow a single drop of oil to leave the Persian Gulf"** if US-led economic pressure escalates — a claim carried by the straits.live board **as reported and unconfirmed**. He said that if Trump **"wants to do something, we will retaliate in a seismic manner,"** repeated that any state joining the sanctions is **"considered an enemy"** whose interests would be harmed, and — the genuinely new element — said Iran would **target the oil-shipping routes out of the Persian Gulf that serve as alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz** if regional states join what he called the economic war. He also **cautioned against any additional US military deployment to the region** and said the transit fees would be pressed through the **Oman channel**. The Iranian threat has therefore widened from the chokepoint to the circumventions, in the same week that Riyadh and Paris convened specifically to build them.

**The most consequential Iranian statement of the cycle was not a threat, and it came from the presidency.** In **two appearances in Tehran on Sunday August 23**, President **Masoud Pezeshkian** said Iran **"cannot continue with war forever"** and that **"one day, a decision must be made to save the country from the state of 'neither war nor peace'."** He **defended the June memorandum of understanding** reached with the United States, saying that all those directly involved in the negotiations believed the memorandum was the best way forward and that **"by implementing this memorandum, we can resolve the problems with logic and dignity."** Reporting states that he did so **despite the purported misgivings of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei**, and describes **"signs of growing differences within the Iranian leadership over negotiations with the United States."** This is the **first cycle of the war in which an open elite split over the settlement has been reported on the record on the Iranian side**, and it runs in the opposite direction from Rezaei's escalation published the same day. **No statement by Mojtaba Khamenei on the memorandum exists in the open record**, so the misgivings are reported rather than attributed; the divergence is entered as unresolved and is tracked in the open-questions register.

**The strike pause held for a twenty-third consecutive night.** No US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory has been confirmed since the President cancelled the planned multi-day energy campaign late on **August 1**. The kinetic activity that continued in the period ran outward rather than inward: an **Israeli drone strike in the south-western Syrian village of Beit Jin** caused injuries, and Israeli operations continued in **Gaza's Khan Yunis** and in **southern Lebanon**.

**The blockade tightened by two hulls.** CENTCOM said that as of **August 23** US forces had **redirected 70 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two** to enforce the US naval blockade against Iran, dating the count from the **July 14 resumption** — up from 68 as of August 21, 67 as of August 20, 64 on August 17, 44 on August 3 and 35 on August 2, with more than **20 warships** supporting. Two interdictions in two days is far below the early-August pace, which remains consistent with traffic that has largely stopped presenting itself rather than with relaxed enforcement.

**And the traffic picture became openly irreconcilable, which is now recorded as an open question in its own right.** For the same late-August period the record carries: **CNN** reporting on August 23 that the number of ships using the Strait **"stands at 20% of the pre-war average"**; the **straits.live** board carrying **one transit** on its most recent daily datapoint against a **73-a-day pre-crisis baseline** — 1% of typical volume — and describing the waterway as **closed to commercial shipping** on war-risk grounds; **UKMTO** figures of **21 inbound and 18 outbound** in the week to August 7, about **4% of pre-conflict levels**; **Iran International** reporting roughly **200 transits in a week** against about 150 the week before; **Al Jazeera's** route analysis counting **236 hulls across August 1-19**, of which **148 (62%) went dark**; and an **unnamed American official**, quoted in reporting on the D-Day announcement, saying US forces are **facilitating 15-20 ship transits a night carrying roughly ten million barrels of oil a day — approximately half pre-war volume** — and adding: **"The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps can be a nuisance, but they don't control the strait. We do."** Other reporting puts flow at **8-9 million barrels a day** moving largely by **dark transit**, **"aided by the US Navy chartering tankers with transponders turned off."** The 236-hull count over nineteen days and the 15-20-a-night claim cannot both describe the same waterway; the spread is roughly **fifty to one**. The briefing logs every figure, adopts none as the volume series, and notes the structural reason the dispute may be unresolvable in principle: a dark transit is invisible to the transponder-based counts that produce the low figures and unverifiable in the escort claims that produce the high ones.

**Diplomacy ran through Cairo.** Egyptian Foreign Minister **Badr Abdelatty** and Iranian Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** held a telephone call on **Saturday August 22** on creating conditions for de-escalation and a return to diplomacy, covering the **Oman-Iran negotiations** and **implementation of the June 18 US-Iran memorandum**. Abdelatty stressed the importance of ensuring **international freedom of navigation** and respecting the **security and stability of Gulf countries**. Egypt has not played an official mediating role between Washington and Tehran — **Pakistan and Qatar** hold that role — so the call adds to the mediation surface rather than changing it.

**The ledger.** The Pentagon's published toll **held at 775 US casualties — 18 killed and 757 wounded** — with no addition since the single-day increase of 60 on August 21 that took the wounded count from 697. **Brent** stood at **$94.39** on the straits.live board at **2300Z on August 23**, unchanged over 24 hours with futures markets closed for the weekend and roughly **31% above the ~$72 pre-crisis baseline**, after a second consecutive weekly gain of about 6%. **War-risk cover** runs about **$10.0m per VLCC passage, forty times pre-crisis**, with **six P&I clubs** having withdrawn coverage. The **AAA national average** for regular gasoline was **$4.0986 on August 23**, down fractionally from $4.1024 the previous day but ninety cents above a year earlier; **diesel reached $5.6074**, a record August level, **$1.92 above the year-earlier $3.6893** and 40 cents above a month ago — the freight cost of the chokepoint, arriving on a lag and transmitting into goods prices rather than into household sentiment. On the Iranian side of the ledger, the **IMF** projects a 2026 contraction of about **6.1%** with inflation near **68.9%**, the rial has been reported at roughly **two million to the dollar**, and the official minimum monthly wage of **166.255m rials** covers about **37%** of an estimated basic living basket.

**Ground rung — one correction and one backfill, both entered against this briefing's own prior record.** *The correction:* **net carrier presence in CENTCOM is TWO, not one**, and the previous cycle's "net presence unchanged at one" is **withdrawn**. **USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77)** entered the CENTCOM area of responsibility on **April 23, 2026** and has operated in the northern Arabian Sea in support of the blockade throughout; **USS George Washington (CVN-73)**, with **USS Robert Smalls (CG-62)** and **USS Shoup (DDG-86)**, arrived on **August 19** and relieved **USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72)**, which sailed for San Diego after roughly **200 consecutive days at sea without a liberty port call**, a length that drew official concern for crew mental and physical health. The substantive judgment is unchanged and arguably firmer: **two carriers is exactly the number CENTCOM published in July**, so the August movement is a **like-for-like rotation inside a static force level**, not a build-up; and **no US carrier is currently positioned in the Western Pacific**. *The backfill:* this briefing had treated the **July 26** New York Post report of a concept requiring **"thousands of ground troops"** as the war's only genuine ground-planning indicator. That understated the record. **CNN reported on June 12, 2026** that the **Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Gen. Dan Caine**, made a **secret and rushed trip on May 19** from a meeting of senior NATO officials in **Brussels** back to **US Central Command headquarters in Tampa** to be briefed on plans for the US military to **send ground troops into Iran to forcibly seize its stockpile of highly enriched uranium** — and that **Trump decided against the operation after warnings that it could result in a large number of US casualties**. **CNN reported on June 13** that Iran had then dramatically escalated efforts to seal the cache, **deliberately collapsing tunnels and booby-trapping entrances with explosive mines**, making the material far more difficult, dangerous and time-consuming to access than a month earlier. **The Washington Post** had reported on **April 1** that the commando concept was drawn up **at Trump's own request**. That is simultaneously the strongest evidence in the whole war that a ground operation was **seriously prepared** — a named four-star, a dated trip, a specific headquarters, a decision point — and the strongest documented instance of that operation being **declined at the presidential level** and of the **target being physically hardened** against it in the weeks that followed. Both halves are entered, and the question is logged in the open-questions register. *The unchanged picture:* every execution indicator remained at **zero for a 179th consecutive day** — no landing, no embarkation, no MEU tasking, no airborne insertion, no relief ARG, no new deployment order, no mobilisation, no draft order, no medical or fuel prepositioning consistent with a lodgement, and no reported special-operations ground activity inside Iran. The amphibious rung is thin **by the Navy's own account**: The War Zone's **August 11** survey records **one amphibious ready group deployed worldwide** against combatant-commander requests for **"well north of three" ARG-MEU pairings**, with three ARGs in maintenance and three in various training states. In theatre that one is the **Boxer ARG** — USS Boxer (LHD-4), USS Comstock (LSD-45), USS Portland (LPD-27) — with the **11th MEU**, in the Arabian Sea as of the August 17 USNI tracker, never tasked and never repositioned toward Kharg; the Navy's other deployed ARG, **Iwo Jima with the 22nd MEU**, is committed to **Caribbean counter-narcotics under SOUTHCOM**; and the **24th MEU** is deployed without an ARG at all as **"Littoral Combat Force 24."** **Iran's own threat model still anticipates a force flow that has not come:** Rezaei's August 23 remarks included a caution against **any additional US military deployment to the region**. And the draft rung did not move: the **December 18, 2026** automatic Selective Service registration date builds the pool and **inducts nobody**, with no amendment to the Military Selective Service Act, no presidential induction order and no award announced under the "readiness simulation" procurement.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 22-23 (DAY 178): TWO SOVEREIGNTY CLAIMS OVER THE SAME WATER ON THE SAME DAY, AND NEITHER PRODUCED A LANDING. TRUMP: 'I VIEW THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ AS AN AMERICAN TERRITORY RIGHT NOW,' AND HE RE-POSTED THE MAP LABELLING IT 'NEW U.S. TERRITORY.' HOURS APART, TEHRAN GRANTED A NUMBER OF IRAQI OIL TANKERS PERMISSION TO TRANSIT — THE FIRST NAMED STATE-LEVEL EXEMPTION OF THE WAR. IRAN'S FOREIGN MINISTRY CALLED THE SANCTIONS DUE MONDAY A 'DECLARATION OF WAR ON ALL NATIONS' AND SNSC SECRETARY MOHSEN REZAEI SAID ANY COUNTRY JOINING THEM IS 'CONSIDERED AN ENEMY,' THAT THE STRAIT 'IS CLOSED AND WILL NOT REOPEN,' AND THAT IRAN WOULD RETALIATE 'IN AN EARTHQUAKE-LIKE MANNER.' A TWENTY-SECOND CONSECUTIVE NIGHT PASSED WITHOUT A CONFIRMED STRIKE INSIDE IRAN. THE FIRST ROUTE-SHARE DATASET OF THE WAR FOUND 83 HULLS OPENLY ON IRAN'S ROUTE AGAINST THREE ON THE US-BACKED OMANI ROUTE. THE MECCA JOINT DEFENCE PACT OF AUGUST 7 IS ENTERED INTO THIS RECORD. GROUND RUNG: EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR AT ZERO FOR A 178TH DAY.

**The American claim on the chokepoint went territorial, and produced no ground signature whatever.** On **August 22** President Trump told a crowd of supporters in South Carolina: **"We don't even know if we won, because I view the Strait of Hormuz as an American territory right now."** He re-posted on Truth Social the image, first published on **August 18**, showing the waterway labelled **"New U.S. Territory."** The claim is the rhetorical maximum of a position he has been building for a week: on **August 17** he said he liked **"the idea of declaring it a territory,"** asserted **"we have total control over the strait"** and called the blockade a **"wall of steel."** No legal instrument giving the claim effect has been published, no occupation of any land accompanied it, and no change in force posture followed it. For an audit tracking the difference between assertion and execution, this is the cleanest instance of the war: the strongest sovereignty claim yet made over the Strait carries no manpower requirement and generated no observable ground movement.

**Hours apart, Iran demonstrated the competing form of control — allocation rather than occupation.** Iran's state news agency **IRNA** announced on **August 22** that Tehran had **granted a number of Iraqi oil tankers permission to transit the Strait of Hormuz**, after repeated requests from Baghdad through several channels including during the visit to Iraq by parliament speaker and lead negotiator **Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf**. It is the **first named state-level transit exemption of the war**. Iraq produced roughly **four million barrels a day** before the conflict, lacks a national tanker fleet and depends on foreign hulls, and is simultaneously building alternative export routes through **Ceyhan** in Turkey, **Baniyas** in Syria and **Aqaba** in Jordan. Iraqi President **Nizar Amidi** said **"everyone is keen to prevent Iraq from being dragged into the ongoing war in the region"** and that Iraqi territory **"will not be used to launch attacks against any other country."** An analyst quoted by Al Jazeera argued Iran favours Iraq because it has **"always stood up to the United States,"** while continuing to punish Gulf states hosting American bases. The audit records both claims without adjudicating between them; the dispute is tracked as an open question.

**The strike pause held for a twenty-second consecutive night.** No US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory has been confirmed since the President cancelled the planned multi-day energy campaign late on **August 1**. The pause is now three weeks old and has outlasted both the **August 17** expiry of the 60-day negotiating window it was meant to protect and the administration's declaration of a financial successor phase.

**Tehran answered the coming sanctions with the broadest threat of the war, and aimed it at third parties.** Foreign ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baghaei** said the package due on **Monday August 24** amounts to a **"declaration of war"** on all countries and goes beyond **"an illegal economic war against a single nation,"** describing it as **"an attempt by the United States to exert extraterritorial sovereignty over all independent UN member states."** Pairing sanctions with a naval blockade, he warned, would end in **"the complete erosion of sovereignty as the foundational basis of the UN-based inter-State system, and a recipe for an abysmal return to full-scale classic colonialism."** **Mohsen Rezaei**, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, went further on state television: **"Any country participating in the imposition of economic restrictions against us is considered an enemy."** States that will not **"distance themselves"** from Washington will have their interests **"harmed,"** he said, naming the disruption of **Persian Gulf and Hormuz oil shipments** as the instrument. He also said **"the Strait of Hormuz is closed and will not reopen"** unless American behaviour changes, that **"if Trump wants to take action, we will retaliate in an earthquake-like manner,"** and — a notable limiting clause — that Iran had **"not yet attacked any American economic interests."** A close ally of the Supreme Leader said Trump's rhetoric came from **"desperation"** and vowed Tehran **"will not submit."**

**Washington's side of the ledger stayed financial and stayed on schedule.** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent's** news conference detailing the package is set for **2 p.m. ET on Monday August 24**, after his pledge of **"the toughest sanctions in history,"** **"the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world,"** and a **"one-two punch"** of blockade plus designations that **"is going to work in Iran and we are going to collapse this regime."** He told third countries they are **"either with us or against us"** and that **"any remaining tie to Tehran will hasten a nation's economic oblivion, whether that tie be purposefully constructed or willfully ignored,"** promising that the Treasury **"will put its full might and force toward enforcing against you."** Bessent has separately said the United States likely would **not restart large-scale combat operations**. Asked about a deal on **August 22**, Trump said: **"Iran would love to make a deal, but they're not ready to make the right deal in my opinion."**

**The first route-share dataset of the war was published, and it cuts against the American claim of control.** Al Jazeera's **August 20** analysis of the period **August 1-19** counted **236 vessels of all cargo types** crossing the Strait: **83 openly using Iran's prescribed northern route**, **three openly using the US-backed Omani route**, **two using the pre-war central route**, and **148 — 62% — going dark or unclassified**. Of **112 oil and gas vessels**: **21 Iranian route, two Omani route, 89 dark** — more than 80%. The article's stated conclusion is that **"the fear of offending Tehran appears to outweigh Trump's threats,"** and that Iran **"still retains significant capacity"** to influence maritime traffic, though ship-to-ship transfers and alternative logistics may eventually erode that advantage. Iran International reported on **August 22** that **nearly 200 ships transited last week, up from about 150** the week before, with over 80% using Omani routes or going dark. UKMTO data cited by CBS put the **week ending August 7** at **21 inbound and 18 outbound** transits — roughly **4% of pre-conflict levels** — and UKMTO still assesses the risk to mariners as **severe**. PortWatch's most recent published day, **August 16**, logged **one transit** against a **73-per-day** pre-crisis baseline. The straits.live board at **2256Z on August 22** carried **Day 175**, **331 hulls holding position away from berth** on a seven-day range of **201-530**, war-risk cover at **40 times pre-crisis levels** or roughly **$10.0 million** to insure a single VLCC, and market-implied odds of a reopening by **September 1 below 1%**.

**The blockade tightened by one hull.** CENTCOM said that as of **August 21** US forces had **redirected 68 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two** — up from 67 as of August 20, 64 on August 17, 44 on August 3 and 35 on August 2 — and published imagery of an **MH-60R Sea Hawk** landing aboard **USS Ross (DDG-71)**, described as one of **more than 20 warships** supporting the blockade. The pace of interdiction has slowed sharply, which is consistent with traffic that has largely stopped presenting itself rather than with relaxed enforcement.

**The shooting that is still happening is happening to merchant crews, and this briefing had not named it.** The August record inside the Strait includes the bulk carrier ***Minoan Pioneer***, struck by an unidentified projectile in her engine room about **20 nautical miles northeast of Khasab** late on **August 3**, causing a complete blackout and a fire in the accommodation block, with the **third engineer reported missing** and no claim of responsibility — the fourth maritime security incident near Oman's Musandam Peninsula in five days. An **ADNOC tanker** was hit by a missile on **August 8**, which Abu Dhabi called an act of **piracy by the IRGC** and which drew condemnation from Gulf and Arab governments. The ADNOC vessels ***Navig8 Messi*** and ***Tarif*** were struck by **drones on August 13**, causing minor damage; the UAE accused Iran. The Greek-owned, Liberian-flagged bulk carrier ***Minoan Dignity*** was attacked on **August 17-18**, **killing her chief engineer**. **ADNOC states that 16 of its vessels have been attacked since February 28, with one crew member killed and 20 injured.** These are civilian maritime casualties inside the chokepoint, distinct from the Bab al-Mandeb deaths already recorded.

**Kharg was throttled, then partly restarted — and still not taken.** TankerTrackers recorded a **National Iranian Tanker Company VLCC loading about two million barrels at the Azarpad jetty on August 14**, the first loading at the island since late July, after the **western terminal sat empty for 22 consecutive days from July 18**, the **LPG terminal for 13 days from July 27** and the **eastern terminal for 10 days from July 30**. This refines the prior cycle's record of a dark VLCC berthing on August 12: loading resumed in the **August 12-14 window after a roughly 25-day halt**. No US amphibious, mine-countermeasures or ground activity against the island accompanied it. The denial of Iran's principal export outlet continues to be produced by **blockade, insurance and counterparty risk** rather than by seizure.

**Two second-order facts are logged with their sourcing stated.** Iran International reported on **August 22** that Russia's **Rosatom has returned 42 specialists to the Bushehr nuclear plant**, with staffing planned to rise to **100 by autumn**, and that **Iran-linked hackers shut down a small British power plant for four days** in what officials described as a first-of-its-kind attack. The cyber report is **single-sourced** and is recorded here as reported rather than as established.

**And Tehran continued to narrate the war as won.** President **Masoud Pezeshkian** said the world had **"approved"** Iran's victory and that America was **"hated around the world,"** repeating that **"it is better to end the war today, while we are strong and honored."** Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** dismissed the sanctions threat as **"same bull, different bullies."** Parliament speaker **Ghalibaf** said the United States and Israel had recognised they could not overcome Iran through conventional military warfare and had turned to **"cognitive and economic warfare,"** and that neighbouring states were seeking to **"reshape new security arrangements"** with Tehran. Iran **finalised a preferential trade agreement with Oman**, pending parliamentary approval, and Iranian officials floated **expanded Omani port trade, new pipelines and rail links to bypass the Strait** — proposals that, if realised, would reduce the value of the chokepoint Tehran is currently holding shut.

**The ledger.** The Pentagon's published toll stands at **774-775 US casualties — 18 killed and 756-757 wounded**, outlets differing by one on the same day's data after a single-day addition of **59-60** on August 21 that took the wounded count from 697. The split is **14 killed and 418 wounded** in Operation Epic Fury since February 28 and **four killed and 339 wounded** in overseas operations since July 7. The Department gave no account of when or where the additional injuries occurred. **Brent** futures closed at **$93.93** on **August 22** against a previous close of $93.78, on a day range of **$92.76-$94.82**, completing a **second consecutive weekly gain of roughly 6%**; straits.live carried **$94.39** with markets closed. The **AAA national average** US pump price stood at **$4.1024** on August 22, close to a dollar above the year-earlier level.

**Ground rung.** Every execution indicator remained at **zero for a 178th consecutive day**: no landing, no embarkation, no MEU tasking, no airborne insertion, no relief ARG, no new deployment order, no mobilisation, no draft order, no medical or fuel prepositioning consistent with a lodgement, and no reported special-operations ground activity inside Iran. The amphibious picture should be stated structurally: the **Boxer ARG** — USS Boxer (LHD-4), USS Comstock (LSD-45), USS Portland (LPD-27) — with the **11th MEU** remains the **sole ARG in CENTCOM**; the Navy's other deployed ARG, **Iwo Jima with the 22nd MEU**, is committed to **Caribbean counter-narcotics operations under SOUTHCOM**; and the **24th MEU is deployed without an ARG at all** as *Littoral Combat Force 24*, spread throughout its region rather than massed. USS Tripoli concluded its deployment on **July 22** with roughly 2,500 Marines of the 31st MEU ashore at Okinawa and **no relief ARG announced in the month since**. Force levels held at **more than 50,000 US personnel** and **330-plus aircraft**; roughly **2,000 soldiers of the 82nd Airborne Division** with divisional headquarters remain in the region since late March, never committed. The only genuine ground-planning indicator in the open record remains the **July 26 New York Post report** that the Pentagon is weighing an operation to seize Iran's enriched-uranium stockpile requiring **"thousands of ground troops"** to storm **Fordow, Natanz, Isfahan and Pickaxe Mountain**, with retrieval by **SEAL Team 6's Silver Squadron**, the Army's **2nd Ranger Battalion** and the **21st Ordnance Company** — single-sourced to an unnamed person familiar with the matter, unconfirmed by any official, undecided, and the same concept the President publicly declined in June as needing **"at least two weeks"** on the ground and the airlift of **"massive equipment"** against material he called **"entombed."** Planning is not force flow.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 2-22 (DAY 177): THE PRESIDENT CANCELLED THE ENERGY CAMPAIGN BY NAME ON AUGUST 1 AND THE STRIKES STOPPED FOR TWENTY NIGHTS. THE 60-DAY MOU WINDOW EXPIRED ON AUGUST 17 WITH NOTHING SIGNED — TRUMP DEMANDED SURRENDER, DISCLAIMED ANY TIMETABLE, THREATENED TO BOMB OMAN AND CLAIMED 'TOTAL CONTROL' OF THE STRAIT 'WITH THE BLOCKADE.' ON AUGUST 20 VANCE DECLARED A 'NEW PHASE' OF ECONOMIC PRESSURE AND BESSENT PROMISED 'THE GREATEST COORDINATED ECONOMIC ISOLATION IN THE HISTORY OF THE WORLD' — AND SAID LARGE-SCALE COMBAT LIKELY WOULD NOT RESTART. IRAN AND OMAN ANNOUNCED A HORMUZ REGIME BARRING US AND ISRAELI VESSELS; WASHINGTON REJECTED IT. THE UAE SUSPENDED ALL TRADE WITH IRAN AFTER A BALLISTIC MISSILE DETECTION. LINCOLN OUT AFTER 252 DAYS AT SEA, GEORGE WASHINGTON IN — A ROTATION, NOT A SURGE. GROUND RUNG: EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR AT ZERO FOR A 177TH DAY.

**The campaign was cancelled by name, and the previous cycle's open question is closed.** The single most testable proposition carried into this cycle was a reported multi-day bombing campaign against Iran's power plants, refineries, Tehran's electricity grid and dual-use bridges, described as able to begin "as soon as this weekend," which did not begin. Late on **August 1** President Trump announced that he was **cancelling the planned attack**, citing progress in negotiations, saying Iran and **"other Middle Eastern countries"** had asked him to hold off, and conditioning the cancellation on **"being able to rapidly make a DEAL"** that **"would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat."** **Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman** had spoken with him that Saturday expressing concern over the strike plans; **Qatar, the UAE, Turkey and Pakistan** had also pressed both sides to de-escalate. Tehran denied requesting a pause, calling the claim **"nothing but a new lie,"** and Defence Minister Majid Ibn al-Reza said Iran would **"neither be caught off-guard nor remain passive."** On **August 2-3** Trump called Iranian leadership **"unbelievably duplicitous"** after Tehran contradicted his claim that negotiations would resume. *Al Jazeera*'s August 2 analysis listed the fall in US Patriot stocks from roughly 2,300 to fewer than 827 among the practical influences on the decision. The audit records the cancellation as fact and does not adjudicate between the leverage and constraint readings — see open question `iran-strike-pause-choice-or-constraint-august-2026`.

**And the pause held for twenty nights.** No US or Israeli strike inside Iranian territory was confirmed by CENTCOM through the **0500 ET cutoff on August 19**, extending the halt to a **twentieth consecutive night**. No new Iranian civilian casualties from strikes were reported across that span. Iran's position through the period was described as **"attack for attack"** — if the attacks stop, Iran halts its own operations. For a war whose escalation had been modelled as a ratchet, this is the second consecutive cycle in which the ladder moved down, and the first in which a decision-maker publicly owned the descent.

**The negotiating window then closed without a deal.** **August 17** marked the expiry of the 60-day period the two sides agreed in June to end the war and settle the nuclear question. Nothing was signed. Trump demanded that Iran **"put up the white flag of surrender,"** said **"I have no time schedule"** and that he was not **"in a hurry,"** and — asked about Oman's mediation — told Fox News that if Oman **"gets in the way, we'll bomb the s*** out of them,"** adding that the longtime US strategic ally had not **"behaved very well"** but **"we'd handle them very easily, just like we do other things."** He also said he was interested in **declaring the Strait of Hormuz a US territory**, asserting **"we have total control over the strait"** and **"we control it with the blockade,"** which he described as a **"wall of steel."** Iranian foreign ministry spokesman **Esmaeil Baghaei** said the United States had violated the MOU weeks after signing it, preventing negotiations from starting properly; FM **Abbas Araghchi** said Tehran **"had not yet made a decision to restart negotiations with the United States"** and insisted the waterway **"will remain Iranian."** On **August 18** Trump said no talks were under way or scheduled, and an IRGC spokesman rejected his claim of backchannel contacts as **"fantasies."** Analyst **Bryan Clark** noted that Washington's military options are limited, with air power alone unable to decide the conflict.

**Then the war changed category. On August 20 the administration named its successor phase and it is financial.** Vice President **JD Vance** said the war with Iran had entered a **"new phase"** of economic pressure: **"We're going to keep that going because we think that's the best way to ultimately accomplish the final objective here"** — the objective being that Iran cannot rebuild its nuclear capacity. Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** told CNBC the United States would impose **"the toughest sanctions in history"** and create **"the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world,"** with a news conference set for **Monday August 24** to detail the package, and threatened **secondary sanctions** on nations and companies conducting business with Iran. In the same interview **Bessent said the US likely would not restart large-scale combat operations** as it steps up economic pressure. Trump said the US would choke Iran's economy by levying major penalties on any country providing **"any type of lifeline"** to Tehran, and the administration briefed the campaign as an **"economic D-Day."** The Treasury separately issued fresh sanctions targeting **Hezbollah**, re-designating it for acting on behalf of the IRGC Quds Force. Iran's Armed Forces chief **Ali Abdollahi** warned of **"revolutionary, crushing, regret-inducing and devastating responses."**

**Iran contested the Strait by announcement rather than by battle.** On **August 6-7** Tehran said it had reached an arrangement with **Oman** on a Hormuz transit route that **bans American and Israeli vessels outright**, **fines violators up to 20% of cargo value**, denies passage to countries and individuals deemed to have caused damage to Iran until Iran is compensated for war damages, and assigns Iran responsibility for **navigation guidance, vessel-traffic monitoring, maritime security and environmental protection**, with Iranian officials overseeing inbound traffic and Omani officials outbound, and with the Iranian and Omani routes to remain in use temporarily before traffic is redirected through a central course. **The Trump administration rejected the plan** and any **"impediments."** Iran's parliament speaker stated the strait **"will not reopen until US sanctions are lifted and frozen assets released."** Traffic itself stayed near zero throughout: PortWatch logged **one transit on August 9** against a **73-per-day pre-crisis baseline**; the week to August 15 ran at about **4% of pre-war levels**; **five vessels crossed on Saturday August 15 and none on Sunday August 16** against thirty-one the previous weekend; and **thirteen vessels transited on Thursday August 16** (four inbound, nine outbound), most of them product tankers. straits.live counted **314 hulls holding position away from berth on August 18 and 386 on August 21**, with **542** Hormuz-area port arrivals in the 24 hours to August 21 and the Hormuz Index composite in its **extreme** band. **War-risk cover for a transit is running near 10% of hull value**, with insurers trimming quotas and some withdrawing entirely. Whether the closure is principally an American blockade effect or an Iranian deterrent effect cannot be adjudicated from the traffic data — see open question `hormuz-control-attribution-august-2026`.

**Force was used at sea, not on land.** On **August 11** a US Navy helicopter fired **two Hellfire missiles into the engine room of the Panama-flagged container ship *Vela Nova*** in the **Gulf of Oman**, disabling its steering gear after the crew ignored repeated warnings while attempting to transit toward an Iranian port in violation of the blockade reimposed on **July 13**. CENTCOM's running blockade tally moved from **35 commercial vessels redirected, 2 disabled and 2 boarded on August 2**, to **44 redirected on August 3**, to **64 by August 17**, to **67 redirected, 3 disabled and 2 boarded as of August 20**. Cumulative figures across the war's two blockade periods are reported as three ships seized and 85 vessels intercepted.

**The southern flank produced the war's first Houthi-attributed shipping deaths.** On **August 11-12** a Houthi missile attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo ship ***Tihamah*** in the **Bab al-Mandeb** killed six — one Indonesian and three Pakistani crew members after a fire broke out aboard, and two members of the Yemeni armed forces killed during a rescue mission when a second missile was launched at the ship. It was the first reported fatality from attacks on Red Sea shipping in more than a year. Houthi-aligned media said the vessel carried Saudi military equipment; Yemen's Transport Ministry said it carried food. The group had declared a **naval blockade of Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea on July 20**, breaking a years-long civil-war truce. On **August 20** a Houthi military spokesman claimed drone attacks on **Najran airport** and an **Aramco facility**. In the same security vacuum, Somali piracy reached a decade high: on **August 20** pirates hijacked the Eritrean-flagged tanker **SIBU 1**, sanctioned by the US Treasury in December as part of Iran's shadow fleet, **136 nautical miles east of Al Mukalla, Yemen** — the second hijacking in four days, with Danish Shipping reporting **13 incidents in the first seven months of 2026 against five in all of 2025**.

**The Gulf littoral moved toward Washington.** On the night of **August 18** Emirati air defences **detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran** — the first such detection since the **May 4** strike on Fujairah port — the first falling outside and the second inside UAE territorial waters, with no damage or casualties and **maritime traffic assessed as the intended target**; nationwide shelter warnings sounded for the first time in weeks. On **August 19** Abu Dhabi **suspended all trade activities, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran until further notice**, citing an escalation that undermines regional and international peace and security. The UAE had been Iran's principal re-export and financial conduit on the Arab littoral, supplying **more than 30% of Iranian imports**. Baghaei called the Emirati statement **"baseless."**

**The naval picture is a relief, not a reinforcement.** **USS Abraham Lincoln** departed the theatre after roughly nine months and **252 days without a port call** — the longest stretch at sea since the early pandemic — amid reporting describing declining morale, suicidal ideation among sailors and an incident in which a sailor was prevented from going overboard. **USS George Washington (CVN-73)**, the Navy's only forward-deployed carrier, arrived in the **CENTCOM** area of responsibility on **August 19** with cruiser **USS Robert Smalls (CG-62)** and destroyer **USS Shoup (DDG-86)**, transiting the Arabian Sea, having come from the South China Sea by way of a port call at **Da Nang**. Net carrier presence is **unchanged at one**; no second strike group was ordered. The **USNI Fleet and Marine Tracker of August 17** continues to show the **Boxer Amphibious Ready Group** — **USS Boxer (LHD-4)**, **USS Comstock (LSD-45)**, **USS Portland (LPD-27)** — with the embarked **11th Marine Expeditionary Unit** in the region, still the **sole deployed ARG fleet-wide**, with **CH-53E Super Stallions** aboard Portland as the MEU's routine aviation combat element. **USS Tripoli** has been home since concluding its 5th and 7th Fleet deployment on **July 22**, with roughly 2,500 Marines of the **31st MEU** ashore at Okinawa and **no relief ARG announced**.

**The capability investments point away from land.** On **August 13** CENTCOM announced **Task Force Falcon Strike**, the first multi-domain, multinational one-way attack drone task force, employing unmanned systems from above, on and below the sea with US and regional partner personnel, following **Task Force Scorpion Strike** established nine months earlier. On **August 17** the Navy awarded **Raytheon** a **seven-year, $22.9 billion Tomahawk contract** to lift annual production above **1,000 missiles**, after roughly **one-third of the US Tomahawk stockpile** was depleted with **more than 1,000 expended** since Operation Epic Fury began — over **850 in the first four weeks**.

**Kharg was throttled, not taken.** Satellite imagery through early August showed the island's loading terminals **empty** with a queue of **16-17 tankers waiting offshore** and **no tanker loaded for a week**; on **August 12** a **dark VLCC berthed and loaded for the first time since July 18**, while the eastern oil terminal and the LPG facility remained idle. Reporting emphasises that the bottleneck is **access, not infrastructure damage** — vessel owners, insurers, crews and traders face heightened risk calling at Iranian ports or transiting the Strait. Chinese imports of Iranian crude fell to **534,000 barrels a day in August from 823,000 in July**, with fewer September and October cargo offers and roughly **40 million barrels stranded in Malaysian waters**. The island has never been seized and was not named as a target in any reporting during this period.

**Iran put a price on American service members who are not there.** On **August 16** Army chief **Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami** announced a reward of **5 billion tomans — about $30,000 — for killing or capturing a US service member, doubled to about $60,000 if carried out by a woman**, telling IRNA the scheme followed **"a large number of requests."** Reporting noted that Iran did not explain where prospective claimants would encounter American troops; there is **no known deployment of US ground forces inside Iran**.

**The ledger.** The **Pentagon added 60 wounded to its rolls on August 21**, taking the published total to **775 US casualties — 18 killed and 757 wounded** — split between **Operation Epic Fury** (14 killed, 418 wounded since February 28) and **overseas operations since July 7** (4 killed, 339 wounded). The Department gave no account of when or where the additional injuries occurred and did not respond to a request for more information; *The Intercept* had reported on **August 4** that the Pentagon had found **"a new way to undercount U.S. casualties in Iran."** **Brent** traded between roughly **$93.40 and $95.29** on August 21 for a second consecutive weekly gain above 5%, its highest since late July; straits.live carried **$94.03**. **AAA** put the US national average pump price at **$4.10 on August 20**, the highest ever recorded on that date, with the August monthly average at **$4.06** against August 2022's **$3.97**. On the Iranian side, the **IMF projects a 5.4% GDP contraction in 2026**, CPI inflation is projected near **69-70%**, point-to-point food inflation reached **128.1%** in late July with meat up **178%** year-on-year, unemployment rose from **7.6% in Q1 to 9.1% in Q2** with roughly **one million jobs lost**, and the dollar passed **187,000 tomans** in mid-August. Baghaei said on **August 4** that there were **no IAEA inspectors in Iran**, with a delegation visit discussed for "less than 10 days" hence. Iran's parliament passed a law punishing citizens who speak to foreign media with up to **two years' imprisonment**, and hijab enforcement intensified across 15-plus cities.

**And Tehran said the quiet part.** On **August 21** President **Masoud Pezeshkian** told a meeting of doctors: **"It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity."** He defended the June MOU as not signalling a defeat for Tehran. Supreme Leader **Mojtaba Khamenei** has said he approved the deal despite holding **"different views,"** and has appointed a former IRGC commander to lead the Supreme National Security Council.

**Ground rung.** Every execution indicator remained at **zero for a 177th consecutive day**: no landing, no embarkation, no MEU tasking, no airborne insertion, no relief ARG, no new deployment order, no draft order, no mobilisation, no medical or fuel prepositioning for a lodgement, and no reported special-operations ground activity inside Iran. Force levels held at **more than 50,000 US personnel** and **330-plus aircraft** across Al Udeid, Muwaffaq Salti and Prince Sultan, assembled via roughly 310 logistics flights since early January. Roughly **2,000 soldiers of the 82nd Airborne Division** with divisional headquarters remain in the region since late March, never committed. The **Selective Service System's "Readiness Simulation"** vendor window **closed on August 14 with no award announced**, and the automatic-registration rule withdrawn on July 23 has still not been re-proposed; **December 19, 2026** remains the statutory start of automatic registration, which is not a draft. US polling put net support for the war at **−19.6** in mid-August, Trump's approval at **35%** overall and **29%** on Iran, and support for deploying troops at roughly **20%**.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — AUGUST 1-2 (DAY 157): THE WEEKEND THE CAMPAIGN WAS TO BEGIN PASSED WITHOUT IT, AND THE REPORTING VERB REVERTED FROM 'HAS ORDERED' TO 'IS WEIGHING.' AL JAZEERA RECORDS THAT TRUMP 'HAD NOT YET AUTHORIZED THE POTENTIAL TWO-WEEK OPERATION TARGETING TEHRAN'S ELECTRICITY GRID'; ABC NEWS REPORTS CENTCOM HAD PREPARED A TWO-WEEK AIR CAMPAIGN WHILE SOME OFFICIALS FAVOURED 'A SHORTER, MORE SEVERE SALVO' TO ADVANCE NEGOTIATIONS — AN ARGUMENT BETWEEN TWO AIR OPTIONS. THE CYCLE'S LARGEST NEW FACT IS A CEILING: CSIS PUTS REMAINING STOCKS UNDER 827 PATRIOT AND UNDER 278 THAAD INTERCEPTORS, MORE THAN 60% EXPENDED, THREE-PLUS YEARS TO REBUILD, WITH GEN. DAN CAINE REPORTED TO HAVE WARNED PRIVATELY. WASHINGTON MOVED PEOPLE INSTEAD OF MUNITIONS — TEN COUNTRIES' EMBASSIES TOLD AMERICANS TO DEPART OR PREPARE TO. HORMUZ TRANSITS FELL 77% IN A DAY WITHOUT A SHOT BEING FIRED. IRAN NAMED US REGIONAL ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE AS ITS RETALIATION TARGET. THE SENATE REJECTED A WAR POWERS RESOLUTION 49-50. THE DRAFT RUNG SPLIT FOR THE FIRST TIME. GROUND RUNG: EVERY EXECUTION INDICATOR AT ZERO FOR A 157TH DAY.

**The campaign did not begin.** The single most testable proposition carried into this cycle was that a multi-day campaign against Iran's energy and civil infrastructure could start "as soon as this weekend," with CBS News reporting internal discussion of concluding before financial markets opened Monday. The weekend arrived. Through the end of August 1 no outlet reported a US strike wave against Iranian territory, and no American munition was reported to have landed on Iranian soil during the cycle. For a prediction-audit project this is a finding of the first order, and it is recorded as a non-event rather than converted into an inference about intent.

**The reporting verb moved backwards.** *Al Jazeera* recorded on August 1 that President Trump "had not yet authorized the potential two-week operation targeting Tehran's electricity grid." That aligns with *CBS News*'s July 31 position that final authorisation had not been given and against the *Wall Street Journal*'s framing that the order had been issued. *ABC News*, updating at 7:34 PM EDT on July 31, described Trump as "considering" strikes that could begin over the weekend, with two US officials cautioning that "those plans could still change."

**And the internal argument is between two air options.** ABC introduced the detail that reframes the package: CENTCOM had prepared a two-week air campaign, but some administration officials favoured "a shorter, more severe salvo" intended to advance negotiations rather than to force capitulation. Two things follow. The dispute is over the duration and severity of an air campaign, conducted in public through anonymous sourcing. And the objective is itself contested inside the administration — capitulation versus leverage in talks — which is a materially different reading of the same package from the one that circulated on July 31. No ground element re-entered the reporting in any version.

**The ceiling: more than 60% of the interceptor inventory is gone.** The cycle's largest new fact is not an event but a constraint. CSIS researchers estimate that fewer than **827 Patriot interceptors** remain in US stocks against a pre-war estimate of roughly **2,200** of the platform's two most-modernised variants — a reduction of about 65% — and fewer than **278 THAAD** against **452**. CSIS assesses that the US military has fired **more than 60%** of its key Patriot and THAAD interceptors during the war with Iran. **Three sources familiar with the matter told *CNN* the CSIS estimates are close to internal government figures.**

**The recovery arithmetic is worse than the inventory.** The United States produces **183 THAAD interceptors a year**, and it takes roughly **three and a half years** from contract signature to delivery. CSIS assesses **three or more years** to return to pre-war inventory levels — even against the **$18.2 billion** allocated for Patriots, THAADs and Tomahawk cruise missiles within the Pentagon's **$67 billion FY2026 emergency funding proposal**. Money buys the schedule; it does not buy relief inside it. CSIS's own strategic framing is that the greater risk is not sustaining the current conflict but **responding to another high-intensity contingency before inventories can be rebuilt**, with depleted stocks forcing the US and coalition partners to accept greater operational risk in air-defence operations.

**The command signal.** **Gen. Dan Caine**, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, is reported to have warned privately about the munitions shortages, and that warning is cited in reporting as a factor in the administration's restraint on broader strikes against Iran. This is continuous with the July 26 reporting in which Gen. Caine warned on dwindling air-defence intercepts and CENTCOM commander Gen. Brad Cooper told the White House the target set was "mostly exhausted."

**Why this is a ground-rung fact and not only an air-defence fact.** An amphibious or airborne lodgement on Kharg Island — a mined island twenty miles off the Iranian coast — would have to be defended against Iranian ballistic and cruise missile fire for the entire period it was held, and the interceptors that would defend it are the same depleted inventory. The open-source force requirement is unchanged at roughly **1,200-plus troops**: a Marine battalion landing team, a reinforced Army airborne battalion, or a combination. What this cycle adds is that the covering asset is now demonstrably scarce and cannot be replenished inside three years. Specialists have identified **holding** the island rather than taking it as the binding problem since March 2026; the interceptor data supplies the arithmetic behind that judgement for the first time.

**Washington moved people instead of munitions.** On August 1 US embassies across **at least ten Middle Eastern countries** — the UAE, Qatar, Oman, Iraq, Jordan, Israel, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Egypt — issued near-simultaneous security alerts telling Americans to **consider departing, or to be prepared to depart**, describing a security environment with **"the potential for unforeseen escalation"** and warning of flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures and travel disruption. The stated rationale was that "the Iranian regime is unpredictable, as seen by its recent decisions to attack areas in the region without warning or provocations as well as to expand attacks to areas not previously targeted" — Egypt cited as the example — together with a drone strike on a US gas tanker in the Mediterranean. Advisories at this scale had not been issued simultaneously across the region at any prior point in the war.

**Directionality note.** The advisories are a genuine escalation indicator and are logged as one. They are **not** a ground-operation indicator. The signature preceding a landing is inbound: force flow, prepositioning, medical and fuel staging, embarkation. This cycle produced outbound civilian movement. It is also worth recording what was **not** done: no **ordered departure** of official personnel or dependents was announced, which is the distinct and more escalatory category.

**The Strait tightened without a decision.** Ship-tracking data showed transits through Hormuz falling **77% in a single day, from 22 vessels the previous day to five**. The straits.live board at 22:59 UTC on August 1 held its established framing — latest published commercial transit volume of **10 vessels against an 88/day pre-crisis baseline, or 11% of normal** — with **371 vessels holding position away from berth**, **36 tankers running AIS-dark** over 24 hours, **war-risk insurance at 8.0 times pre-crisis rates** (approximately **$2.5 million per VLCC**), **eight of the nine largest container lines** routing via the Cape of Good Hope, and market-implied odds of the strait reopening by **August 15 at 2%**. The Crisis Pressure Index stood at 92/100. CENTCOM's tally of commercial vessels redirected since the blockade restart rose to **24**. The collapse occurred with no US strike wave and no new Iranian declaration: the threat alone was sufficient.

**Two tanker incidents in Omani waters, both unattributed.** UKMTO logged a tanker reporting a large splash followed by an explosion about **21 nautical miles northeast of Khasab**, Oman, with the master reporting no damage; and a tanker **struck by an unknown projectile about 11 nautical miles northeast of Limah**, Oman, sustaining **engine-room damage** and declaring itself **not under command**. No casualties, no environmental impact, no claim of responsibility, and no attribution by any reporting outlet. This repeats the evidentiary structure that has left the Damietta attack unresolved.

**Iran named its targets.** A senior Iranian security official told the semi-official *Tasnim* news agency that Iran has **"prepared a comprehensive plan to respond to any potential American recklessness,"** naming **US energy infrastructure in the region** and **Israeli critical infrastructure** as explicit retaliation targets should Iran's own energy sites be struck. **Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi**, head of Iran's wartime military command, said at 4:27 AM on August 1 that **"the United States is rapidly moving down the path of escalating tensions,"** and warned that countries acting as **"a defensive shield for criminal, aggressor America will burn in the fire of war."** Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** warned against **"adventurous action"** in calls with Turkish and Pakistani counterparts, stating Tehran's readiness for a **"decisive and proportionate response"** to any aggression by the US and Israel or to regional participation in it. President **Masoud Pezeshkian** said **"the future of Iran will be shaped by the people of Iran."**

**The threat has a documented precedent.** Iran executed this playbook in **March 2026**, striking Saudi Arabia's **SAMREF** refinery and **Jubail** petrochemical complex, the UAE's **Al Hosn** gas field, and Qatar's **Ras Laffan** LNG complex and **Mesaieed** petrochemical facility within 24 hours. Combined damage across Gulf energy facilities has been put at **up to $58 billion**, covering **more than 80 facilities**, more than a third of which sustained severe damage. Israel assesses that Iran will fire missiles at it regardless of whether it joins a new US offensive.

**Kuwait again.** Kuwait's military said early on Saturday August 1 that its air defences had **intercepted and destroyed Iranian drones**. Iran's army stated the strikes came **"in response to the recent aggression by the terrorist U.S. military against our country and its brutal attack on a residential home on Qeshm Island"** — the July 30 strike in which IRNA reported three killed, identified as a couple and their two-year-old child. No Kuwaiti casualties were reported.

**Domestic constraint, twice tested and twice held.** The **Senate rejected 49-50** a resolution to discharge from the Foreign Relations Committee a measure offered by **Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand** directing the President to withdraw US forces from hostilities against Iran absent specific congressional authorisation. Republicans **Susan Collins**, **Lisa Murkowski** and **Rand Paul** crossed over to support it; **Sen. John Fetterman** was the only Democrat voting to block. It was the second war powers measure to fail in the Senate in two weeks. Separately, the **FBI and CISA** are investigating cyberattacks on community water systems in **at least seven states**; US intelligence agencies assessed **Iran likely responsible** for a coordinated attack on **more than 30 Minnesota municipal water systems**, with Michigan also affected. **Programmable logic controllers** used for remote monitoring and control were the common target; no water supply has been reported compromised.

**Markets, restated.** Brent settled at **$87.93**, up $1.05 or **1.21%**, closing July **+22.86%** and **+26.21% year-on-year**; the straits.live board carried the same **$87.93** at 22:59 UTC on August 1, +2.38% over 24 hours against a roughly **$72** pre-crisis baseline. **This revises down by about $2.30 the $90.24 intraday print logged in the previous cycle** — the direction and the monthly magnitude are unchanged, the level is lower. Futures markets were closed for the weekend, so no August 1 or August 2 settle exists. **Exxon Mobil's** second-quarter profit doubled to **$14.53 billion** (+105% year-on-year) and **Chevron's** nearly quadrupled to **$12.07 billion** (+385%).

**A casualty-ledger divergence, flagged rather than reconciled.** This project's running tally stands at **685 wounded and 18 killed in action** as of July 31. The Pentagon's published figure, after the July reclassification that split the war into "Operation Epic Fury" and a new "Overseas Operations" category tracking casualties from July 7 onward, is **18 killed and 624 wounded** — a figure also carried by Wikipedia's infobox (which adds one contractor and gives 19 military dead) and by the militaryspend.org tracker, last updated July 30. The 61-casualty gap is an accounting-basis artefact of that reclassification, not a contradiction, and it is recorded here rather than silently reconciled.

**Ground-invasion indicators — zero for a 157th day, with a measurable reason for the first time.** Nothing on the ground rung moved. (1) The reported weekend campaign did not begin, and with it no landing, no embarkation order, no Marine Expeditionary Unit tasking, no airborne alert and no Kharg operation. (2) The internal argument reported in its place is between two air options. (3) The munitions ceiling is now quantified and cuts directly against a lodgement that would require sustained air-defence cover. (4) The mass departure advisories moved people out of the theatre, the inverse of a ground-operation signature, and stopped short of ordered departure. (5) The amphibious picture is unchanged for an eleventh day: **USS Boxer (LHD-4)** with **USS Comstock (LSD-45)**, **USS Portland (LPD-27)**, the **11th MEU** and expeditionary sea base **USS Miguel Keith (ESB-5)** in the Arabian Sea, still the **sole deployed Amphibious Ready Group fleet-wide**, with **USS Tripoli** home at Sasebo and no relief ARG announced. The USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker of July 27 remains the most recent edition; the August 3 edition is the next scheduled test. (6) **Kharg was not named** as a target in any version of the reported campaign and has never been seized; the island's only kinetic event of the war remains the **March 13, 2026** USAF raid on roughly 50 military sites — air defences, naval-mine and missile storage — which reporting states deliberately avoided the oil and gas infrastructure that handles up to 90% of Iranian crude exports. (7) Force posture is unchanged at approximately **50,000** US personnel in the Middle East, roughly 10,000 above baseline, including about **2,000 soldiers of the 82nd Airborne** with divisional headquarters in theatre since late March and never committed to Iranian territory.

**The draft rung split for the first time in the war.** The two sub-indicators moved in opposite directions. **Regulatory sub-rung, down:** the automatic-registration rule withdrawn on **July 23** after the White House held it for nearly four months has still **not been re-proposed**, and no explanation has been given by the agency or the White House. **Administrative sub-rung, up:** the Selective Service System has published a federal contracting request for a government-owned **"Readiness Simulation"** — a model capable of testing staffing, processing and mobilisation scenarios across multiple draft scenarios before a national emergency — with **vendor submissions due August 14, 2026**. *Military Times* headlined the procurement "Selective Service System wants to wargame the draft." The agency's framing is explicit that the contract does **not** announce a draft and is intended to prepare for the possibility that Congress and the President could authorise conscription during a future national emergency. The statutory backdrop is unchanged: automatic registration of men aged 18 to 26 begins **December 19, 2026**, using federal data in place of self-registration. Automatic registration is not a draft; it automates the register should one be called. Reinstating conscription requires authorisation from **both Congress and the President** during a declared national emergency. The briefing records the split rather than netting it to a single direction, and flags December 19 as the next scheduled test.

**Countervailing signals, logged not dismissed.** The Pentagon was reported on **July 24** to be readying options for weeks of limited ground operations — a Kharg seizure plus coastal raids by special operations and conventional infantry — pending presidential approval, and that reporting has never been retracted. Secretary **Hegseth**'s March non-foreclosure ("Our adversary right now thinks there are 15 different ways we could come at them with boots on the ground. And guess what: There are") stands unretracted, as does **Gen. Caine**'s statement that the range of options is "not just limited to... forces on the ground." Neither was renewed this cycle.

**Other theatres (August 1-2, 2026).** *Russia-Ukraine:* Russia's overnight barrage into August 1 killed **at least nine** and wounded **thirty** across **Kyiv** and surrounding regions, four children among the casualties, and Ukrainian air defences shot down **one of twenty-seven ballistic missiles**. **Zelensky** warned that air defences are being **overwhelmed** and said Ukraine **has run out of interceptors**; it was the second major aerial assault in two days and the second ballistic attack on Kyiv within a week. Across two consecutive barrages the ballistic intercept rate is **two of thirty-six**. Ukraine **sank a Russian container ship** in the Black Sea. **ISW** assessed on July 31 that Russia's **Northern Grouping of Forces and high military command are likely lying to the Kremlin** about gains in northern Ukraine, that battlefield evidence does not corroborate claimed advances in **northern Sumy and Kharkiv**, and that Ukrainian forces are **counterattacking** — within its standing judgement that the spring-summer 2026 offensive has failed to achieve operationally significant gains. **Poland formally protested to the Russian ambassador** over the July 30 Kh-101 detonation near Tarnawa-Kolonia and asserts the missile was recently manufactured; **Article 4 was not invoked**. *The cross-theatre coupling:* the interceptor Ukraine lacks against ballistic missiles is **Patriot**, and more than 60% of US Patriot and THAAD stocks were expended defending against Iran, with three-plus years to rebuild — three days after Zelensky pressed Trump for **licences to produce Patriot interceptors in Ukraine**. *Gulf:* the **Houthi** maritime embargo against Saudi shipping moved from declaration to effect, with **eight Saudi tankers claimed turned** and ship-tracking identifying the VLCC **Xin Long Yang** and the tanker **Rodos**, both loaded at **Yanbu**, abandoning **Bab al-Mandeb** for **Suez**; an **Iraq-Turkey pipeline** arrangement provides a **750,000 bpd** route around Hormuz. *Lebanon:* Israeli forces conducted large controlled detonations across southern Lebanon including near **al-Mansouri**, **Majdal Zoun** and **Haddatha**, following the demolition of a Hezbollah tunnel complex beneath the **Beaufort ridge** with roughly 700 tonnes of explosives; trilateral **Israel-Lebanon-US** talks remain set for **Rome, August 4-6**. *Latin America:* Venezuela's **ninth** government-opposition dialogue opened August 1 with a **joint working agenda** announced by **Jorge Rodríguez** and **Dinorah Figuera**, Machado outside by choice; a **truck bomb in Cúcuta**, Colombia injured **eleven** — eight police officers and three civilians — six days before **de la Espriella's August 7 inauguration** in Cali, with Defence Minister **Pedro Sánchez** blaming **ELN** "narcoterrorists" and **Petro** in **Havana** discussing the US "policy of strangulation" with **Díaz-Canel**; **Cuba's** energy ministry reports **all fuel reserves exhausted** with blackouts of **20-22 hours a day**. *Asia:* **Qatar** cannot meet its long-term Asian LNG delivery schedules, rippling from Seoul to Singapore, with **Japan** scored highest for exposure at 6.4, **South Korea** 5.3 and **India** 4.9, and **Qatar and the UAE** supplying **99%** of Pakistan's LNG. *DPRK:* **Kim Yo Jong** denounced denuclearisation calls, describing nuclear weapons as the **"ultimate shield"**; **Zelensky** states Pyongyang is preparing **30,000 further troops** for Russia atop roughly 15,000 committed, with around **2,000 DPRK troops killed**; the destroyer **Kang Kon** remains on course for **September commissioning**. *US-China:* no new development; the USTR **12.5% Section 301 forced-labour tariff** (effective July 24) remains the operative measure, exclusions on 178 products run to **November 10**, **Xi's** White House visit is still expected around **September 24**, and the **MANPADS** report remains denied by both Beijing and Islamabad and unverified — while CSIS's stated concern about responding to another high-intensity contingency before interceptor inventories recover applies directly to any Taiwan scenario.
