## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 28-29 (DAY 153): THE PAUSE BREAKS — AND IT BREAKS FROM TEHRAN, ON THE BALLISTIC RUNG, FULLY INTERCEPTED. AT 5:45 P.M. ET THE IRGC FIRES MULTIPLE BALLISTIC MISSILES AT US FORCES IN AN 'ATTEMPTED SURPRISE ATTACK' AND CENTCOM SAYS ALL WERE INTERCEPTED, WITH NO CASUALTIES AND NO IRANIAN CLAIM. HOURS EARLIER TRUMP HOSTS NETANYAHU FOR THEIR FIRST MEETING SINCE THE WAR BEGAN, AFTER PUBLICLY REBUFFING HIS PICKAXE MOUNTAIN INTELLIGENCE — 'I DON'T NEED BIBI TO TELL ME THAT… HE WANTS ME TO STAY INVOLVED' — AND ISRAEL'S OWN PUBLIC-DIPLOMACY CHIEF THEN CALLS THE INTELLIGENCE STORY 'A SORT OF FAKE NEWS.' TRUMP: 'WE'LL HAVE TO TAKE OUT PICKAXE… WE'LL TAKE IT VERY EASILY' AND 'IF THEY DON'T MAKE A DEAL THEN I GO BACK AND I FINISH THE JOB.' ON THE STRAIT: 'WE CONTROL THE STRAIT. OUR NAVY IS INCREDIBLE. NOT ONE SHIP HAS GOTTEN TO IRAN DURING ANY BLOCKADE.' OMAN'S GULF-BACKED PLAN OFFERS VOLUNTARY NAVIGATION FEES ON THE MALACCA MODEL, NOT IRANIAN TOLLS. BRENT SLIPS A THIRD SESSION TO ~$86.6 AND THE SHIPPING BACKLOG EASES FOR THE FIRST TIME. THE GROUND RUNG STAYS AT ZERO FOR A 153RD DAY, WITH USS BOXER CONFIRMED AS THE SOLE DEPLOYED ARG FLEET-WIDE.

**Iran breaks the pause.** At 5:45 p.m. ET on July 28, US Central Command said Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces "launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on U.S. forces" based in the Middle East, that "all Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted," and that "U.S. forces remain vigilant and at a high state of readiness." CENTCOM specified neither the number of missiles nor the targeted location; initial estimates put the salvo at no more than four ballistic missiles, with reporting indicating a trajectory toward a US military base in Jordan — the axis Iran struck on July 9 and again on July 17, when three US air-defence personnel were killed at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base. No US casualties were reported. Iran issued no claim of responsibility and no explanation, in contrast to both earlier Jordan attacks, which the IRGC announced with stated justifications. The launch came roughly a day after Trump said the US had halted strikes and that Iran wanted to talk, and two days after Iran's army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia declared on state television that "since our strategy has essentially been retaliatory, we have also halted our retaliatory operations" — a halt a senior Iranian source told Reuters would hold as long as Washington's did, and which Washington had not broken. It ends the longest reciprocal quiet of the war at four days and reverses a kinetic indicator that had been falling since July 24. Critically for this briefing's central question, it moves on the ballistic and air rung: there was no ground contact, no landing and no territorial movement by either party. Whether it terminates Iran's halt or is a bounded signalling shot fired precisely because it could be defeated is not resolvable from the public record — an intercepted salvo produces the same observable trace either way. CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED: `iran-strike-pause-reload-or-climbdown-july-2026`.

**Trump and Netanyahu meet — and the Pickaxe Mountain story collapses in public.** Benjamin Netanyahu arrived at the White House just before 11 a.m. for his first meeting with Trump since the war began on February 28, joined by Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The session ran a little over an hour behind closed doors with reporters excluded, concluding around 12:25 p.m. and formally wrapping at 1:08 p.m. EDT. Press secretary Karoline Leavitt called it "positive and productive"; a senior Israeli source said the leaders "held an excellent and comprehensive discussion on the key issues of the day, first and foremost Iran" and "reaffirmed their ironclad commitment to ensuring that Iran never has nuclear weapons"; Netanyahu called it "one of the best we've ever had." The warmth followed a public rebuke. Netanyahu had been reported across Israeli and US outlets to be bringing updated intelligence on Iran's efforts to rebuild its missile, drone and nuclear capabilities, centred on the fortified underground facility at Pickaxe Mountain near Natanz, to which Israeli assessments say Iran has transferred centrifuges and nuclear equipment and where Israel fears Tehran is moving its remaining enriched-uranium stockpile. Trump pre-empted it on Fox: "I don't need Bibi to tell me that… I know exactly what's going on there," adding that "Bibi's telling me that because he wants me to stay involved" and asking, "Why didn't you just tell it to me, why did you have to announce it to the world?" On *Fox & Friends* he said the US could take out Pickaxe "very easily," that Space Force has state-of-the-art cameras trained on the site, and that it is "not a big problem." After the meeting, Tzipi Hotovely, head of Israel's National Public Diplomacy Directorate, said Pickaxe Mountain did not come up at all and that "the idea that we have some intelligence here is a sort of fake news that ran throughout the day" — even as Trump publicly said, "We took out their nuclear sites and we'll have to take out Pickaxe." Senior US administration officials separately described the Israeli collection as "amazing" while criticising its interpretation: Israel "sees what it wants to see" and was "not assessing the intelligence objectively," giving insufficient weight to the possibility that Iran may genuinely be prepared to compromise; they described Netanyahu as "seeking another escalation against Iran, even if he avoids saying so explicitly because he does not want to appear to be pushing for war." Iran has asserted publicly since July 26 that Israel is pushing Washington to resume strikes. CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED: `netanyahu-pickaxe-intelligence-escalation-july-2026`.

**The stated escalation path is air; the claim of control is naval.** Trump's post-meeting framing kept Pickaxe Mountain conditional on diplomacy failing — "If we don't make a deal, we don't make a deal. We'll take it very easily" — and his summary of the war's terms was blunt: "If they don't make a deal then I go back and I finish the job." On the division inside his own party he said, "Some Republicans said, 'why don't we hit them harder?' … Then you have a group that says, this is actually a good time to make a deal." At the chokepoint he claimed a maritime rather than a territorial victory: "We control the Strait. Our navy is incredible. Not one ship has gotten to Iran during any blockade." CENTCOM's supporting figures as of July 28: more than 20 US Navy warships enforcing the blockade of Iranian ports, 18 commercial vessels stopped from entering or exiting (up from 12 redirected on July 27), two disabled and two boarded. The blockade has run unpaused through every day of the strike halt; Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned on July 27 that it "will be regarded as an expansion of the war in the region." No ground formation, amphibious operation or Kharg landing was named at any point in the day's statements.

**The Hormuz governance track acquires an instrument.** Oman has presented Iran with a Gulf-backed proposal for joint regional management of the Strait and carried it to Washington. It draws in part on the Malacca Strait/Singapore model, in which voluntary industry contributions fund safe navigation, and contrasts with Iran's stated preference for unilateral control and mandatory tolls; a person familiar with the US position said the proposals as delivered contain no mandatory transit tolls, and US negotiators have "concerns" but are confident differences can be resolved at a technical level. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly: "President Trump has been clear that Iran cannot toll the Strait, which is an international waterway." Rubio: "No country is allowed to charge tolls or fees on an international waterway. That's existing international law." Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Tehran will take "any action" to maintain control of the Strait and repeated that Iran has not requested negotiations with the United States and has no current plans to negotiate directly with Washington — a second consecutive day of the flat public split with Trump's "very deep talks" characterisation. Mediators and one US official said Iran and Oman remain far from agreement on whether to charge transit fees. CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED: `iran-hormuz-administration-tolls-dispute-june-2026`; `us-iran-direct-talks-existence-july-2026`.

**Casualties and attrition.** Iranian government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani told a Tuesday press conference that more than 350 government employees had been killed in the line of duty — telecommunications engineers, power-line workers, doctors, nurses and other service personnel — and that Bushehr Airport had been "completely knocked out of service" with the aircraft stationed there destroyed, while the Bushehr Meteorological Centre, "which is completely of a civilian nature, has almost nothing left of it." The same day Health Minister Mohammad-Reza Zafarghandi put the toll from recent US strikes in the southern provinces at 60; IranWire noted the two figures were issued on the same day and cannot be reconciled from the public record. All Iranian figures remain unverified independently, within a cumulative Iranian toll above 3,400 since February 28. On the American side, *The Intercept* reported that Iran has fired between 8,000 and 9,000 drones and missiles since the war began, that at least nine US outposts across the Middle East have been struck since July 9 with several sustaining "significant" damage, and that US Patriot and THAAD interceptor stocks are severely depleted — more than 11,000 munitions expended in the first 16 days of the conflict, with experts putting restoration of pre-war inventory at "three or more years." It reported that the United States now "allows missiles through its defenses only in cases where a strike is judged not to imperil U.S. lives," and asserted that the Pentagon drastically understates casualty figures — a second independent line of assertion alongside the July 26 reclassification that moved four deaths and 207 wounded into a separate "Overseas Operations" category. Official Defense Casualty Analysis System figures remain 14 killed and 420 wounded for the Iran war, with no restoration and no published accounting rule. CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED: `pentagon-casualty-reclassification-july-2026`.

**Markets and the Strait.** Brent fell a third consecutive session to about $86.58, down 1.54% on the day, with the straits.live tracker showing $87.66 (−0.11% over 24 hours) at 22:59Z — a move of roughly $1-2 against the $9-13 falls of the two prior sessions, and a cumulative decline of about $14 from the July 23 settle of $100.69. The Iranian launch came at 5:45 p.m. ET, after the day's pricing. AAA's national average eased to $4.099 for regular from $4.110 while diesel rose again to $5.321, a fresh war high, against $3.143 and $3.731 a year earlier. For the first time in the resumed phase the shipping backlog measurably eased: 405 vessels stranded against 426 the day before and 77 tankers running dark against 97, with 13 tankers transiting and 107 transiting vessels overall. IMF PortWatch's most recent count remains 10 transits on July 23 against an 88-per-day pre-crisis baseline — about 11% of normal throughput. The tracker's Crisis Pressure Index stood at 90 (Extreme), its escalation forecast at 55 (Elevated), VLCC war-risk insurance at 8.0× pre-crisis levels, and the market-implied probability of a normal reopening by August 31 at 11%.

**Ground-invasion indicators — unchanged for a 153rd day, and this was the cleanest directional test.** The pause broke upward in intensity but on the ballistic rung and from the Iranian side, fully intercepted. Every US escalation option the President stated on the record was an air option against a nuclear site, and his claim of control at the chokepoint was naval. The amphibious picture contracted further on the record: The War Zone's July 28 fleet count confirms USS Boxer (LHA-4) as the flagship of the sole deployed amphibious ready group fleet-wide, in the Middle East region, while USS Tripoli (LHA-7) has returned to Sasebo, Japan after a six-month CENTCOM and PACOM deployment, having disembarked 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit elements at Okinawa on July 22 — and six days on, no relief ARG has been announced. Fleet-wide the count is one ARG deployed, five training or in port and three in maintenance; carriers USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) and USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77) remain in CENTCOM/5th Fleet, with USS George Washington (CVN-73) in 7th Fleet after transiting the Luzon Strait into the South China Sea on July 22 and USS Theodore Roosevelt off Pearl Harbor after RIMPAC 2026. Kharg Island remains fortified and unseized, with Iranian anti-personnel and anti-armour mines laid around it including on the shoreline where an amphibious landing would stage. Force generation remains maritime and allied: the US/UK London conference on a multinational Hormuz shipping-protection coalition is expected to ask participating governments for equipment and personnel for a naval escort operation. The attrition evidence cuts against a ground phase rather than toward it — thin Patriot and THAAD stocks argue against concentrating fixed-position ground forces inside Iranian missile range. Draft indicators are unchanged: automatic Selective Service registration begins December 18, 2026 under the December NDAA requirement, automating registration should a draft be called without activating one, and reinstating conscription would require an act of Congress. Estimated US strength in the region holds around 50,000. No US troops in Iran, no landing, no Kharg seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft. **The predicted US GROUND seizure of Hormuz/Kharg remains DISCONFIRMED.**

**Sources (July 28-29, 2026):** U.S. Central Command statement via CBS News live blog, "Iran War Updates: Trump meets Israel's Netanyahu as his threat to resume bombing Iran looms over diplomacy"; CNN live blog, "Live updates: US says it intercepted Iranian ballistic missile attack on American forces in the Middle East"; ABC News live blog, "Iran live updates: US intercepts Iranian missiles in 'attempted surprise attack,' CENTCOM says"; Fox News Digital live blog, "Trump, Netanyahu reaffirm 'ironclad' commitment to keeping nuclear weapons from Iran"; *The Times of Israel* liveblog, July 28, 2026, and "Trump, ahead of meet with Netanyahu: 'I don't need Bibi' for intel on Pickaxe Mountain" and "Iran's Pickaxe Mountain did not come up in Netanyahu-Trump meeting, says Israel's public diplomacy chief"; *Ynetnews*, "After Trump jab, Netanyahu arrives at White House with Pickaxe Mountain intelligence"; *Jewish Insider*, "Trump expresses frustration with Netanyahu's reported warnings about Iranian nuclear activity"; *The Washington Times*, "Trump says he doesn't need Israel's help in dealing with Iran's Pickaxe Mountain"; *The Jerusalem Post*, "Netanyahu, Trump conclude 'positive, productive' meeting at White House"; Al Jazeera liveblog, "Iran war live: Tehran vows Hormuz control, Trump-Netanyahu talks 'positive'"; AGBI, "US reviews Oman plan for Hormuz transit"; NBC News, "Iran and Oman propose fee plan for Strait of Hormuz, sources say"; *Forbes*, "Hormuz Is Becoming A Fee-And-Permission Regime"; IranWire, "Iran Gives Two Different Death Tolls for U.S. Strikes on Same Day"; *Tehran Times*; *The Intercept*, "Iran Has Figured Out How to Overwhelm U.S. Air Defenses"; The War Zone, "Where Are The Aircraft Carriers: July 28, 2026"; USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker, July 27, 2026; TradingEconomics; straits.live Strait of Hormuz tracker, July 28, 2026 22:59Z; IMF PortWatch; AAA Fuel Prices national averages, July 28, 2026.

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 27-28 (DAY 152): THE PAUSE HOLDS A THIRD DAY AND THE PENTAGON'S PLAN FOR A 14TH CONSECUTIVE NIGHT OF STRIKES IS PRESENTED TO TRUMP AND DECLINED. TRUMP: 'I HAVE A LOT OF PATIENCE. I HAVE PLENTY OF TIME' — BUT IF TALKS FAIL 'WE GO BACK TO DOING WHAT WE WERE DOING TWO DAYS AGO,' WITH STRIKES RESUMING AT GREATER FORCE, AND 'NOT MUCH TIME. EITHER IT GOES FAST OR NOT AT ALL.' A FLAT FACTUAL SPLIT OPENS ON WHETHER TALKS EXIST AT ALL: TRUMP SAYS 'WE ARE IN VERY DEEP TALKS WITH IRAN'; FM SPOKESMAN ESMAIL BAQAEI SAYS IRAN 'CURRENTLY HAVE NO NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE UNITED STATES' AND THAT THE WEEK'S DISCUSSIONS WERE 'EXCLUSIVELY WITH OMAN.' IRAN'S KHATAM AL-ANBIYA CENTRAL HEADQUARTERS DECLARES THE US NAVAL BLOCKADE 'AN EXPANSION OF THE WAR IN THE REGION.' THE US AND UK CONVENE A LONDON CONFERENCE ON A MULTINATIONAL HORMUZ SHIPPING-PROTECTION COALITION — A MARITIME RUNG, NOT A GROUND ONE. BRENT COLLAPSES A SECOND SESSION TO $85-90 WHILE PUMP PRICES HOLD AT WARTIME HIGHS. REUTERS/IPSOS PUTS WAR SUPPORT AT ONE IN THREE, THE LOWEST OF THE CONFLICT. GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED FOR A 152ND DAY, AND FOREIGN POLICY'S SURVEY OF FORMER COMMANDERS FINDS THE US 'DOES NOT APPEAR TO BE MOVING TOWARD A MAJOR GROUND OPERATION IN IRAN.'

**A third day of two-sided quiet — and a declined 14th night.** The United States and Iran held fire for a third consecutive day, the longest reciprocal halt since the resumed phase began on July 7-8. The pause originated on Friday July 24, when President Trump directed the military not to conduct new strikes, breaking a thirteen-night streak; Iran reciprocated publicly on July 26 and has held, with its halt explicitly conditional on continued US restraint. The most significant new fact of the cycle concerns what did not happen: reporting compiled in *Just Security*'s July 27 Early Edition recorded that the Pentagon presented Trump with a plan for a 14th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, and that he declined to authorise it, preferring to let the diplomatic track run. For the second consecutive cycle, the documented decision point reaching the President concerned whether to continue or halt an **air** campaign — not whether to open a ground phase. (*Just Security*, "Early Edition: July 27, 2026"; *The Times of Israel*, July 26, 2026; American Bazaar/AP; NPR, July 27, 2026.)

**Trump: patience, with an explicit air-resumption threat on a short clock.** Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump said, "I have a lot of patience. I have plenty of time. Plenty of time," and that he saw "a good chance that something could happen. If it doesn't, we go back to doing what we were doing two days ago" — warning that renewed strikes would come with greater force than before. To *Axios* he was blunter and attached a shorter clock: "We are in very deep talks with Iran. If they don't work out, we will go back to very strong military action," and, on the window available, "Not much time. Either it goes fast or not at all." He again rejected reporting on munitions and interceptor shortages: "We have plenty. We have a lot of ammunition. Different types." No ground formation, landing or Kharg operation was named in any of it; the threatened resumption is an air threat. (Reuters via France24, "Trump sees 'good chance' for Iran deal, warns strikes could resume," July 27, 2026; CBS News live blog; CNBC, July 27, 2026.)

**A flat contradiction on whether negotiations exist.** Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baqaei said on Monday that Iran "currently have no negotiations with the United States," and that "the discussions we have had over the past few days have been exclusively with Oman" on mechanisms for managing traffic through the Strait. Deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Washington had presented "extreme demands" that Iran rejected, describing Tehran's approach as "dignified diplomacy" — an account that presupposes a channel carrying American positions to Tehran without conceding that it constitutes a negotiation. Against those statements stand Trump's "very deep talks with Iran," Amb. Mike Waltz's July 26 description of conversations running "at every level, from the more technical aspect of it all the way to the highest levels," and Associated Press reporting, citing regional officials, that mediators led by Qatar and Pakistan had made significant progress toward bringing the two sides back to negotiations and restoring the interim ceasefire deal that collapsed this month. Neither government has published a meeting record, venue, delegation list or agreed agenda. The dispute is logged as contested-unresolved (`us-iran-direct-talks-existence-july-2026`): mediated message-passing and indirect negotiation are not distinguishable from the public record, and both capitals have obvious incentives to characterise the same contacts differently. (CBS News live blog; Iran International liveblog; American Bazaar/AP, July 27, 2026.)

**Iran's joint command aims its tripwire at the blockade, not a landing.** The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters — the Iranian armed forces' joint command — said the US naval blockade of Iran amounted to an expansion of the war in the region, stating that over the previous three days the United States had threatened Iranian vessels, commercial ships and oil tankers in Iran's coastal and territorial waters. "We warn that this US action will be regarded as an expansion of the war in the region," the statement said, adding that the armed forces "will not leave unanswered any threat or hostile action by that country's terrorist army and will confront it." Separately, army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia had warned on July 26 that if the US resumes strikes, "geographically this will expand further," noting Iran had already extended operations to the Bab el-Mandeb and the wider Persian Gulf, and Tehran publicly attributes pressure for a US resumption to Israel. Tehran's declared red line this cycle is maritime interdiction. (WANA, "Naval Blockade of Iran Would Amount to an Expansion of the War"; Iran International liveblog, July 27, 2026; *The Times of Israel*, July 26, 2026.)

**The blockade does not pause.** US naval enforcement continued unchanged through the third day of the strike halt. CENTCOM's running tally since re-imposition on July 14 stands at 12 commercial vessels redirected, 2 disabled and 2 boarded — most recently the July 24 disabling of the Mozambique-flagged M/T Lavine in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored repeated warnings, and the verification boarding of the Comoros-flagged M/T Charminar in the Arabian Sea, which was cleared to continue its voyage. The IRGC has separately turned back six vessels with warning shots, and one oil tanker was reported to have struck a mine. Interdiction and visit-board-search — not a port seizure or a landing. (CENTCOM via JNS and voz.us, July 26; CBS News live blog, July 27, 2026.)

**Washington and London move to build a maritime coalition.** The United States and United Kingdom are convening a high-level conference in London this week on a potential international coalition to protect maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, potentially bringing together defence ministers and top military commanders from Western and regional states. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Gen. Dan Caine could attend, and Washington is expected to ask participating governments to contribute military equipment and personnel to a coordinated maritime-security operation, building on discussions the UK and France have held with multiple countries in recent months. The itinerary and date were still being finalised at the time of reporting. Reopening the Strait for commercial shipping is described as a key element of any US exit strategy from the war and of efforts to stabilise global energy markets. The distinction matters for the ground-invasion tracker: the personnel being solicited are allied naval escort and maritime-security forces, not US ground forces committed to Iranian territory. (*Axios*, "Scoop: U.S., U.K. planning international conference on Strait of Hormuz," July 24, 2026; *Just Security*, July 27, 2026.)

**Markets: crude collapses a second session, pump prices refuse to follow.** Brent extended the pause-driven slide. TradingEconomics recorded Brent at $90.28, down 8.23% on the day, and WTI at $82.62, down 8.68%; UPI and Yahoo Finance reported Brent closing down 8.7% at $88.36 with US crude off 7.5% at $82.61; CBS cited Brent at $85.49, −6.8%; CNBC headlined Brent below $90; and the straits.live tracker showed $87.76, −4.87%, at 23:03 UTC. Sources differ on the settle but agree on direction and magnitude: a two-session fall of roughly $10-15 from the July 23 settle of $100.69, reversing a week in which prices had gained more than 9% and Brent reached as high as $102. It remains far below the roughly $126 April wartime peak and the $130-plus a sustained US ground commitment would imply. Retail did not follow: the AAA national average held flat at $4.110 for regular and rose to $5.296 for diesel, against $4.003/$5.108 a week earlier, $3.878/$4.905 a month earlier and $3.145/$3.735 a year earlier — the consumer-facing cost of the war still at its wartime high. (TradingEconomics; UPI/Yahoo Finance; CBS News; CNBC; straits.live; AAA Fuel Prices, July 27, 2026.)

**The Strait stays shut.** The strike pause has not yet produced a measurable reopening. The straits.live tracker recorded 426 vessels stranded across the zone, 97 tankers running dark with no AIS broadcast, and 14 tankers in transit as of 23:03 UTC on July 27, against the 15 AIS-visible transits IMF PortWatch logged on July 19 and an 88-per-day pre-crisis baseline. Trackers caution that with roughly 90-100 tankers dark, true flow may exceed AIS-derived counts. The tanker waiting area off Kharg Island was reported at 24 vessels on July 26, up from 21 the previous day. (straits.live, July 27, 2026; IMF PortWatch; Lloyd's List Intelligence, Strait of Hormuz Brief.)

**Domestic support reaches its wartime low.** A Reuters/Ipsos poll released July 27 found just one in three Americans support the war on Iran — the lowest reading since the five-month-old conflict's early days — with 69% saying Trump has failed to clearly explain its goals, which have shifted between aiding Iranians to topple their leaders, destroying Iran's ballistic-missile capability, and preventing a nuclear weapon. Trump's overall approval ticked up three points to 37% from a reading that had tied the lowest of his presidency; independent registered voters favoured Democratic congressional candidates over Republicans by 36% to 20%. The finding tracks the CBS News/YouGov survey fielded July 22-24, in which 67% wanted the conflict ended now and 35% approved of Trump's handling of it. (Reuters/Ipsos via Al-Monitor and Internazionale, July 27, 2026; CBS News/YouGov, July 26, 2026.)

**Netanyahu flies out secretly; Zelensky arrives the same day.** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu departed for Washington on July 27 from Nevatim Air Force Base rather than Ben Gurion Airport, aboard the *Wings of Zion* aircraft, with his office declining to publicise the departure time in advance, citing security concerns tied to a reported Iranian threat. He meets Trump at 11 a.m. on Tuesday July 28 — their first in-person meeting in more than five months, and Netanyahu's seventh White House visit of Trump's second term — with Iran topping an agenda that also covers Gaza reconstruction under Trump's 20-point plan, Lebanon security arrangements and Saudi normalisation tied to a potential civilian nuclear deal. Netanyahu: "In these complex times one must act with both great determination and great wisdom," adding that "our goal is to safeguard our security while also expanding the circle of peace around us." He will also attend the memorial service for Senator Lindsey Graham. Trump separately hosts Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky the same day, making July 28 a single-day convergence of the Iran and Ukraine tracks at the White House. *Axios* has reported that Trump is weighing a resumption of major combat operations that would likely take the form of a joint campaign with Israel on the model of the February 28 launch of Operation Epic Fury; on July 27 he separately said there had been no discussions yet with the Saudis about joining the Abraham Accords. (*The Times of Israel*; *Foreign Policy*; Kyiv Post; CBS News, July 27, 2026.)

**Intelligence on the new Supreme Leader.** US intelligence assesses that Iran's new Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, shows greater interest in pursuing nuclear weapons than his predecessor — with the caveat that most of the underlying intelligence predates the war. Mojtaba remains out of public view months after Ali Khamenei was killed in the February 28 airstrike; Iranian state media republished October 2024 photographs of him. (*Just Security*, Early Edition July 27, 2026; Iran International liveblog, July 27, 2026.)

**Regional spillover continues through the pause.** Saudi air defences intercepted drones launched from Iraq at petroleum facilities, attributed to Iran-backed militias — the US-Iran halt does not extend to the militia and Houthi vectors. Shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait fell to its lowest monthly level, with eleven vessels transiting on Sunday July 26, following the July 25 Houthi missile-and-drone attacks on Aramco installations at Jizan and Yanbu; Saudi Arabia has begun shifting crude export routing toward Suez, with Yanbu — the East-West Pipeline outlet that handled roughly 92% of the Kingdom's seaborne crude exports in June with Hormuz shut — and the 400,000 bpd Jizan refinery both under attack. Bahrain's Defence Force announced the GCC-wide "Bahrain Shield" joint exercise for July 28-30 (CBS reported the window as July 29-31), with the armed forces of all six Gulf Cooperation Council states participating to enhance joint military action, exchange expertise and evaluate shared military systems. Iran's parliamentary national security committee head Ebrahim Azizi threatened retaliation for Ukraine's July 25 Caspian Sea strike on an Iranian commercial vessel, in which a sailor was killed. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun condemned Israeli destruction of southern villages as a human rights violation, and the UN called on Iran to cancel death sentences against ten protesters, with twelve men condemned over January protests. (CBS News live blog; *Just Security*; *The National*; Gulf Daily News; Anadolu, July 26-27, 2026.)

**Ground rung — unchanged for a 152nd day, with the strongest negative evidence of the war.** No US troops entered Iran; there was no landing, no Kharg seizure, no new amphibious ready group or Marine expeditionary unit deployment order, no relief for the departed Tripoli ARG, and no draft. More than 50,000 US personnel remain in the CENTCOM area of responsibility, the figure CENTCOM confirmed on July 19 and described as the largest US footprint in the region since the 2003 invasion of Iraq. Three developments this cycle point away from a ground phase rather than toward one. First, the escalation option documented as reaching the President was an air option, and it was declined. Second, the only force generation actually under way is the multinational maritime coalition being assembled in London, which solicits allied naval personnel rather than committing US ground forces. Third, *Foreign Policy*'s July 24 survey of former US military officials and experts found that the United States "does not appear to be moving toward a major ground operation in Iran," which would require far more troops than the roughly 50,000 currently deployed; they allowed for the possibility of ground forces in more limited operations — seizing an island such as Kharg, or special-operations raids on military sites — with retired Gen. Joseph Votel framing the realistic case as "the use of ground forces in limited raids that are going after key locations," and senior officials continuing to state that no final decision on ground deployments has been made. The capability picture also remains net-negative: the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group (USS Tripoli LHA-7, USS New Orleans LPD-18, USS Rushmore LSD-47) offloaded roughly 2,500 Marines of the 31st MEU at White Beach Naval Facility, Okinawa on July 22 after four months under CENTCOM, and five days on no relief ARG has been announced — leaving the Boxer ARG / 11th MEU (USS Boxer LHD-4, USS Portland LPD-27, USS Comstock LSD-45, ~2,200 Camp Pendleton Marines, on station since late June) as the theatre's sole amphibious group alongside the *Abraham Lincoln* and *George H.W. Bush* carrier strike groups and more than 20 warships in the Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean including about 14 guided-missile destroyers. Kharg Island remains fortified by Iran — traps laid, personnel and air defences moved in — struck from the air, blockaded at sea, and unseized. On the domestic rung, automatic Selective Service registration for men aged 18-26 takes effect December 18, 2026 under the National Defense Authorization Act, but it automates registration only and does not activate conscription, which requires an act of Congress. **The corpus-predicted US GROUND seizure of Hormuz/Kharg remains DISCONFIRMED.** (*Foreign Policy*, July 24, 2026; *Just Security*; CBS News; *Axios*, July 27, 2026; *Stars and Stripes*; USNI News; Marine Corps Times; DVIDS, July 22, 2026; The War Zone, July 20, 2026; CNN, March 25, 2026; CNBC, April 9, 2026.)

**Gulf states (July 27).** Bahrain's Defence Force opened the GCC-wide "Bahrain Shield" exercise with the participation of the armed forces of all six Gulf Cooperation Council states, aimed at enhancing joint military action, exchanging expertise and evaluating joint military-action systems — a collective-defence signal staged during the first sustained lull of the resumed phase. Saudi Arabia intercepted Iraq-launched drones aimed at petroleum facilities and continued shifting export routing toward Suez as Houthi pressure drove Bab al-Mandeb oil exports toward zero. The cumulative regional reckoning is now substantial: since February the World Bank has cut its 2026 GCC GDP growth forecast from 4.4% to 1.3%, with Oxford Economics projecting recession for some Gulf economies in the second half; around 80 energy facilities have been hit by Iranian missile and drone attacks with damage estimated at about $58 billion; Qatar stands to lose up to $20 billion a year in export revenue; and IMF projections from April showed contractions for Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar against positive growth for Saudi Arabia (+3.1%), the UAE (+3.1%) and Oman (+3.5%). Damage to Qatar's Pearl GTL plant, Kuwait's Mina Al-Ahmadi and Mina Abdullah, and the SATORP refinery has raised jet fuel costs by roughly 95%. (Gulf Daily News; Anadolu; CBS News; *The Conversation*; Stimson Center; Middle East Council on Global Affairs, July 2026.)

**Russia-Ukraine (July 27).** President Zelensky travels to the White House on July 28 carrying a proposal for a ceasefire in the air war, developed with US officials to put to Russian negotiators as part of a renewed round of peace proposals — a narrower ask than the comprehensive settlement that has repeatedly stalled over Russian demands that Ukraine withdraw from territory it still holds. On the ground, a spokesperson for Ukraine's Khortytsia group of forces confirmed on July 27 that Russian troops had advanced in the area between Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka in Donetsk Oblast, extending the partial wedge Moscow has been driving between the two towns; the Pokrovsk axis remains the main Russian effort, with an attempt under way to break through toward Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and DeepState and front-line accounts reporting Russian forces inside Pokrovsk with a "search and destruction" operation ongoing. ISW's assessments through late June and early July judged that Russian forces lack the density to sustain simultaneous offensives against both Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka and that Kostiantynivka gains remained small-group infiltration rather than consolidated control; *The Economist* estimated Russian gains of about 31 square kilometres over the thirty days to June 30, with Ukraine's occupied share holding at roughly 20%. Zelensky separately warned that Russia is preparing to receive an additional 30,000 North Korean troops, with facilities readied in Voronezh oblast since June, atop the roughly 11,000 DPRK personnel in Kursk Oblast at the start of 2026 and Pyongyang's estimated 25-40% share of Russian artillery ammunition supply, and Kyiv is requesting a prototype European anti-ballistic system, "Freyja," operational by mid-2027. (Kyiv Post; HNGN; Bloomberg via Liga.net; Ukrinform/Yahoo; Critical Threats/ISW; *Just Security*, July 26-27, 2026.)

**Other theatres (July 27).** *US-China/Taiwan:* the July 24 tariff transition remains the operative regime — the 10% Section 122 global tariff, ruled unlawful by the Court of International Trade in May 2026 but kept in force by a Federal Circuit stay pending appeal, hit its 150-day statutory limit on July 24 and was replaced the same day by Section 301 forced-labour duties of 10-12.5% covering about 60 economies including Taiwan, with China still most heavily taxed at roughly 35% above MFN on most goods and well over 100% on certain strategic products. Running alongside the escalation, China's Ministry of Commerce confirmed the two sides have "agreed in principle" to include agricultural products in a framework for reciprocal tariff reductions and to set indicative targets for expanding two-way agricultural trade. Chinese seaborne crude imports are expected to average about 7.8 million barrels a day in July, rebounding from a more-than-decade low as Gulf flows partially resumed after the June interim agreement before the July escalation snarled Hormuz again; China moves roughly 5.4 mb/d through the Strait and takes an estimated 80-90% of Iranian exports. *DPRK:* Kim Jong Un has ordered the guided-missile destroyer *Kang Kon* commissioned within two months of its July 3 cruise-missile tests, targeting operational status before September 2026, within a programme aiming at twelve Choe Hyon-class destroyers by 2030 and a 10,000-tonne guided-missile cruiser; he made 92 public appearances in the first half of 2026, 30 of them military-related, his highest first-half military total since 2012. *Latin America:* a US judge set June 1, 2027 as the trial date for Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores, who pleaded not guilty to drug-trafficking and firearms charges after their January seizure; acting president Delcy Rodríguez continues normalising with Washington after April's sanctions relief; Cuba's grid has collapsed repeatedly through July under the halted Venezuelan crude supply and Executive Order 14380 of January 29, with blocked shipments having covered about 60% of the roughly 100,000 barrels a day the island's power system requires; and Colombia's president-elect takes office on August 7 following the June 21 runoff. *Elsewhere:* Bangladesh's President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned citing health concerns amid political pressure over former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's potential return; ICC member states voted 82 of 125 to dismiss Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual-misconduct allegations; Belgian authorities arrested a Canadian NATO intern of Chinese origin on espionage suspicion; Brazil denied visas to two State Department officials planning to question electoral integrity before October elections; and Israel's security cabinet approved frameworks allowing a multinational force of about 200 personnel, from nations including Uganda and Morocco, to enter Gaza under Trump's ceasefire plan. (Trade Compliance Resource Hub; TaiwanPlus; China Briefing; PIIE; Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance; AEI Korean Peninsula Update; NK News; CNN; ABC News; Democracy Now!; CRS; *Just Security*, July 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 26-27 (DAY 151): THE PAUSE HOLDS A SECOND NIGHT AND BECOMES TWO-SIDED — IRAN'S ARMY SPOKESMAN SAYS TEHRAN HAS 'ALSO HALTED OUR RETALIATORY OPERATIONS' AND A DEFENSE DEPARTMENT SOURCE SAYS US OPERATIONS ARE 'ON A HOLD.' AXIOS REPORTS CENTCOM COMMANDER GEN. BRAD COOPER TOLD THE WHITE HOUSE THE TARGET SET WAS 'MOSTLY EXHAUSTED' AND GEN. DAN CAINE WARNED ON DWINDLING AIR-DEFENCE INTERCEPTS. IRAN-OMAN DEPUTY-FM TALKS IN TEHRAN REPORT PROGRESS ON HORMUZ TRANSIT MECHANISMS WHILE AMB. WALTZ SAYS TRUMP IS 'GIVING DIPLOMACY SOME SPACE' AND THAT 'THERE'S MORE MOVING INTO THEATER.' BRENT PLUNGES MORE THAN 5% TO ~$91/BBL AND HORMUZ TRAFFIC HITS THE WAR'S LOWEST READING (ONE VESSEL, ZERO TANKERS IN 24 HOURS). THE PENTAGON CUTS ITS OFFICIAL IRAN-WAR TOLL FROM 18 KILLED / 482 WOUNDED TO 14 / 420 VIA A NEW 'OVERSEAS OPERATIONS' CATEGORY. UKRAINE STRIKES IRAN-LINKED MILITARY CARGO VESSELS IN THE CASPIAN, KILLING A SAILOR. GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED — AND THE AMPHIBIOUS RUNG FALLS FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE WAR: THE TRIPOLI ARG OFFLOADS ~2,500 MARINES OF THE 31ST MEU AT OKINAWA WITH NO RELIEF ARG ANNOUNCED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU ORDER, NO DRAFT; 50,000+ PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**A second night without strikes — and Iran matches it.** No US strikes on Iran were reported overnight into Sunday July 26, a second consecutive quiet night after thirteen. A Department of Defense source told CNN that operations are "on a hold." Iran reciprocated openly: army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said on state television, "Since our strategy has essentially been retaliatory, we have also halted our retaliatory operations." CNN reported that Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait — all struck by Iranian missiles and drones during the resumed phase — logged no Iranian attacks overnight. This is the first *reciprocated* de-escalation since the war resumed on July 7, and the second consecutive day on which the kinetic indicator fell rather than rose. Sources: Al Jazeera, "US and Iran hit pause on strikes for second day," July 26, 2026; CNN live blog, "Trump administration signals that pause in Iran strikes will allow talks to progress," July 26, 2026; Fortune/AP, July 26, 2026; NPR/OPB, "U.S. pauses attacks on Iran for a second straight day and Tehran does too," July 26, 2026.

**Why the campaign stopped: exhausted targets and thinning interceptors.** *Axios* reported that CENTCOM commander Gen. Brad Cooper informed the White House that two weeks of intensive strikes in the Strait of Hormuz area had "significantly degraded" Tehran's ability to target commercial vessels, and that the designated bombing targets were "mostly exhausted." At the July 24 White House meeting where President Trump weighed a larger escalation, Vice President JD Vance and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine both raised concerns about escalating — Caine warning that "a dwindling supply of air defence intercept" could expose US personnel and allies to retaliation, and citing the US munitions stockpile. CBS separately reported a shortage of interceptors. Regional officials indicated the bombing was intentionally paused so as not to disrupt the in-person diplomacy in Tehran. These are constraints that argue against opening a new phase, not toward one. Sources: Middle East Monitor citing *Axios*, "CENTCOM chief advised halt of Iran strikes due to 'exhausted' targets: Report," July 26, 2026; CBS News, July 26, 2026; Anadolu, July 26, 2026.

**Washington's framing: diplomacy with the option preserved.** On CBS's *Face the Nation*, US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said the pause was "giving diplomacy some space," that conversations "to do with the Straits of Hormuz" are running "at the highest levels, all the way down to the technical levels," and that Oman is "engaging in a helpful way." He framed the president's record as "he tried diplomacy last year. He's tried it this year. He is a president of peace" — while declining to foreclose force: "I'm not going to take that option off the table for the president." Pressed on CBS reporting of an interceptor shortage, he pivoted to Iranian degradation and said: "I also want to address this nonsense that somehow we don't have the assets that we need. Not only do we have what we need in theater, there's more moving into theater." He named no unit, type or destination, and made no reference to ground troops, ground operations, an invasion or Kharg Island. He restated the objectives as preventing Iran from "ever having a nuclear weapon," opening the Strait of Hormuz, and stopping regional threats, and described a Russia-Iran "symbiotic relationship" in which Iran supplies drones used against Ukraine, saying Trump had warned Putin and Xi that "bad things will happen" if they continue assisting Iran. Trump, for his part, denied reports of dwindling US munitions and posted AI-generated images depicting attacks on Iranian facilities. Sources: CBS News, "Transcript: U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz on *Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan*," July 26, 2026; CBS News, "Full transcript of *Face the Nation*," July 26, 2026; Al Jazeera live blog, July 26, 2026.

**The Iran-Oman channel reports progress.** The deputy foreign ministers of Iran and Oman held talks in Tehran on Friday July 24 and Saturday July 25, exchanging views on "shared principles and operational mechanisms for managing the safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while respecting the sovereign rights of the two coastal states." The Omani delegation has since departed, with technical and political consultations continuing. Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said the talks "had made progress and continued," and that the Strait's status "remains unchanged" while they proceed; Tehran maintains that the June interim deal permits it to manage shipping through the waterway and objects to the US-backed alternative route near Oman. Two regional sources told CBS News the talks were "moving in a positive direction" but that the diplomacy needs more time to reach a deal; the compromise under discussion centres on Iran operating vessel transit with fewer restrictions on ships. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Tehran's position remains "attack for attack" — "if the attacks stop, Iran will also halt its operations" — while cautioning that there is "more skepticism than optimism about the halt in attacks," which Iran reads as "tactical rather than genuine." Baghaei added that mediators including Qatar and Pakistan are exchanging messages, while saying Iran's diplomatic efforts had been "betrayed." Sources: Fortune/AP, "The U.S. and Iran pause attacks on each other for a second straight day while Tehran continues talks with Oman over Hormuz," July 26, 2026; CBS News live blog, July 26, 2026; *The Jerusalem Post*, "Iran says it will halt attacks if US keeps up latest pause in strikes," July 26, 2026; Outlook India; newkerala, July 26, 2026.

**The blockade does not pause.** The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remained "in full effect" throughout the strike halt. The running enforcement tally reached 12 commercial vessels redirected, 2 disabled and 2 boarded since the blockade was re-imposed on July 14. The most recent US actions were the July 24 disabling of the Mozambique-flagged M/T Lavine in the Gulf of Oman — a fraudulently-flagged, sanctioned LPG tanker whose crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to breach the blockade at least four times, prompting disabling fire into the engine room — and the verification boarding of the Comoros-flagged M/T Charminar in the Arabian Sea, which was cleared onward. Iran's Revolutionary Guard has separately stopped six vessels with warning shots, and one oil tanker was reported to have struck a mine. This remains interdiction and visit-board-search, not port seizure or landing. Sources: Al Jazeera, July 26, 2026; Fortune/AP, July 26, 2026; CBS News live blog, July 26, 2026; AP via Türkiye Today; CENTCOM, July 24-25, 2026.

**Hormuz traffic hits the lowest reading of the war.** Windward recorded a single vessel — a Comoros-flagged general cargo ship, outbound via the northern corridor — transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the 24 hours to July 25. Zero vessels transited inbound; zero tankers crossed in either direction; and a separate 12-hour stretch that morning recorded no crossings at all. Against the pre-crisis baseline of about 88 transits per day, that is under 2%, and below the 15 transits IMF PortWatch recorded on July 19. Roughly 85 tankers continue to run dark, broadcasting no AIS signal, and the International Maritime Organization still assesses the waterway as too dangerous for commercial vessels. Sources: Windward Daily Intelligence, July 25-26, 2026; IMF PortWatch, July 19, 2026.

**Markets: crude collapses off the spike, pump prices keep climbing.** Brent fell more than 5% to about $91.20/bbl as the pause entered a second day; TradingEconomics showed $91.45, down 7.05% on the session — the sharpest single-day decline of the resumed phase and a fall of roughly $9 from the July 23 settle of $100.69. Brent nonetheless remains about 23.7% above a month earlier and 31.9% above a year earlier, and far below the roughly $126 April wartime peak or the $130-plus that a sustained US ground commitment would imply. Retail lagged: the AAA national average reached war highs of $4.111 a gallon for regular and $5.295 for diesel, against $3.998 and $5.101 a week earlier, $3.901 and $4.934 a month earlier, and $3.151 and $3.738 a year earlier — regular up about 13 cents on the week and 96 cents year-on-year, diesel up about 19 cents on the week and $1.56 year-on-year. Sources: Fox News Digital live blog, July 26, 2026; TradingEconomics, Brent crude, July 26, 2026; AAA Fuel Prices, July 26, 2026.

**The Pentagon cuts its own casualty series.** The Defense Casualty Analysis System's Iran-war totals fell from 18 killed and 482 wounded to 14 killed and 420 wounded, with four deaths and 207 wounded moved into a newly created "Overseas Operations" category dated from July 7 — the date the resumed strike-and-retaliation phase began. The four reclassified deaths are the three service members killed in the July 17 Iranian missile-and-drone strike on a base in Jordan and one killed July 18 in a drone detonation in Iraq; among them is Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad of Ozone Park, New York. Seven of the remaining 14 are classified "hostile." Pentagon press secretary Joel Valdez characterised the changes as "anomalies" and "temporary data disruptions"; spokesman Sean Parnell called it a "temporary data disruption." US officials say the true wounded figure exceeds 500, and CBS reported that more than 400 US service members have been airlifted out for treatment since Operation Epic Fury began in February, most for non-combat causes — against the Pentagon's own July 23-24 statement that nearly 100 had been injured since July 7. It is the second unexplained downward revision of the war's casualty accounting, after the May 11-12 episode in which the wounded tally rose to 428 and then dropped to 413. Sources: *The Washington Post*, "Pentagon's official Iran war death toll no longer lists 4 troops killed during renewed fighting," July 26, 2026; CNBC, "Pentagon removed four from official Iran war death toll," July 24-26, 2026; *The Philadelphia Inquirer*/AP; KSAT, July 26, 2026; CBS News live blog, July 26, 2026.

**Ukraine opens a Caspian front against Iranian military cargo.** President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Ukrainian forces struck a Russian warship and vessels "used in military cargo shipments involving Iran" in the Caspian Sea, part of a long-range wave that also hit a weapons-components factory in Kirov roughly 1,200 km from Ukraine, an oil refinery in Tyumen, a logistics facility in Yekaterinburg and a fuel-and-lubricants depot in Rostov-on-Don. Iran's foreign ministry said the attack on an Iranian commercial vessel killed one sailor and injured others, summoned Ukraine's chargé d'affaires in Tehran, and described the action as "hostile and criminal" and as reflecting an "irrational and hostile approach." Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi blamed Zelensky personally, said the strike was carried out "at Israel's behest," called it a "blatant UN Charter violation" and said it "cannot go unanswered." Zelensky separately alleged that Russia has been passing satellite imagery to Iran, saying Kyiv had recorded "active Russian satellite surveillance of the Gulf states and U.S. military facilities located there" since early July that "subsequently appear in Iran," with "a clear correlation between Russia's satellite imagery of these sites and Iranian strikes." This is the first direct Ukraine-Iran kinetic vector of the war; the two theatres had previously connected only through arms transfers. Sources: *The National*, "Ukraine claims Caspian Sea attack on ships carrying Iranian military hardware to Russia," July 26, 2026; CNBC, July 26, 2026; Al Jazeera, "Iran accuses Ukraine of deadly attack on Caspian commercial vessel," July 25, 2026, and live blog July 26, 2026; Defense News; *The Times of Israel*; ThePrint/Reuters, July 26, 2026.

**Domestic politics: a 35% war approval and a Senate split on ground troops.** A CBS News/YouGov survey of 2,193 US adults fielded July 22-24 found that 67% want the conflict to end now against 33% who would continue until Iran makes further concessions; 35% approve of President Trump's handling of the war; 9% expect it to end within days or weeks, 37% say months and 21% say years. Majorities describe their feelings as uncertain and frustrated, say the war has been harder than Trump expected, and say he "makes things sound better than they really are." On *Face the Nation*, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) said "the war in Iran is unconstitutional. It is illegal, should never have been started," and called for immediate negotiations to "stop the killing, let's stop the devastation to our economy." Sen. John Kennedy (R-LA) argued for tightening sanctions on Iranian oil sales and continuing the blockade to "starve them out" rather than running daily strikes, said "I don't think we ought to just cut and run" — and stated plainly, "I don't think we need to send in troops." Kennedy also questioned the administration's $67 billion emergency funding request and asked for a classified detailed briefing. Sources: CBS News, "CBS News poll finds Iran conflict marked by feelings of uncertainty," July 26, 2026; CBS News, "Full transcript of *Face the Nation*," July 26, 2026; Mediaite, July 26, 2026.

**Netanyahu to the White House Tuesday.** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu travels to Washington to meet President Trump on Tuesday July 28, in a visit expected to focus on possible military action against Iran, regional security and the future of Middle East diplomacy. Netanyahu said he plans to press Trump to keep a "constant, constant watch" on Iran's nuclear programme, while acknowledging he has no new evidence that Tehran's ability to build a weapon has been destroyed. *Axios* reported that Trump is considering resuming major combat operations that would likely include a joint military campaign with Israel similar to the February 28 launch of Operation Epic Fury — that is, an air campaign. Netanyahu will also attend the funeral service for Senator Lindsey Graham. Sources: *Axios*, "Trump to meet Netanyahu on Tuesday amid Iran escalation," July 24, 2026; Bloomberg, "Netanyahu Plans to Urge Trump to Monitor Iran's Nuclear Program in Meeting," July 26, 2026; Al Jazeera, July 24, 2026; i24NEWS; Outlook India, July 26, 2026.

**Ground rung — unchanged, and the amphibious rung falls for the first time in the war.** No US troops entered Iran; there was no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new amphibious ready group or Marine expeditionary unit deployment order, and no draft. More than 50,000 US personnel remain in the CENTCOM area of responsibility, the figure CENTCOM publicly confirmed on July 19 and described as the largest US footprint in the region since the 2003 invasion of Iraq. But for the first time the theatre's forcible-entry capability contracted. On July 22 the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group — the America-class amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli (LHA 7), the San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock USS New Orleans (LPD 18) and the Whidbey Island-class dock landing ship USS Rushmore (LSD 47), all homeported at Sasebo — concluded a six-month deployment to the US 5th and 7th Fleet areas of operations and offloaded approximately 2,500 Marines of the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit at White Beach Naval Facility, Okinawa. The group had pivoted from a routine deployment in mid-March to the northern Arabian Sea in support of Operation Epic Fury, spending four months under Central Command supporting the blockade of Iranian ports, conducting precision strikes, logging more than 1,600 combat aviation hours, moving more than 800,000 pounds of cargo, boarding at least two commercial ships suspected of running the blockade, and seizing the Iranian-flagged container ship M/V Touska in April. Strike group spokesman Lt. Mohammad Issa said "the Tripoli and 31st MEU are built to pivot immediately to wherever our nation needs us most." No relief amphibious ready group has been publicly announced. The significance for the ground question is specific: the March 2026 reporting that the Pentagon was preparing "weeks" of agile raids by a mix of Special Operations forces and conventional infantry named the 31st MEU and the 82nd Airborne as the forces that "could conduct raids and seizures," prioritising shoreline threats to commercial shipping, with Kharg Island among the candidate targets — reporting that resurfaced on July 24 as options awaiting an undecided presidential approval. The force those options named has now gone home. What remains in theatre is the Boxer ARG — USS Boxer (LHD 4), USS Portland (LPD 27) and USS Comstock (LSD 45) with the embarked 11th MEU, roughly 2,200 Marines, which arrived at the end of June — alongside the USS Abraham Lincoln and USS George H.W. Bush carrier strike groups and more than 20 warships including some 14 guided-missile destroyers, plus the 82nd Airborne headquarters element and brigade combat team deployed in the spring, with no forcible-entry movement reported. Against that, retired Vice Adm. Robert Harward suggested on Fox that the administration "may be preparing for boots on the ground" to demonstrate commitment to regime change, and Amb. Waltz said "there's more moving into theater" without naming a unit — intent readings with no reported order or movement behind them. On conscription there is no signal: no Selective Service activation, stop-loss or Guard/Reserve call-up, and the only standing item remains the FY2026 NDAA's automatic Selective Service registration of men aged 18-26 beginning December 18, 2026 — an administrative automation passed with bipartisan support months before the war and unconnected to it, with induction still requiring an act of Congress. Sources: *Stars and Stripes*, "USS Tripoli drops off Okinawa-based Marines following return from Iran war," July 22, 2026; USNI News, "Amphib USS Tripoli Wraps 6-month Indo-Pacific, Middle East Patrol," July 22, 2026; Marine Corps Times, July 22, 2026; US Navy/US Pacific Fleet/DVIDS, "Tripoli ARG, 31st MEU return from U.S. 5th, 7th Fleet deployment," July 22, 2026; *The Washington Post*/Al Jazeera/Middle East Eye, March 2026; Foreign Policy, July 24, 2026; The War Zone, "Where Are The Aircraft Carriers: July 20, 2026"; Fox News Digital live blog, July 26, 2026; CNN/CNBC, April 9, 2026.

**Gulf states (July 26).** Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani held discussions with the UAE's national security adviser on bilateral relations and regional diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, and publicly urged diplomacy and a US-Iran deal; Kuwait's emir discussed regional developments with the British prime minister. Kuwait separately signed into law, by decree-law published in the official gazette *Kuwait Alyawm*, its Defence Cooperation Agreement with Pakistan — formalising a framework originally signed in Kuwait in 2023 and covering military training and education, logistical support, exchanges of military personnel and technical experts, defence science and technology, and military intelligence, with implementation supervised by a joint military committee of the two defence ministries. It makes Pakistan a formal security partner to a second Gulf state after the Saudi pact, and lands in the same week Islamabad is mediating between Washington and Tehran. On the Red Sea front, the Houthi maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia declared July 20 remains in force and the July 25 strikes on Aramco facilities at Jizan (refinery set ablaze) and Yanbu retain their significance: Yanbu is the outlet of the East-West Pipeline, which became the Kingdom's only functioning crude-export route after Hormuz closed and handled approximately 92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June 2026, leaving Saudi Arabia interdicted on both flanks with no third corridor. The Wall Street Journal report that Bahraini and Kuwaiti warplanes struck inside Iran drew no new corroboration or retraction; Kuwait's formal denial stands and Bahrain and the UAE have neither confirmed nor denied. Sources: CBS News live blog; Fox News Digital live blog, July 26, 2026; *Arab Times*, "Kuwait ratifies defense cooperation agreement with Pakistan"; *Times Kuwait*; *Daily Pakistan*; ProPakistani; Middle East Online, July 26, 2026; TechTimes, July 25, 2026; Al Jazeera, "New front in US-Iran war escalates as Houthis fire at Saudi oil facilities," July 26, 2026.

**Russia-Ukraine (July 25-26).** Beyond the Caspian strikes, Ukrainian forces struck a Chornomornaftogaz facility and relay equipment used to control Russian strike drones in Russian-occupied Crimea, and a bridge in the occupied part of Donetsk Oblast, overnight into July 26. Russian attacks across Ukraine killed at least seven civilians and injured 58 over the preceding day; Russia bombarded Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight July 25, striking a residential building, with air-raid sirens again around 11:20 a.m. on July 26. Ukraine's General Staff put cumulative Russian losses at 1,438,990 since February 24, 2022, including 1,440 over the past day. Kostiantynivka remains contested with no confirmed net change. Zelensky warned on July 25, citing intelligence, that Putin is "preparing the conditions for expanding mobilization" as Russian losses continue to outpace recruitment, and that Russia is preparing to receive another 30,000 North Korean troops, with facilities readied in Voronezh oblast since June; roughly 11,000 DPRK personnel (about 10,000 combat and 1,000 engineer troops) were in Kursk Oblast at the start of 2026, and Pyongyang supplies an estimated 25-40% of Russian artillery ammunition, reportedly reaching some 15 million 152mm shells by March 2026. Putin met DPRK Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui in Moscow on July 20 and thanked Pyongyang for its wartime support. No US-brokered negotiation is in session; Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called for the war to be frozen and for a return to peace negotiations on a revised version of the Istanbul framework. There is no NATO combat-troop commitment to Ukraine. Sources: Kyiv Independent, July 26, 2026; Kyiv Independent, "Zelensky warns Putin planning new mobilization wave," July 25, 2026; UPI, "Zelensky says Russia seeks 30,000 more North Korean troops," July 26, 2026; *Korea JoongAng Daily*, July 26, 2026; Russia Matters, July 2026.

**Other theatres (July 26-27).** *US-China/Taiwan:* the tariff wave that took effect July 24 is now the operative regime — the 10% Section 122 tariff, ruled unlawful by the Court of International Trade in May 2026 but kept in force by a Federal Circuit stay pending appeal, reached its 150-day statutory limit on July 24 and was replaced the same day by Section 301 forced-labour duties of 10-12.5% covering about 60 economies including Taiwan. China remains the most heavily taxed, at roughly 35% above MFN on most goods and well over 100% on certain strategic products because its own Section 301 duties continue; Taiwan, separately governed, is not subject to the China Section 301 regime, and Taiwan and the EU were the only partners assigned a 10% rate not stacked on existing MFN duties. The *Taipei Times* argued on July 27 that the pattern signals a durable shift in the trade order rather than a bargaining round. Amb. Waltz said Trump had warned Putin and Xi that "bad things will happen" if they continue assisting Iran, while Beijing has separately confirmed support for Pakistani and other mediation between Washington and Tehran. *DPRK:* the peninsula's principal development remains manpower for Russia (above); Kim Jong Un logged 92 public activities in January-June 2026, 30 of them military — his highest military tempo since 2012 — and the guided-missile destroyer Kang Kon, which conducted strategic cruise-missile launch tests on July 3, remains on track for a September commissioning. *Latin America:* no material change — Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores are set for trial in the Southern District of New York on June 1, 2027 under Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein's July 22 order, both having pleaded not guilty; Delcy Rodríguez remains Venezuela's acting president amid reported Chavista disillusionment over crisis response; Cuba's grid has collapsed repeatedly through July, the July 10 failure being the fourth of 2026 and the ninth since late 2024 after a record 2,341 MW deficit on July 8 affecting 73% of the population, under a US oil blockade in force since January; and Colombia's incoming de la Espriella administration will close the country's embassies in Cuba and Nicaragua, reversing Petro's regional alignment. *Hormuz-affected economies:* Japan carries the highest supply-disruption risk score (6.4), followed by South Korea (5.3) and India (4.9), with Japan importing 87% of its total energy and South Korea 81%; South Korea sources 14% of its LNG from Qatar and the UAE and Japan 6%, while Qatar and the UAE account for 53% of India's LNG imports; Korean LNG reserves stand at about 3.5 million tonnes and Japanese at about 4.4 million tonnes, roughly two to four weeks of stable demand. Sources: TaiwanPlus, "New US Tariffs for Taiwan, Other Countries — July 24, 2026"; Trade Compliance Resource Hub, Trump 2.0 tariff tracker, July 21-24, 2026; *Taipei Times*, July 27, 2026; CBS News, *Face the Nation* transcript, July 26, 2026; AEI Korean Peninsula Update, July 14, 2026; CNN Politics, July 22, 2026; Al Jazeera, July 22, 2026; Democracy Now!, July 15, 2026; Latin America Daily Briefing, July 2026; Zero Carbon Analytics; CNBC; IEEFA, 2026.
