## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 25-26 (DAY 150): THE THIRTEEN-NIGHT AIR CAMPAIGN STOPS — IRAN REPORTS ITS FIRST NIGHT WITHOUT US STRIKES AND CENTCOM ANNOUNCES NOTHING AND DECLINES COMMENT. TRUMP SAYS THE US IS 'LOCKED AND LOADED' BUT THE THREATENED 'MASSIVE' ATTACK 'MAY BE UNNECESSARY,' CALLING IRANIAN NEGOTIATORS 'BY FAR THE MOST SERIOUS THAT WE'VE SEEN THEM' (AND HE HAS NOT DECIDED — 'FINGER ON TRIGGER'). TWO MEDIATION CHANNELS OPEN: AN OMANI DELEGATION IN TEHRAN ON HORMUZ TRAFFIC MECHANISMS, AND A PAKISTAN-LED, CHINA-ENCOURAGED PUSH TO RESTART TALKS. THE WAR'S KINETIC CENTRE MIGRATES TO THE RED SEA (HOUTHI STRIKES ON ARAMCO AT JIZAN AND YANBU; SAUDI STRIKES ON HODEIDAH AND KAMARAN), AND THE WSJ REPORTS THE FIRST DIRECT GULF ARAB STRIKES ON IRAN — WHICH KUWAIT CALLS 'ENTIRELY FALSE.' HORMUZ STILL FUNCTIONALLY SHUT (15 TRANSITS VS AN 88/DAY BASELINE); BRENT $96-98; US PUMP AVERAGE $4.111. GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED AND THE KINETIC INDICATOR FELL (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; 50,000+ PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**The strike streak breaks.** After thirteen consecutive nights of US strikes, Iran reported no attacks overnight into Saturday July 25. Iranian Health Ministry spokesman Hossein Kermanpour posted on X that "Iran had a peaceful night." US Central Command did not announce new strikes and declined immediate comment when contacted — it did not declare a pause, a ceasefire, or a resumption. It is the first reduction in the war's kinetic indicator since the resumed phase began on July 8, and no successor operation accompanied it. (Fortune, "U.S. military suddenly goes silent on Iran airstrikes," July 25, 2026; The Washington Post, "Iran reports no new U.S. strikes as tensions remain high," July 25, 2026; Fox News Digital live blog, July 25, 2026.)

**"Locked and loaded" — and "may be unnecessary."** President Trump said dialogue between Washington and Tehran continues and that the threatened "massive" attack "may be unnecessary," while the United States remains "locked and loaded" for a major strike and could escalate "to a much higher level" if diplomacy fails. He said Iranian negotiators "are being by far the most serious that we've seen them," adding "that doesn't mean we get there," and repeated the administration's bottom line: "They cannot have a nuclear weapon." *The Jerusalem Post*, citing sources, reported that Trump has not decided on large-scale attacks — "finger on trigger." (Al Jazeera live blog, "Trump says US 'locked and loaded' as it seeks Iran talks," July 25, 2026; The Epoch Times, July 25, 2026; RFE/RL, "Trump Says Iran 'Far More Serious' In Talks, Even As Attacks Intensify, Widen In Region," July 25, 2026; The Jerusalem Post, July 25, 2026.)

**Two mediation channels open.** An Omani diplomatic delegation arrived in Tehran on July 24 to discuss establishing "appropriate mechanisms for managing ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz," according to Iran's state news agency IRNA. Tehran has consistently offered to co-manage the waterway with Oman, the Strait's only other littoral state; the United States and the Gulf states have rejected any Iranian-led transit regime, Washington insisting Iran "does not control" it. Separately, Pakistan explored a route back to US-Iran negotiations in a push encouraged by China, with momentum from Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni's second visit to Islamabad in under two weeks; China's foreign ministry confirmed its support for Pakistani and other mediation, citing its interest in restoring stability to Gulf trade routes. Sources cautioned that the obstacles to talks remain high and that Islamabad faces a delicate balance between its Saudi, Chinese and Iranian ties. (Middle East Eye; Anadolu; Al Jazeera, "Oman talking with Tehran on Hormuz," July 24-25, 2026; Reuters via Pakistan Today and BOE Report, "Pakistan, Iran explore path towards new talks with US in a China-initiated push," July 24, 2026; China-Global South Project, July 25, 2026.)

**The kinetic centre moves to the Red Sea.** Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree announced in a prerecorded statement that the group had fired "dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones" at Saudi Aramco-affiliated facilities in the Red Sea towns of Jizan and Yanbu, and that the operations "successfully achieved their objectives." Video geolocated by CNN showed large fires burning in Jizan's industrial area, home to a major Aramco refinery; Saudi civil defence confirmed alerts sounded repeatedly early Saturday, and Saudi air defences intercepted further ballistic missiles from Yemen later in the day. As of early Saturday neither Aramco nor the Saudi government had issued a damage assessment. The strikes answered a Saudi-led coalition attack on Hodeidah port and its telecommunications infrastructure and on Kamaran Island — which coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki described as a "firm, resolute and proportionate military response" against sites used to "threaten commercial vessels," and which Houthi-run al-Masirah said wounded a woman on Kamaran (Fortune reported two injured). The Houthi political wing vowed to meet "escalation with escalation." The targeting is economically pointed: Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export terminus and, with Hormuz functionally shut, its principal remaining crude corridor; the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of the Kingdom on July 20 and struck two Saudi crude tankers on July 23. Roughly 12% of world trade, including a quarter of container traffic, transits Bab el-Mandeb. (Fortune, July 25, 2026; The Washington Post, "Houthis claim attack on Saudi oil refinery as Iran war widens to Red Sea," July 25, 2026; Türkiye Today, July 25, 2026; Al Jazeera; The National, July 24-25, 2026.)

**A contested first: did Gulf Arab states strike Iran?** *The Wall Street Journal* reported on July 24, in "Bahrain, Kuwait Warplanes Struck Iran in Rare Gulf Retaliation," that Bahraini and Kuwaiti warplanes had secretly struck Iranian missile and drone storage depots and other military installations earlier in July — the first direct military action by Gulf Arab states against Iran — with the United Arab Emirates providing intelligence on targets and defensive air cover. The paper described the strikes as a significant departure from the proxy-war playbook that has defined regional conflict for decades; both states host US forces and have absorbed months of Iranian missile and drone attacks justified by Tehran on exactly that basis. On July 25 Kuwait's ambassador to the United States, Sheikha Zain Al-Sabah, sent a formal letter to the paper's editorial board calling the report "entirely false," stating that Kuwait has not participated in any military operations against Iran and has not allowed the use of its territory, airspace or territorial waters to launch offensive operations against any neighbouring country. Bahrain and the UAE neither confirmed nor denied, and no imagery, flight-tracking, battle-damage assessment or Iranian attribution of the strikes to Gulf aircraft has been published. This briefing records the report as reported-not-confirmed and the Kuwaiti denial as an on-the-record official position; the question is logged as contested-unresolved (`gulf-states-direct-strikes-iran-july-2026`). Note the narrower point not in dispute: any such action is allied AIR activity, not US ground forces. (WSJ via TASS, ANI, The Jerusalem Post and Defence Security Asia, July 24-25, 2026; Arab Times, "Kuwait Denies Participation in Military Operations Against Iran, Calls WSJ Report False," July 25, 2026.)

**Iran's response.** Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that "we believe that there is no military solution to the issue of Yemen, Bab al-Mandab, and other regional issues," called for dialogue, and said the situation in Yemen "cannot be attributed to Iran," being "rooted in old disputes and issues between Yemen, Saudi Arabia and the countries of the region." He has separately warned that the targeting of Iranian infrastructure would compel "a powerful and decisive response" under an "eye for an eye" doctrine. (Türkiye Today; Free Malaysia Today, "Iran's Araghchi says 'no military solution' to Yemen conflict," July 25, 2026.)

**Blockade enforcement continues through the pause.** US forces disabled the tanker M/T Lavine in the Gulf of Oman after the crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to breach the blockade at least four times, firing into the ship's engine room; US forces separately completed a verification boarding of the Comoros-flagged M/T Charminar in the Arabian Sea, which was cleared to continue its voyage. Since the naval blockade of Iranian ports was re-imposed on July 14, CENTCOM has redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled two that did not comply. Trump said damage to ships "will be paid for by Iranian money that the United States has in its possession and controls." This remains interdiction and visit-board-search — not a port seizure or a landing. (AP via Türkiye Today, "US military disables another tanker for breaching Iran blockade," July 25, 2026; NewsNation; Fox News Digital live blog; CENTCOM, July 25, 2026.)

**Hormuz stays functionally shut — and partly unobservable.** IMF PortWatch recorded 15 transits on July 19, its most recent published day, against a pre-crisis baseline of 88 per day; roughly 85 tankers were running dark, broadcasting no AIS signal and therefore untracked, and the International Maritime Organization continued to assess the waterway as too dangerous for commercial vessels. Late-June and early-July averages had run about 25 ships a day against roughly 100 a year earlier. Saudi loadings from inside the Gulf remain slumped in the wake of the strikes on supertankers. (IMF PortWatch; Statista; Windward; Bloomberg, July 2026.)

**Markets: crude off the spike, pump prices at a war high.** Brent ended the week in the $96-98 range — reports differ on the precise Friday July 24 settle (about $97 per CNBC and Yahoo Finance; $98.38, down 2.29%, per TradingEconomics) — after the July 23 spike that closed at $100.69, up about 7%. Brent finished more than 12% higher on the week and roughly 30% higher on the month. Weekend quotes are indicative only with futures markets closed: one outlet reported an early-Saturday move back above $100 on the Jizan and Yanbu strikes, another a retreat toward $96 on reports that Pakistan is exploring renewed US-Iran talks with Chinese encouragement. The AAA United States national average pump price reached $4.111 a gallon on July 25, up from $3.95 on July 16 and about 95 cents above the year-earlier $3.15 — California highest at $5.59, Indiana lowest at $3.53 — while US gasoline futures eased below $3.45 from a two-month high above $3.50 on July 23. Crude remains below the roughly $126 April wartime peak and the $130-plus that a sustained US ground commitment would imply. (CNBC; Yahoo Finance; TradingEconomics; TechTimes; Fox News; AAA Fuel Prices via Clarksville Online; CNN, July 23-25, 2026.)

**Casualties.** Running cumulative tolls reported on July 25: more than 3,400 killed in Iran (Iranian Health Ministry), 18 US service members, 24 Israeli civilians and 38 Israeli troops, and more than 4,000 in Lebanon. Iranian officials put the July 8-25 phase at more than 100 US air attacks across Iran, at least 50 killed and more than 500 wounded. No new US combat death was reported on the strike-pause day. Iranian-sourced figures are not independently verified and outlets continue to differ on the US KIA running count. (Fortune, July 25, 2026; Al Jazeera, July 18-25, 2026.)

**US intelligence on the new Supreme Leader.** A *New York Times*-reported US assessment holds that Mojtaba Khamenei is more open than his father to pursuing an advanced nuclear weapons capability: where the elder Khamenei's religious prohibition was treated for decades as a genuine obstacle to crossing the threshold, Mojtaba is assessed not to share that hesitation and to seek a warhead that could eventually be miniaturised and mounted on a missile. US officials cautioned that much of the underlying intelligence was collected before the war began and that the new leader has been in hiding, with limited communication with other Iranian officials, since he was injured in the strike that killed his father on February 28. (NYT via Ynetnews, The Jerusalem Post and ANI, July 25, 2026.)

**Ground rung — unchanged, with the kinetic indicator falling.** No US troops entered Iran; there was no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new amphibious ready group or Marine expeditionary unit deployment order, and no draft. More than 50,000 US personnel remain in the CENTCOM area of responsibility — the level CENTCOM publicly confirmed on July 19 and described as the largest US footprint in the region since the 2003 invasion of Iraq — broadly unchanged. The July 24 reporting that the Pentagon is preparing options for potential ground operations lasting weeks (limited special-operations and conventional raids on Kharg Island and coastal weapons sites, explicitly not a full-scale invasion) still stands, but remains unexecuted and, per *The Jerusalem Post*, undecided. The Boxer ARG and 11th MEU (about 2,200 Marines) and the Tripoli ARG and 31st MEU held routine and contingency posture, with Marines used only for at-sea boardings; the 82nd Airborne headquarters element and brigade combat team deployed in the spring remain in place with no forcible-entry movement reported. Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper read the pause the other way, arguing the administration may have stopped strikes to "reposition, prepare, reload, et cetera, for something much bigger that looks like the beginning of the war," possibly "a 24- or 48-hour respite" — an intent reading of an observed reduction, and framed as an expanded war rather than specifically a ground campaign. On the draft, nothing changed: the only standing item remains the statutory plan for automatic Selective Service registration of men aged 18-26 beginning December 18, 2026, an administrative automation mandated by the NDAA, not a draft activation; under the Military Selective Service Act only Congress can authorise induction. (Fortune; Fox News; The Jerusalem Post; MEAWW/Fox News; Foreign Policy, July 24-25, 2026; Sputnik/GlobalSecurity, July 19, 2026; CNBC, April 9, 2026.)

**Other theatres (July 25-26).** *US-China/Taiwan:* following the July 24 entry into force of Section 301 forced-labour duties of 10-12.5% on about 60 economies, the *Taipei Times* reported that Taiwan and the EU were the only two partners assigned a 10% rate not added to their existing MFN duties — the package's most favourable treatment, which Taipei assesses could improve the competitiveness of Taiwanese traditional manufacturers against Japanese and Chinese rivals; China's 12.5% stacks on existing Section 301 and 232 duties for a combined burden around 35% above MFN on most goods and well over 100% on some strategic products, yet Beijing signalled it would look past the levies ahead of Xi's planned US trip while reciprocal-cut talks worth roughly $30 billion a side continue. *Russia-Ukraine:* Ukrainian attacks in the partly Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia region killed 12 on July 25 and a Russian drone strike in Sumy region killed three; the preceding 24 hours logged 192 combat engagements (24 in the Pokrovsk direction), five missiles, 186 guided bombs across 56 airstrikes, 5,746 one-way attack drones and 2,297 shelling attacks, with three Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles fired at Kyiv Oblast's Bucha district (one intercepted, two struck); ISW recorded confirmed Russian advances near Kryva Luka and Hlushkivka in the Lyman/Kupiansk sector and near Novodanilovka in the Orikhiv direction against decelerating overall momentum, while Peskov reaffirmed on July 22 that Putin's June 2024 maximalist terms remain the precondition for negotiations and Moscow reiterated its refusal to negotiate directly with Kyiv. *DPRK:* Kim Jong Un made 92 public activities in the first half of 2026, 30 of them military-related — his highest first-half military count since 2012 — with July 3 weapons tests aboard the guided-missile destroyer Kang Kon including evaluation of "strategic" cruise missile launch capability, a September commissioning target, and a 10,000-ton guided-missile cruiser in development; analysts continue to flag the July 27 armistice anniversary. *Latin America:* the Maduro and Cilia Flores trial stands set for June 1, 2027 with Delcy Rodríguez continuing as acting president in Caracas, while Cuba suffered another total grid collapse leaving roughly 10 million without power, largely halting public transport, cancelling tens of thousands of surgeries and drawing scattered pot-banging protests in Havana — the island produces only about 40% of the oil it consumes after the US blockade and the cutoff of Venezuelan crude (outlets differ on the running count of 2026 total outages). *Hormuz-affected economies:* about 80% of the crude and products and 90% of the LNG transiting the Strait is Asia-bound; Japan and South Korea normally route 93% and 70.7% of their oil imports through it, while Pakistan and Bangladesh are most exposed on gas, with Qatar and the UAE supplying 99% and 72% of their LNG respectively; India faces LPG shortfalls, stocks in India, Japan and Pakistan have hit 10-year lows, and the IEA's executive director has warned the global economy is in peril if the crisis persists. *Qatar:* the Ministry of Transport restored normal maritime navigation for all vessel types within its roughly seven-nautical-mile coastal zones. *Israel-Lebanon:* Israeli strikes continued across southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire framework, including blasts across the south on July 24 and a strike on an ambulance in Nabatieh al-Fawqa that injured two medics. (Taipei Times, July 25; Bloomberg; SCMP, July 24; AP via The Washington Times; Ukrainian General Staff via GlobalSecurity; ISW/Critical Threats, July 22-25; AEI Korean Peninsula Update, July 7 and 14; ABC News; US News; Fox News; CBS News; Al Jazeera; East Asia Forum; Gulf International Forum; EnergyConnects; Qatar Tribune; PortNews, July 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 24-25 (DAY 149): A 13TH STRAIGHT NIGHT AS TRUMP WEIGHS A 'BIGGER THAN OPERATION EPIC FURY' ESCALATION (NO DECISION) AND IRAN REJECTS AN IRAQI-BROKERED CEASEFIRE OVER HORMUZ CONTROL. OIL RETREATS ~4% TO SETTLE NEAR $97/BBL (BIGGEST ONE-DAY DROP SINCE LATE JUNE) AFTER BRIEFLY TOPPING $100, AS CRUDE STILL TRAVERSES ROUTES DESPITE THE HOUTHI RED SEA ATTACK. THE PENTAGON IS REPORTED READYING OPTIONS FOR 'WEEKS' OF LIMITED GROUND OPERATIONS (KHARG + COASTAL RAIDS) PENDING TRUMP'S APPROVAL; IRAN'S FM WARNS OF 'REPERCUSSIONS' AND 'WE NEVER ACCEPT HUMILIATION.' STILL AIR/MARITIME — PLANNING UP, EXECUTION AT ZERO; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**Thirteenth consecutive night of US strikes.** The US ran a 13th straight night of strikes on Iranian military command centers and coastal/maritime targets tied to the Hormuz threat. Trump signaled he could go "bigger," telling Axios he was considering restarting major combat operations larger than those carried out during "Operation Epic Fury," while stressing that no decision had been made. He also said talks were continuing and that Tehran was "getting more serious," even as he insisted "they need more of the same." A continuation of the AIR campaign, not a landing. (NPR, "Trump threatens a major escalation in Iran after 13 straight nights of strikes"; CNN live blog, "Trump mulls escalation but says Tehran is getting more serious"; GlobalSecurity, July 24, 2026.)

**Iran rejects an Iraqi-brokered ceasefire.** Iran rejected a US ceasefire proposal delivered Thursday by the Iraqi prime minister, with Iranian officials saying Tehran was not interested in a temporary deal that left the question of control of the Strait of Hormuz unresolved. The Houthi Red Sea attack this week pulled Iran's key ally further into the conflict; Trump threatened "major military punishment" if the Houthi attacks continue. (CNN live blog, July 24, 2026.)

**Oil retreats ~4% to settle near $97.** After Brent briefly topped $100 and settled at $100.69 (up about 7%) on July 23 on the Houthi attack on two Saudi tankers (the *Incilia* and *Layla*), Brent fell roughly 4% on Friday July 24 to settle near $97 a barrel — its biggest one-day drop since late June — as traders judged that crude was still traversing Middle East routes despite the escalation, with Kazakhstan output cuts adding supply. Prices remain below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. (Yahoo Finance, "Brent crude surges past $100 on Houthi tanker attacks"; CNBC, "Oil set for weekly rise amid Red Sea shipping attacks, Kazakhstan output cuts," July 24, 2026.)

**The Pentagon readies options for weeks of limited ground operations.** The Pentagon was reported to be preparing options for potential US ground operations in Iran that could last weeks if Trump approves an escalation — plans that reportedly envision limited raids by special operations and conventional forces rather than a full-scale invasion, with possible targets including Kharg Island and coastal weapons sites near the Strait of Hormuz. Reported options and an undecided presidential "consideration" are planning, not a movement of troops. (Foreign Policy, "How a U.S. Ground Operation in Iran Could Unfold"; Just Security, "Early Edition: July 24, 2026.")

**Iran: "repercussions" over Kharg; "we never accept humiliation."** Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei warned of "repercussions" if the United States moves against Kharg Island, responding to Trump's threats to seize the oil-export hub, and Tehran said it would "never accept humiliation" in response to the reports of possible US ground operations. (Fox News, "Iran responds to reports US weighing ground operations: we never accept humiliation," July 24, 2026.)

**Ground rung — unchanged; planning up, execution at zero.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, and no draft accompanied the 13th night, Trump's "bigger than Epic Fury" threat, or the reported ground-ops options. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR remained unchanged, and the standing Boxer ARG / 11th MEU (~2,200 Marines) and Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU held routine/contingency posture. The "bigger" attack Trump is weighing is described as an air/standoff escalation; the reported ground "options" are planning pending an undecided approval; a Kharg seizure is still reported to need at least ~1,200 ground troops. The predicted US ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure has still not occurred, and the rising planning signal keeps the intent question live (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: **kharg-seizure-total-control-threat-june-2026**). (NPR; Foreign Policy; CNN live blog; The Times of Israel, July 15-24, 2026.)

**Other theatres (July 24-25).** *US-China:* New US tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on ~60 economies took effect July 24 as the temporary Section 122 duties expired, covering over 99% of US trade (fuel, food and USMCA-covered goods exempt); the levies flow from a Section 301 forced-labour investigation, with China drawing a 12.5% rate and Taiwan, the EU, Japan and South Korea covered. Bloomberg assessed the China rate "might irk Beijing without provoking retaliation" as China looks past the tariffs ahead of Xi's planned US trip, and US-China teams accelerate consultations on a framework for reciprocal tariff reductions each valued at ~$30B. (NBC News, "US sets tariffs on 60 trade partners as temporary duties expire"; Bloomberg, "US Hits 60 Economies With Duties" and "China Set to Look Past New Trump Tariffs Before Xi's US Trip"; SCMP, July 24, 2026.) *Latin America:* US District Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein (SDNY) set a June 1, 2027 trial for ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and wife Cilia Flores, who pleaded not guilty to drug-trafficking and firearms charges after their January seizure by US troops; acting president Delcy Rodríguez continues to meet many US demands, and Cuba's US-blockade-driven energy crisis persists with repeated island-wide blackouts (~10M without power). (CNN, "Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro gets a June trial date"; ABC News; GlobalSecurity, July 22-23, 2026.) *Russia-Ukraine:* Kostiantynivka stays contested — Russia again claims to hold the Donetsk town, Ukraine denies; Moscow's Defense Ministry proposed a six-hour local ceasefire to hand over fallen soldiers' bodies, and Peskov mocked Zelensky's suggestion that Putin meet him in the city; ISW-adjacent analysis holds the Russian spring-summer 2026 offensive failed to achieve operationally significant advances (~20% held, no net change; no US ground surge) (open-question: **kostiantynivka-control-contested-july-2026**). (Al Jazeera; Critical Threats/ISW; Russia Matters, July 2026.) *DPRK:* No new confirmed July launch after the July 11 salvo (~10 ballistic missiles) and the July 3-4 Kang Kon destroyer naval-weapons trials; analysts watch the July 27 armistice anniversary. *Hormuz-affected economies:* Japan (~75% of crude via Hormuz), South Korea (~60-70%) and India (~half of crude, ~60% of gas) remain the most exposed, with Pakistan and Bangladesh especially vulnerable on LNG (Qatar/UAE supply ~99% of Pakistan's and ~72% of Bangladesh's LNG imports) — now compounded by the Bab el-Mandeb attack on the Red Sea route. (Seatrade Maritime; East Asia Forum; Gulf International Forum, 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 23-24 (DAY 148): THE AIR CAMPAIGN REACHES A 12TH STRAIGHT NIGHT AS OIL TOPS $100/BBL FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE MAY (BRENT ~$98.44, +4.6%; WTI ~$90.14) AND THE HOUTHIS MOVE FROM THREAT TO ATTACK, STRIKING SAUDI VESSELS IN THE RED SEA. TRUMP REFUSES A NEW CEASEFIRE ('THEY NEED MORE OF THE SAME'), TELLS AXIOS IRAN HAS NOT 'RECEIVED ENOUGH PAIN YET' AND IS WEIGHING A 'MASSIVE ATTACK'. UN'S GUTERRES WARNS THE WAR IS 'GETTING OUT OF CONTROL... TEETERING ON THE EDGE OF THE UNIMAGINABLE.' A NEW US SERVICE MEMBER KILLED (NORTHERN IRAQ, DRONE DETONATION); ~100 TROOPS INJURED SINCE JULY 7. STILL AIR/MARITIME COERCION — NOT A GROUND SEIZURE; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**Twelfth consecutive night of US strikes.** The US ran a 12th straight night of strikes on Iranian military and coastal targets tied to the Hormuz threat. After 12 nights, Trump said he was considering a "major"/"massive" attack, telling Axios that Iran had not "received enough pain yet." The war, now in its sixth month, has killed US troops, paralysed Hormuz shipping and driven oil above $100. (CNN live blog, "Oil tops $100 a barrel as Houthi attack on Saudi vessels in Red Sea marks new escalation"; Axios via Sinclair, July 23, 2026.)

**Oil tops $100/bbl for the first time since May.** Brent crude crossed $100/bbl before settling; Thursday's futures gained about 4.6% to $98.44 and US WTI rose about 3.8% to $90.14, putting Brent on course for a monthly gain of roughly 35.3% — one of the three biggest monthly jumps in a decade. Prices remain below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. (CNBC, "Oil prices: WTI, Brent rise as Trump threatens more strikes on Iran"; CNN Business, July 23, 2026.)

**The Houthis move from threat to attack on Saudi Red Sea shipping.** After declaring a Bab el-Mandeb blockade earlier in the week, the Iran-aligned Houthis actually attacked vessels carrying Saudi crude in the Red Sea, converting a threatened second chokepoint into an active one and — with Hormuz already functionally shut — leaving oil (in CNN's framing) with "no way out." Trump warned the US would hold Iran responsible for Houthi strikes and threatened "major military punishment." A maritime/proxy escalation, not a US ground move. (CNN live blog; NPR, "Houthis declare a blockade of another key strait: Bab el-Mandeb," July 21-23, 2026.)

**Trump refuses a new ceasefire.** Trump said he was not ready to negotiate a new ceasefire — "they need more of the same" — leaving the Qatar/Pakistan 10-day proposal unanswered as he weighed intensifying rather than pausing strikes. (CNN live blog; Jerusalem Post live updates, July 22-23, 2026.)

**UN: the war is "getting out of control."** UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said "the situation is getting out of control. It's teetering on the edge of the unimaginable. The region is being pulled into an ever-widening circle of confrontation," urging warring leaders to end attacks on civilian infrastructure and return to diplomacy. (UN News, "Guterres calls for stepping up diplomatic efforts to end US-Iran conflict"; NewsChannel9/Sinclair, "Iran war is getting out of control, United Nations leader warns," July 23, 2026.)

**US casualties.** CENTCOM reported another US service member killed — in northern Iraq during the controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone — and said it had located unidentified remains in Jordan tied to an earlier attack that left two dead and one missing. The Pentagon said nearly 100 US service members have been injured (mostly minor) since July 7. These are losses from the AIR/maritime fight on bases, not a ground deployment. (CNN live blog; CENTCOM via CNN, July 23, 2026.)

**Ground rung — unchanged; the weighed "massive attack" is air-framed.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, and no draft accompanied the 12th night, the $100 oil print, or the Houthi Red Sea attack. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR remained unchanged. China, Japan, South Korea, India, EU) hours before the temporary 10% Section 122 blanket levy expired — 10-12.5% under a Section 301 forced-labour finding, with China drawing a 12.5% added rate (~35%+ effective) and Canada/Mexico/India/Indonesia/UK at 10%; USTR Jamieson Greer framed it as correcting "both a human rights abuse and distortive trade practice." US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 22-23 (DAY 147): THE AIR CAMPAIGN REACHES AN 11TH STRAIGHT NIGHT (~75 MIN) AS WASHINGTON DOWNPLAYS DIPLOMACY — RUBIO SAYS TEHRAN IS 'NOT SERIOUS' ABOUT TALKS AND TRUMP DISMISSES CEASEFIRE CALLS, VOWING TO 'BOMB AND DESTROY ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT' FOR EVERY HORMUZ SHIP ATTACK. **Eleventh consecutive night of US strikes (~75 minutes).** CENTCOM said the latest assault lasted about 75 minutes and targeted "Iranian military operations centres, maritime capabilities, aircraft hangars, drone storage facilities, and military logistics infrastructure" — a continuation of the AIR campaign to further degrade Iran's ability to threaten Hormuz shipping, not a landing. The war, now in its sixth month, has killed US troops, paralysed Hormuz shipping and pushed oil higher. The Qatar/Pakistan 10-day ceasefire proposal (which Iran confirmed receiving a day earlier) was left unanswered as the White House signaled it could keep striking. (CNBC, "Trump vows to bomb Iran's bridges, power plants if it shoots at ships in Hormuz Strait"; CNN live blog, "Rubio warns Tehran not serious about talks," July 22, 2026.)

**Oil surges past $95; the Houthi Bab el-Mandeb blockade leaves oil "no way out."** Brent crude rose almost 5% to more than $95/bbl — its highest in nearly six weeks — as the US downplayed diplomacy and the Iran-aligned Houthis' Bab el-Mandeb blockade threatened Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export "relief valve," with both the Hormuz and Red Sea routes now compromised. Two tankers carrying Saudi crude to Asia turned back near Bab el-Mandeb after the Houthi threat. Prices remain below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. Oil faces 'no way out'," July 22, 2026.)

**Hormuz near-zero.** Shipping-analytics firm Kpler said only 3 commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from 4 on Monday — the chokepoint remains functionally shut at well under 5% of pre-war flows. (Middle East Eye/Kpler, July 22, 2026.)

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told lawmakers the Iran war has cost about $37.5 billion, and Trump is seeking roughly $70 billion more for the military — an air/naval-campaign budget signal, not a ground order. (CBS News, "Pentagon identifies 4th service member killed in recent days"; Middle East Eye, July 22, 2026.)

Reuters/Times-of-Israel reporting that the strikes are "shaping operations" degrading Iranian defenses ahead of possible "more intensive operations" describes preparatory targeting and standing planning, not an executed landing; a Kharg seizure is still reported to need at least ~1,200 troops. The predicted US ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure has still not occurred (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: **kharg-seizure-total-control-threat-june-2026**). Hellerstein at the SDNY in Manhattan; the judge set a June 1, 2027 trial date in their drug-trafficking case at both sides' request, with defense sovereign-immunity motions to begin in early September and oral arguments Nov 17. Venezuela stays under acting President Delcy Rodriguez. ## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 21-22 (DAY 146): THE WAR WIDENS ON THREE NEW NON-GROUND AXES — TRUMP THREATENS TO STRIKE IRAN'S BURIED 'PICKAXE MOUNTAIN' NUCLEAR-ENRICHMENT SITE 'PROBABLY PRETTY SOON'; IRAN-ALIGNED HOUTHIS DECLARE A BLOCKADE OF THE BAB EL-MANDEB (A SECOND CHOKEPOINT) AND TWO SAUDI CRUDE TANKERS U-TURN FROM YANBU; AND QATAR/PAKISTAN (WITH EGYPT/OMAN) FLOAT A 10-DAY US-IRAN CEASEFIRE AND A HORMUZ 'MIDDLE CORRIDOR' THAT IRAN CONFIRMS RECEIVING. THE 10TH STRAIGHT NIGHT (SIRIK, BANDAR ABBAS, QESHM, SHIRAZ, ISFAHAN) IS DONE AND AN 11TH IS ANTICIPATED; BRENT ~$91. STILL AIR/MARITIME/NUCLEAR-STRIKE-THREAT COERCION — NOT A GROUND SEIZURE; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**Trump threatens Iran's "Pickaxe Mountain" nuclear-enrichment site.** Trump said the US would strike Iran's "Pickaxe Mountain" — a deeply buried enrichment complex (Kuh-e Kolang Gazla) ~220 km south of Tehran and ~2 km from Natanz, built to survive bombing — "probably pretty soon, and there's not a thing they can do about it," adding that the US would target "any site where they've been thinking about nuclear." Israeli intelligence assesses Iran moved thousands of centrifuges and possibly some 60%-enriched uranium there after the 2025 fighting. Iran's top military command warned that an attack on the site would widen the war and trigger broader strikes on US regional allies. This extends the declared target set from military/energy/nuclear-adjacent sites to a core enrichment facility — but as an AIR/standoff-strike THREAT against a hardened underground target, not a ground operation, and not yet executed. (The Times of Israel, "Trump claims US will strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain 'probably pretty soon'"; ABC News, July 21, 2026.)

**Iran-aligned Houthis declare a Bab el-Mandeb blockade — a second chokepoint.** The Houthis announced a blockade of the Bab el-Mandeb strait in stated retaliation for Saudi strikes on Sanaa's airport, potentially opening a new front in the war. Two tankers that had just loaded Saudi crude at the Red Sea port of Yanbu for China and India made U-turns toward the Suez Canal. Bab el-Mandeb had become Saudi Arabia's principal export "relief valve" after Hormuz went functionally shut — the Saudis diverting crude via the East-West pipeline to Red Sea terminals — so the threat compounds the global supply squeeze and pressures oil higher. This is a maritime/proxy widening of the war, not a US or Iranian ground campaign; no US amphibious response followed. (CNBC, "Iran's Houthi allies declare maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia"; NPR; The Washington Post; Honolulu Star-Advertiser, July 20-21, 2026.)

**Mediators float a 10-day US-Iran ceasefire and a Hormuz "middle corridor."** Qatar and Pakistan, with Egyptian and Omani officials, formally proposed a 10-day halt to hostilities to revive the suspended June MOU: suspend fighting, revert to pre-July-9 positions, fully restore Hormuz shipping, and open a "middle corridor" between Omani and Iranian waters for safe transit. Iran's Foreign Ministry (spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei) confirmed receiving the proposals; Reuters/JPost reported Iran quietly submitted its own 10-day idea while under strikes. A source familiar with White House deliberations said Washington could keep striking for several more days before seriously weighing the offer, and Trump claimed Iran is "desperate" to talk while vowing Tehran "will pay" for the US service members killed. A diplomatic off-ramp reintroducing deal-durability and Hormuz-administration questions — not a ground move. (The New Arab; US News/Reuters, "Mediators propose 10-day Iran-U.S. ceasefire"; JPost; Axios, July 20-21, 2026.)

**Tenth straight night done; eleventh anticipated; Brent ~$91.** CENTCOM ran a 10th consecutive night of strikes, with Iranian media citing explosions in Sirik, Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Shiraz and Isfahan; CENTCOM said it hit "command centers, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defense systems" "to further degrade Iranian military capabilities used to attack commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz." Analysts watched for an 11th night potentially extending to Iran's transmission grid, Pickaxe Mountain or Kharg Island. Iran struck more shipping (two Greek-owned tankers Monday; a tanker abandoned off Oman's Limah coast; IRGC claims of "massive fires" on additional tankers) and sustained Gulf retaliation (fresh fires at a Kuwaiti desalination-and-power complex; strikes on Bahrain and Jordan). Brent settled ~$91/bbl (TradingEconomics cited $91.10, +2.11%), its highest in over a month, still below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called for ending the conflict. (Al Jazeera, "US attacks Iran for 10th consecutive night"; PBS; CBS News; TradingEconomics; Fortune, July 21, 2026.)

**Ground rung — all three new axes are non-ground.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, and no draft accompanied the Pickaxe threat, the Houthi Bab el-Mandeb blockade, the 10-day ceasefire proposal, or the 10th night. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR remained unchanged. The Pickaxe threat is an AIR/standoff-strike threat against a buried site; the Houthi move is maritime/proxy; the ceasefire track is diplomatic. Reuters reporting that the strike waves also destroy capabilities the US would want gone before "more complex operations" describes preparatory targeting and standing planning — consistent with the war's pattern of maximal ground/Kharg talk paired with zero ground execution — not an executed landing. The USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU (~2,200 Marines) and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU held routine/contingency posture; a Kharg seizure is still reported to need at least ~1,200 troops. The predicted US ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure has still not occurred (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: **kharg-seizure-total-control-threat-june-2026**). (Al Jazeera; The Times of Israel; NPR; CNBC; Axios; Task & Purpose, July 20-21, 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 20-21 (DAY 145): THE AIR WAR REACHES A NINTH-TO-TENTH STRAIGHT NIGHT AND STRIKES A SECOND NUCLEAR-ADJACENT SITE — MULTIPLE LOCATIONS IN BUSHEHR (IRAN'S ONLY CIVILIAN NUCLEAR PLANT). IRAN IMMOBILIZES A SECOND OIL TANKER AT HORMUZ AND CLAIMS FOUR VESSELS INTERCEPTED; KUWAIT'S POWER-AND-WATER PLANT BURNS A THIRD DAY AND BAHRAIN TAKES FRESH STRIKES; BRENT CROSSES ~$90 AND ONLY ~8 SHIPS TRANSIT HORMUZ; THE INTERCEPT REPORTS US CASUALTIES UNDERCOUNTED (~446 KILLED/WOUNDED). TRUMP VOWS TO 'HIT THEM VERY HARD... TONIGHT AND TOMORROW' AND WON'T RULE OUT TAKING KHARG ('I CAN'T SAY... IT WOULD BE FOOLISH'). STILL AN AIR/MARITIME CAMPAIGN — NOT A GROUND SEIZURE; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**US runs a ninth-to-tenth consecutive night of strikes and hits Bushehr.** CBS reported the US completed a ninth straight night of strikes (ending ~10pm ET July 19), with CENTCOM citing Iranian military command centers, air-defense, coastal-surveillance and missile/drone-launch sites "to further degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping"; a tenth consecutive night was reported into July 20-21. US projectiles hit multiple locations in the southern port city of BUSHEHR — home to Iran's only civilian nuclear power plant — per Bushehr governor Mohammad Mozaffari ("several locations in Bushehr city were hit by American enemy's projectiles"). It is the second nuclear-adjacent target in three days after the July 18-19 strike on the under-construction Darkhovin plant; unlike Darkhovin (IAEA: no nuclear material present), damage or radiological impact at Bushehr's operating plant was not independently confirmed. (CBS News, "American service member killed in Iraq; U.S. strikes Iran for 9th straight night"; NPR; Al Jazeera, July 20, 2026.)

**Iran immobilizes a second oil tanker at Hormuz and claims four vessels intercepted.** Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a second oil tanker had been struck and immobilized at the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran said it had intercepted four vessels transiting the Strait over the weekend. Only ~8 ships transited Hormuz on Thursday — the lowest in three weeks — leaving the chokepoint functionally shut (<5% of pre-war flows). This is continued maritime interdiction and blockade enforcement from the sea and air, not a landing. (CBS News; NPR; TradingEconomics, July 20, 2026.)

**Iran's Gulf retaliation deepens: Kuwait burns a third day, Bahrain is struck.** A Kuwaiti power-and-water plant caught fire for a third consecutive day; the cumulative Kuwait toll from Iranian strikes was reported at 4 soldiers and 7 civilians killed and 82 soldiers and 105 civilians wounded. Bahrain — host to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet — saw air-raid sirens and explosions in Manama, with 3 killed and 51 wounded reported. Iran framed the strikes as retaliation for US attacks on southern Iranian infrastructure alongside the Strait. (NPR, "U.S. and Iran launch new strikes after 3 U.S. service members are killed"; ABC News; Casualties of the 2026 Iran war, July 20, 2026.)

**US casualties reported undercounted.** The Intercept quoted a US official saying Iranian attacks injured "far more" troops than the Pentagon admits — "dozens" treated after recent strikes, with cumulative US casualties (killed and wounded) "at least 446," a ~15% rise since the April 8 ceasefire; 4-10 injured at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Jordan. It named Pvt. Isabella Gonzales (19, Carrollton, TX) and Lt. Tyler James Feehan (25, Ewa Beach, HI) among ~17 US KIA in the theatre and said a third (previously missing) soldier's remains had been identified. This is a single-official aggregate against the Pentagon's lower official count, not a reconciled DoD roster, and concerns air/missile-strike casualties on bases in Jordan/Iraq/the Gulf — not a ground deployment. (The Intercept, "U.S. Official: Iran Attacks Injured 'Far More' Troops Than Pentagon Admits," July 20, 2026.)

**Oil crosses ~$90; Trump won't rule out taking Kharg.** Brent crude crossed ~$90/bbl on Monday July 20, extending gains to its highest in over a month (~+30% from early-July lows), still below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US GROUND commitment would imply. Trump said "We're going to hit them very hard tonight, and we're going to hit them hard tomorrow," and — asked whether the US would take Kharg Island — declined to rule it out: "I can't say that to you because if I did, it would be foolish." No landing, port seizure, or troop movement toward Iran accompanied the remark. (TradingEconomics; CNBC; Newsweek; Fox News, July 20, 2026.)

**Ground rung — the escalation was air/maritime, not amphibious.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new amphibious-ready-group/MEU order, and no draft accompanied the ninth-to-tenth night, the Bushehr strike, or the second immobilized tanker. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR remained unchanged. Trump's refusal to rule out taking Kharg is declared strategic ambiguity — a coy non-denial, not a movement of troops; the war's established pattern of maximal Kharg talk paired with zero Kharg execution held. The Intercept's casualty-undercount report, even if borne out, concerns strike casualties on bases, not a ground commitment. The USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU — the units repeatedly named as the Kharg toolkit, alongside ~1,000-1,200 82nd Airborne paratroopers — held routine/contingency posture; a Kharg seizure is still reported to need at least ~1,200 troops, with plans "continuously shelved" as too risky. The predicted US ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure has still not occurred (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: **kharg-seizure-total-control-threat-june-2026**). (CBS News; NPR; The Intercept; Newsweek; Fox News; Task & Purpose, July 20, 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 18-19 (DAY 143): AN EIGHTH STRAIGHT NIGHT OF US STRIKES WIDENS FOR THE FIRST TIME INTO CENTRAL IRAN, WITH MANNED FIGHTER JETS STRIKING ~650 KM INLAND TO YAZD; THE US SURGES DOZENS MORE AERIAL-REFUELING TANKERS TO ISRAEL AS TRUMP WEIGHS A 'BROADER CAMPAIGN,' AND THE DISABLED TANKER BELMA IS RE-STRUCK AT KHARG; AN IRGC ADVISER'S 'FULL-SCALE OFFENSIVE' ULTIMATUM WINDOW (~JULY 19-20) NEARS EXPIRY. STILL AN AIR/MARITIME CAMPAIGN — NOT A GROUND SEIZURE; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**US runs an eighth consecutive night of strikes and widens into central Iran with manned jets.** The US ran an eighth straight night of strikes and, for the first time, expanded the target map into central Iran, employing manned fighter jets (reported as requiring heavy aerial-refueling support) rather than the standoff cruise missiles and drones that had defined the first seven nights — reportedly pushing ~650 km inland to Yazd. CENTCOM described striking "multiple sites throughout central and southern Iran, including through the use of jet fighters." Al Jazeera reported five explosions at Yazd; Iran's Mehr agency said the Yazd strikes fell "outside the city limits" with no casualties there, while Iranian media reported at least three killed and eight wounded across Hormozgan (plus additional deaths in bridge strikes near Bandar Khamir). A widening and intensification of the air campaign — deeper geography, first use of manned jets — not a landing. (Al Jazeera; Euronews, "US forces strike Iran for seventh consecutive night"; CENTCOM public release; Mehr News; en.wikipedia.org, "Timeline of the 2026 Iran war," July 18, 2026.)

**US surges dozens more aerial-refueling tankers to Israel; Trump weighs a 'broader campaign.'** The US notified Israel it will send dozens more aerial-refueling tankers as Washington prepares for a possible expansion of operations against Iran; the Pentagon already operates about 30 tankers from Ben Gurion Airport and a similar number from Ramon, with roughly 10 more arriving Friday-Saturday to be based at air-force fields after congestion at Ben Gurion threatened civilian flights. Reporting said President Trump is weighing a broader campaign than the strikes conducted so far. This is air-campaign enablement — aerial-refueling tankers feed aircraft, not amphibious landings — a buildup to strike harder from the air, not a ground/amphibious order. (The Times of Israel, "US sending dozens of refueling aircraft to Israel ahead of potential attack on Iran"; Ynet; Israel Hayom; Haaretz; The War Zone, July 17-18, 2026.)

**The disabled tanker M/T Belma is re-struck at Kharg; maritime interdiction continues.** The disabled Curaçao-flagged tanker M/T Belma (first hit July 15 by a Hellfire into its smokestack) was struck again by two US missiles at Kharg Island, per Bushehr's deputy governor — a maritime interdiction action against a vessel at the island's approaches, not a landing on or seizure of Kharg. (en.wikipedia.org, "2026 Kharg Island attack"; NPR, July 2026.)

**IRGC 'full-scale offensive' ultimatum nears expiry.** IRGC adviser Mohsen Rezaei (to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei) warned Iran would move "from the phase of retaliation to the offensive phase" if US attacks continue "another two or three days," vowing "no political border will be safe" — an ultimatum window analysts placed at ~July 19-20. (Iranian state TV/IRIB via Al Jazeera; Haaretz live blog, July 18, 2026.)

**Oil-figure caution.** Oil stayed elevated at multi-week highs, with Hormuz functionally shut; the last reliable mainstream print was Brent ~$88/bbl on the July 17 close (+~14% on the week). A far higher ~$113/bbl figure circulated via a single unverified aggregator and could not be corroborated by CNBC/Bloomberg/Al Jazeera; it is not adopted here. (CNBC; Al Jazeera; TradingEconomics, July 15-18, 2026.)

**Ground rung — the escalation was air/maritime, not amphibious.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new amphibious-ready-group/MEU order, and no draft accompanied the eighth night, the widening into central Iran, or the refueling-tanker surge. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR remained unchanged. The new means — manned jets ~650 km inland, dozens of KC-46/KC-135 tankers surging to Israel to enable a broader air effort, and a second strike on the Belma at Kharg — deepen the air/maritime campaign; aerial-refueling tankers enable aircraft, not amphibious assault. The USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU — the units repeatedly named as the Kharg toolkit, alongside ~1,000-1,200 82nd Airborne paratroopers — held routine/contingency posture; Task & Purpose reiterated a Kharg seizure would need at least ~1,200 troops and that seizure plans stay "continuously shelved" as too risky. Speculative claims — a single National Security Journal panelist's account of Marines "storming Kharg within the week," a widely-recycled Jerusalem Post "no alternative but a ground operation" report actually dated March 22, 2026, and unverified Iranian state-media footage claiming captured US Marines on Kharg (no US confirmation; flagged as likely disinformation) — do not amount to an executed or ordered US landing. The predicted US ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure has still not occurred (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: **kharg-seizure-total-control-threat-june-2026**). (The Times of Israel; Ynet; Haaretz; The War Zone; 19FortyFive; Task & Purpose; The Jerusalem Post, article-890834 [dated March 22, 2026]; National Security Journal; en.wikipedia.org "2026 Kharg Island attack," July 17-18, 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 17-18 (DAY 142): A SEVENTH STRAIGHT NIGHT OF US STRIKES LEVELS SOUTHERN IRANIAN INFRASTRUCTURE (SIX HORMOZGAN BRIDGES, AN AIRPORT, RAIL, POWER) AND IRAN WIDENS ITS RETALIATION — HITTING A KUWAITI DESALINATION-AND-POWER PLANT AND KILLING AT LEAST 8 US-BACKED KURDS IN IRAQ; THE TREASURY OIL-SANCTIONS WAIVER EXPIRES, BRENT SURGES TO ~$88, AND HORMUZ GOES FUNCTIONALLY SHUT (<5% OF PRE-WAR TRANSITS); AN IRGC COMMANDER WARNS OF 'FULL-SCALE OFFENSIVE OPERATIONS.' STILL AIR/MISSILE/MARITIME COERCION — NOT A GROUND SEIZURE; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**US runs a seventh consecutive night of strikes; southern infrastructure leveled.** The US launched another round of strikes against Iran for a seventh consecutive night, CENTCOM said. Iran reported the targets included six bridges in Hormozgan province facing the Strait of Hormuz, an airport, railway stations and power infrastructure across southern Iran; Iranian state media said at least seven people were killed and 20 wounded. The campaign stayed on the air rung; no US ground forces entered Iran. (NPR, "U.S. strikes bridges in Iran; Tehran targets U.S. bases in the Gulf"; CNN, "US launches another round of strikes after Iran widens its attacks on regional allies"; ABC News; France 24, July 17, 2026.)

**Iran strikes a Kuwaiti desalination-and-power plant and widens its Gulf salvo.** Iran hit a Kuwaiti water-desalination plant and a power plant; Kuwait's military said several members of its ground forces were wounded and military and civilian facilities were damaged after a ballistic-missile-and-drone attack — an escalation that exposed the region's water vulnerability. Iran also fired at Qatar and Jordan as its retaliation for the intensifying US strikes broadened. (CNBC, "Oil prices rise after Kuwait says Iran attacked water desalination and power plant"; France 24; Al Jazeera, "Gulf states come under Iranian fire as US strikes intensify," July 17, 2026.)

**Iran kills at least 8 US-backed Kurds in Iraq.** Iran attacked with drones and rockets a camp of the Komala party and its vicinity near Sulaimaniyah early in the morning, killing at least eight members and wounding others; the US-led anti-jihadist coalition shot down several drones over Erbil. KRG President Nechirvan Barzani condemned the strikes as "a serious escalation and a blatant violation of Iraq's sovereignty." A horizontal widening of the war onto Iraqi soil, not a US or Iranian ground campaign in Iran. (France 24, "Iran launches drone, missile attacks on dissident bases in Iraqi Kurdistan"; Al Jazeera; en.wikipedia.org, "2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region," July 17, 2026.)

Still elevated but far below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. (Al Jazeera; NBC News, "Oil hits $87 per barrel again"; CNBC, July 17, 2026.)

**Hormuz "worst case scenario" — functionally blocked.** Maritime-risk analysts said tanker traffic faced a "worst case scenario" in Hormuz, with transits below 5% of the pre-war baseline (about 2% throughput), leaving the chokepoint functionally blocked under the re-imposed US blockade and Iranian attacks on shipping. (CNBC, "Oil tankers face 'worst case scenario' in Hormuz as Iran steps up attacks on ships," July 17, 2026.)

**IRGC warns of 'full-scale offensive operations'; Kharg stays air-only.** An IRGC commander (Mohsen Rezaei, via IRIB) warned that "if US attacks continue for another two or three days, we will enter a phase of full-scale offensive operations," and Iran reiterated that US interference in the Strait is its "invincible red line." Trump declined to rule out taking Kharg Island but said it would be foolish to announce it, noting prior strikes deliberately spared the island's oil terminals; reporting said he had authorized strikes on Kharg contingent on verified US casualties or an Iranian strike on critical infrastructure — but no landing was ordered. (CNBC, "Iran warns U.S. of Hormuz 'red line'"; ABC News; Britannica, July 17, 2026.)

**Ground rung — Marines used for boardings, not a landing.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new amphibious-ready-group/MEU order, and no draft accompanied the seventh night of strikes or the widened Iranian retaliation. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR remained unchanged. US Marines boarded the commercial vessel M/T Wen Yao to enforce the naval blockade, and a US fighter jet disabled the Curaçao-flagged tanker M/T Belma (a Hellfire missile into its smokestack) as it transited toward Kharg Island — visit-board-search-and-seizure and interdiction actions at sea, not an amphibious landing on Iranian soil. The USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU — the units repeatedly named as the toolkit for a Kharg operation, alongside ~1,000-1,200 82nd Airborne paratroopers — held routine/contingency posture; Task & Purpose reiterated a Kharg seizure would need at least ~1,200 troops and that seizure plans stay "continuously shelved" as too risky. The predicted US ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure has still not occurred (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: **kharg-seizure-total-control-threat-june-2026**). (The Hill, "US military disables first tanker in Arabian Sea since blockade was reimposed"; NPR; CBS News; Stars and Stripes; Task & Purpose, July 16-17, 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 16-17 (DAY 141): THE US-IRAN FIGHT ENTERS A SIXTH STRAIGHT DAY AS THE US WIDENS ITS STRIKES INTO NORTHERN IRAN AND, UNDER THE RE-IMPOSED BLOCKADE, DISABLES AN UNLADEN TANKER HEADED FOR KHARG ISLAND THAT WAS TRYING TO RUN THE BLOCKADE; TRUMP TELLS FOX THE US WILL 'KEEP THE STRAIT' AND BE ITS 'GUARDIAN ANGEL' (AND BE 'REIMBURSED'), WHILE IRAN'S FM RETORTS THAT IRAN IS 'THE GUARDIAN OF THE STRAIT… FOREVER.' BRENT HOLDS BELOW $85. STILL AIR/NAVAL COERCION AND MARITIME INTERDICTION — NOT A GROUND SEIZURE; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**US-Iran fighting enters a sixth straight day; strikes widen into northern Iran.** The US and Iran traded fire for a sixth consecutive day, with US strikes targeting Iranian command centers and missile sites — reporting noting the US EXPANDED its strike map into NORTHERN Iran, beyond the southern coastal/Hormuz belt it had concentrated on in earlier rounds — while Iran again targeted US military bases in Gulf countries. CENTCOM framed the wave as further degrading Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The exchange stayed on the air/missile rung; no US ground forces entered Iran. (CNN, "US expands strikes into northern Iran and disables ship trying to run blockade"; CBS News, July 16, 2026.)

**US disables an unladen tanker headed for Kharg Island under the blockade.** Under the re-imposed naval blockade, the US military said it disabled an unladen (empty) oil tanker that was headed for a port in Iran and trying to avoid the blockade; CENTCOM said the vessel was steaming toward Kharg Island. This was the interdiction campaign's closest approach to the island — but a maritime INTERDICTION, not a landing on or seizure of Kharg. (NPR, "The U.S. fires a new wave of strikes on Iran and hits a tanker trying to skirt its blockade"; CBS News; en.wikipedia.org, "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis," July 15-16, 2026.)

We'll become the guardian of the Strait. Maybe we'll call it the 'Guardian Angel of the Strait.' And we should be reimbursed for that" — reasserting the "guardian"/reimbursement framing days after he reversed his 20% Hormuz "toll." Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi replied that compensation for safe passage was fair but that "Iran has always been the GUARDIAN of the Strait and will remain so FOREVER." A rhetorical sovereignty contest over who governs the chokepoint, not a ground move. (Britannica, "2026 Iran war," July 2026.)

**Oil holds below $85; Hormuz traffic "grinding to a halt."** Brent's September contract settled about $84.95/bbl (+22¢) on July 15 and closed below $85, while WTI traded above $80 after adding more than 11% over three prior sessions. Analysts said Hormuz traffic was "grinding to a halt," back to or below the pre-MOU pace, contributing to elevated prices despite the fighting. Still >15% above the late-February pre-war level, but far below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. (Bloomberg, "Latest Oil Market News for July 16"; CNBC; Al Jazeera, July 15-16, 2026.)

**Hormuz traffic and the shipping toll.** Maritime tracking (Kpler) showed only about 21 ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday — primarily crude, LPG, methanol and iron-ore carriers — as three further attacks off Oman were verified, bringing the running war tally to about 56 confirmed shipping incidents and 17 seafarer fatalities. (Kpler via CBS News/NPR, July 15-16, 2026.)

**Ground rung — wider air campaign and a Kharg-bound interdiction, still no landing.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new amphibious-ready-group/MEU order, and no draft accompanied the sixth day of strikes or the Kharg-bound tanker interdiction. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR remained unchanged; the USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU — the units repeatedly named as the toolkit for a Kharg operation, alongside ~1,000-1,200 82nd Airborne paratroopers — held routine/contingency posture in the Arabian Sea/Indian Ocean. Reporting reiterated a Kharg takeover would require a significant number of ground troops (Task & Purpose: at least ~1,200) and that seizure plans stay "continuously shelved" as too risky; a Daily Caller op-ed (July 13) called a Kharg invasion "a disaster waiting to happen." The predicted US ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure has still not occurred (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: **kharg-seizure-total-control-threat-june-2026**). ## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 15-16 (DAY 140): WITH THE NAVAL BLOCKADE BACK ON, THE US RUNS A FIFTH STRAIGHT NIGHT OF STRIKES AND — IN A COMBAT FIRST — HITS THE BANDAR ABBAS NAVAL BASE WITH ONE-WAY ATTACK SEA DRONES; THE BLOCKADE MAKES ITS FIRST INTERDICTIONS (TWO VESSELS 'REDIRECTED'); IRAN'S IRGC THREATENS TO HALT ALL MIDDLE EAST ENERGY EXPORTS ('EITHER FOR EVERYONE OR FOR NO ONE') AND STRIKES JORDAN, KUWAIT AND BAHRAIN; BRENT HOLDS A ONE-MONTH HIGH NEAR $85. STILL AIR, NAVAL AND UNMANNED-MARITIME COERCION — NOT A GROUND SEIZURE; GROUND RUNG UNCHANGED (NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG LANDING/SEIZURE, NO NEW ARG/MEU, NO DRAFT; ~50,000 PERSONNEL UNCHANGED).

**US runs a fifth consecutive round of strikes.** US CENTCOM launched a new wave of strikes on Iranian military positions beginning ~1:30pm Tehran time Wednesday July 15 and continued overnight-plus-daytime attacks — hitting missile and drone facilities, naval assets and coastal-defense systems in the fifth consecutive round since the blockade re-imposition. CENTCOM framed the campaign as degrading "Iran's ability to continue attacking commercial shipping." It stayed on the air/naval rung; no ground forces entered Iran. (IranWire; NPR, "The U.S. fires a new wave of strikes on Iran and hits a tanker trying to skirt its blockade," July 15, 2026; CBS News, July 15, 2026.)

**US combat first — one-way attack sea drones hit the Bandar Abbas naval base.** For the first time in combat, US forces used one-way attack unmanned surface vessels — three "Corsair" sea drones — against the Bandar Abbas naval base, CENTCOM releasing video of the drones speeding toward and detonating on a raised dock that held a small submarine. CENTCOM said the strikes "degraded Iran's ability to continue attacking commercial shipping." This is a new unmanned-maritime rung of the campaign — a way to hit Iran's shipping-attack infrastructure from stand-off/unmanned platforms — not a ground operation. (Task & Purpose, "US military uses one-way attack sea drones for first time"; CBS News, "U.S. uses sea drones in combat for first time to attack Iranian naval base"; Breaking Defense; Army Recognition, July 12-15, 2026.)

**The re-imposed blockade makes its first interdictions.** Within roughly 17 hours of restarting the naval blockade of Iranian ports, US forces said they had "redirected" two commercial vessels attempting to breach it, and CENTCOM reported striking a tanker trying to skirt the blockade. This is maritime interdiction — the instrument the US has used throughout — not a landing or port seizure. (CNN, "US military says it has redirected 2 commercial vessels since restarting blockade," July 15, 2026; NPR, July 15, 2026.)

**Casualties.** US strikes killed at least seven Iranian troops at an army barracks in Sistan and Baluchestan province, with more than 260 people wounded across the country; Iranian officials reported more than 30 deaths in recent days overall. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said Iran had "deliberately" targeted civilians and attacked seven commercial vessels over the previous week, leaving "nearly a dozen" crew members killed, wounded or missing. (Fortune; Washington Times; Al Jazeera, July 15, 2026.)

**Iran threatens to halt all regional energy exports.** Iran's Revolutionary Guard declared, "The export of oil and gas from the region will be either for everyone or for no one," threatening to stop all Middle East energy exports over the US blockade and warning it could block additional vital seaways — again weaponizing the chokepoint to coerce a lifting of the blockade. (Fortune, "'Either for everyone or for no one': Iran turns oil into a weapon again"; Washington Times; MSNBC/ms.now; Gulf Today, July 15, 2026.)

**Iran strikes Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain.** Iran launched dozens of missiles and drones at neighboring Gulf Arab states hosting US forces; Jordan said it shot down three incoming Iranian missiles, and missile-alert warnings sounded in Bahrain and Kuwait. Iran said it had targeted US sites in Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain. These were Iranian air/missile strikes on US partners, not a US or Iranian ground move. (AP, "Tehran attacks Jordan as US reimposes its blockade on Iran"; Al Jazeera, "Iran launches attacks across region as US strikes continue," July 15, 2026.)

**Oil holds a one-month high but does not spike further.** Brent's September contract settled about $84.95/bbl (+22 cents, ~+0.3%) and WTI's August contract about $79.60 (+26 cents) — "little changed"/"steadying near a one-month high" after the prior day's ~10% weekly surge and the intraday move above $86. Brent stayed more than 15% above the late-February pre-war level; one analyst said the escalation "shows how expectations of a rapid opening of the Strait were premature" and warned oil could retest $100 if the intensity persists for weeks — but far below the ~$126 April wartime peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. (CNBC, "Oil little changed after U.S. reimposes naval blockade on Iran, launches more airstrikes"; Bloomberg, July 15, 2026.)

**Hormuz traffic and the shipping toll.** Maritime tracking showed only about 21 ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz on July 15; the running tally of the tanker-war reached roughly 56 confirmed shipping incidents and 17 seafarer fatalities. Talks remained stalled and the interim US-Iran deal derailed, with regional mediators still trying to return the parties to the table. (2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis tracking; Fortune; NPR, July 15, 2026.)

**Ground rung — deeper coercion, still no landing.** No US troops entered Iran; no Kharg landing or port seizure; no new ARG/MEU order; no draft or mobilization. ~50,000 US personnel in the CENTCOM AOR unchanged; the standing USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU (2,200 Marines, with USS Portland) and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU (~3,500 troops) held routine/contingency posture. The renewed coercion of the chokepoint ran through the blockade (interdiction), air strikes and — newly — unmanned sea drones, all stand-off or maritime instruments. The combat debut of one-way attack USVs is an escalation of means that substitutes for boots ashore rather than presaging them; the predicted US ground seizure of Hormuz/Kharg stays disconfirmed. (CBS News; NPR; Stars and Stripes; Task & Purpose, July 15, 2026.)

## 1-PRIOR. US-Iran Military Actions — JULY 14-15 (DAY 139): THE US RE-IMPOSES ITS NAVAL BLOCKADE OF IRANIAN PORTS (20+ WARSHIPS, HUNDREDS OF AIRCRAFT) AND TRUMP ANNOUNCES — THEN THE SAME DAY REVERSES — A 20% HORMUZ 'TOLL,' CASTING THE US AS THE STRAIT'S 'GUARDIAN'; CENTCOM RUNS A FOURTH STRAIGHT NIGHT OF STRIKES AND IRAN HITS THREE MORE TANKERS; BRENT SURGES ABOVE $85 (HIGHEST SINCE JUNE 15). **US re-imposes its naval blockade of Iranian ports.** On July 14 (~4pm ET) US forces launched strikes against Iranian targets shortly before the US resumed its naval blockade of Iranian ports in and around the Strait of Hormuz; CENTCOM said "more than 20 US Navy warships and hundreds of military aircraft" were operating in the region. The restart ended the ~27-day period the blockade had been lifted since the June 17 MOU — a return of the US maritime-interdiction instrument, and the sharpest US coercion of the chokepoint since the June lift, but a naval/air move, not a ground operation or Kharg landing. (NPR; CBS News; CNBC, July 13-14, 2026.)

**Trump's 20% Hormuz 'toll' — announced, then reversed.** Trump said the US would charge a 20% toll/reimbursement on cargo passing through the Strait in exchange for US protection, casting the US as the Strait's "guardian" and saying beneficiary states (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait) should compensate the US for keeping the waterway open. He reversed the fee the same day — "I don't think anybody should be able to charge a fee" — and pivoted to Gulf-state investment deals instead. The US DoE said 8.5 million barrels passed through the Strait the previous day "with military assistance." (Al Jazeera; CBS News, July 14, 2026.)

**Fourth consecutive night of US strikes.** US CENTCOM conducted a fourth consecutive night of strikes (begun ~4:45pm ET Monday and continuing Tuesday) to "continue degrading Iranian capabilities used to attack commercial shipping," hitting military targets across Iran including Bushehr, Chah Bahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa and Bandar Abbas. (NPR; CBS News; CNN, July 13-14, 2026.)

**Iran's tanker attacks and casualties.** Early July 14 Iran attacked three tankers — the chemical tanker Stolt Magnesium (projectile NE of Qalhat) and the UAE-owned oil tankers Mombasa B and Al Bahyah (cruise missiles); the IRGC said it targeted "offending supertankers" entering a "mined route." One Indian national was killed aboard Mombasa B; eight others (six Indians, two Ukrainians) were injured; three crew aboard Al Bahyah were declared missing. The disabled M/V GFS Galaxy's missing crewman (from Pune, India) was confirmed dead, his body recovered by the Omani Navy. Iran also fired a missile/drone salvo at US assets in Kuwait and Bahrain (Kuwait reported intercepting 33 drones, five cruise missiles and one ballistic missile). (en.wikipedia.org, "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis," accessed July 15, 2026; CBS News, July 14, 2026.)

**Oil — Brent above $85, highest since June 15.** Brent's September contract reached ~$85.92/bbl as of 08:00 GMT July 14 (up ~3.8% on the day after a ~9.6% gain the prior session) and traded above $86 — its highest since June 15, up ~19% from late-February pre-conflict levels; the week's gain topped 10%. WTI rose in step. Hormuz crossings dropped by more than half from the prior week (only ~57 transits Friday-Sunday). Still war-risk repricing far below the ~$126 April peak and the $130+ a sustained US ground commitment would imply. (Al Jazeera, "Oil hits 1-month high as US-Iran fighting clouds Strait of Hormuz outlook"; TradingEconomics; CNBC, July 14, 2026.)

**Ground rung unchanged; the sharpest test of the seizure prediction.** There were no US troops in Iran, no Kharg landing or port seizure, no new ARG/MEU order, and no draft; ~50,000 US personnel were unchanged, with the USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU in the Arabian Sea in routine/contingency posture. Reporting continued to note a Kharg takeover "would require a significant number of ground troops" and that seizure plans remain "continuously shelved because the operation was considered too risky." This is the closest the war has come to the corpus-predicted US control of the Strait — but the US is asserting that control via a naval blockade and air power, not the predicted ground invasion / Kharg landing / troop seizure, which has still not occurred. The imminent-US-ground-seizure / Hormuz-and-Kharg thesis stays disconfirmed (CONTESTED-UNRESOLVED — open-question: iran-hormuz-administration-tolls-dispute-june-2026). After two days of **indirect** talks, the US and Iran **concluded the round July 2.** Qatar's spokesman reported **"positive progress"** on technical matters, but negotiators focused on issues both sides had previously indicated were **largely resolved** rather than the core disagreements, producing **no apparent breakthrough** toward lasting peace. The outputs were implementation mechanics: a **goods-purchase mechanism for the first tranche of frozen assets** (reports of a **~$3B humanitarian-goods arrangement,** which **US officials said was not finalized**), a **communications channel to flag and address ceasefire violations,** and an **agreed focus on restoring reliable Hormuz passage.** (Al Jazeera, "US-Iran talks in Doha: What were the outcomes and what's next?"; The National, "US and Iran conclude Hormuz-dominated indirect talks in Doha," July 2, 2026.)

A US official said the **US and Iran had agreed to stop attacks and allow vessels to move freely through the Strait of Hormuz** after the weekend exchange, and that **"no drones or missiles launched by Iran at US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait last night reached their targets."** The mutual halt ended the three-day breach-retaliation cycle that had peaked June 28 with the US 10-target airstrike near Hormuz and Iran's missile/drone attack on US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Trump posted on Truth Social that **"Iran has requested a meeting"** and that **"it will take place tomorrow in Doha,"** Qatar. White House press secretary **Karoline Leavitt** said special envoy **Steve Witkoff** and **Jared Kushner** would fly to Doha for **"high-level meetings"** held alongside **"technical talks."** The talks were **originally planned for Switzerland** but the flare-up **moved them to Qatar and re-scoped the agenda to the Hormuz standoff.** (NPR, "Trump says the U.S. and Iran will meet in Qatar after weekend attacks"; CNBC; NBC News, June 29, 2026.)

Iran and Oman **separately confirmed they held their first meeting on managing the Strait of Hormuz,** with disagreements persisting over **corridor management and demining operations.** Iran's deputy FM said **Iran would conduct demining alone and rejected international involvement** — including a **France-Oman joint demining initiative** it objected to — calling the situation **"sensitive and complex."** **Oman rejected Iran's proposed transit fees,** affirming its commitment to international maritime law, and the **GCC secretary-general called tolls "not acceptable."** (CBS News; Euronews, "Iran and Oman hold first Hormuz talks as US-Iran deal stays on edge"; The National, June 29, 2026.)

Iran's president announced that Tehran had received **"$6 billion out of the total $12 billion of Iranian resources in Qatar"** under the memorandum of understanding, with reports that the **unfrozen funds were designated to purchase American wheat and corn** — a tangible MOU-implementation step even as the broader deal stayed strained. **Brent rose only slightly to about $69.70/bbl on June 29,** rebounding marginally off a **four-month low** reached after the US-Iran agreement to halt attacks (Brent had hit **~$72 on June 26,** its lowest since Feb 27); **Trump said oil prices were "charging down"** after the Hormuz reopening, and analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya said the weekend clashes' impact stayed **"relatively contained"** given strategic-reserve releases and resumed tanker movements. Hormuz traffic stayed thinned by the weekend clashes — **29 commodity vessels crossed Saturday and 12 Sunday, down from 70 the prior Wednesday** — but **major container lines resumed Gulf services** and the **first commercial flight from Tehran landed in Dubai.** (TradingEconomics/CNBC, Brent crude; CBS News; The National, June 29, 2026.)

Every EXECUTION indicator stayed at zero as the cycle resolved into a stand-down.
