### August 25 Update — Ukraine Marks Its 35th Independence Day Under a 143-Drone Barrage; European Leaders Come to Kyiv and Washington Does Not (August 23-24, 2026)

**The anniversary was observed and the war was not interrupted for it.** Overnight into **August 24** Russia launched **two Oniks anti-ship missiles**, **six Kh-31P and Kh-59 guided air-launched missiles** and **143 drones** — approximately one third of them **jet-powered** — into Ukraine. Ukrainian air defences downed **109 drones, one Oniks, two Kh-31P/Kh-59 missiles and two Banderol munitions**. Strikes were recorded at **22 locations** with debris falling at five more.

**The toll.** Russian attacks killed at least **eight** people and injured at least **43** across Ukraine over the day. **Kharkiv Oblast** took the worst of it with **five killed and 23 injured including two children**; in the **Lozova community** two women were killed and six injured, among them an **eleven-year-old girl with burns**. **Donetsk Oblast** recorded two killed and seven injured, both deaths in **Kramatorsk**. **Sumy Oblast** recorded one killed and 12 injured. **Zaporizhzhia** and **Dnipropetrovsk** each recorded three injured and **Chernihiv** one. Governor **Oleh Syniehubov** reported strikes across Kharkiv and sixteen other settlements.

**The diplomatic picture at the ceremony is the more significant fact, and it is an absence.** European leaders travelled to Kyiv for the official commemoration of the **35th anniversary** of the 1991 Act of Declaration of Independence; **no United States representative attended**. British Prime Minister **Andy Burnham** made his first foreign trip since taking office and pledged that the defence firm **MBDA would release classified data on UK components for the SCALP missile** to help Ukraine establish **local assembly lines** — a transfer of *production capability* rather than of *stock*, which is a different category of commitment from a donation and is what sponsors do when inventories are constrained. Norwegian Prime Minister **Jonas Gahr Store** committed **$9 billion** in support for **2027**, described as matching this year's record total.

**What Zelensky asked for.** He pressed the **"Coalition of the Willing"** — roughly **34 nations** led by London and Paris — for expanded **air-defence systems**, and pressed the European Union to deliver quickly on a promised **€90 billion loan** against a Ukrainian military budget deficit of **$27 billion**. **No NATO commitment and no foreign troop deployment was announced.**

**The front and the talks.** The Institute for the Study of War assessed that Russian forces recently **advanced east of Slovyansk**, prioritising favourable positions east and south-east of the city ahead of frontal assaults toward Slovyansk and the rest of the **Fortress Belt**, and that President Putin continues to **set unrealistic deadlines** for the seizure of all of Donetsk Oblast, likely in part because of his misunderstanding of battlefield realities. On **August 23** Zelensky reportedly presented a **joint Ukraine-US-Europe proposal** to end the war offering **significant Ukrainian concessions**, while Putin and other Kremlin officials continue to refuse to compromise on any core demand. Net Russian territorial gains for 2026 remain approximately **81.1 square kilometres**.

*Sources: The Kyiv Independent, "Russian attacks kill 8, injure 43 over past day as Ukrainians celebrate Independence Day," August 24, 2026; Ukraine Air Force overnight air-attack summary via Kyiv Independent, August 24, 2026; i24NEWS, "Ukraine marks 35 years of independence under fire as allies pledge fresh support," August 24, 2026; AP via The Philadelphia Inquirer and The Washington Times, "European leaders mark Ukraine's 35th Independence Day as Russian invasion pushes on," August 24, 2026; Institute for the Study of War, Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 23-24, 2026, via Kyiv Post; Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Syniehubov, statement of August 24, 2026.*

### August 24 Update — The Line Holds, the Strike War Continues Both Ways, and Moscow's Opening Carries Its Precondition Inside It (August 21-23, 2026)

**The kinetic record for August 23 is two-sided and unremarkable by this war's standards.** Russian forces launched **guided bomb strikes on Izyum** in Kharkiv oblast, **wounding two people** and damaging **at least twenty buildings, vehicles and power lines**. Overnight into August 23, Ukraine's Defence Forces struck **a radar station and a site used by Russian forces to store and launch unmanned surface vessels** in temporarily occupied **Crimea** — a continuation of the campaign against the Black Sea Fleet's remaining sensing and naval-drone infrastructure rather than a new axis. Ukraine's General Staff put cumulative Russian personnel losses since February 2022 at approximately **1,476,580** as of August 23; the figure is a **Ukrainian claim** and is recorded as such. **Net Russian territorial gains for 2026 remain 81.1 square kilometres.**

**The diplomatic signal is an opening with the precondition built into it.** Deputy Foreign Minister **Sergey Ryabkov** said on **August 21** that Moscow is ready to listen to **"new ideas"** for ending the war provided they align with **President Putin's position** and are in line with **"realities on the ground."** The second phrase does the work: it converts occupied territory from a subject of negotiation into a starting assumption. Against that, President **Zelensky** said Ukraine, together with its partners in the **United States and Europe**, has developed a plan to end the war envisaging **a ceasefire, the creation of a free economic zone, and the withdrawal of troops**. The two positions are not in the same document, and the second explicitly contemplates the withdrawal the first defines away.

**The Iran war continues to reach this theatre through the interceptor market.** Ukrainian forces are developing **domestic technological solutions** for targeting Russian ballistic launchers and jet-powered drones specifically in order to **circumvent the need for foreign materiel** amid global air-defence interceptor shortages — the munitions drain of the Gulf war translated into Ukrainian procurement doctrine. **North Korean drone operators** remain reported deployed to **Kursk oblast**, a move up the capability ladder from the infantry deployments of earlier phases.

*Sources: Institute for the Study of War, Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 21-23, 2026; Ukrinform war-update wire, August 23, 2026; Al Jazeera, "Russia says ready for 'new ideas' on Ukraine war that match Putin's goals," August 21, 2026; The Moscow Times, August 20, 2026.*

### August 23 Update — Kyiv Begins Engineering Around American Resupply, and North Korea Sends Drone Crews (August 21, 2026)

**The interceptor shortage has stopped being a supply problem for Kyiv and become a design brief.** The Institute for the Study of War's assessment of **August 21** records that **Ukrainian forces are adapting their tactics and domestically developing technological solutions to target Russia's ballistic missile launchers and jet-powered drones in ways that circumvent the need for foreign materiel assistance amid global air-defence interceptor shortages.** This is the second-order consequence this briefing has tracked since CSIS put remaining US stocks below **827 Patriot** and **278 THAAD** interceptors, with more than **60% expended** and **three-plus years to rebuild**: Ukraine has concluded it cannot wait for the pipeline to refill and is shifting from intercepting the shot to killing the shooter. It is a recipient state's judgement about the reliability of the American arsenal, expressed in procurement policy rather than in rhetoric.

**The strike exchange continued at scale.** The same assessment records **Russia launching 135 long-range strike drones**, and **Ukrainian strikes on Russian military airfields and oil infrastructure**.

**North Korea's contribution has changed category.** ISW reports that **North Korea has deployed drone operators to Kursk Oblast** to support Russia's war, assessing that the deployment will allow North Korean forces to gain tactical and technological skills critical to contemporary warfare. Pyongyang's earlier contribution was infantry and artillery ammunition; drone crews are a capability that returns home with the operators, and they are being trained in the most heavily contested electromagnetic environment in the world. The deployment overlaps with Pyongyang's own August ballistic testing campaign.

**The diplomatic track remains closed and the line remains static.** A senior Russian official reiterated the Kremlin's continued unwillingness to engage in meaningful negotiations. Kremlin spokesman **Dmitry Peskov** confirmed on **July 22** that Putin's **June 2024 maximalist terms** — complete Ukrainian withdrawal from Ukrainian-held territory in Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia and Kherson oblasts, and abandonment of NATO accession — remain the basis of Russian conditions for ending the war. US-mediated talks have produced no ceasefire, and the parties remain divided over territory and security guarantees. **Russian forces have seized a net total of 81.1 square kilometres so far in 2026**, a figure depressed in part by the Ukrainian spring-summer counteroffensive — a rate of advance that cannot deliver the Kremlin's stated territorial objective on any timeline it has named.

*Sources: Institute for the Study of War, "Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 21, 2026," via Kyiv Post; Critical Threats / AEI-ISW, "Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 2, 2026" and "July 22, 2026"; Council on Foreign Relations Global Conflict Tracker, "War in Ukraine," August 2026.*

### August 22 Update — Moscow Builds Its Campaign Around the Patriot Gap the Iran War Created, and Accepts Spillover Into NATO States (August 8-21, 2026)

**Russian production has been retuned to exploit an American shortage.** Ukraine's GUR deputy head **Maj. Gen. Vadym Skibitskyi** said on **August 10** that Russia has been **reprioritising the production of ballistic and cruise missiles since April 2026** in an effort to exploit Ukrainian shortages of **Patriot interceptors**, and that Russian forces have **more than tripled monthly ballistic missile launches** against Ukraine between **April and July 2026**. The shortage is downstream of the Iran war: **CSIS** assesses fewer than **827** US Patriot interceptors remain against roughly **2,200** pre-war, with **more than 60% of Patriot and THAAD stocks expended** and **three or more years** required to rebuild. Zelensky said on **August 1** that Ukraine had **run out of interceptors** after only **one of twenty-seven** ballistic missiles was downed in a barrage that killed nine to ten people in Kyiv.

**The next blow is telegraphed.** Ukraine's **Strategic Communications Centre** reported on **August 8**, citing US intelligence, that Russia is preparing a **major strike campaign against energy infrastructure in Kyiv City ahead of Ukraine's Independence Day on August 24**. **Zelensky** said the same day that Ukraine has **effectively no undamaged power plants left**. The campaign being prepared targets the civilian grid rather than the line of contact.

**NATO spillover is no longer accidental-looking.** On **August 20** Russian aerial drones **penetrated Moldovan and Romanian airspace**, and **Romania deployed two F-16s** to destroy an explosive **naval drone near a Black Sea natural gas platform**; Ukraine denied ownership and Bucharest attributed it to Russia. **ISW assessed that these incidents demonstrate the Kremlin has accepted the risk that its war against Ukraine will cause damage to other states, including NATO states.** No Article 4 consultation followed, as none followed Poland's formal protest over the July 30 Kh-101 incursion near Lublin.

**The line is unchanged and Russia's domestic politics are being militarised.** Ukrainian forces recently **advanced northeast of Kharkiv City**. ISW's standing assessment that **Russia's spring-summer 2026 offensive has failed to achieve operationally significant gains** has not been revised, nor has its **July 31** finding that Russia's **Northern Grouping of Forces and high command are likely misreporting gains to the Kremlin**. On **August 20** ISW assessed that the Kremlin will likely cause a significant number of **Ukraine war veterans to be elected to the State Duma in the September 2026 elections**, particularly through United Russia, as part of a concerted effort to militarise Russian society; that the Russian government's response to domestic **gasoline shortages** remains inadequate and improvised; and that neither the Kremlin nor Russian milbloggers believe Russia can fully intercept Ukrainian strike packages any time soon. On **August 20-21** Russian authorities arrested **eight people** over an alleged plot against a defence enterprise and detained a foreign national accused of scouting it, alleging Ukrainian special-services involvement; Kyiv did not comment. In Ukraine, ousted Defence Minister **Mykhailo Fedorov**'s call for wartime elections backfired and protests faded after a successor was approved, with most Ukrainians preferring elections only after the war ends. **No negotiating round convened in this cycle.**

*Sources: ISW, "Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment," August 8, 10 and 20, 2026, via Critical Threats and Kyiv Post; RFE/RL via GlobalSecurity.org, August 2026; CNBC, August 1, 2026; The Wall Street Journal and Reuters via Just Security Early Edition, August 21, 2026; CSIS, "Rebuilding U.S. Missile Inventory: A Multiyear Project," 2026.*


### August 1 Update — The Kh-101 in Poland Is Assessed and Ukraine Answers Deep: Refineries and Logistics Hubs Struck in Volgograd, Tatarstan and Krasnodar (July 30-31, 2026)

**The Polish incursion, resolved as to weapon if not as to intent.** Experts assessed the projectile that detonated in eastern Poland on the morning of July 30 as a **Russian Kh-101 cruise missile**. It exploded in a field near the village of **Tarnawa-Kolonia**, close to **Lublin**, leaving a crater about **ten metres** wide. A spokesman for NATO's military headquarters said the alliance had **activated a wide range of air defences** in response to the intrusion and NATO fighter aircraft were scrambled; the alliance said it would **"defend territory."** Polish authorities blamed Russia. No Polish casualties were reported. The incident joins a growing series of NATO airspace violations that analysts have flagged as raising the risk of escalation beyond Ukraine's borders — and, as with every prior incursion of this war, it produced an air-defence and diplomatic response rather than an Article 4 or Article 5 process.

**Ukraine's answer ran into Russia's fuel and logistics chain.** On **July 31** a new wave of Ukrainian long-range strikes hit multiple supply hubs across Russia, with **oil refineries** and multiple **Wildberries logistics facilities** reported struck in the **Volgograd, Tatarstan and Krasnodar** regions overnight. Zelensky had said in a video address on July 30 that Ukraine's defence forces would **intensify their strikes on Russian territory**, and had ordered what he described as asymmetric defensive measures after the mass missile attack.

**The deep-strike campaign is now the negotiating argument.** Senior Ukrainian negotiator **Sergiy Kyslytsya** told NPR on July 28 that Kyiv believes it now has the leverage to force Russia into serious negotiations because Ukraine's long-range drones are repeatedly hitting Russian oil and gas facilities, causing fuel shortages and weakening the Kremlin's ability to wage war. On the Ukrainian home front, **66% of Ukrainians** told pollsters the government should seek to negotiate an end to the war as soon as possible.

**The line barely moved.** Ukraine's General Staff recorded **226 combat clashes** by 22:00 on July 30, with the heaviest activity on the **Kostiantynivka** and **Pokrovsk** axes. *The Economist*'s estimate showed Russia gaining **zero square miles** over the thirty days to July 28; **DeepState** OSINT data put the net gain at **ten square miles** over the four weeks from June 30 to July 28, against **thirty-one square miles** in the preceding four-week period. Both series describe the slowest sustained rate of advance of the war's current phase.

*Sources: The Washington Post, "Russian missile landed in Poland amid strikes on Ukraine, NATO says," July 30, 2026; Al Jazeera, "NATO jets scramble as Russian missile detonates in Poland," July 30, 2026; Foreign Policy, "NATO Says Russian Missile Violated Polish Airspace," July 30, 2026; The Irish Times, July 30, 2026; Stars and Stripes, July 30, 2026; CNN, July 29-30, 2026; NPR, July 28 and July 30, 2026; TIME, July 30, 2026; Mezha/Bukvy, July 30-31, 2026; Charter'97, July 30, 2026; Institute for the Study of War, July 30, 2026; Russia Matters, "The Russia-Ukraine War Report Card, July 29, 2026."*


### July 31 Update — Russia Fires 70+ Missiles and ~280 Drones at Kyiv and Lviv, Killing at Least Eight; a Russian Cruise Missile Crosses Into Poland and NATO Scrambles Jets; Ukraine Intercepts Only ONE of NINE Ballistic Missiles (July 29-30, 2026)
Russia attacked Ukraine overnight into July 30 with **more than 70 missiles and approximately 280 drones**, killing **at least eight people** by President Zelensky's count; subsequent Associated Press-sourced reports gave tolls of nine and then ten, with dozens injured. **Kyiv and the western Lviv region**, on the Polish border, were the main focus. Ukraine's air force said it shot down **55 of the missiles and 265 of the drones — but only ONE of NINE ballistic missiles**. That single ratio is the operative fact of the cycle: Ukrainian air defence remains highly effective against cruise missiles and drones and nearly helpless against ballistic ones, which is precisely the gap Patriot interceptors fill and precisely the inventory the Iran war is consuming, with Patriot and THAAD stocks reported three or more years from restoration after more than 11,000 munitions were expended in the first sixteen days of the resumed Iran phase.

**The missile in Poland.** Ukrainian Foreign Minister **Andrii Sybiha** said a Russian cruise missile crossed into Poland during the strike. **NATO confirmed** that a Russian missile entered Polish airspace and landed in a rural area, and **scrambled jets**. Polish Prime Minister **Donald Tusk** told an emergency meeting: **"all the indications are that it was a Russian Kh-101 ballistic missile, but we want to be 100% certain about the type of missile and who launched it,"** adding that there was **no direct threat** because the missile landed in an uninhabited area, and ordering an investigation. (The Kh-101 is an air-launched **cruise** missile, not a ballistic missile; the Prime Minister's on-the-record characterisation is recorded as given.) Warsaw's handling — investigate, decline to attribute before certainty, emphasise the absence of threat — matches every prior incursion of this war and continues to run against predictions of an automatic Article 5 cascade.

**Context.** The attack came two days after Zelensky met Trump and representatives of US defence companies in Washington, pressing for swifter and larger Patriot deliveries specifically to stop Russian ballistic missiles, and two days after the Senate advanced the **Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by 86-12** — authorising tariffs of up to 200% on the largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas, including China and India, and expanding sanctions on Russian financial institutions. No negotiation development was reported this cycle; talks remain frozen.
*Sources: Just Security, "Early Edition: July 30, 2026"; NPR/Associated Press, "Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 10 and a missile falls in Poland," July 30, 2026; The Philadelphia Inquirer/AP, "Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 10 and NATO scrambles jets after a missile falls in Poland," July 30, 2026; Daily Herald/AP and Press Democrat/AP, July 30, 2026; The Intercept, July 28, 2026 (interceptor depletion).*


### July 29 Update — Zelensky Gets the Oval Office With an Air-Only Ceasefire Proposal; the Kremlin Denies Such Talks Exist; the Senate Advances the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026" (July 28, 2026)
President Volodymyr Zelensky met Trump behind closed doors in the Oval Office on the morning of July 28, hours before Netanyahu, and wrote afterwards: "Good meeting with President Trump in the Oval Office. Thank you for all that we are doing together to protect the lives of Ukrainians and achieve peace." A White House official said the two discussed the peace process and that "now is the time to end the war." The Ukrainian ask was narrower than the comprehensive settlement that has repeatedly stalled over Russian demands that Kyiv withdraw from territory it still holds: Ukrainian and US officials had been working on a proposal for a ceasefire in the AIR war to put to Russian officials. **Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied that talks over an aerial ceasefire are under way at all**, and Moscow warned that intensified Ukrainian strikes inside Russia would prolong the war — leaving the proposal without a counterparty on the record, the same asymmetric-existence pattern now visible on the Iran track. On Capitol Hill the Senate took a procedural vote Tuesday night on sweeping Russian energy sanctions, setting up final passage later in the week and timed as a tribute to the bill's late author on the day of his funeral, with Zelensky visiting the Capitol. The bill is now the **"Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026"** — renamed for Graham and expanded at President Trump's request to add Iran sanctions. It carries more than 60 cosponsors and targets Russian officials, oligarchs and their family members, foreign persons, Russian banks and financial institutions and the Russian shadow fleet, plus stiff tariffs on China, India and other states to reduce their dependence on Russian oil and gas. On the ground, Ukraine's General Staff recorded **226 combat engagements on July 28**, with the **Pokrovsk sector again the hottest at 29 Russian assaults** and **27 assaults repelled in the Kostiantynivka sector** near Kostiantynivka, Illinivka and toward Stepanivka — following the Khortytsia group's July 27 confirmation, via Suspilne, of Russian advances in the area between Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka. ISW assesses that Russian forces may achieve tactical gains at Kostiantynivka this summer but are unlikely to achieve operational victories against the Donetsk "belt of fortresses," and lack the density for simultaneous offensives against both towns; occupied territory holds at roughly 20% with no confirmed net change. Separately, **Netanyahu and Zelensky spoke in person at Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral** — their first face-to-face encounter since September 2023, described as serious but cordial, with both smiling during the handshake; they explored arranging a formal meeting and did not. Ukraine's foreign minister told his Iranian counterpart to "end any support for Russia's war"; Iran's foreign minister demanded "restitution for losses" over Ukraine's July 25 Caspian strike on an Iranian vessel, in which Iran says one sailor was killed. Zelensky's standing manpower warning is unchanged: Russia is preparing to receive 30,000 more North Korean troops, with facilities readied in Voronezh oblast since June.
*Sources: Al Jazeera, "Ukraine's Zelenskyy hails 'good meeting' with Trump at White House," July 28, 2026; Channels Television; Kyiv Post; Reuters via WSAU/WHBL/KELO, "US Senate to vote on Russia sanctions bill in tribute to Graham," July 28, 2026; CNBC; ABC News; U.S. Senate Committee on Foreign Relations release, July 28, 2026; Ukrinform, "War update: 226 clashes on front line as Pokrovsk sector remains hottest combat zone," July 28, 2026; Institute for the Study of War; The Times of Israel liveblog, July 28, 2026.*


### July 11 Update — Talks Stay Stalled; US NATO Envoy Says Kyiv "Seized the Initiative"; Kherson-Direction Strikes (July 11, 2026)
Peace talks remained frozen. The US Permanent Representative to NATO said "Kyiv has seized the initiative, it's time for Moscow to negotiate," while Putin's demands stayed maximalist (recognition of occupied territory, Ukrainian neutrality, force curbs, sanctions relief) and Russia "touts war with NATO" amid battlefield losses. Front-line summaries noted Kherson-direction airstrikes and artillery on July 11; polling continued to show ~66% of Ukrainians favoring a negotiated end to the war as soon as possible. No US ground-deployment surge. (Pravda NATO, "Kyiv has seized the initiative"; Russia Matters, "Russia-Ukraine War Report Card"; Al Jazeera, "Russia touts war with NATO," July 1-11, 2026.)

### July 1 Update — Peace Talks On Hold but US/Ukraine/Europe "Appear Ready to Restart"; Kostiantynivka Gains Limited; Publics Shift Toward a Deal (July 1, 2026)

The July 1 war report card found **peace talks remain on hold** but the **US, Ukraine and Europe "appear ready to restart negotiations,"** while **Putin reiterated Russia's original war aims** — insisting Russia will negotiate **only on the basis of the 2022 Istanbul Protocols** and other conditions that amount to **demands for Ukrainian capitulation.** Public opinion shifted toward a settlement: **~60% of Russians support peace negotiations** and **~66% of Ukrainians believe the government should seek to end the war as soon as possible.** On the ground, **Kostiantynivka stays Russia's main Donbas effort** but Russian gains are **limited to small-group infiltration with no consolidated territorial control** — Ukraine's tactical situation is **deteriorating** and Ukrainian forces are **counterattacking,** even as the Russian MoD and Putin **"falsely frame" the city's seizure as imminent.** (Russia Matters, "The Russia-Ukraine War Report Card, July 1, 2026"; ISW/Critical Threats, June 23, 2026.)

- **Ukrainian drone strikes on June 12 sent plumes of smoke over St. Petersburg** as Putin participated in Russia's flagship economic forum.
- On **June 15, Putin reiterated that any negotiations must happen on Moscow's terms,** with his war aims unchanged; heavy fighting continued on the **Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors,** and **Russia still holds no operationally significant advance west of Pokrovsk** since December 2025. Ukraine retains roughly **80% of its territory (~20% occupied).**
- The next direct (Istanbul) round was still expected **June 20-30.** The theatre continues to stress US bandwidth but has triggered **no US ground-deployment surge.** *(Kyiv Independent; Critical Threats / ISW; Wikipedia "Timeline of the Russo-Ukrainian war," June 12-15, 2026.)*

- The first stage of the **1,000-for-1,000 POW exchange** proceeded; **Putin still refuses to meet Zelensky outside Moscow**; a second negotiating round is expected **~June 2**. *(Euromaidan Press; Wikipedia Black Sea Grain Initiative; Wikipedia Timeline of the Russo-Ukrainian war — May 18-19, 2026.)*

### Orthodox Easter Ceasefire — Expired With Massive Violations (April 11-13, 2026)
- **Putin declared a 32-hour ceasefire** from **16:00 (13:00 GMT) on April 11** until the end of the day on **April 12, 2026**, in connection with the Orthodox feast of Easter.
- **Zelenskyy confirmed** Ukraine will **"act accordingly"** — honoring the ceasefire. He stated that **"people need an Easter without threats and real progress toward peace."**
- Defense Minister **Belousov** and Chief of General Staff **Gerasimov** ordered to cease combat operations along **all fronts**, though troops must be prepared to thwart **"any possible provocations."**
- This is the **first mutually agreed pause since the 2025 Easter truce**, which collapsed with both sides accusing each other of breaking it.
- **However**: Even hours after the announcement, the governor of **Dnipropetrovsk region** reported that Russian artillery and aerial attacks had **killed 2 people** — raising doubts about compliance.
- **MASSIVE VIOLATIONS — BOTH SIDES**: Ukraine's **General Staff** recorded **2,299 Russian ceasefire violations** by 7:00 AM Sunday, including: **28 enemy assault actions**, **479 shellings**, **747 attack drone strikes**, and **1,045 FPV drone strikes**. Russia's **Defence Ministry** recorded **1,971 Ukrainian violations**, including drone strikes. Russia accused Ukraine of striking **Nova Kakhovka** (occupied Kherson). A **Ukrainian drone** hit a **gas station** in Russia's **Kursk region** — **2 adults and a 1-year-old child** injured (TASS).
- **Zelenskyy called for longer ceasefire** in his **Saturday evening address**, saying **"the ball is in Moscow's court."**
- The ceasefire **expired at midnight April 12-13**. Combat is presumed to have **resumed in full**.
- The pattern mirrors the **2025 Easter truce collapse**, which similarly devolved into mutual accusations.
- *Sources: Al Jazeera, PBS, Euronews, Spokesman-Review, Manila Times, NBC, CNN, Washington Times, RFE/RL, Moscow Times, TASS, The National*

### Dnipro Missile Strike and Crimea Attacks (April 14-15, 2026)
- A Russian missile struck a **highway in Dnipro** at approximately **11:30 AM local time** on April 14, killing **5 civilians** and wounding **24**. All victims were driving their own cars on the road.
- **21** of the wounded were hospitalized, **10 in serious condition**. A 40-year-old man later died in hospital, raising the death toll from 4 to 5.
- **April 15 was declared a day of mourning** in Dnipro for those killed.
- Separately, Ukraine launched a **massive overnight attack on occupied Crimea** — explosions heard in the areas of **Simferopol, Feodosia, and Kerch**.
- Russia's total estimated losses since February 2022 reached approximately **1,312,960 personnel** per Ukrainian figures.

### Ukraine-Germany €4 Billion Defense Deal (April 14, 2026)
- President **Zelenskyy** visited **Berlin** and announced a **€4 billion ($4.7 billion) defense package** with Germany.
- Under the **"Build with Ukraine"** initiative, Kyiv and Berlin will launch **joint production of mid-range AI-enabled strike drones**, with **5,000 drones** to be produced initially for the Ukrainian military.
- The German Defence Ministry agreed to fund contracts for **several hundred Patriot missiles** from the United States.
- Germany gains access to **Ukraine's cutting-edge drone expertise** in exchange for additional military support.
- The deal deepens the German-Ukrainian defense partnership, building on Germany's **€108 billion defense budget** and **€650 billion five-year commitment**.
- *Sources: AP, KyivPost, Al Jazeera, CNN, KSAT, CP24*

### Territory
- Russia occupies approximately **20% of Ukraine's territory** (~45,778 sq mi), including Crimea and parts of Donbas.
- Frontline movement is slow and contested. In Feb 10-March 10, 2026, Russia **lost** 57 sq mi of territory (vs. gains of 182 sq mi in the prior 4 weeks).
- Ukraine has **cleared 400 km² (150 sq mi)** since the beginning of counteroffensive operations. February 2026 became the first month since 2024 when Ukraine regained more territory than it lost.
- Russia is focused on the logistical hub of **Kostiantynivka** (entered December 2025), pushing toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk -- the last major Ukrainian-held cities in Donetsk.

### Ukraine Has NOT "Lost"
- The war continues as a grinding attritional conflict. Ukraine maintains significant territory and fighting capability.
- Ukraine has become a **drone superpower**, with its drone technology being noted in context of the Iran war.
- **RUSSIA'S DEADLIEST OVERNIGHT STRIKE OF 2026 (April 15-16)**: Russia launched **659 drones + 44 missiles** at **Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro** overnight — Ukraine's air force shot down **636 drones and 31 missiles**. **16 killed** (including a **12-year-old in Kyiv**) and **100+ wounded**. Breakdown: **Odesa 9 killed**, **Dnipro 3 killed**, **Kyiv 4 killed**. The salvo was the largest single overnight package since the start of the year and signals Russia is using the diplomatic window around the US-Iran ceasefire to surge strikes on Ukrainian cities. *(Euronews, NPR, ABC News, Al Jazeera, PBS, EMPR)*
- **UKRAINE STRUCK TUAPSE OIL REFINERY (April 16)**: Ukrainian forces hit Rosneft's **Tuapse Oil Refinery** in **Krasnodar Krai** — a top-10 Russian refinery — continuing the pattern of deep-strike targeting of Russian energy infrastructure as both leverage and as price-pressure on Russian war financing. *(EMPR, Kyiv Independent)*
- **Zelensky says frontline "best for Ukraine in 10 months"** (Apr 3) — **British intelligence concurs**. First time since mid-2025 that Ukraine's position assessed as improving. *(US News, Ukrinform)*

Russian daily losses (Apr 9): **1,040 personnel**, 1 tank, 2 APCs, **64 artillery systems**, 1 MLRS, **2,238 UAVs**, 229 vehicles. Russia deployed **10,100 kamikaze drones** + **250 guided aerial bombs** + **3,625 shellings** (107 MLRS) in single day. *(Ukrinform, EMPR)*

- Earlier: Combat engagements rose to 157/day on April 7 (up from 120 on Apr 6; 213-230 peak on Apr 2-3). Russian **FPV drone** struck **passenger bus** in Nikopol, killing **3 people** and injuring **16**; **11-year-old boy** killed in separate attack. *(Ukrinform, Kyiv Independent)*

Part of broader regional tour seeking air defense missiles in exchange for Ukrainian drone technology. *(Al-Monitor, Daily Sabah, SANA, AA, Asharq Al-Awsat)*

On March 30: Russia launched **9,355 kamikaze drones**, carried out **70 airstrikes** dropping **237 guided aerial bombs**, and conducted **3,912 shelling attacks**. *(EMPR Media, Ukrainian General Staff)*.

Oleksandr Komarenko** claimed Ukrainian forces restored control over **285.6 km²** in the Oleksandrivka direction and cleared **400 km²** since the beginning of counteroffensive operations — **February 2026 was the first month since 2024 when Ukraine regained more territory than it lost**. *(Wikipedia timeline)*

### Manpower
- Average Ukrainian soldier age: **~43 years old**.

- Citizens 60+ allowed to volunteer (no upper age limit).
- January 2026: Defense Minister estimated **200,000 soldiers AWOL** and **2 million men avoiding draft notices**.
- Since Feb 24, 2022: over **1 million Ukrainians conscripted**.

### Peace Negotiations
- **Late January-February 2026**: Three rounds of US-facilitated trilateral talks (Abu Dhabi, Geneva) -- first sustained direct negotiations since Turkey's 2022 efforts. No breakthrough.
- **December 2025**: US offered Ukraine a **15-year security guarantee**.
- **January 6, 2026**: Paris summit -- UK and France signed a "Declaration of Intent" to deploy troops to Ukraine to safeguard a peace deal. Germany said forces could join for ceasefire monitoring. Belgium offered naval/air support.
- **Russia rejects** any NATO troop deployment to Ukraine as part of a peace deal.
- Trump has ruled out deploying American forces to Ukraine.
- Key deadlock: territory. Russia demands control of all of Donbas and denial of NATO membership for Ukraine.
- **March 2026**: Trilateral talks on **"situational pause"** due to the Iran war. Abu Dhabi round (originally planned Mar 5-9) postponed indefinitely.
- **March 21-22**: **US-Ukraine bilateral talks** held in **Miami** — Witkoff and Kushner met Ukrainian delegation (Umerov, Budanov, Kyslytsia, Arakhamia). Witkoff called talks "constructive," focused on "narrowing and resolving remaining items." **Russia was NOT present** — a shift from the trilateral format. Last trilateral meeting was Geneva Feb 17-18.
- **Trump and Zelensky** agreed on **90-95% of a peace proposal** but fundamental gaps remain; analysts say war unlikely to end in 2026. *(Russia Matters, Apr 1)*
- A **record 67% of Russians** now support peace negotiations (Euronews, Mar 2026).
- The Iran war has diverted US attention and driven energy prices up; **Urals crude at $123.45/bbl** (Apr 3) — Russian oil commanding premium, indirectly funding war effort.

## 8. US Military Industrial Capacity

### August 23 Update — A Recipient State Prices the Depletion Too (August 21, 2026)

**The clearest measure of the American munitions problem is now what an allied government is doing about it.** ISW assessed on **August 21** that Ukrainian forces are domestically developing means to target Russian ballistic launchers and jet-powered drones **specifically in order to circumvent the need for foreign materiel assistance amid global air-defence interceptor shortages**. Where the **$22.9 billion, seven-year Raytheon Tomahawk contract** of **August 17** prices the depletion from the supplier's side — lifting annual production above **1,000 missiles** after roughly a third of the stockpile was expended — this prices it from the recipient's side. A state fighting for its existence has concluded it should design around the American pipeline rather than queue for it.

**The stock position is unchanged.** CSIS puts remaining US inventories below **827 Patriot** and **278 THAAD** interceptors, more than **60% expended**, with **three-plus years** required to rebuild. CENTCOM's answer in theatre remains standoff and unmanned: **Task Force Falcon Strike**, announced **August 13**, is a multi-domain, multinational one-way attack drone force employing unmanned systems from above, on and below the sea.

*Sources: Institute for the Study of War, August 21, 2026; Defense News, "US awards Raytheon $22.9 billion deal to boost Tomahawk output," August 17, 2026; CSIS interceptor inventory assessment, August 2026; CENTCOM public release, August 13, 2026.*

### August 22 Update — A $22.9 Billion Tomahawk Contract Prices the Depletion (August 17, 2026)

**The Navy bought seven years of production.** On **August 17** the US Navy awarded **Raytheon**, an RTX business, a **$22.9 billion, seven-year contract** to accelerate **Tomahawk** production to **more than 1,000 missiles a year**, funding workforce expansion, faster throughput and supply-chain stabilisation. The contract quantifies the war's consumption: by August 2026 roughly **one-third of the American Tomahawk stockpile** was depleted, with **more than 1,000 expended** since Operation Epic Fury began and **over 850 in the first four weeks**.

**It sits alongside the interceptor picture.** CSIS assesses fewer than **827 Patriot** interceptors remain against roughly **2,200** pre-war and fewer than **278 THAAD** against **452** — more than **60% of both expended** — with production at **183 THAAD a year**, roughly **three and a half years** from contract signature to delivery, and **three or more years** to pre-war levels against **$18.2 billion** allocated within a **$67 billion** FY2026 emergency request. Gen. **Dan Caine** was reported in late July to have warned privately about the shortages, cited as a restraint on broader strikes. CSIS's stated strategic concern is the ability to respond to another high-intensity contingency before inventories recover.

**The capability the theatre added instead was cheap and expendable.** On **August 13** CENTCOM announced **Task Force Falcon Strike**, the first multi-domain, multinational **one-way attack drone** task force, employing unmanned systems from above, on and below the sea with regional partners, following **Task Force Scorpion Strike** established nine months earlier — which achieved the first launch of an aerial attack drone from a US Navy warship in December and employed unmanned systems during Operation Epic Fury and in July strikes on Iranian port facilities.

*Sources: Defense News, RTX, The Hill, Fox News and Manufacturing Dive, August 17, 2026; CENTCOM public release and DefenseScoop, August 13, 2026; CSIS, 2026; CNN Politics, July 29, 2026; Military Times, July 30, 2026.*


### Shipbuilding: The 232:1 Claim Is Real
- Per Office of Naval Intelligence briefings (late 2025): China's shipbuilding capacity is **232 times** that of the United States.
- Chinese shipyards: ~23,250,000 tons capacity. US shipyards: <100,000 tons.
- In 2024: China built **1,000+ commercial vessels**; the US built **8**.
- China manufactures **80% of ship-to-shore cranes** and **96% of shipping containers** used in the US (domestic production: zero).
- US relies on a handful of private contractors (General Dynamics Electric Boat, Huntington Ingalls), both operating at **>115% of rated theoretical capacity**.
- The US has lost **300+ large-scale shipyard facilities** since the Cold War peak.
- PLAN projected to reach **395 ships**; US Navy projected to shrink to **283 ships** by 2027.

### Ammunition Production
- **155mm shell production**: surged from 14,000/month (early 2022) to **40,000/month** (as of mid-2025).
- **Target**: 100,000/month, now expected by mid-2026 (originally targeted for October 2025).
- New facility in Camden, Arkansas (General Dynamics) will produce 50,000/month when fully operational.
- $5.5 billion appropriated over 3 years for production expansion.

## 9. Saudi Arabia-Iran Relations

### September 4 Update — The Human Cost of the Sidr Attack Is Counted in Manila, and the Kingdom's Hormuz Bypass Is Now Itself a War-Risk Zone (September 3, 2026)

**The Sidr's dead were named by their own government.** The Philippine **Department of Migrant Workers** confirmed that **two Filipino seafarers** were killed aboard the Saudi-flagged crude tanker **Sidr**, operated by the Saudi national shipping company **Bahri** and struck by unidentified projectiles late on **August 31** while approaching the Strait. **Sixteen Filipinos** were aboard; the fire was contained by the crew; the **remains have been taken to Oman** and the **fourteen survivors** are being prepared for repatriation. The dead were from **Cabuyao, Laguna** and **Daanbantayan, Cebu**. President **Ferdinand Marcos Jr.** ordered immediate assistance for the families. **Cumulatively since February 28: 31 vessels carrying 421 Filipino seafarers have been attacked in Strait of Hormuz incidents — 406 unharmed, 10 injured and since recovered, 3 killed and 1 still missing.** The **UAE condemned** the attack on the Saudi tanker, and President **Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed** spoke with President Trump about regional developments.

**The kingdom's workaround is now inside a war-risk zone of its own.** Saudi Arabia is moving **1.9 million barrels per day** through the **Egyptian pipeline** to the Mediterranean rather than through Hormuz, adding weeks and cost to delivery — and marine underwriters have extended the war-risk area **800 kilometres further up Saudi Arabia's west coast** into the Red Sea, with the **Houthis targeting the Port of Yanbu** and Saudi-linked commercial tankers. **Yanbu is the Mediterranean-facing end of the bypass.**

**Sources:** Philippine Department of Migrant Workers via Philippine News Agency, Philstar and Manila Bulletin, September 3, 2026; The Filipino Times, September 2-3, 2026; gCaptain, “War Risk Claims Top $2 Billion as Shipping Attacks Spread Beyond Hormuz,” September 3, 2026; *The National* live blog, September 3, 2026.

### August 25 Update — Riyadh Declines to Endorse the Sanctions It Is Building Around, and Takes Fire at Sea the Same Day (August 24-25, 2026)

**The Gulf states that have invested billions in Hormuz-bypass pipelines have not commented publicly on Operation Economic Outcast.** That silence sits directly against the previous cycle's record, in which Crown Prince **Mohammed bin Salman** met President **Macron** in Paris on **August 24** at the **Franco-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council** with Hormuz alternatives as the headline file — increased trade through **Omani ports outside the Gulf**, **expanded and possibly doubled pipeline capacity**, and **new regional rail links** — alongside a standing **France-Saudi joint task force on energy and logistics** meeting at ministerial level. Riyadh and Paris separately urged a **negotiated solution** and a **resumption of Iranian cooperation with the IAEA**. A government that is building a workaround and declining to endorse the sanctions that make the workaround strategically central is hedging, and the hedge is recorded.

**The cost of that position arrived the same day.** Yemen's **Houthis** struck the Saudi VLCC **Amzan**, operated by the national shipping company **Bahri**, about **63 nautical miles west of Yanbu** in the Red Sea with **ballistic missiles and drones** on **August 24**. A fire broke out on the main deck and nearby vessels fled the target area; **all crew are safe** and no environmental impact was reported. Houthi military spokesman **Yahya Saree** described the strike as part of a **"siege for siege"** operation targeting the Saudis — an explicit linkage between the American blockade of Iran and attacks on Saudi shipping.

**And Tehran aimed its deterrent at the hosts rather than at the issuer.** Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman **Esmail Baghaei** said Iran has the **right to target any location used to launch attacks against it**, warning countries against **providing territory or facilities** to the United States. With SNSC Secretary **Mohsen Rezaei** having said on August 23 that any state joining the sanctions is **"considered an enemy"** and that not a drop of oil would leave the Gulf — including by the alternative routes — the Iranian threat now runs against the American basing structure inside Gulf states.

**The UAE is the only Gulf state on the first designation list, and the only one to have moved further.** Abu Dhabi suspended **all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions** with Iran on **August 19**, and is reported to be preparing **phased** reductions in trade and financial engagement in parallel with the American measures, beginning with restrictions on cargo and trade flows. Emirati air defences remain on high alert. Gulf civil aviation remains degraded: Emirates cancelled Dubai-Bahrain services **EK835** and **EK837**; **flydubai** cancelled **FZ8504** to Bahrain; Air Arabia carried cancellations across UAE-Kuwait-Bahrain routes.

*Sources: Al Jazeera, "US launches 'Operation Economic Outcast' to cut Iran's economic lifeline," August 24, 2026; Al Jazeera, "Yemen's Houthis report attack on Saudi oil tanker in Red Sea," August 24, 2026; gCaptain, "Houthis Escalate Saudi Shipping Campaign With VLCC Strike," August 24, 2026; Marine Log, "Saudi tanker Amzan struck by Houthi missile," August 24, 2026; Gulf News, "US-Iran standoff: What UAE residents need to know today (Aug. 24, 2026)"; Iran International live blog, entries of August 24, 2026; Solace Global, "Gulf States: Situation & Travel Update, 21 August 2026."*

### August 24 Update — Riyadh Builds the Bypass in Paris and Tehran Puts the Bypass on Its Target List (August 21-24, 2026)

**Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is in France for his first visit since 2023, and the headline file is routing around the Strait.** He meets President **Emmanuel Macron** on **August 24** at the **Franco-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council**, with **expanding oil pipelines as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz** as the principal item. French presidency officials described the proposals as **increasing trade through Omani ports located outside the Persian Gulf**, **expanding and potentially doubling pipeline capacity** in Saudi Arabia and other countries, and **developing new rail links**. The two governments have established a **joint task force on energy and logistics connections between the Middle East and Europe**, which meets at **ministerial level on the same day**, and agreements covering **transport, energy, technology and health** were prepared alongside. This is the first occasion in the war on which Hormuz substitution has been the headline agenda of a bilateral summit between a Gulf producer and a European power rather than a line in an analyst's note.

**Iran named the same infrastructure as a target the day before.** On **August 23** SNSC Secretary **Mohsen Rezaei** said Iran would **target the oil-shipping routes out of the Persian Gulf that serve as alternatives to the Strait** if regional states join what he called the economic war, restating that any participating country is **"considered an enemy"** whose interests would be harmed, and warning via IRNA that Tehran **"will not allow a single drop of oil to leave the Persian Gulf"** if pressure escalates. The logic is legible: if the Gulf can route around the chokepoint, the chokepoint stops being leverage, and the only way to preserve the leverage is to make the alternatives unsafe as well.

**The littoral is still not moving as a bloc.** The **UAE's** indefinite suspension of all trade, commercial exchange and financial transactions with Iran, announced on **August 19** after its air defences detected two Iranian ballistic missiles, removes a partner that supplied **more than 30% of Iranian imports (~$21bn)** and took **nearly 13% of Iranian exports (~$7bn)**; Tehran denies the launches and warns of **"false flag"** operations. **Iraq** holds a transit exemption granted by Tehran on August 22. **Oman** is negotiating both the transit arrangement and the fee regime. **Saudi Arabia** is in Paris designing the bypass. **Egypt**, from outside the Gulf, used its **August 22** foreign-ministers' call with Tehran to stress freedom of navigation and Gulf security. Four postures, one coastline. **ADNOC** counts **16 vessels attacked since February 28**, one crew member killed and 20 injured; IMF April-vintage projections are **−14.7% for Qatar** and **−1.4% for Saudi Arabia** in 2026, with Gulf energy-facility repairs estimated at about **$58bn**. The **August 7 Mecca Joint Defence Agreement** binding Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan remains in force.

*Sources: The National, "France's Macron and Saudi Crown Prince to discuss oil pipelines to by-pass Strait of Hormuz," August 23, 2026, and "Saudi Crown Prince visits France to sign deals and discuss Strait of Hormuz," August 22, 2026; Bloomberg, "Macron and MBS to Focus on Hormuz, Deals in Paris Talks," August 21, 2026; Energy Connects, August 2026; Gulf News, August 2026; The Washington Post/AP, August 22-23, 2026; Fortune, "UAE halts all trade with Iran after new missile fire in Gulf," August 19, 2026; Egypt Today, August 23, 2026.*

### August 23 Update — The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement Enters This Record, and Riyadh Goes to Paris to Route Around the Strait (August 7-24, 2026)

**The largest Gulf security development of the month had not been recorded in this briefing, and is entered here.** On **August 7, 2026** Saudi Crown Prince **Mohammed bin Salman**, Turkish President **Recep Tayyip Erdogan** and Pakistani Prime Minister **Shehbaz Sharif** signed the **Mecca Joint Defence Agreement**, declaring in a joint statement that **an armed attack on any one of the three would be regarded as an attack on all three**. Sharif had arrived in Jeddah on **August 6** and performed the Umrah in Mecca the following day while Erdogan met the Crown Prince. Turkish Foreign Minister **Hakan Fidan** said the pact would function similarly to NATO, with a **ministers' committee, political and military committees and a permanent secretariat** overseeing implementation of decisions. Pakistan's foreign ministry described it as guided by **"longstanding historical ties"** and **"Islamic solidarity"** and as **"purely defensive"** and open to others; a Turkish official told Reuters it is **"defensive in nature and not directed at any specific actor."** The combination is deliberate: Turkey's NATO-standard forces and growing defence industry, Saudi financial weight, and Pakistan's position as the Muslim world's only nuclear-armed state.

**Washington welcomed it.** On **August 16-17** President Trump said: **"Very happy to see that Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have recently, and finally, signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement,"** calling it a **"big, bold, and important first step"** and saying he did not mind the Middle East finding ways to defend itself.

**The analytical reading split immediately and has not converged.** The **Council on Foreign Relations** published *The U.S.-Led Middle East Order Is Over. The Mecca Agreement Proves It.*; the **Middle East Council on Global Affairs** asked *What Is the Mecca Joint Defense Pact — and What It Is Not?*; the **Arab Center** called it **"diversification without substitution"**; **OSW** called it **"a loose alliance."** On **August 22** Iran's SNSC secretary **Mohsen Rezaei** said the agreement signalled that **"the US was leaving the region."** This briefing records the fact and logs the interpretive dispute as an open question rather than resolving it. The relevance to the ground-invasion tracker is direct: these are the three states whose territory, airspace, basing and overflight a US ground campaign against Iran would most require.

**And Riyadh took the bypass problem to Paris.** The Crown Prince travelled to France with a large ministerial delegation for a **Franco-Saudi Strategic Partnership Council** meeting with President **Emmanuel Macron** on **Monday August 24** — his first visit to France since 2023. The published agenda is explicitly about routing around the chokepoint: **diversifying transport routes for energy and logistics, alternative maritime routes, pipeline projects and regional rail links** between the Middle East and Europe, alongside agreements on technology, transport, energy and health. The political agenda covers **Saudi-Iranian relations, the Strait, Lebanon, Syria and the Palestinian question**.

**Tehran named the neighbours as the target of its counter-sanctions retaliation.** On **August 22** Rezaei said **"any country participating in the imposition of economic restrictions against us is considered an enemy,"** that states which will not **"distance themselves"** from Washington will have their interests **"harmed,"** and that Iran could disrupt oil shipments through the **Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz** in response. The threat converts Monday's sanctions package from a US-Iran matter into a test of every Gulf capital's willingness to comply.

**The macroeconomic ledger.** The IMF's April projections for 2026 put **Qatar at −14.7%, Kuwait at −4.2%, Bahrain at −3.8%, the UAE at −1.9%, Saudi Arabia at −1.4% and Oman at −0.05%**. The IEA and Rystad estimate that damage to **more than 80 energy facilities** across the Arab Gulf states may cost **$58 billion** to repair. Qatar is tightening public spending after losing roughly **17% of LNG export capacity** and an estimated **$20 billion** in annual revenue, recording a first-quarter deficit of **QR10.3 billion ($2.83 billion)** — more than **twenty times** the year-earlier shortfall — on revenues down **23.5%** year on year. In Bahrain the closure has throttled oil and aluminium exports supplying around **two-thirds of government revenue** and about **a quarter of GDP**.

**And the littoral is not moving as a bloc.** The UAE suspended all trade with Iran on **August 19**; Iran granted Iraq a tanker exemption on **August 22**; Oman finalised preferential trade terms with Tehran pending parliamentary approval; Saudi Arabia is in Paris. **ADNOC** states that **16 of its vessels have been attacked since February 28**, with **one crew member killed and 20 injured**.

### August 22 Update — Riyadh Presses for Restraint and Is Blockaded From the South (August 1-20, 2026)

**Saudi Arabia was among the states that pressed Washington to stand down.** **Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman** spoke with Trump on Saturday **August 1**, expressing concern over the reported strike plans against Iranian energy and civil infrastructure; Qatar, the UAE, Turkey and Pakistan also pressed both sides to de-escalate. Trump announced the cancellation later that day, saying Iran and **"other Middle Eastern countries"** had asked him to hold off.

**The kingdom's exposure has moved to the Red Sea.** Houthi forces declared a **naval blockade of Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea on July 20**, breaking a years-long civil-war truce and calling it retaliation for a Saudi **"siege"** of Yemen, which Riyadh denies. On **August 11-12** a Houthi missile attack on the ***Tihamah*** in the **Bab al-Mandeb** killed six — the first Houthi-attributed shipping deaths since the war began — with Houthi-aligned media saying the vessel carried Saudi military equipment. On **August 20** a Houthi spokesman claimed drone attacks on **Najran airport** and an **Aramco facility**.

**Economically, Riyadh remains among the better-insulated Gulf states**, expected to keep growing more slowly, protected by a relatively large non-oil sector and by pipelines that bypass the Strait — against a regional picture in which the World Bank has cut 2026 GCC growth from **4.4% to 1.3%** and **Kuwait and Qatar are expected to contract**.

*Sources: Al Jazeera and NPR, August 2, 2026; Al Jazeera and UPI, August 11-12, 2026; Reuters via Just Security Early Edition, August 21, 2026; AGBI, August 2026; The Conversation, 2026.*


### August 1 Update — Riyadh Convenes 43 Nations for a Maritime Defence Coalition It Would Headquarter, and Carries a De-escalation Message to the White House Days After Flying Strikes (July 29-31, 2026)

**The kingdom becomes a security provider rather than a consumer.** Saudi Arabia's Defence Ministry convened **military representatives of 43 countries in Riyadh on Thursday, July 30**, to stand up a multinational **maritime defence coalition**. The stated objectives are to enhance maritime security, protect international maritime corridors, safeguard freedom of navigation, secure trade routes and energy supply lines, and counter threats targeting maritime navigation and global trade, with a geographic focus on the **Bab al-Mandeb strait, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden**. Proposed activities are joint maritime operations, intelligence sharing, training programmes and joint exercises, and the **headquarters would sit in the kingdom**. Thirteen states issued a joint statement of support: **Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Yemen, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Sudan, Djibouti and Somalia**.

**The contrast with the American effort is the point.** Two days earlier POLITICO reported that Secretary of Defense Hegseth was urging **Britain and France** to help lead the American naval coalition for the Strait of Hormuz, with UK Defence Minister Wes Streeting assisting, and that European allies were **refusing** until they saw an enduring ceasefire in the Iran war, with four British officials and one US official saying no movement was expected soon. A US-led escort coalition for the Gulf could not obtain a European co-lead; a Saudi-led coalition for the Red Sea drew 43 delegations within a week of the Houthi blockade taking hold.

**The driver is Riyadh's own export geography.** The Houthis declared a maritime blockade of the kingdom on **July 20**, and **Yanbu** — the outlet of the East-West Pipeline and Saudi Arabia's only functioning crude-export route since the Strait of Hormuz closed — handled roughly **92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June 2026**. Every cargo loading there must transit the Bab al-Mandeb, inside the declared blockade zone.

**The posture remains dual.** Saudi jets flew joint precision strikes with CENTCOM against Iran-aligned militia targets in Iraq on July 28 — Riyadh's first claimed strikes inside Iraq of the war, invoked under Article 51 — and on July 29 Defence Minister **Prince Khalid bin Salman** carried a de-escalation message to President Trump and Vice President Vance, conveying that the Kingdom had struck in self-defence but regarded diplomacy as "a more fruitful path" and that Netanyahu was the party pushing escalation, while lobbying for F-35s. On July 31 Baghdad stated it had had **no prior knowledge** of the joint strikes, contradicting Trump's account that they were coordinated with Iraq, and suspended Prime Minister al-Zaidi's planned visit to Saudi Arabia.

*Sources: The National, "Saudi Arabia proposes 43-nation 'maritime defence coalition' in Red Sea," July 30, 2026; Al Jazeera, "Saudi Arabia announces maritime defence alliance to secure vital waterways" and "Why is Saudi Arabia forming a coalition to protect the Red Sea?", July 30, 2026; Bloomberg, July 30, 2026; The Hill, July 30, 2026; MarineLink, July 30, 2026; Dawn, July 31, 2026; POLITICO, July 28-29, 2026; Middle East Monitor, "Iraq denies Trump's claim of prior knowledge of US-Saudi strikes," July 31, 2026.*


### The China-Brokered Rapprochement Has Held
- The March 2023 Beijing-brokered restoration of Saudi-Iran diplomatic relations has survived multiple crises.
- **December 9, 2025**: Third meeting of the China-Iran-Saudi Arabia Trilateral Joint Committee held in Tehran.
- Practical cooperation: 85,000+ Iranian pilgrims performed Hajj in 2025; 210,000+ performed Umrah. Increased quotas and direct flights agreed for 2026.
- **Critical test passed**: Saudi Arabia **refused** to allow its territory or airspace to be used for the June 2025 US-Israeli strikes on Iran, and **publicly condemned** Israeli "aggressions against the brotherly Islamic Republic of Iran."
- The rapprochement remains intact even amid the 2026 Iran war, though Pakistan faces pressure to pick sides.

## 10. Houthi/Red Sea Situation

### September 4 Update — Underwriters Move the War-Risk Boundary 800 km Up the Saudi West Coast as the Houthis Target Yanbu (September 3, 2026)

**The insurance market has redrawn the map.** War-risk areas have been **extended 800 kilometres further up Saudi Arabia's west coast**, with the **Houthis targeting the Port of Yanbu** and Saudi-linked commercial tankers in the Red Sea. This matters structurally rather than only tactically: **Yanbu is where the Hormuz bypass surfaces on the Mediterranean side**, and Saudi Arabia is routing **1.9 million barrels per day** through the Egyptian pipeline to reach it.

**The claims total behind the repricing.** **David Osler** of *Lloyd's List* puts war-risk claims at **around $2 billion** across **more than 70 cases**, against **more than 72 attacks on ships since March** — the **second-largest marine underwriting loss in over a decade**, behind only the 2024 Baltimore bridge collapse — with market-wide claims for the war, terror and political violence segment projected at **$2-3 billion** against an estimated **annual global premium volume of $1.5-2 billion** for the entire segment.

**Sources:** gCaptain, “War Risk Claims Top $2 Billion as Shipping Attacks Spread Beyond Hormuz,” September 3, 2026; AGBI, “War insurance adds $8 to a barrel of oil,” September 3, 2026; Insurance Business, “Hormuz war risk claims could exceed $3 billion as US-Iran fighting resumes,” September 2026.

### August 25 Update — A VLCC Strike Off Yanbu, Declared as "Siege for Siege" (August 24, 2026)

**The Houthi campaign against Saudi shipping escalated to a very large crude carrier.** On **August 24** the Houthis targeted the Saudi oil tanker **Amzan**, operated by the Saudi national shipping company **Bahri**, approximately **63 nautical miles west of Yanbu** in the Red Sea, using **ballistic missiles and drones**. UKMTO reported the vessel struck by an unknown projectile with a **fire on the main deck**; reporting describes the strike as accurate and direct, with a number of other ships in the target area fleeing. **All crew are safe and accounted for** and **no environmental impact** has been reported. Bahri confirmed the *Amzan* was involved in a hostile incident in regional waters.

**The framing is the significant part.** Houthi military spokesman **Yahya Saree** said the attacks were carried out with ballistic missiles and drones **"as part of the implementation of the 'siege for siege' operation targeting the Saudis."** That is an explicit doctrinal linkage between the **US naval blockade of Iran** and attacks on **Saudi-flagged and Saudi-operated shipping** — a proxy front reopening in response to an economic instrument rather than to a strike. Bab el-Mandeb transit was reported slightly up on the period despite the attack.

**This is the second reported Houthi strike on a Saudi tanker in under a month,** following a claimed missile attack on a Saudi oil tanker on **July 28, 2026**.

*Sources: Al Jazeera, "Yemen's Houthis report attack on Saudi oil tanker in Red Sea," August 24, 2026; OilPrice.com, "Houthis Target Saudi Oil Tanker in Red Sea Missile and Drone Attack," August 24, 2026; gCaptain, "Houthis Escalate Saudi Shipping Campaign With VLCC Strike," August 24, 2026; Marine Log, "Saudi tanker Amzan struck by Houthi missile," August 24, 2026; Euronews, "Houthis claim strike on Saudi tanker in latest Red Sea escalation," August 24, 2026; Deccan Herald/Marine Link via UKMTO, August 24, 2026; ZeroHedge, "Houthis Attack Saudi Oil Tanker In Red Sea, As Bab el-Mandeb Transit Is Up Slightly," August 2026; Al Jazeera, "Yemen's Houthis claim missile attack on Saudi Arabia oil tanker," July 28, 2026.*

### August 23 Update — Najran Airport and the Aramco Facilities; Marib Fighting; a Reported Saudi Ground Option (August 18-22, 2026)

**The Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia widened to an air-defence node.** On **August 20** the Houthis claimed two drone attacks, striking what they called a **"sensitive target" at Najran airport** — described in reporting as hosting **Patriot and other air-defence systems** — and an **Aramco facility** in southern Saudi Arabia. The claim follows a claimed strike on the **Jazan refinery on August 18**, described by the group as part of a sustained and expanding campaign against Saudi energy infrastructure and maritime assets, and the **Jizan refinery fire of August 9** in which a linked attack on a Yemeni port killed seven. The group has framed the strikes as retaliation for Saudi drone attacks on Yemen's **Saada** and **Hajjah** provinces.

**Ground fighting inside Yemen intensified.** On **August 22** Yemeni government forces engaged Iran-aligned Houthi positions **northwest and south of Marib**.

**And a ground option is being reported — Saudi, not American, and directed at Yemen rather than Iran.** Reporting indicates Saudi Arabia is preparing for a possible major escalation in Yemen that could involve a **ground offensive**, following its reignition of the war last month with strikes on Sanaa international airport to prevent a flight from Iran landing. This briefing logs the development because a Saudi ground commitment in Yemen would consume coalition manpower any US Iranian option would draw on — but it points away from, not toward, the predicted American ground event.

**The maritime picture in the south is unchanged from the previous cycle.** The **Tihamah** deaths of **August 11-12** in the Bab al-Mandeb remain the war's first Houthi-attributed shipping fatalities, and the hijacking of the sanctioned Iranian shadow-fleet tanker **SIBU 1** on **August 20** stands within the worst year for Somali piracy in a decade.

*Sources: Shafaq News, "Houthis claim drone strikes on Najran airport, Aramco facility," August 20, 2026; Al-Monitor, "Houthis claim new strikes on Saudi Arabia after IRGC warning: What to know," August 2026; Al Jazeera, "Houthi attacks kill seven in Yemen, refinery targeted in Saudi Arabia," August 9, 2026; Antiwar.com, "Ansar Allah Launches More Attacks on Oil Sites in Saudi Arabia, Saudi-Backed Forces in Yemen," August 13, 2026; Iran International live blog, August 22, 2026; Naked Capitalism, August 2026.*

### August 22 Update — The First Houthi-Attributed Shipping Deaths of the War, and a Decade High in Somali Piracy (August 11-20, 2026)

**Six killed aboard the *Tihamah*.** On **August 11-12** a Houthi missile attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo ship ***Tihamah*** in the **Bab al-Mandeb Strait** killed six: **one Indonesian and three Pakistani crew members** after a fire broke out aboard, and **two members of the Yemeni armed forces** killed during a rescue mission when a second missile was launched at the ship. It was the **first reported fatality from attacks on Red Sea shipping in more than a year** and the first shipping deaths linked to the Houthis since the war began on February 28. A Houthi-aligned outlet said the group's forces had targeted a ship carrying **Saudi military equipment**; Yemen's Transport Ministry said the vessel was carrying **food**. The group has not addressed the casualty figures.

**The blockade of Saudi Arabia stands.** The Iran-aligned group declared a **naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea on July 20**, breaking a years-long civil-war truce and calling it retaliation for a Saudi **"siege"** of Yemen, an allegation Riyadh denies. On **August 5** the Houthis claimed an attack on a Saudi oil tanker; on **August 17** they claimed the **"complete burning"** of a Saudi military vessel; and on **August 20** a military spokesman claimed drone attacks on **Najran airport** and an **Aramco facility**.

**Piracy has filled the enforcement vacuum.** On **August 20** Somali pirates hijacked the Eritrean-flagged tanker **SIBU 1** — sanctioned by the US Treasury in December as part of Iran's shadow fleet — **136 nautical miles east of Al Mukalla, Yemen**, after it broadcast a distress call on VHF 16. It was the **second hijacking in four days**. Danish Shipping reports **13 piracy incidents off Somalia in the first seven months of 2026**, against five in all of 2025 and eight the year before — the highest in a decade. Analysts attribute the surge to Houthi attacks pushing shipping closer to the Somali coast, to the value of energy cargoes at current prices, and to enforcement resources drawn off by the Iran war.

*Sources: Al Jazeera, "Six killed in Houthi attack on Bab al-Mandeb ship," August 12, 2026; UPI, August 11, 2026; PBS NewsHour; CNBC, August 12 and 20, 2026; CBS News live updates, August 17-18, 2026; gCaptain; Hiiraan Online; The New York Times and Reuters via Just Security Early Edition, August 21, 2026.*


### August 1 Update — Bab el-Mandeb Crossings Recover to 39 as a 43-Nation Coalition Forms Against the Houthi Blockade (July 29-31, 2026)

S&P Global recorded **Bab el-Mandeb crossings rising to 39** in the same reporting cycle in which Hormuz transits hit a two-week high, with very large crude carriers increasingly gathering at Egypt's **Sidi Kerir** terminal, complicating voyage logistics for cargoes routed away from the Gulf. The recovery is partial and takes place inside a declared blockade: the Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia on **July 20**, accusing Saudi leaders of imposing "an unjust and oppressive siege" on Yemen for nearly twelve years, and have since claimed missile attacks on the Saudi tankers **Encelia**, **Layla** and **NCC Ghazal**.

The Saudi response is institutional. On **July 30** Riyadh convened military representatives of **43 countries** to form a maritime defence coalition headquartered in the kingdom and covering the Bab al-Mandeb, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, with thirteen states — including **Yemen**, **Egypt**, **Djibouti**, **Somalia** and **Sudan**, the littoral states of the corridor itself — publicly backing it. The strategic exposure is unchanged: **Yanbu** handled roughly **92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June 2026**, and every cargo loading there must pass through the blockade zone.

*Sources: S&P Global via webindia123, "Hormuz vessel transits hit two-week high as LNG tanker traffic resumes," July 31, 2026; The National; Al Jazeera; Bloomberg; The Hill; MarineLink, July 30, 2026; TechTimes, July 25, 2026.*


### July 29 Update — The Houthis Claim the Saudi State-Owned Tanker NCC Ghazal; Bab el-Mandeb Traffic at Its Lowest Monthly Level (July 23-28, 2026)
The Houthis claimed responsibility for the missile attack on the **NCC Ghazal**, a 50,000 dwt Saudi-flagged, state-owned product tanker built in 2014, which was struck by anti-ship missiles, turned around and returned to port; she dropped off AIS tracking on July 23 after last being seen at the Saudi oil port of Yanbu. Houthi military spokesman **Yahya Saree** said the group "carried out a military operation against the Saudi oil tanker NCC Ghazal, due to violation of the maritime embargo imposed on the Saudi enemy and ignoring warning calls." The strike is the latest in a campaign against Saudi energy shipping and infrastructure that has run alongside the July 25 attacks on Aramco installations at **Jizan** (400,000 bpd) and **Yanbu**, the East-West Pipeline outlet that handled roughly 92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports in June with Hormuz shut. **Bab el-Mandeb transits fell to eleven vessels on July 26**, the lowest monthly level recorded, and Riyadh has been shifting export routing toward Suez. Saudi air defences separately continued intercepting Iraq-launched drones aimed at petroleum facilities, attributed to Iran-backed militias. The Kingdom remains interdicted on both flanks, and the Red Sea front is unaffected by the US-Iran strike pause.
*Sources: The Maritime Executive, "Saudi Tanker Hit by Houthi Missiles in the Red Sea"; ABC News live blog, July 28, 2026; The National, "Saudi Arabia shifts to Suez as Houthis drive Bab Al Mandeb oil exports to near zero," July 26, 2026; Al Jazeera; The Washington Times, July 23-28, 2026.*


### Operation Prosperity Guardian (December 2023 - Ongoing)
- US-led multinational coalition formed to counter Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping.
- Achieved **limited deterrent effect**. Houthis retained capability and intent.

### Operation Rough Rider (March 15, 2025+)
- Trump escalated significantly: **1,000+ airstrikes** on Houthi targets across seven Yemeni provinces.
- First day: dozens of strikes hit targets, killing 53 people.
- Administration officials admitted to the NYT that **airstrikes were not achieving their objectives** and the US **failed to achieve air superiority** against the Houthis.

### Ceasefire
- **May 6, 2025**: Trump announced cessation of US strikes following a bilateral US-Houthi ceasefire.
- Houthis halted attacks on international shipping and Israel after the **Gaza peace plan went into effect October 10, 2025**.

### Current Status — Houthis Enter the War (March 28, 2026)
- **February 28, 2026**: Following the 2026 Iran war, Houthis threatened to escalate and resume Red Sea attacks.
- For nearly four weeks, Houthis remained on the sidelines — analysts cited weapons stockpile running low, strategic patience, Tehran coordination, prior deal with Washington.
- **March 28, 2026**: Houthis **broke their pause** and fired ballistic missiles at Israel — their **first strikes since the conflict began**. Targeted "sensitive Israeli military sites" in southern Israel; both intercepted. Houthi spokesperson Saree vowed continued strikes.
- A second missile was launched hours after the first. **Washington Post** warned of **renewed Red Sea shipping disruption** fears.
- The entry of the Houthis adds a **new front** to the conflict and could compound the Hormuz crisis if Red Sea attacks resume.
- **March 29**: Houthis weigh **closing the Bab al-Mandeb Strait**. Deputy information minister **Mohammed Mansour** stated: **"closing the Bab al-Mandeb strait is among our options."** Any closure would be **selective** — targeting ships linked to hostile nations (similar to Iran's Hormuz model).
- A Bab al-Mandeb closure combined with Hormuz would create a **"double chokepoint"** scenario, disrupting **~30% of the world's seaborne oil** and a massive share of Asia-Europe trade. Approximately **12% of global trade** by value transits Bab al-Mandeb annually, carrying an estimated **4.8 million barrels of oil per day**.
- Major shipping lines **Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd, and CMA CGM** paused all **Trans-Suez sailings** citing the "deteriorating security situation" — even before a formal blockade. Despite no formal blockade, **Bab al-Mandeb traffic has been "sharply reduced."**
- **Saudi Arabia** has rerouted **~5 million barrels per day** — half its total production — across the Arabian Peninsula to **Red Sea terminals at Yanbu** to bypass Hormuz (Foreign Policy, Mar 30).
- **MARAD** (US Maritime Administration) issued security advisory for Red Sea / Bab al-Mandeb area.
- Houthis have been **aggressively moving toward rival-held territory** on Yemen's southwest coast, which if occupied would give them launching positions for further Bab al-Mandeb attacks.
- *Sources: Al Jazeera, CNN, PBS, NBC News, CNBC, Axios, Washington Post, Military.com, CGTN, France24, Sunday Guardian, Bloomberg, MARAD, Haaretz, Foreign Policy*
